## Goal

The deployed engine refuses a real delivery unit's close on its Definition of done when no certificate exists, and the refusal body is committed beside the certificate that lets the same unit close.

## Plan / audit source

- #837 P3.2 — the deployment-gated live refusal its handoff named as the follow-up.
- `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md` § How a certificate is produced, § Gate evidence.
- `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live on the released engine — the method this reuses.
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § Definition of done.
- #855 — the precedent: a live part a merged unit could not carry is its own unit.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `1` — authorised (`seed/programme-definition.json` tranches[1]) |
| Brief | `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery/project-brief.md` |
| ADM phase/plateau | `G`; capability |
| Benefits | `B1 — Auditable decisions`: the refusal and certificate ids are the re-checkable evidence that the DoD gate exists |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/871-live-gate` |
| HEAD | `e6de8e084` |
| Session | m4 · georgedekker · claude-code |
| Updated | 2026-11-27 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/actions/src/development.rs:unit_dod` — the close gate | main@279504718 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/proof/facts.rs:derive_unit_record` | main@279504718 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/proof/mod.rs` — `proofs.attest`, `proofs.record` | main@279504718 |
| Migration | `migrations/0081_unit_proof_policy.sql` | main@279504718 |
| Evidence | `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live on the released engine | main@279504718 |
| Script | `scripts/proof/collect_units.py:Engine.call` — the live transport | main@279504718 |
| Issue | #837 (closed), #855 (closed), #844 (closed) | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@279504718` · measured 2026-11-27T17:44Z.
- Docs: evidence `3665b74f` · plan `79b7890d` · contract `f6888695` · model `278eb0a8` · facts `d9f96e88`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The deployed gate | **LIVE** | `select max(version) from _sqlx_migrations` = 81 on the primary, 2026-11-27T17:38Z; pods on `sha256:dbb665e1…` |
| P1 the unit record | ABSENT | `development_project` has 0 rows live; no unit has been chartered |
| P2 the gates | ABSENT | same — no development gate exists |
| P3 the refusal | ABSENT | no live `development_projects.close` refusal is recorded |
| P4 the open path | ABSENT | no live `unit`-subject certificate exists |
| P5 the record | ABSENT | the evidence doc has no unit-gate section |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — #837's delivery chartered from real rows

`crates/actions/src/development.rs` charter · `proof/facts.rs` derivation.
Requirement: a `development_project` for #837's real delivery, a `proof_policy` pinned to `docs/SPEC_V2.md` and `required: true`, and the seven required steps recorded from the delivery's own facts.

- **P1.1** Given the deployed engine, when #837's delivery is chartered, then the read-back shows the policy with the SPEC_V2 digest and `required: true`.
  Verify: the `development_projects.get` answer recorded in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md`; `proof_policy.required = true` and `spec_sha256` is the committed SPEC_V2 content hash.
- **P1.2** Given the charter, when the seven steps are recorded, then `proofs.attest` derives facts with no `null` in any required field.
  Verify: the `proofs.attest` answer recorded; `facts_canonical` carries repo, lane, issue_ref, pull number/url/head, ci run/sha/verdict, merge sha, deploy digest, serving digest, health and the three gate booleans.

### P2 — the three gates approved

`crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs`.
Requirement: the review, merge and deploy gates are requested with their evidence and decided, and the review decision is a principal other than the implementer.

- **P2.1** Given the complete record, when the three gates are decided, then `development_projects.get` shows all three approved.
  Verify: the read-back recorded; each gate's status `approved` with its evidence id.
- **P2.2** Given the review gate, when its decision is read, then the approver id differs from the charter's `implementer_id`.
  Verify: the two ids recorded side by side in the evidence doc; they differ.

### P3 — the refusal

`crates/actions/src/development.rs:unit_dod` step 4.
Requirement: `development_projects.close` with no certificate answers the typed DoD refusal, and the engine records it.

- **P3.1** Given the complete record and no certificate, when `close` is called, then the engine answers `422 gate_evidence_missing`.
  Verify: the exact response body committed in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md`.
- **P3.2** Given the refusal, when the engine's own record is read, then the refused invocation is recorded.
  Verify: the `action_invocation` row for `development_projects.close` and the matching audit event, recorded.

### P4 — the path opens

`crates/actions/src/proof/mod.rs` attest/record · the prover's `lean4.check`.
Requirement: attest → kernel check → record stores a `unit` certificate, and the same close then succeeds.

- **P4.1** Given the refusal, when the rendered source is checked and recorded, then the certificate carries the kernel verdict and the derived facts digest.
  Verify: the certificate id, `facts_sha256`, `verdict` and `model_sha256` recorded.
- **P4.2** Given the certificate, when `close` runs again, then the closure succeeds with `lean_proof: proven`.
  Verify: the close answer recorded, naming the proof id and the facts digest.

### P5 — the record

`docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md`.
Requirement: every live body above is committed with its ids and digests, and the design pack builds.

- **P5.1** Given the bodies, when the evidence doc is committed, then the pack builds and the ids are greppable.
  Verify: `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check` exits 0; `git grep -c '<certificate id>' docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` is ≥ 2.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #837 | the gate this proves; its P3.2 is the source | closed |
| related | #855 | the live-transport method and the evidence-doc pattern | closed |
| related | #844 | the unit model the certificate closes | closed |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #18 | deployment — measured satisfied: 0081 is live | closed |

Blocker: none — the deployment prerequisite is met (measured 2026-11-27T17:38Z).

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every cited path resolves at `main@279504718`.
- [x] Every part has at least one scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed; the deployment prerequisite is measured satisfied.
- [x] One-PR scope: the evidence doc and no code.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] The refusal and the certificate are the deployed engine's own answers, recorded verbatim.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- No code, action, migration or schema change.
- Re-certifying the whole unit ledger (#865 owns the findings).
- The S2/S3 wings (#815/#816).

## Deployment prerequisite

The deployed engine must carry migration 0081. Measured satisfied 2026-11-27T17:38Z
(`max(_sqlx_migrations) = 81`, pods on `sha256:dbb665e1…`). If the engine moves below 81 before the
drill, the drill stops and names it.

## Open questions

- None.

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Evidence |
|---|---|
| P1.1 | `development_projects.get` read-back: policy `docs/SPEC_V2.md` `0651b0ec…`, `required: true` |
| P1.2 | `proofs.attest`: facts `3d390203…`, model `bbbc56e1…`, theorem `unit_record_ok`, no `null` in a required field |
| P2.1 | `approval_decision`: three `approve` rows (review `01a21e1e-dd58…`, merge `01a21e1f-dde2…`, deploy `01a21e21-7e45…`) |
| P2.2 | approver `01a1e8a7-8b23-…f7a545` ≠ implementer `01a21820-…3279e9`; closure `reviewer_id` names the same |
| P3.1 | 422 `gate_evidence_missing` body, verbatim, § The unit gate on the released engine |
| P3.2 | `action_invocation | development_projects.close | refused` and `audit_event | refused` at 17:51:53Z |
| P4.1 | certificate `01a21e24-9de2-…f459`, `verdict: proven`, `certificate_sha256 fd1eda04…`, `trust: kernel` |
| P4.2 | close `201`; closure `dod {required: true, lean_proof: proven, proof_id 01a21e24-…}` |
| P5.1 | `build-docs.py --check` 300 sources, 0 failures; PR #872 |

The eight merged PRs that carry no unit issue have a recorded owner decision — adopted retroactively or covered by an exemption written into the contract — so the ledger's remaining orphan count is a policy outcome instead of an unresolved defect.

| P2 the record | ABSENT | no issue carries the decision and `03-DELIVERY.md` has no exemption |

The eight, by branch and class: docs/deps — #64 (`lane/repo-standard`), #96 (`lane/licensing-readme`), #335 (`lane/deps-latest`), #774 (`lane/gemba-walk-docs`); code/CI — #465 (`lane/gate-ci`), #591 (`lane/ir-reasoning-dialect`), #597 (`lane/ir-stream-reasoning`), #613 (`lane/pgx-client-fixes`). ### P2 — the record

Requirement: the chosen outcome is durable — a retro unit record per PR, or the exemption in the contract that the collector's rule names.

- **P2.1** Given adoption, when the records exist, then a fresh render pairs each PR and `orphan_subkinds.no-issue` drops by the adopted count.
  Verify: `scripts/proof/collect-units.sh fetch/render` into a new run dir, then `jq '.orphan_subkinds' findings.json`

## Goal

The ledger stops counting non-unit bug/docs/ci/security/design issues as Definition-of-ready failures, because the model carries the `unit` fact that scopes the rule.

## Plan / audit source

## Goal

The live design snapshot carries the deployed image's build time, and the programme page shows a stale badge when the published data (`generated_at`) predates that build, or the commit and time when it does not.

## Plan / audit source

- #782 P3.2 (the one open part of the closed unit; the freeze and the site landed in `5a7d02dd`).
- `docs/design/README.md` (the live window) and `crates/api/src/design.rs` (the served snapshot).

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `unmapped` → PLATFORM (delivery-system rework; no programme tranche) |
| Brief | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.1 and §10.5.9 |
| ADM phase/plateau | — (no architecture change) |
| Benefits | `enabling — no direct benefit`: it makes the public page honest about how old its data is relative to the software serving it |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/867-deployed-build-stamp` |
| HEAD | `cc866c988dfcf7479eda2842277dab2e3a81737d` |
| Session | m4 · georgedekker · claude-code |
| Updated | 2026-11-27 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/api/src/design.rs:build_or_cached` (passes `state.config.git_sha` into `SiteArgs`) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `crates/pack/src/live.rs:SiteArgs` (`git_sha` = the served image's commit; `generated_at` = the newest published document's `updated_at`) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs:snapshot_js` (the snapshot header) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `crates/api/src/config.rs` (`git_sha` at the `CONVEYOR_GIT_SHA` pattern) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `Dockerfile` (`ARG GIT_SHA` → `ENV CONVEYOR_GIT_SHA`) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` (image build `--build-arg GIT_SHA`) | main@949e95c8c |
| Code | `docs/design/v2.js:liveSrc` (the live ribbon) | main@949e95c8c |
| Test | `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs::tests` (to extend) and `docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs` (fixture checks) | main@949e95c8c |
| Issue | #782 (closed; P3.2 is its remaining part) | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@949e95c8c` · measured 2026-11-27.
- Blobs: `crates/api/src/design.rs` `969867396887a07c9fcab5d5570b38aff125251a`; `crates/pack/src/live.rs` `4937af9c7932df842706d8c2bff56441e266b85e`; `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs` `8cd71feca7d1aa7e8684babcf1197842ba9a5f42`; `crates/api/src/config.rs` `b1df27ef5664bf93ff9fc39964d4753189eda965`; `docs/design/v2.js` `084a869c5a698ba1d85a486e77bdfb465d9bb6f0`; `Dockerfile` `0c30e1c0386b98fa7f86f0e2b24afa33349302da`; `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `5b20904b0d796cac78768a547c2ca6506ba74b3b`; `docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs` `7e8f69cdbf3596421ca14e109863ed40bbfdb8f3`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 the deployed build stamp | ABSENT | the live snapshot carries `git_sha` (the image commit) but no build time; `curl -fsS https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/snapshot.js` has no `deployed_at` |
| P2 the stale badge | ABSENT | `v2.js:92` renders `LIVE · snapshot <hash> · <generated_at> · <sha7>`; nothing compares it to the deployed build |
| P3 the live check | ABSENT | no deployed-commit signal to compare against (the #782 handoff's measured block) |

The comparison is `generated_at` (the newest published document's `updated_at`, i.e. the data's age) against the deployed image's **build time** (when the deployed commit reached the host), not the commit's author date. Absent stamp → no badge, never a fabricated time.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the deployed build stamp

Requirement: the image build records its build time, the server carries it, and the live snapshot header exposes it as `deployed_at` beside `git_sha`.

- **P1.1** Given an image built at time B from commit D, when the server serves `/design/data/snapshot.js`, then the snapshot carries `deployed_at = B` and `git_sha = D`; with no build arg both are `unknown`.
  Verify: `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs::tests::the_header_carries_the_deployed_build` (to create).
- **P1.2** Given a main-push image build, when CI builds the image, then the build receives `BUILD_TIME` and the runtime exports `CONVEYOR_BUILD_TIME`.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'BUILD_TIME' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml Dockerfile` (to contain both).

### P2 — the badge

Requirement: the live ribbon states stale or fresh from `generated_at` vs `deployed_at`.

- **P2.1** Given a snapshot whose `generated_at` predates `deployed_at`, when the programme page renders, then a badge names both times and the deployed sha (`STALE`).
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs` (fixture case, to extend).
- **P2.2** Given `generated_at` ≥ `deployed_at`, then the page shows the fresh state with the commit and time and no `STALE` badge.
  Verify: the same check's fresh fixture case.
- **P2.3** Given no `deployed_at` (local/dev), then no badge is rendered.
  Verify: the same check's absent-stamp case.

### P3 — the live check (deployment-gated)

- **P3.1** Given the deployed image after this merges, when the public site is fetched, then `/design/data/snapshot.js` carries `deployed_at` and the page's badge state matches the comparison.
  Verify: `curl -fsS https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/snapshot.js | grep -o '"deployed_at":"[^"]*"'` and a page fetch.

### P1 — the live evidence, committed

`docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Units · #836 P3.2, P3.3.
Requirement: the deployment-gated live run is committed beside the snapshot, with every id and digest named.

  certified, then two `unit_ledger` certificates are stored with verdict `unproven` and the programme
  bundle over their digests is `proven`.

- **P1.2** Given the ledger is certified, when the passing-subset control runs over the same

  Verify: `python3 scripts/proof/control_units.py docs/evidence/units/2026-11-27 https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai ~/.conveyor/nonagentic.token docs/evidence/units/2026-11-27/control`, then the same `certificates.json` check.

  then the fresh verdict equals the stored one and the response is committed.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/proof/control_units.py reverify …` (or the recorded command), and `python3 -c` over `reverify.json` asserting `verdict == "unproven"` and `fresh_check_valid is False`.
- **P1.4** Given the committed evidence, when the design pack is built, then § Evaluation names
  every certificate id and digest and the index is current.
  Verify: `git grep -c '01a21d8a' docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` is ≥ 3 and `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check` exits 0.

  Verify: `python3 scripts/proof/collect_units.py --self-test` asserts the header (extend the self-test).
- **P2.2** (live) Given the deployed engine, when the collector certifies through the public host,
  then it receives action responses, not an edge refusal.
  Verify: the P1.1 command exits 0 and its output contains no `403` / `1010`.

### P3 — the token trap, recorded

`apps/server/src/admin/upstream_tokens.rs:114` · #776.
Requirement: the evidence doc states the sealed prover token's lifetime and the operator renewal.

- **P3.1** Given the evidence doc, when a reader looks for the credential's lifetime, then it states
  the 60-minute mint and the `conveyor admin upstream-token --service lean4 --mint` renewal.
  Verify: `git grep -n '60-minute' docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` returns the paragraph.

- Plan blob: `aa9f03ad17e87127da9735aeb3058d620ad27dd4` (`docs/plans/T18-real-v2-ui.md`).
- Measured 2026-11-27 on the `#526` lane that carries this unit; the coverage gate currently reports `T18` as a non-built project with no open unit.

## Current state (measured)

Every destination has a route in `apps/web/src/app.rs` and a spec in `apps/web/e2e/`. What is missing is assertion coverage inside five specs:

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the five under-asserted destination specs

Plan §10. Requirement: each destination's spec asserts empty, error, happy and one refusal.

- **P1.1** Given a tenant with no portfolio rows, when the spec loads `/portfolio` with a failing read stubbed or forced, then it asserts the error notice and one server refusal, not only the happy table.
  Verify: `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/portfolio.spec.ts`
- **P1.2** Given a tenant with no programmes, when `/programme` is loaded and a refused action is attempted, then the spec asserts the empty state's successor, the error notice and the refusal.
  Verify: `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/programme.spec.ts`
- **P1.3** Given a tenant with no boards or WBS, when `/plan` is loaded, then the spec asserts the empty project list before the populated path.
  Verify: `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/plan.spec.ts`
- **P1.4** Given no incidents, when `/operations` is loaded, then the spec asserts the empty list.
  Verify: `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/operations.spec.ts`
- **P1.5** Given no toolkits, when `/tools` is loaded, then the spec asserts the empty list.
  Verify: `npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/tools.spec.ts`

### P2 — the coverage record and the programme unit set

Plan §8, §10. Requirement: the V2 coverage record reports each destination from a real route and spec, and the programme gate sees the unit.

- **P2.1** Given the ten specs, when the record is rebuilt, then it matches the routes and specs.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-v2-coverage.py --check`
- **P2.2** Given the record, when the programme's project/unit set is checked, then no non-built project lacks an open unit.
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs`

### P3 — the browser gate

Plan §10. Requirement: `web.yml` is the verdict for `apps/web/**`.

- **P3.1** Given the pushed branch, when `web.yml` runs, then every spec passes on the stock runner.
  Verify: the PR's `web` workflow run (no local compile is a verdict)

|---|---|---|---|
| related | #846 | the `#526` lane publishes the coverage record this unit's `T18` status reads; rebase and regenerate, never hand-merge | open |
| related | #526 | the programme rework lane; this unit is its T18 gate remainder | open |
| acceptance-blocked-by | none | the destinations' live backends are already merged (#562–#566) | — |

No `blocked-by`: construction and specs do not wait on another unit.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the plan blob recorded.
- [x] Every cited path resolves at `origin/main 54e1ffcaa`.
- [x] Every part has a `Verify:` command or a workflow target.
- [x] Dependencies typed; no `blocked-by` is open.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint: the five spec files only, plus no production code unless a state is genuinely unreachable.

## Definition of done

- [ ] The five specs assert the missing states; every other destination's spec still passes.
- [ ] `web.yml` green on the PR.
- [ ] `build-v2-coverage.py --check` and `check-coverage.cjs` green.
- [ ] The PR carries `Closes #<n>`; one branch, one PR; no acceptance weakened or skipped.

## Out of scope

- New destinations, new tables/actions/events, SSR, a second router, retiring the design pack.
- Reopening the closed T18 units (#562–#566); this unit covers only the gate's remainder.
- Any change to the `#526` lane's generated record.

## Deployment prerequisite

None. `apps/web` is served by the existing binary; the gate is the browser workflow, not a rollout.

## Open questions

- Should a destination's empty-state assertion be a dedicated `test` per destination, or a shared helper table? Default: one dedicated test per destination, so a failure names the destination.

| P1 | spec files + `web.yml` run | |
| P2 | `build-v2-coverage.py --check`, `check-coverage.cjs` output | |

### P1 — The record reconciles to the live close-out

- **P1.3** Given a live id is written, when the record is reviewed, then the unit's evidence table carries the read-back command and result for it — or, where the record transport was unavailable, a provenance line naming the issue record instead of the id.
  Verify: the Evidence at completion table (one row per id class); `git grep -n 'provenance' docs/plans/inception/GEMBA-WALK/`.

### P2 — The instrument sees the action sheet by capability

Requirement: `modules_present()` detects the manifest, the action sheet and the schema form by capability, wherever the implementation provides them; the self-test pins present/absent/renamed shapes.

- **P2.1** Given the delivered client, when the instrument prints coverage, then every action is `schema-rendered` and none is `absent`.

### P3 — The workflow feeds the report

  Verify: `gh workflow run walk.yml --ref <branch>` → the run's log line `walk coverage: … verified N` with N equal to the registered rows; run id recorded in Evidence at completion.
- **P3.2** Given the committed record, when the PR is reviewed, then the record was regenerated by the instrument, never hand-edited, and `--check` exits 0.

## Goal

Any signed-in tenant user can report a bug or request a feature from inside the conveyor UI, and the
platform operator can read every tenant's submission with one admin command.

## Plan / audit source

feedback about the platform and request features inside the ui". The surface is T18's real UI —
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12 T18 (every V2 destination is a route in `apps/web` with a screen module and a
Playwright spec). The design pack's GitHub-derived feedback list is a different surface and stays
as-is (`docs/design/README.md`).

Requirement: a feedback row carries tenant, author, kind (`bug`|`feature`|`other`), title, body,

- **P1.2** Given an empty title or body, or an unknown kind, when the write is attempted, then it is

### P2 — the actions

Requirement: `feedback.create` and `feedback.list` are tenant-scoped member actions. Retries are

- **P2.1** Given a signed-in member, when they invoke `feedback.create`, then 200 with the row and

  Verify: `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test feedback` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given the same `idempotency-key`, when the create is retried, then one row exists and the
  second call replays the first outcome.
  Verify: the same test binary, `a_retry_with_the_same_key_is_one_row` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given the new actions, then the pinned registry, the served spec, the HTTP/MCP parity and
  the design-pack action dump move in the same PR.
  Verify: `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test registry`; the `parity` workflow;
  `conveyor admin actions dump --json --out docs/design/data/actions.json`;
  `node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs --self-test`

### P3 — the UI surface

Requirement: every route carries an accessible feedback affordance; the form captures the current
route automatically.

- **P3.1** Given any signed-in page, when the user opens Feedback, chooses a kind, writes a title and
  body, and submits, then the receipt is shown and the row appears in the tenant's list.
  Verify: `apps/web/e2e/feedback.spec.ts` (to create) — happy, empty-submit refusal, error state,
  empty list.
- **P3.2** Given a signed-out visitor, then no anonymous submission exists: the affordance is absent
  or leads to sign-in.
  Verify: the same spec's signed-out case.

### P4 — the operator's cross-tenant read and the tenant's history

Requirement: the tenant's app page keeps its own submission history; the platform operator reads
every tenant's feedback with one admin command. The operator is a `platform_admin` (the one global
grant, `Session.is_super_admin`), but no action declares `Tenancy::Platform` and the agent surface
refuses one for a tenant-bound caller (`agent_surface.rs:82`); a GitHub bridge cannot use the
operator's token either (it is a per-tenant sealed secret, `publish.rs:8`). The admin CLI therefore
runs on the platform pool and scopes each tenant in turn, exactly like `seed_programme(pool, None)`.
A super-admin HTTP route (`crates/api/src/routes/platform.rs`) is the later in-UI option.

- **P4.1** Given two tenants' rows, when the operator runs `conveyor admin feedback list --json`,
  then every tenant's rows are listed with tenant slug, author, kind, status and age;
  `--tenant <slug>` and `--status open` filter; no tenant can read another tenant's rows through the
  HTTP action.
  Verify: `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test feedback` (the isolation case) and
  `apps/server/tests/feedback_admin.rs` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a row, when a tenant opens its feedback page, then it sees only its own rows and
  their status.
  Verify: `apps/web/e2e/feedback.spec.ts::the_tenant_sees_only_its_rows` (to create)

- **P5.1** Given the route and the spec, then the design-pack's screen coverage and the docs index
  are current.
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs`; `node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs`;

## Goal

Every delivery unit on the real ledger carries a kernel-checked certificate that names the rule it fails, produced from committed raw evidence, so the conveyor's current delivery is evaluated by proof instead of by opinion.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md` § What is proven, § The certificate, § Units.
- `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Measurement, § Live — the method reused here (a check run with `lake env lean` in the prover's own project).
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § The unit, § Claim — four checks, § Enforcement, § The PR — exactly one, § CI budget — the rules the model encodes.
- `docs/spec/lean/DeliveryModel.lean` — the model being extended; `docs/spec/lean/README.md` — what a certificate does not prove.

**Written split (03-DELIVERY exception, 2 issues, reason in both).** #744/#746 established the
capability (store, actions, gate evidence). The remaining work is two genuinely independent
deliverables with different acceptance and different deployment gates: this unit is the *model and
the evaluation* — no engine path changes beyond the subject kind needed to record a unit; its sibling
is the *engine-derived facts and the required gate*, which changes actions and gate resolution. The
sibling is `blocked-by` this one because it consumes `checkUnit`.

## Programme

| Field | Value |

| Migration | `migrations/0076_lean_proof.sql` — `proof.subject_type` | main@34a87d781 |
| Script | `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` — the prose-rule check this is compared against | main@34a87d781 |
| Script | `scripts/ci/gate.sh`, `scripts/check-parity.py` | main@34a87d781 |
| Code | `scripts/proof/collect-units.sh`, `scripts/lean/check-model.sh` | to create |
| Issue | #744, #746, #762 — the capability this extends | closed |

## Baseline

- Docs: plan `eb049fa38e40` · contract `105143f04715` · evidence `a3313b932358` · model `9da3879dc086` · spec README `acdf916e5896` (`git rev-parse origin/main:<path>`).

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Certificate machinery: store, renderer, refusals, gate evidence kind | **DONE** | #744, #746, #762 closed; live drills in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live |
| A formal statement of a delivery unit's rules | **ABSENT** | `docs/spec/lean/DeliveryModel.lean` has `checkSlice`/`checkProgramme`/`checkPackage` only; `proof.subject_type` has no unit kind |
| A certificate over any real delivery record | **ABSENT** | every measured certificate is a drill or a synthetic corpus |
| Facts with provenance a third party can re-derive | **ABSENT** | `proofs.record` takes `facts_canonical` from the request |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the spike: chunk size from bytes, not guesswork

**P1.1** Given the certificate source embeds the model and its facts, when rendered `UnitFacts` are
checked at N = 40, 80 and 200, then each source stays under the prover's 100 000-character limit, the
chunk size is recorded with its byte count and wall clock, and no check uses `native_decide`.
`Verify:` `scripts/lean/check-model.sh corpus --sizes 40,80,200` (to create) — exit 0 and its table
appended to `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md`.

**P1.2** Given the measured byte cost per unit, when one chunk is chosen, then the full ledger's chunk
count is stated in the evidence doc and every chunk's source is re-measured at that size.
`Verify:` the recorded table; `wc -c` on each rendered source.

### P2 — `checkUnit` in the model

**P2.1** Given a unit with one live branch, one non-draft PR, at most two CI runs, and a merge whose
issue is closed and branch deleted, when `checkUnit` runs, then it holds.
`Verify:` exit 0 for that rendered positive case.

**P2.2** Given a unit with two live branches, or two PRs, or three CI runs, or a merge whose issue is
still open, when `checkUnit` runs, then each of the four is refused by the kernel.
`Verify:` exit 1 on each of the four named negative cases — a model that cannot fail is not a model.

**P2.3** Given the model is embedded verbatim in every certificate, when it is checked, then the three
existing universal theorems still hold and the file stays core Lean: no Mathlib import, no
`native_decide`, no compiler dependency.
`Verify:` `git grep -n 'import Mathlib\|native_decide' -- docs/spec/lean/DeliveryModel.lean` returns
nothing, and the model's own theorems exit 0.

**P2.4** Given a unit certificate must be storable, when `proofs.record` is called with the unit
subject, then `proof.subject_type` accepts it and no prior value is removed.
`Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/proofs_record.rs::unit_subject_kind` (to create) against real
PostgreSQL 18; the migration's `\d+ proof` shows the new value beside the old six.

### P3 — the collector and the evaluation

**P3.1** Given a window of real units, when the collector runs, then every field carries an extraction
rule id and the id of the raw payload it was read from, no field is defaulted, and an unestablished
fact is `unknown`, which fails closed.
`Verify:` `scripts/proof/collect-units.sh` (to create) run twice on the same window — identical
`facts_sha256`, and a unit with a missing input shows `unknown`, not `true`.

**P3.2** Given the collected facts, when a unit's certificate is recorded, then the engine re-renders
the source, accepts it, and a fresh check re-verifies the stored certificate.
`Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/proofs_record.rs::unit_certificate` (to create) plus one live
`proofs.record` 201 and one `proofs.reverify` recorded with its response body.

**P3.3** Given the full window, when the evaluation completes, then it reports per-rule totals, the
violating units by number, the corpus hash, the model and spec digests, and at least one real unit is
refused — the first genuine refusal cycle.
`Verify:` the evaluation section in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` and the programme bundle
certificate id it names; re-running the collector reproduces the same verdicts.

**P3.4** Given `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` and the two plan audits state the same rules in
prose, when the kernel verdict disagrees with them, then the disagreement is reported as a finding
with both answers, never reconciled silently.
`Verify:` a disagreement table in the evidence doc with one row per differing unit, or an explicit
"no disagreement" with the sample size.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Source | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #744 | the store and actions this extends | closed |
| related | #746 | the corpus and renderer this extends | closed |
| related | #762 | the live drills whose method P1 reuses | closed |
| blocks | #837 | the split above | open |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #18 (deployment) | live records in P3.2 need the deployed engine | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the plan/audit blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/plan/code/test reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `Blocker:` line, no `status:blocked`.
- [x] One-PR scope; the sibling unit is sequenced behind this one.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`preflight.yml` for the compile/lint verdict, the PR's CI for the rest).
- [ ] Tests added/updated per part; none skipped.
- [ ] Docs updated: `docs/spec/lean/README.md` (the unit subject), `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md` § Units, and the evidence section.
- [ ] Migrations and `--check-lock` handled: the subject-kind change refreshes `served-spec.lock.json`,
      `docs/design/data/actions.json` (`scripts/build-coverage.py`) and the `parity` samples.
- [ ] Live verification recorded where deployment is a prerequisite.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Deriving facts engine-side and refusing caller-supplied facts — the sibling unit.
- Deriving `required` from the issue brief's BDD `Verify:` parts (needs the body stored engine-side).
- Rust-level verification, model-to-implementation refinement, prover-signed certificates.
- Any new service: the collector is a CLI, the certificate path is the existing `proofs.*` actions.

## Deployment prerequisite

The deployed engine carrying `0076` and the prover external, plus the sealed `lean4.token` — all live
per `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live, so P3.2 records against it rather than waiting.

## Open questions

  measurement and recorded, not guessed.

## Evidence at completion

| P1.1 | `check-model.sh corpus --sizes 40,80,200` | exit 0; 14 554 / 22 094 / 44 714 B |

## Goal

The broker enforces the run's declared spend budget before any dispatch: a `spend` tool call with no budget, or with the budget exhausted, is refused `429 tool_budget_exceeded` with the upstream untouched, and every dispatched call's cost is written to the tool ledger.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json` — entry `v1-w4a-1` (T13, P0) and `v1-p75-1` (T11, P0), the same mechanism (blob `8fe5db1`).

- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.3 step 2 (the typed 429), §11.4 (the spend row's "budget check + ledger"), §11.8/§11.9 (cost per call).

| P3 the ledgered cost | ABSENT | `tool_call.cost` is never written for a dispatched call |
| P4 the live proof | ABSENT | no receipt names a refusal with the upstream untouched and a ledgered cost at the deployed image |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the budget resolver

- **P1.1** Given a job release's `anatomy.limits.cost_budget_usd`, a binding `meta.limits` override, and a run's `inputs.limits`, when the broker reads the budget, then the run's value wins over the binding's, which wins over the release's, and the resolver is the one function those three sources pass through.
  Verify: a test to create (ported from the lane's `tool_budget.rs`) asserting each precedence.

### P2 — the refusal happens before dispatch

- **P2.1** Given a run with no declared budget, when a `spend`-class tool is called, then the call is refused `429 tool_budget_exceeded` and the stub upstream's hit counter does not move.
  Verify: the ported test with the hit counter; the error's code is exactly `tool_budget_exceeded`.

- **P2.2** Given a run whose spent total has reached its limit, when a `spend` tool is called, then it is refused `429` with the spent and limit values in the detail, again with zero upstream calls.
  Verify: the ported test.

### P3 — the cost is ledgered

- **P3.1** Given a dispatched spend-class call, when it completes, then `tool_call.cost` carries its cost (a capturing action's inference cost is counted once, from the derived ledger), readable from the row, not from the broker's return value.
  Verify: the ported test reads back the `tool_call` row's cost.

- **P3.2** Given an internal-agent binding with no ceiling, when its run starts, then the start is refused (the `v1-p75-1` half of the same mechanism).
  Verify: the ported test asserting the run-start refusal.

### P4 — the live proof (deployment-gated)

- **P4.1** Given the merged image, when a spend call runs with no budget and one with a budget, then the first answers `429 tool_budget_exceeded` with the upstream untouched and the second writes a `tool_call.cost` row.
  Verify: two live `tools.call` invocations at the deployed digest, with the responses and the ledger row recorded under `docs/evidence/`.

- **P8.1** Given the dev seed, when `/organisation` opens, then industries, departments, job
  catalogue, policies, refinements, ladder and Laya configs render with the four states.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio-organisation/organisation.spec.ts` (to create)
- **P8.2** Given `departments.create`, when submitted, then it carries `Idempotency-Key`, the
  section refetches, and a duplicate is refused verbatim.
  Verify: the same spec

### P9 — `jobs` (`/jobs`)
`GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4 Organisation row · `jobs.rs:JobsScreen`
Requirement: the catalogue, releases, bindings and agents render; publish, bind and run behave as
`apps/web`.

- **P9.1** Given the dev seed, when `/jobs` opens, then the positions and the selected detail
  render with the four states.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio-organisation/jobs.spec.ts` (to create)
- **P9.2** Given a stale binding, when `runs.create` submits with `release_hash`, then the server's
  `409 job_binding_stale` is shown verbatim and the bindings refetch.
  Verify: the same spec

### P10 — `agents` (`/agents`)
`GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4 Organisation row · `agents.rs:AgentsScreen`
Requirement: the capability-agent read renders as `apps/web`; no write.

- **P10.1** Given the dev seed, when `/agents` opens, then the agents render with the four states.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio-organisation/agents.spec.ts` (to create)

### P11 — `tools` (`/tools`)
`GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4 Organisation row · `tools.rs:Tools`
Requirement: the read surface and its writes render as `apps/web`, including the plan gate and the
`If-Match` requirements.

- **P11.1** Given a principal without `tools.list`, when `/tools` opens, then it renders "Tools is
  planned" naming `tools.list`, exactly as `apps/web`.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio-organisation/tools.spec.ts` (to create)
- **P11.2** Given `tool_bindings.retire` without a version, when submitted, then the form refuses
  client-side; with the version it carries `If-Match` and the list refetches.
  Verify: the same spec

### P12 — `project-types` (`/project-types`)
`GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4 Organisation row · `project_types.rs:ProjectTypesScreen`
Requirement: the project-request read and its approval write render as `apps/web`.

- **P12.1** Given the dev seed, when `/project-types` opens, then the requests render with the four
  states, and `project_requests.approve` shows the server's refusal verbatim when refused.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio-organisation/project-types.spec.ts` (to create)

### P13 — the S1 route file
`GEMBA-WALK.md` §8 S1 row · `GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §6.1
Requirement: `portfolio-organisation.js` exports the 15 rows (12 modules) and no other wing's file
is edited.

- **P13.1** Given the S1 route file, when the registry composes it, then each row carries the
  census's `walk`, `app`, `room` and `spec` exactly, and the instrument sees 15 registered rows.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-walk-coverage.py --check`

### P14 — the deployed read-only spec
`GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §11 · `playwright.config.ts` OIDC mode
Requirement: a read-only spec signs in as `conveyor-e2e` on the game host and asserts S1's routes
render without a server error, run only through `npm run test:deployed`.

- **P14.1** (live, deployment-gated by the image) Given the deployed build, when the spec signs in,
  then S1's routes render with their reads/gates and no 5xx; the spec never writes.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/deployed/s1-portfolio-organisation.spec.ts` (to create)

## Dependencies

## Definition of ready

- [x] Every cited path resolves at the claim sha; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.

- [ ] Each spec asserts loading, empty, happy and error/denied, plus one refusal or write; manifest gating is asserted.
- [ ] The instrument's rows for S1 are green by the same run's report; the coverage record is regenerated, never hand-edited.

## Out of scope

- The `portfolio.*` destination, which G0 owns as the exemplar.
- S2, S3 and S4 destinations; the shared seams (`api`, `forms`, `shell`, `router`, `world/port`, `a11y`), which are parent-owned.

- Primacy, `apps/web` retirement, the P6 gate.

issues.title: S1 — Gemba Walk: Portfolio & plan + Organisation read/write parity

issues.body:
## Goal

The game client is served at `https://game.nonagentic.ai/` at the root, with its own public Keycloak client `conveyor-game`, and works end to end for the Portfolio destination — the frozen census and serverless parity instrument, the measured renderer decision (ADR 0023), the `bevy_ecs 0.20.1` world crate, the foundation with one real write, and a real production sign-in proven with `conveyor-e2e` — with every acceptance evidenced. Change control: CR-WALK-001 (`docs/plans/inception/GEMBA-WALK/08-change-request-001-host-and-identity.md`), ADR 0024, C-WALK-3; the owner's 2026-11-27 direction amends ADR 0021 decisions 1 and 4 in part.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` §6–§8.1 — the parity model, the stage gates and the delivery split.
- `docs/plans/inception/GEMBA-WALK/07-governance-and-evidence.md` — W0, W1, W1a–W1d, W2.
- `docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4–§12 — routing, the action contract, the client modules, deployment.
- `docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §1–§16 — the world-layer architecture.
- Not in `docs/evidence/2026-11-10-plan-audit.md`: this is a project plan, not an `S##` slice; the WBS is its work-package source.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `0 (cross-cutting)` — GEMBA-WALK is registered in `scripts/build-programme-seed.py`; live project `01a21af4-f064-79b3-b302-7d9d81f9d072` |
| Brief | published project brief `01a21af5-3413-736b-935b-fdfff5968e78`; ADR 0021; `docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` |
| ADM phase/plateau | `Preliminary–D / PSA+HLD` — the unit changes the architecture (renderer ADR 0023, the world layer, the host and identity ADR 0024) |
| Benefits | `01a21af9-cfcd-73ab-8eff-39cab33f7525` (B8) — enabling, no direct benefit; the client enables the P6 primacy decision |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/813-walk-g0` |
| HEAD | `b50225cc7` (rebased onto `origin/main` `4a26b1617`) |
| Session | `m4/Claude Code (claim nonce 98071326-4AEE-47C0-9903-4416E7CFFFA5)` |
| Updated | `2026-11-27` |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §4–§12 | main@e2507c860 |
| Plan | `docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` §6–§8.1 | main@e2507c860 |
| WBS | `docs/plans/inception/GEMBA-WALK/07-governance-and-evidence.md` W0–W2 | main@e2507c860 |
| Architecture | `docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §1–§16 | main@e2507c860 |
| ADR | `docs/decisions/0021-gemba-walk-client.md` | main@e2507c860 |
| ADR | `docs/decisions/0022-bevy-ecs-world-layer.md` | main@e2507c860 |
| Code | `crates/api/src/web.rs:serve` | main@e2507c860 |

| Code | `apps/web/src/auth.rs` | main@e2507c860 |
| Code | `apps/web/src/screens/v2.rs` (the Portfolio read trace) | main@e2507c860 |

| Test | `crates/walk-world/tests/*` | to create |

## Baseline

- Code: rebased onto `origin/main@4a26b16174f4fa49926506bc2b23e68510b0c1ce`, measured 2026-11-27; the earlier baseline was `e2507c860`.
- Docs: plan blob at the new head; WBS/SPEC/ECS as published; `actions.json` still 598 names (572 attributes + 26 manual). The host/identity change is CR-WALK-001 and ADR 0024.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| W0 census/instrument | DONE on the branch; re-key pending | `scripts/build-walk-coverage.py`, `docs/evidence/walk-{census,coverage,exemptions}.json`; `--check` 52/598 green; the host-rooted re-freeze is W2c |
| W1 renderer spike | DONE | run 45953201576; `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md`; ADR 0023 |
| W1a ECS core | DONE | `crates/walk-world`, 11 headless tests, golden `e454532d51893682` |
| W1b command/wasm | DONE | the command/wasm tests in `crates/walk-world/tests` |
| W1c replay/determinism | DONE | `replay_is_deterministic`, `no_schedule_ambiguity` |
| W1d FrameView/canvas | PARTIAL | the crate view/wasm surface exists; the browser adapter is W2b |
| W2a serving/identity | ABSENT | the sub-site fallback exists (commit `41442e06e`); the host dispatch, the `azp` allowlist and the `conveyor-game` client are to build |
| W2b client | ABSENT | `apps/walk` carries only `data/world.json` |
| W2c tests/CI | ABSENT | no `walk.yml`; no deployed OIDC spec |
| Context: project, brief, SoAW, B8, ten artefact rows, ECS doc | DONE | #792 and #806 close-outs; live project `01a21af4-…`, brief `01a21af5-…`, B8 `01a21af9-…` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — W0: census and the serverless parity instrument
`docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` §6 · WBS W0
Requirement: freeze the route/action census at the branch base and make every coverage claim machine-checkable with no server or database.

- **P1.1** Given the branch base, when the census is frozen from the 572 `#[crate::action]` attributes and the 26 manual `inventory::submit!` registrations, then the union set-equals the names in `actions.json`, the routes equal the measured router set, and both counts and the baseline sha are recorded.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-walk-coverage.py --freeze --check` (to create) + `docs/evidence/walk-census.json` (to create).
- **P1.2** Given a census route that claims coverage without a registry row, when `--check` runs with no server/DB/network, then it exits non-zero naming the gap.
  Verify: `bash scripts/ci/tests/walk_coverage.sh` (to create).
- **P1.3** Given an action that claims `reachable`/`schema-rendered` without evidence, or an expired exemption, when `--check` runs, then it exits non-zero for each.
  Verify: the same self-test fixtures (to create).
- **P1.4** Given an absent census row, when `--gate=P6` runs, then it exits non-zero; `--check` alone accepts the absence.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-walk-coverage.py --gate=P6` (to create; expected failure on the fixture).
- **P1.5** Given the same inputs, when the instrument runs twice, then the output is byte-identical.
  Verify: the determinism case in `scripts/ci/tests/walk_coverage.sh` (to create).

### P2 — W1: the renderer spike and ADR 0023
`docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` §7 P0 · WBS W1
Requirement: prove every risky client contract in a browser before the foundation depends on it, and record the canvas-2D vs WebGL2 measurement.

- **P2.1** Given the dev origin, when the spike runs the auth-code + PKCE S256 flow, then it reaches `/walk/` or records the exact redirect mismatch; the dev-cookie path also works.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md` (to create) + the spike workflow run id.
- **P2.2** Given the spike, when it opens the schema sheet for a read, a write and a destructive action, then the form renders, the approval requirement is shown, the refusal is verbatim, and the `If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key` and `approval_id` headers are captured.
  Verify: `spike/walk/e2e/spike.spec.ts` (to create; deleted with the spike) + the captured trace in the record.
- **P2.3** Given the reference scene, when it runs five times under 4× CPU and Slow 4G, then bytes gzip, cold load → interactive, frame p50/p95, heap, browser requirements, CI build time and DOM focus are recorded, and ADR 0023 names the winner and the budgets.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md` + `docs/decisions/0023-gemba-walk-renderer.md` (to create).
- **P2.4** Given `apps/web`'s Portfolio screen, when its read trace is captured, then the walk uses the same contract — `programmes.list` is a POST action invocation, not a literal GET — and any SPEC §5 wording correction is recorded.
  Verify: the trace in `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md` (to create).

### P3 — W1a: the ECS core
`docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §1–§9 · WBS W1a
Requirement: the entity, component, resource, schedule and projection layer compiles natively and passes its headless scenarios.

- **P3.1** Given a snapshot, when it is projected twice, then every component and the key set are identical.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/projection.rs::projection_is_idempotent` (to create).
- **P3.2** Given a record absent for one generation, when the next snapshot also misses it, then it despawns; with an open sheet, it is pinned.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/projection.rs::despawn_requires_two_generations` and `::sheet_subject_is_pinned` (to create).
- **P3.3** Given the avatar outside a wall, when it walks into it, then a prompt names the destination.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/scenarios.rs::walk_to_wall_prompts` (to create).

### P4 — W1b: the command path and the wasm boundary
`docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §8, §11 · WBS W1b
Requirement: a write is an intent that leaves only through the manifest, and the boundary is JSON at the edge.

- **P4.1** Given a destructive action without approval, when submitted, then no call leaves and the refusal is shown.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/command.rs::destructive_requires_approval` (to create).
- **P4.2** Given a submitted call, when a refusal arrives, then `PendingCall` clears and the problem is surfaced.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/command.rs::refusal_clears_pending` (to create).
- **P4.3** Given a reader ordered before its writer in a set, when unchained, then it sees the message on the next frame; chained, the same frame.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/command.rs::same_frame_ordering` (to create).
- **P4.4** Given the same JSON input, when it crosses the wasm surface and the native API, then the values are equal.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/wasm_boundary.rs::wasm_json_roundtrip_matches_native` (to create).

### P5 — W1c: replay and determinism
`docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §10, §14 · WBS W1c
Requirement: the simulation is deterministic and its schedule is ambiguity-free under the test settings.

- **P5.1** Given a replay log, when replayed twice, then the FrameView hash is equal.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/replay.rs::replay_is_deterministic` (to create).
- **P5.2** Given the built schedule with ambiguity detection set to error, when initialized, then no ambiguity is reported.
  Verify: `crates/walk-world/tests/ambiguity.rs::no_schedule_ambiguity` (to create).

### P6 — W1d: the FrameView adapter and the canvas-2D baseline
`docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` §13 · WBS W1d
Requirement: the renderer consumes the FrameView and the browser reproduces the native view.

- **P6.1** Given the golden scenario, when the native crate and the wasm module each produce a FrameView, then the quantized hashes are equal.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/walk-frame.sha256` (to create) + `apps/walk/e2e/world/world.spec.ts::view_hash_matches_native_golden` (to create).
- **P6.2** Given the world canvas, when a wall is selected, then the destination sheet opens and focus returns on close.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/world/world.spec.ts` (to create).

### P7 — W2: foundation, Portfolio and serving
`docs/plans/GEMBA-WALK.md` §7 P1 · SPEC §4–§6, §10 · WBS W2
Requirement: sign-in (dev cookie in CI, the real `conveyor-game` PKCE flow in the deployed proof), tenant switch, manifest navigation, the world entrance, the Portfolio read and one real write, deep links, the host dispatch and boundary, and the `/walk` 308 work.

- **P7.1** Given the dev cookie, when the walk opens, then sign-in, tenant switch, manifest-driven navigation, the world entrance and the Portfolio read render with loading, empty, error and denied states.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/shell/*.spec.ts` and `apps/walk/e2e/portfolio/*.spec.ts` (to create).
- **P7.2** Given the Portfolio read, when one real write is submitted through the action sheet, then the request carries the correct headers, the read refetches, and a refusal is shown verbatim.
  Verify: the same portfolio spec + the captured trace (to create).
- **P7.3** Given the game host, when `/`, `/portfolio` and an asset are requested, then the walk entry/asset is served; a missing asset 404s; `/mcp` and `/design` 404; the operator host is unchanged and `/walk/portfolio` 308s to the game path.
  Verify: the host matrix in `crates/api/src/web.rs` and `crates/api/tests/web_hosts.rs` (to create).
- **P7.4** Given a browser session, when it visits the walk, then no `conveyor.gemba.*` storage is written and no snapshot URL is fetched.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/shell/*.spec.ts` (to create).
- **P7.5** Given the five route files, when the registry composes them, then core holds the Portfolio rows (host-rooted paths) and the four sibling files exist as empty arrays.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-walk-coverage.py --check`.
- **P7.6** Given the git-managed realm patch, when the manual Job runs, then `conveyor-game` exists with PKCE S256, the game redirect/web origin and the `conveyor` audience mapper; the API accepts its `azp` and rejects any other.
  Verify: the Job log + the admin-API read-back + the auth tests (to create).
- **P7.7** Given a deployed game host, when the OIDC project signs in as `conveyor-e2e`, then the Portfolio read renders and `/api/me` is 200.
  Verify: `apps/walk/e2e/deployed/*.spec.ts` against `BASE_URL=https://game.nonagentic.ai` (to create).

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | gitops-production change (this unit) | the realm patch (`conveyor-game`), the cloudflared ingress, the VirtualService host and the deployment env; CR-WALK-001 | open |
| related | #792 | the inception set and the live project this unit builds on | closed |
| related | #806 | ADR 0022 and the ECS architecture this unit implements | closed |
| blocks | #814 | the S1 wing; plan §8 | open |
| blocks | #815 | the S2 wing; plan §8 | open |
| blocks | #816 | the S3 wing; plan §8 | open |
| blocks | #817 | the S4 gate; blocked by the three wings | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (rebased to `01544010f`); plan/WBS/SPEC/ECS/ADR 0024/CR-WALK-001 recorded.
- [x] Every cited path resolves at main@e2507c860 or is marked `to create`.
- [x] Every part has at least one BDD scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no `blocked-by`, so `status:ready`.
- [x] One-PR scope; the five-issue split is the written exception (plan §8, ADR 0021).
- [x] Scope corrections applied: no backend surface, no primacy claim, no mock fixtures.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; one Evidence row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head: preflight (compile/lint) and the PR's CI; docs `build-docs`, `check-docs`, `check-outputs`, `no-private-refs`.
- [ ] Tests added per part; none skipped.
- [ ] The walk workflow (`walk.yml`) green; the preflight and spike run ids recorded.
- [ ] `Cargo.lock` updated and `cargo metadata --locked` clean; no local compile used as a gate.
- [ ] The parity record and the four failure modes pass; `--gate=P6` fails the absent fixture.
- [ ] Docs updated: ADR 0023/0024, CR-WALK-001, WBS/risk/SAFe/evidence, the design indexes, the generated pack.
- [ ] Live: the changed documents and the Phase-F delivery contract published and read back; B8 stays enabling/unmeasured.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted; the deployed game host serves the walk at `/` and `/portfolio`, the operator host 308s `/walk/*`, and the real `conveyor-game` sign-in lands on the Portfolio read.

## Out of scope

- The S1–S4 destination wings; they are separate issues and blocked by this one.
- Any new table, action, event or read route; the server changes are limited to the host dispatch, the router gate, the per-host `/config.json`, the `/walk` 308 and the auth `azp` allowlist.
- A new Keycloak realm, a second deployment, image or port, or a change to `apps/web`'s client; the game client is `conveyor-game` in the existing `conveyor` realm.
- Primacy or `apps/web` retirement; that is the P6 owner decision.
- The mock's fixtures, programme store or studio pack; it stays untracked.
- No old-system shutdown, ledger import, 218-item parity or 348-flow retirement.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes — the image is deployed first with the game host configured but not routed; then the gitops PR routes the host and sets the env; then the realm Job runs; then the host and the real sign-in are proven. Every step is read back.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Is the game client admin-managed or git-managed? | owner/ops | **resolved:** git-managed realm-patch ConfigMap + the manual Job; a dedicated public client `conveyor-game` in the `conveyor` realm, read back from the admin API |
| 2 | Which non-destructive Portfolio write is the exemplar? | build (manifest at claim) | **resolved:** `programmes.create` with `Idempotency-Key` (the dev seed has no programmes), then `programmes.update` with `If-Match` on the created row |

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W0 | P1.1–P1.5 | `build-walk-coverage.py --check` / `--self-test` / `walk_coverage.sh` | 52 routes / 598 actions; 0 failing; census re-frozen at `01544010f` | `f5b9aa163` |
| W1 | P2.1–P2.4 | run 45953201576; `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md`; ADR 0023 | green | `eb9a959a7` |
| W1a | P3.1–P3.3 | the walk-world suite (CI) | 11 native tests | `c2d7ce63c` |

issues.body:
The deployed prover (`registry.redacted:5000/lean4-prover`, ns `lean4-prover`, node hp2) is built from
`nonagenticai/lean4-prover` by hand. Nothing in this repo's CI publishes that image: `ci` builds
`ghcr.io/nonagenticai/conveyor` and a fixed list of `conveyor-*` service images, and neither
`Dockerfile` nor `docker/Dockerfile.service` carries elan/Mathlib. Measured while closing #787: the
code fix merged here at `b3409437`, the conveyor image rolled — and the prover kept answering the
old behaviour because its binary comes from the other tree.

Meanwhile `apps/lean4-prover` here is a second copy of the same crate (it differs from the release
repo only in the comments that name estate paths), so every prover change has to be made twice and
the operator has to remember a hand build.

## Why this is worth a decision, not a patch

- **Silent drift:** a merged change looks delivered (CI green, issue closed) while the running
  binary is older. #787's live re-check found it only by calling the deployed prover.
- **Two sources of truth:** conveyor's copy is what the tests and the contract live in; the release
  repo is what the image is built from.
- **The build is not cheap:** ~10.6 GB image, ~25 GB build disk, Mathlib cache download; today it
  took ~12 min on worker3 once the base was warm.

## Options

1. **Build from this repo in CI.** Move the elan/Mathlib Dockerfile into `apps/lean4-prover`, add
   the image to `publish-service-images`, and retire the hand build. Keeps one source of truth and
   the existing gates; costs a long CI job per prover change (Mathlib stage can cache).
2. **Declare the release repo the source of record.** Stop carrying the crate here (or keep it
   read-only as a contract fixture), and give the release repo a documented, scripted publish path
   (`scripts/publish-image.sh`) wired to a manual `workflow_dispatch`.
3. **Do nothing and document the hand build.** Cheapest, keeps the trap.

Owner decision needed: which tree is the prover's source of record.

**Portability note.** The lane's `resolved_by` commits are multi-finding waves, not surgical
fixes: `92e6b223` executes twelve P0s (40 files), `8f1e5770` carries `migrations/0062_release_layers.sql`
(main's 0062 is `s21_prompt_selection`), and `78bb25d5` carries `migrations/0063_tool_verify.sql`
(main's 0063 is `async_invocation`). The fixes are therefore **re-implemented against main**,
guided by the lane's code and its named tests — never cherry-picked.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the baseline guard reads the approval, not the row status

**P1.1** Given a change row created or updated with `status: "approved"` and no `change` gate
approval, when `registers.create` / `registers.update` is called, then it is refused (422,
naming the status) — approval is only ever a gate effect.
**Verify:** `crates/actions/tests/spine_gates.rs` (to create) —
`a_register_cannot_be_born_approved`.

**P1.2** Given a tranche whose baseline is re-pointed at a change row that merely *says*
approved, when the tranche update runs, then it is refused `change_not_approved`. Given the same
change approved through the `change` gate, when the update runs, then it succeeds.

## Goal

Seven role playbooks cover the authoring, build/ops, architecture, procedural-management and analysis roles, and the six existing playbooks prove their acts with real commands instead of grepping their own files.

### P2 — the seven new playbooks

- **P2.1 `standards-author` (authoring)** Given an output category or a standard, when it is authored, then the playbook names the artefact standard, `check-output-standard.py`, `generate-standards.py` and the publish path, and refuses to approve its own artefact.

- **P2.6 `pmo-lead` (procedural management)** Given the programme office, when registers, change control or assurance run, then the playbook names the register, `changes.request` and the board preparation; it never decides a tranche.
  Verify: `test -f .claude/skills/pmo-lead/SKILL.md && grep -qi 'register' .claude/skills/pmo-lead/SKILL.md && grep -q 'changes.request' .claude/skills/pmo-lead/SKILL.md`.

### P2 — the owner

  resolved, then `api_client` answers `owner_key = platform`.

issues.body:
A failing `lean4.check` returns `diagnostics: []`. Lean writes its errors to **stdout**, and
`apps/lean4-prover/src/runner.rs` parses only stderr, so the one thing an operator needs — why the
proof failed — is discarded. `valid` comes from the exit code, so certificates are unaffected; the
damage is that every refusal is undebuggable and every certificate failure is a black box.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `1` |
| Brief | `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery/project-brief.md` |
| ADM phase/plateau | `G`; capability |
| Benefits | `B1 — Auditable decisions`; a refusal nobody can read is not auditable |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/lean4-prover/src/runner.rs` — `parse_diagnostics(&run.stderr)` at the check and elaborate call sites | main@`985cb4ba` |
| Code | `apps/lean4-prover/src/runner.rs:43-44` — both streams are already captured (`RunOutput`), so the text is present and only unparsed | main@`985cb4ba` |
| Doc | `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live on the released engine — "Found, not ticketed" | main@`985cb4ba` |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@985cb4ba` · measured 2026-11-26
- Observed on the deployed prover: a deliberately broken certificate answered
  `{"valid": false, "diagnostics": [], "stdout": "…error text…", "stderr": ""}`.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-26)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Both streams captured | DONE | `RunOutput { stdout, stderr }`, runner.rs:43 |
| Diagnostics parsed from stderr only | WRONG | `parse_diagnostics(&run.stderr)` at the check and elaborate paths |
| `valid` correctness | UNAFFECTED | it is the exit status, not the diagnostics list |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — a failing check explains itself

Requirement: the diagnostics a caller receives are the errors Lean actually printed, whichever
stream carried them.

- **P1.1** Given a source with a type error, when `lean4.check` runs, then `valid` is `false` **and**
  `diagnostics` is non-empty, with the message Lean printed.
  Verify: `apps/lean4-prover` test `a_failing_check_returns_the_error_it_printed`, asserting
  `diagnostics` is non-empty for a deliberately broken source.
- **P1.2** Given a source that compiles, when `lean4.check` runs, then `diagnostics` stays empty and
  `valid` is `true` — the fix must not turn success into noise.
  Verify: the existing golden/parity test for a valid source still passes.

### P2 — one parser, every call site

Requirement: no path keeps the stderr-only behaviour.

- **P2.1** Given the check, elaborate and prove paths, when each parses a run, then all three use
  the same stdout+stderr parse.
  Verify: a search of `runner.rs` finds no `parse_diagnostics(&run.stderr)` left, and a test per
  path.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #746 | the certificate corpus whose failures this makes readable | closed |
| related | #762 | the evidence doc that recorded the defect | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the reference commits recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at `main@985cb4ba`.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] One PR: the parser change and its tests.
- [x] No owner decision and no infrastructure outside this repository.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [x] Repo gate green at the exact head.
- [x] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- The certificate corpus and the delivery gate — #746, #762.
- The mint credential — #776.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/787-prover-diagnostics` (conveyor) |
| HEAD | `0ae0d6f7` (marker re-pushed as issue/787-prover-diagnostics) |
| Session | claude-code m4 2026-11-27 |
| Updated | 2026-11-27 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 (local) | a failing check returns the error it printed | `cargo-guard test -p conveyor-lean4-prover --lib runner::` — three stub-`lake` tests (error on stdout, stderr empty) | before the fix: 3 failed, `diagnostics must carry Lean's own error (stdout here)`; after: 12 passed, 0 failed |
| P1.2 (local) | success is not turned into noise | `a_clean_run_reports_no_diagnostics` | passes: `valid: true`, `diagnostics: []` |
| P2.1 | one parser, every call site | `git grep 'parse_diagnostics(&run.stderr)'` | only inside the new helper; `check`, `elaborate` and `prove` call `diagnostics_for` |
| live, pre-fix | the deployed prover reproduces the defect | `POST :8812/api/check {"source":"def x : Nat := \"oops\"\n"}` | `{"valid":false,"diagnostics":[],"stdout":"…1:15: error: Type mismatch…","stderr":""}` — the reason in stdout |
| live, post-merge | the deployed prover now explains the failure | same request on `lean4-prover` @ `sha256:6caa4704…` (built from lean4-prover#3, `694434e1`) | `200 {"valid":false,"diagnostics":[{"severity":"error","line":1,"column":15,"message":"Type mismatch"}],…}`; clean source `200 {"valid":true,"diagnostics":[]}` |

issues.body:
**One programme, one record.** This issue is the static entry point to the conveyor buildout. It is
not a generated table — the tables are read from rows and served by the site.

## The record

- **The site:** https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/ — the programme, tranches, benefits, the
  delivery view and every published output, rendered from the conveyor's own rows.
- **The programme definition:** `docs/SPEC_V2.md`, `docs/plans/00-INDEX.md`, `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md`.
- **The delivery view:** `https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/` → the Programme view; a unit's
  steps, gates and closure are the `development_projects` row, read live.

## The units

Every unit of work is a GitHub issue labelled `unit`, carrying its contract (Definition of ready,
BDD acceptance per part, typed dependencies, Definition of done). The units are linked here as
**sub-issues**, grouped by the tranche milestone (`T0`–`T13`) they deliver.

To find work: `gh issue list --label unit --state open`. To claim one: the `issue-pickup` skill.
A unit is delivered as one branch `issue/<n>-<slug>` and exactly one PR that closes it.

## The gates

- An issue is ready when its body satisfies the content contract; the `issue-dor` workflow enforces
  it on every open/edit and carries the verdict as `status:not-ready`.
- A delivery records its steps and gates in the row (`branch → pull_request → ci → review gate →
  merge gate → rollback plan → deploy gate → deploy → live verify → close`), through the
  `delivery-unit` skill.
- A tranche closes on its review (`tranches.review`), with the mandatory artefact set.

_This issue is static by design: it is not regenerated. The rows are the record._

## Parts and acceptance criteria

## Goal

GitHub carries intent and rollup — a structured unit issue, a Definition-of-ready check on every
open/edit, native sub-issues under the programme parent and one milestone per tranche — and the
generated programme issue body is deleted.

## Plan / audit source

§ "Issue content contract" and `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.1 (GitHub is intent, not the programme store).

precedent).

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the structured unit form

- **P1.1** Given the form, when a unit issue is created, then the baseline, programme fields, parts,
  at least one `Verify:` scenario, typed dependencies and DoD are required fields, and the Markdown
  template remains as the reference.
- **P1.2** Given the form is invalid YAML or names an unknown label, then GitHub refuses to render it;
  the file is not merged until the new-issue page shows the form.

Verify: `test -f .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.yml` and
`grep -q 'name: Unit of work' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.yml` and
`grep -q 'id: verify' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.yml`; after merge,
`gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/contents/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.yml --jq .name` → `unit.yml`.

### P2 — Definition of ready on every open and edit

- **P2.1** Given an issue opened or edited without a `Verify:` line, when the workflow runs, then it
  applies `status:not-ready` and posts one comment naming every missing field.
- **P2.2** Given a conforming body, when the workflow runs, then it removes `status:not-ready` and
  writes no comment; a body it cannot parse is reported, never guessed.

Verify: `bash scripts/ci/tests/board.sh` (the existing fixtures) and the new
`scripts/ci/tests/issue_dor.sh` (to create) over a conforming and a malformed body; the workflow run
on the PR's own issue is the live record.

### P3 — native sub-issues

- **P3.1** Given the programme parent issue, when a unit is created, then `issue-create` links it as a
  native sub-issue; the parent's rollup lists every open unit.
- **P3.2** Given a unit with no parent, when the sweep runs, then it is reported, not silently
  parented to the wrong programme.

Verify: `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/issues/<parent>/sub_issues --jq '.[].number'` lists the
units; `gh issue list --label programme --state open --json number` returns exactly one parent.

### P4 — tranche milestones

- **P4.1** Given `tranches.list`, when the one-time milestone write runs, then one milestone exists
  per tranche (`T0`–`T13`) and its state matches the row (`closed` for 0–2, open for 3–13).
- **P4.2** Given a tranche review closes a tranche, then the milestone is closed in the same act; a
  milestone with no tranche row is reported, never invented.

Verify: `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/milestones --jq '.[].title'` → the tranche set;
`gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/milestones --jq '.[] | "\\(.title) \\(.state)"'` matches
`tranches.list`.

### P5 — the static programme issue and the deletion

- **P5.1** Given `build-programme-view.py` and its `programme-issue` job deleted, when
  `issue-registry` next runs, then no generated programme body is written; the pinned programme issue
  is static and links the site.
- **P5.2** Given the deletion, when `ci-public` runs, then no job references the removed script or
  job.

Verify: `test ! -e scripts/build-programme-view.py`;
`! grep -q build-programme-view .github/workflows/issue-registry.yml`;
`gh issue view <programme> --json body --jq .body` contains the site URL and no generated table.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — idempotent charter by key

- **P1.1** Given a development project chartered with key `issue-42-slug`, when `charter` runs again
  with the same key, repo, lane and implementer, then it returns the same row and creates no second
  project.
- **P1.2** Given the same key with a different repo or lane, then it refuses `409 charter_mismatch`
  naming the field that differs.

Verify: `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --lib` → the tests

### P2 — the issue reference

- **P2.1** Given `issue_ref = "nonagenticai/conveyor#42"` on a charter, when `get` reads the unit,
  then the row carries the same ref.
- **P2.2** Given a bare number, an empty owner/name or a non-public slug, then the action answers

`development::charter_records_the_issue_ref`; the migration is
`migrations/0077_development_issue_ref.sql` (to create; renumber at merge if the number is taken).

### P3 — list the units

- **P3.1** Given three units across two repos and two statuses, when `development_projects.list`
  filters by repo and status, then only matching rows return, each with id, project key, repo, lane,

Verify: `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --lib` →

### P4 — the machine grant

- **P4.1** Given the tenant's `mcp` grant set, when `channels.policy_set` adds
  `development_projects.*`, then a machine bearer can invoke `charter` and `list`, and an ungranted
  act still answers `403`.

Verify: with the #760 bearer,
`curl -fsS -X POST "$CONVEYOR_URL/api/actions/development_projects.list/invocations" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":{}}'`
returns 200; the same call for an ungranted act returns 403;
`psql -d conveyor -Atc "select count(*) from channel_action_grant where channel_kind='mcp' and action like 'development_projects.%'"` → 9.
