## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the record

Requirement: a missing operation is recorded as a governed tool request — an `authoring_asset` of kind `tool_request` whose payload names the operation, the step and the procedure. No new table: the kind is already admitted and the draft lifecycle is the one SPEC §11.6 describes (`draft → validation → review → publish`).

- **P1.1** Given a procedure draft whose step needs an operation no tool provides, when validation runs, then a `tool_request` asset exists naming the operation, the step position and the procedure id.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`
- **P1.2** Given that asset, when it is read back through the store, then its `key` is stable and re-running validation for the same draft does not create a second asset for the same operation and step.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`

### P2 — the per-step trigger

Requirement: resolution is per step. A step's `action` that is neither a declared engine action nor a published tool is a missing operation; the document-level `requested_tools` list is intent to attribute, never the trigger.

- **P2.1** Given a step naming an operation with no tool, when `procedures.validate` runs, then it returns success with a `missing_operations` list naming that operation and does **not** return `sop.cannot_grant_tool`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`
- **P2.2** Given a step that resolves to a declared engine action or to a published tool, when validation runs, then no tool request is opened.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test sop_ingestion`
- **P2.3** Given the old refusal test, when the suite runs, then it asserts the new behaviour (a card, not a blanket 422) and is rewritten rather than deleted.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::an_sop_cannot_grant_a_tool`

### P3 — the rebind

Requirement: publishing a tool binds the steps that asked for its operations, at the published version.

- **P3.1** Given an open tool request for an operation, when a tool providing it is published, then every step with that action carries the tool id and the published version.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`
- **P3.2** Given a step already pinned, when another version is published, then the existing pin is left untouched (idempotent, no error) — binding is a forward act, not an overwrite.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test sop_ingestion`
- **P3.3** Given the pin exists, when the procedure is validated again, then it is retryable and no longer reports the operation missing.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`

### P4 — the proof

- **P4.1** Given a clean tenant, when a procedure needing an unknown operation is ingested, validated, the tool published and validation re-run, then the asset exists, the step is pinned and the procedure validates.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test sop_ingestion a_missing_operation_opens_a_tool_request_and_rebinds`

### P5 — the ledger receipt

- **P5.1** Given the behaviour is proven, when the rework acceptance command runs, then the package is cleared.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot docs/design/data --findings docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json --findings docs/evidence/standards-findings.json --rework-check v1-p116-1:T13`
- **P5.2** Given the ledger carries the resolution, when the ledger verifier runs, then `v1-p116-1` is not among the reported drifts, and its receipt names an ancestor commit, an existing test path and the run that proved it.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/verify-findings.py docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json 2>&1 | grep -c 'FAIL v1-p116-1'` prints `0`. (Measured 2026-11-26: the ledger carries 195 line-drift failures on `main@0d6db794` — stale line numbers across 230 evidence quotes, unrelated to this unit; a resolved finding is exempt from the quote check, so this unit removes its own.)

| related | #755 | the tranche-3 review's first precondition is T13 meeting its acceptance | open |

## Definition of done

## Out of scope

- The executor consuming the step's tool pin — the DoD asks for the rebind, not for run-time dispatch through it.
- A board `card` row for the request: the authoring asset is the record; if review concludes otherwise it is an addition to P1, not a redesign.

## Goal

`conveyor admin upstream-token --service lean4 --mint` authenticates with its own dedicated minter
credential instead of the backend's, and refuses loudly when that credential is not configured.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live on the released engine — the drills this credential
  serves, proven with a BYO token on 2026-11-26.
- Split from #762, whose P1 could not close in the same PR as the drills.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `1` |
| Brief | `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery/project-brief.md` |
| ADM phase/plateau | `G`; capability |
| Benefits | `B1 — Auditable decisions`; a credential the operator can rotate is what keeps the certificate loop runnable |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/776-bundle-minter` |
| HEAD | `cda7b554` |
| Session | claim 2026-11-26 |
| Updated | 2026-11-26 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/server/src/admin/upstream_tokens.rs` — `fill`, `TokenSource::Mint` | main@0d6db794 |
| Code | `crates/auth/src/licence.rs` — `mint_bundle_token`, the injected credential | main@0d6db794 |
| Code | `crates/auth/src/oauth.rs` — the `client_credentials` client the sender builds | main@0d6db794 |
| Code | `apps/licenses/src/router/internal_bundles.rs` — the role guard and owner scoping this credential must satisfy | main@0d6db794 |
| Doc | `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live on the released engine | main@0d6db794 |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@0d6db794` · measured 2026-11-26
- Docs: `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` blob `efe11016` · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` blob `8de8b7fe`

## Current state (measured 2026-11-26)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The mint route | DONE | `POST /internal/tenants/{id}/bundle-token`, guarded by the realm role `bundle-token-minter` (licensing service) |
| The caller's credential | WRONG | the CLI builds its licensing client from `SERVICE_CLIENT_ID=conveyor-backend`; `--mint` → `HTTP 403: Role required: bundle-token-minter` |
| The caller's owner | WRONG | `api_client` row `secure-apps/conveyor-backend` has `owner_key=fr`; the tenant it must mint for is `owner_key=platform`, and the route owner-scopes — a role grant alone would still be refused |
| The prover's licence app | ABSENT | app key `lean4-prover` does not exist; `UpstreamService::Lean4::licences_app()` names it, so the mint would answer `404 no_app_licence` even once authorized |
| The drills | DONE (#762) | a BYO token on the tenant's `conveyor` licence sealed as `lean4.token`; gate refusal, gate acceptance and tamper refusal measured live |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the mint uses its own credential

Requirement: the licensing call is made as a dedicated minter client, selected by environment, not
by whatever the rest of the process uses.

- **P1.1** Given `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_ID` / `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET`, when the admin CLI mints,
  then the token request names the minter client and the minted envelope is sealed.
  Verify: `crates/auth` unit test `the_mint_uses_the_minter_client` (asserts the `client_id` in the
  form body), plus the live command in P3.
- **P1.2** Given only `SERVICE_CLIENT_*` (the deployment as it stands), when the mint runs, then it
  is authorized as before — the change is additive, and no existing caller changes behaviour.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-auth --lib` and the existing admin CLI tests.

### P2 — no silent fallback

Requirement: a mint with no minter credential is refused before the HTTP call, naming the variable.

- **P2.1** Given a process with no `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET`, when `--mint` runs, then it exits
  non-zero with `bundle minter credential not configured: BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET` and writes no
  secret row.
  Verify: `crates/actions`/`crates/auth` unit test `a_mint_without_the_minter_credential_is_refused`
  plus a row-count assertion for `secret` in the same test.

### P3 — live acceptance (acceptance-blocked by the infrastructure)

Requirement: on the deployed engine, the mint seals a token that the prover accepts.

- **P3.1** Given the minter client exists, holds `bundle-token-minter` and nothing else, and its
  `api_client` row is `owner_key=platform`; and given the licence app decision (P3.2), when the mint
  runs on the deployed pod, then it seals a token the prover accepts.
  Verify: `kubectl -n conveyor exec deploy/conveyor -c conveyor -- conveyor admin upstream-token --tenant nonagentic --service lean4 --mint`
  → `{"secret":"lean4.token","source":"licences", …}`; then one `lean4.check` invocation answers
  `valid: true`.
- **P3.2** Given the owner's decision on metering (a new `lean4-prover` app with a plan and a licence
  for `01a1cf6d-…`, or the tenant's existing `conveyor` licence), when the mint names that app, then
  the licensing service answers a token, not `404 no_app_licence`.
  Verify: the mint's own envelope names the licence id and app.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #762 | the drills this credential serves | open |
| related | #744 | the sealed secret the certificate path reads | closed |
| related | #746 | the certificate corpus and the gate | closed |
| acceptance-blocked-by | — | the realm-patch client, the `api_client` row and the licence-app decision live outside this repository | owner |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at `main@0d6db794`.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] One PR: the code change and its tests; the live acceptance is a recorded command, not a
      second PR.
- [x] The only blocker is an owner decision plus infrastructure outside this repository, so the
      label is `status:needs-human`, not `status:blocked`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Creating the licence app, its plan and its pricing — P3.2 is a decision, never invented here.
- The realm patch and the `api_client` row: a different repository and a different service.
- The live drills and their evidence — #762.
- Every other upstream service's mint path: `laya` and `inference` go through the same route and the
  same role, and P1.2 keeps them working unchanged.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes: a `conveyor-bundle-minter` client in the secure-apps realm holding `bundle-token-minter` and
nothing else, a matching `api_client` row with `owner_key=platform`, its secret in the sealed
secrets, and `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_ID` / `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET` on both conveyor containers.

## Open questions

1. ~~Is the prover metered as its own app (`lean4-prover`: new app, plan, licence), or on the
   tenant's existing `conveyor` licence?~~ **Answered 2026-11-26 (owner): a new `lean4-prover` app
   with its own plan and licence.** The pricing row is created by mirroring the existing `conveyor`
   plan unless a number is given.

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | the mint names the minter client in the token form body | the workspace test suite in `checks-shard (1)`/`(2)` at `985cb4ba` | PASS — `the_mint_uses_the_minter_client` asserts `client_id=conveyor-bundle-minter`; `the_minter_uses_its_own_credential_and_refuses_without_one` asserts the config builds it |
| P1.2 | no existing caller changes behaviour | `checks-shard` full suite + `checks` + `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` at `985cb4ba` | PASS — `service_credentials()` is untouched at `crates/api/src/services.rs:42` (provisioning/billing/licence.sync) and `apps/server/src/worker.rs:233`; the only changed caller is the mint |
| P2.1 | a mint with no minter credential exits non-zero, names the variable, writes no row | the workspace test suite at `985cb4ba` | PASS — `a_mint_without_the_minter_credential_is_refused` asserts `bundle minter credential not configured: BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET` and `count(*) FROM secret = 0` |
| P3.1 | the deployed mint seals a token the prover accepts | not run | **BLOCKED** — needs the realm client, the `api_client` row and the `lean4-prover` app: filed as #788 |

The Phase-G compliance rule reads the live delivery contract only; a v2 project's Statement of Architecture Work is not a compliance subject, so a SoAW without a review is not a gap.

## Plan / audit source

<!-- status:ready · unit · platform (delivery-system rework) -->

## Goal

A Claude session authenticates to the conveyor as a machine principal of the programme tenant and
records and reads programme rows over HTTPS and `/mcp`, with no per-action `kubectl exec`.

## Plan / audit source

Platform unit (delivery-system rework), not a V2 slice: the source is `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.2 (the
`agent → conveyor` seam is `/mcp` with a licence bearer) and §10.1 (the conveyor owns every progress
row). The measured state below is the brief; the session plan is not committed to the repo.

## Programme

| Tranche | `unmapped` → PLATFORM (delivery-system rework; no programme tranche) — the convention #745 uses |

| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.1 (ownership matrix), §10.2 (seams: `agent → conveyor`, MCP licence bearer) | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `crates/auth/src/machine.rs:MachineAuthenticator` — opaque bearer → introspect → `licence:<subject_id>` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `crates/auth/src/authn.rs:identify` — JWT vs licence dispatch, machine-row refusal | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/channel/mod.rs:MCP_DEFAULT_ACTIONS`, `allows` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs:Authority::of` — REST machines get the channel authority | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/control/channels.rs:channels.policy_set` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `apps/licenses/src/router/licence_tokens.rs:create_license_token` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `apps/licenses/src/auth.rs:attach_and_authorize` — `api_client` owner, `X-Tenant-Id` retarget | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `apps/licenses/src/db/issuance.rs:authorize_issuance` — owner must be an `app_issuer` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Code | `apps/server/src/main.rs` — `admin` subcommand surface | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Test | `crates/auth/src/machine.rs::tests`, `apps/licenses/tests/introspect.rs` | main@49ffa3b2 |
| Issue | #756 (provenance register), #753 (role skills) | open |

## Baseline

`main@49ffa3b2` (measured 2026-11-26). Doc blob shas: SPEC_V2 `8de8b7fe`, 03-DELIVERY `6284617a`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 owner mapping + tenant access | ABSENT | no `api_client` row for a session client; `app_issuer` for the conveyor app is `{agent, fr}`; the tenant is owned by `platform` and holds no grant for `agent` |
| P2 mint | ABSENT | no `auth` subcommand in `apps/server/src/main.rs`; the bundle-token route cannot resolve the conveyor app (no held bundle contains it) |
| P3 machine principal | ABSENT | `select kind, count(*) from app_user group by 1` → `human 4`; no `licence:` subject exists |
| P4 channel grants | ABSENT | `channel_action_grant` 0 rows; `channel_binding` 0 rows; machine sessions get only the 48 compiled defaults |
| P5 proof | ABSENT | `/api/actions` and `/mcp` answer 401 without a bearer; no bearer exists |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — Owner mapping and tenant access (licences)

Requirement: a secure-apps service client maps to owner `agent` (an issuer of the conveyor app) and
that owner can reach the programme tenant.

- **P1.1** Given the realm role exists, when the licences migration runs, then `api_client`
  carries `(secure-apps, conveyor-channel) → owner agent, cross_owner false`.
  Verify: `psql -d licenses -Atc "select owner_key, cross_owner from api_client where realm='secure-apps' and client_id='conveyor-channel'"` → `agent|f`
- **P1.2** Given owner `agent` and the programme tenant, when a `tenant_app_grant` is written by the
  tenant's owner, then `owner_can_access_tenant(agent, tenant)` is true.
  Verify: `psql -d licenses -Atc "select grantee_owner_key from tenant_app_grant where tenant_id='<tenant>' and revoked_at is null"` → `agent`

### P2 — The mint (`conveyor auth token`)

Requirement: the binary mints a short-lived opaque licence bearer for the conveyor app on the
programme tenant's active licence and caches it 0600.

- **P2.1** Given a service-client credential and an active licence, when `conveyor auth token
  --tenant <slug>` runs, then it writes a 0600 file containing the token and its expiry, and prints
  the path.
  Verify: `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-server --lib` (tests to create at `apps/server/src/auth.rs`)
- **P2.2** Given a cached token with under an hour left, when the command runs again, then it
  re-mints and replaces the file.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/auth.rs::token_refreshes_before_expiry` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given the licences service is unreachable or refuses, then the command exits non-zero
  naming the refusal and leaves the previous file untouched.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/auth.rs::mint_failure_keeps_the_previous_token` (to create)
- **P2.4** Given the issued token, when it is presented to the licences introspection route, then
  it is active for the conveyor app and the programme tenant.
  Verify: `curl -fsS -d "{\"token\":\"$(cat ~/.conveyor/<slug>.token | head -1)\"}" <licences>/license/introspect | jq -e '.active and .app.key=="conveyor"'`

### P3 — The machine principal (`conveyor admin machine-principal ensure`)

Requirement: the CLI derives `licence:<subject_id>` from a live token and idempotently provisions
the machine `app_user` row and its membership.

- **P3.1** Given a live token, when `conveyor admin machine-principal ensure --token-file <path>`
  runs, then `app_user` holds a `service` row keyed `licence:<subject_id>` and `membership` holds a
  `kata_executor` row in the tenant, and a second run changes nothing.
  Verify: `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-server --lib` (tests to create at `apps/server/src/admin/machine_principal.rs`)
- **P3.2** Given a token whose subject resolves to a `human` row, then the command refuses and
  writes nothing.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/admin/machine_principal.rs::refuses_a_human_row` (to create)

### P4 — The channel grant set

Requirement: the tenant's `mcp` channel carries exactly the governance acts the role skills invoke.

- **P4.1** Given the empty grant table, when `channels.policy_set` runs for kind `mcp` with the
  programme action list, then stored rows cover `programmes.*`, `tranches.*`, `registers.*`,
  `benefits.*`, `documents.*`, `changes.*`, `approvals.*` and `meetings.*`.
  Verify: `psql -d conveyor -Atc "select count(*) from channel_action_grant where channel_kind='mcp'"` → non-zero
- **P4.2** Given the grants, when a machine session invokes a granted act it returns 200 and an
  act outside the grant list returns 403 with the action code.
  Verify: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":{}}' <public>/api/actions/<granted>/invocations` → 200; the same for an ungranted act → 403

### P5 — The proof over HTTPS and MCP

Requirement: the bearer works from the developer box for both surfaces, and the refusals hold.

- **P5.1** Given the minted bearer, when a session POSTs `programmes.list` to the public host, then
  it returns 200 with rows and the invocation row names `actor_kind=service` and the `licence:`
  principal.
  Verify: `curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":{}}' <public>/api/actions/programmes.list/invocations | jq -e '.result | length > 0'`
- **P5.2** Given the minted bearer, when `/mcp` receives `initialize` then `tools/list`, then the
  granted acts are listed.
  Verify: `curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}' <public>/mcp | jq -e '.result.tools | length > 0'`
- **P5.3** Given the licence is revoked or expires, when the next call runs, then it is refused
  within the 60-second introspection cache.
  Verify: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <stale-token>" <public>/api/actions/programmes.list/invocations` → 401

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #756 | the register reads the same rows the session will write | open |
| related | #753 | role-skill allowlists must be a subset of P4's grant set | open |
| related | #526 | shared programme-action files; rebase if it lands first | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/code/test reference resolves at `main@49ffa3b2`; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no `blocked-by`, so `status:ready`.
- [x] One-PR scope in this repo (two subcommands + one migration); the realm patch is a separate
      infrastructure-repo PR named under Deployment prerequisite.

      `ci-public` as the final gate).

renders them as a machine-readable block (`data-provenance` attributes) and `outputs.js` emits the
same fields. `apps/server/src/publish.rs` supplies the git sha the publish already knows.

- **Given** a published output whose `document.meta` carries the stamped provenance, **when** the
  pack renders it, **then** the page carries kind, version, sha256, status, owner, gate and a
  non-empty source commit.
  **Verify:** `cargo test -p conveyor-pack output_page_renders_provenance` *(test to create)*.
- **Given** a legacy published row with no `meta` provenance, **when** it is rendered, **then** the
  block is still present with `status:"unrecorded"` and no field is invented.
  **Verify:** `cargo test -p conveyor-pack output_page_marks_unrecorded_provenance` *(test to create)*.

### P2 — the register section

`crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs` writes `data/register.json`/`.js`: per project, the declared output
kinds (from the standard) against the evidenced published rows, plus the gap-register posture.
`docs/design/studio.html` renders it with a drill-down to the page and the issue.

- **Given** the snapshot of tenant `nonagentic`, **when** the register is built, **then** every
  project row names its declared kinds, its evidenced ones and its gaps, and the counts reconcile
  with `outputs.js`.
  **Verify:** `cargo test -p conveyor-pack snapshot_register_reconciles_with_outputs` *(test to
  create)*, then `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` green.

### P3 — delete the dead checker half

The retained lint (templates, headings, sources) stays; the comparison logic P4 names goes.

- **Given** the standard and the seed, **when** the retained lint runs, **then** it exits 0 and the
  deleted rules leave no dangling helpers.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py && ! git grep -n "class_to_seed_meta\|orphan" scripts/check-output-standard.py`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #714 | the gap register's reproducibility fix; the register section must not regress it | closed |
| related | #156 | store-level provenance (authors, revisions, attachments, publish gate) — P1 renders it, never re-collects it | closed |
| related | #749 | adds `proofs.*` and the `lean_proof` evidence kind; P2's evidence column must name the kind once it lands | open |
| related | #526 | the programme rework lane owns `programmes.*`; this unit touches no programme action | open |

No `blocked-by`: every part is buildable on `main`.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline recorded (`main@ba56759a`, 2026-11-26)
- [x] Every referenced path resolves at the baseline
- [x] Every part has a BDD scenario with a `Verify:` line
- [x] No `blocked-by` edge is open
- [x] Dedupe run: #156 (closed, store-level), #714/#715 (gap-register plumbing), no branch or PR carries this work

## Definition of done

- [ ] P1–P3 accepted on the baseline
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo metadata --locked` green; the preflight compile job green
- [ ] `design-pack` and `parity` green locally
- [ ] deployed: a published page on the public site carries the block, and the register section renders
- [ ] the rework plan committed at `docs/plans/delivery-system-rework.md`
- [ ] one PR, `Closes #<this>`

## Out of scope

The role skills and the GitHub channel (U2/U3, their own issues); the `apps/web` UI (T18);
regenerating the standards record; the proof store (#749).

## Deployment prerequisite

The server image carries the pack change; one publish (or a republish of the public tenant) is needed
for existing pages to gain the block.

## Open questions

- The standard's categories are keyed by project class. If class → project type → tranche does not
  resolve from the rows, the register ships per project type and the class rollup waits.

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Evidence | At |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 provenance on a recorded page | `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-pack --lib` (`output_page_renders_provenance`) → pass | 9816f91ff |
| P1.2 unrecorded page invents nothing | `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-pack --lib` (`output_page_marks_unrecorded_provenance`) → pass | 9816f91ff |
| P2 register reconciles with outputs | `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-pack --lib` (`snapshot_register_reconciles_with_outputs`) → pass | 9816f91ff |
| P2 the pack's data | `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` → 33 checks passed | 9816f91ff |
| P3 retained lint | `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` / `--self-test` → exit 0 / 14 of 14 | 9816f91ff |
| design-pack inputs | the job's checks incl. `check-docs.cjs` and `build-docs.py --check` → all green locally | 9816f91ff |
| live: a published page carries the block | the first publish that regenerates the pack | pending |
| live: the register renders | `data/register.js` + the programme view | pending |

## Goal

Record the end-of-tranche reviews that close tranches 7–12 and authorise tranches 8–13, each on a zero-open-package record and with its published `tranche-review` document.

## Plan / audit source

- Owner decision 2026-11-25: the retrospective tranche reviews carry the programme, with the full mandatory artefact set per phase advance and no token-spend KPI.
- Owner decision 2026-11-27 (scope): the done bar is **zero open audit packages of any severity** on a tranche's members; the review ownership is split — the rework chain records tranches 3–6 (#852 tranche 3, #854 tranches 4–5, #838 tranche 6) and this unit records tranches 7–12.
- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 (the end-of-tranche review is a programme decision).
- `crates/store/src/spine.rs::review_tranche_tx` — `continue` closes the reviewed tranche and authorises the next in the same write.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `7` — slice 1 reviews tranche 7 and authorises tranche 8; slices 2–6 review tranches 8–12 |
| Brief | the P0 programme definition set |
| ADM phase/plateau | — (no architecture change) |
| Benefits | enabling — each review is the spend gate for the next tranche; no direct benefit |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/755-tranche-reviews` |
| HEAD | `aba3aa478` |
| Session | claude-code, m4 |
| Updated | 2026-11-27T14:20Z |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Rule | `crates/store/src/spine.rs::review_tranche_tx` | main@746f5a90f |
| Rule | `crates/actions/src/spine/mod.rs::tranches_review` (gate target `tranche/<id>/review`) | main@746f5a90f |
| Standard | `seed/output-standard.json` → `tranche-review` (four required headings, sources from `msp.json`) | main@746f5a90f |
| Code | `scripts/check-tranche-exit.py` — every member's receipt green and fresh at the snapshot sha | `issue/526-u5a` (to land with #526) |
| Code | `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` — the zero-package measurement | main@746f5a90f |
| Data | the live `msp.json` `tranches` and `tranche_reviews` | live |
| Evidence | `docs/evidence/tranche-review/tranche-7.md` … `tranche-12.md` | to create |
| Issue | #838 | open |
| Issue | #852 | open |
| Issue | #854 | open |
| Issue | #853 | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@746f5a90f` · measured 2026-11-27
- Docs: spine `ed1c7af5` · actions `bebee1bb` · output-standard `424051b6` · SPEC_V2 `60af87ab` · audit script `0e4dbef9`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 the tranche-7 review | ABSENT | production `msp.json`: tranche 7 `planned`; the four existing review rows cover tranches 0–2 |
| P2 the tranches 8–12 reviews | ABSENT | production `msp.json`: tranches 8–13 all `planned` |
| P3 the tranche-review documents | PARTIAL | the `tranche-review` standard exists with its four headings and sources; it renders from `msp.json` rows, so it cannot resolve before its review row exists |
| P4 the receipts | ABSENT | no tranche-review receipt for tranches 7–12 on `origin/main` |

**Preconditions, re-measured at each slice:** each tranche is authorised only by the previous review (tranche 7 by #838's tranche-6 review; tranche 8 by this unit's first review; …). Under the 2026-11-27 bar, the tranche's members carry zero open packages of any severity and `check-tranche-exit.py --tranche N` exits 0 at the deployed snapshot before the review is recorded.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the tranche-7 review (slice 1)

Precondition: #838's tranche-6 review authorises tranche 7, and the tranche-7 record is zero-open.

- **P1.1** Given tranche 7 authorised and its members zero-open, when the review is recorded `continue` under the approval gate, then tranche 7 closes and tranche 8 becomes `authorised` with a non-null `authorisation_review_id`.
  Verify: the live `msp.json` rows for 7 and 8 show `7 closed`, `8 authorised`.
- **P1.2** Given the review row, when the `tranche-review` document is composed and published, then it carries Evidence, Benefit status, Risk and issue register, and Decision, and reads back with `published_at`.
  Verify: `documents.get` on the published id; the generated standards findings show no `tranche-review` finding for tranche 7.
- **P1.3** Given every act of the slice, when it is recorded, then `docs/evidence/tranche-review/tranche-7.md` names each action's result, id and version.
  Verify: the file exists; each id resolves in the live read-back.

### P2 — the tranches 8–12 reviews (slices 2–6)

Precondition per slice: tranche N's members zero-open and the previous review has authorised tranche N.

- **P2.1** Given the green record, when the review records `continue`, then tranche N is closed and tranche N+1 authorised with a non-null `authorisation_review_id`.
  Verify: the same `msp.json` assertion for N and N+1, plus the slice's receipt `docs/evidence/tranche-review/tranche-N.md`.
- **P2.2** Given each review, when its document is published, then it reads back with `published_at` and the four headings.
  Verify: `documents.get`; the receipt names the id.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| acceptance-blocked-by | #838 | Tranche 7 is authorised only by the tranche-6 review; construction may start, the live act waits | open |
| related | #852 | The rework chain's tranche-3 review (the first in the chain) | open |
| related | #854 | The rework chain's tranche-4 and tranche-5 reviews | open |
| related | #853 | Each review's benefit-status evidence reads the live profiles | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the cited doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/code/data reference resolves at its ref; the lane-only script is marked to land with #526; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has at least one scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no `Blocker:` line because the live acts are `acceptance-blocked-by`, not `blocked-by`.
- [x] One-PR scope: six slices on the existing branch, one PR when the series completes.
- [x] Scope corrections applied: no old-system shutdown/parity, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every slice's scenarios pass, each with a row in `Evidence at completion`.
- [ ] Tranche 13 authorised; every review's document published; the live `msp.json` shows the full chain for 7–13.
- [ ] Receipts committed under `docs/evidence/tranche-review/`.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` green.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Tranches 3–6 (the rework chain: #852, #854, #838) and tranche 13 (T12's closure).
- The member packs and code findings — their owning tranche units.
- Benefit measurement (#853) and the strict pack publish (#830).
- Old-system freeze/dump/shutdown, 348-flow retirement, old-ledger import, 218-item parity, old-service rollback.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes — every slice is a live governance act (`tranches.review` behind a dual-controlled approval, then `documents.compose`/`documents.publish`). A slice that cannot reach the live primary is blocked, never simulated as done.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Does a tranche with zero open findings also need a fresh exit receipt at the deployed sha? | this unit | Yes — `check-tranche-exit.py` exit 0 is the precondition, per the 2026-11-27 bar |
| 2 | What happens if a member's residue is a lifecycle pack rather than code? | this unit | It is fixed in that tranche's own unit before this review; this unit records the review only |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — measure the live set

Requirement: the live P0/P1 gap set and the exact strict failure lists are measured from a fresh live snapshot, not inferred from the repo.

- **P1.1** Given a fresh live snapshot, when the strict audit runs against the accepted ledger, then the grown, new, worsened and expired lists are recorded in this issue verbatim.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot <live> --findings docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json --findings <standards-findings> --strict --fail-on P0,P1 --baseline docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json`

### P2 — reconcile the ledger

Requirement: every grown entry is verified and pruned; every live gap stays a failure unless it is fixed or dispositioned with an owner and an unexpired date.

- **P2.1** Given a `ledger grew` entry whose rule and subject are verifiably absent from the live gap set, when the ledger is reconciled, then the entry is removed and the strict run no longer names it.
  Verify: `jq -e '.entries | map(select(.rule == "<rule>" and .subject == "<subject>")) | length == 0' docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` then the P1.1 command.
- **P2.2** Given a live P0/P1 gap, when reconciling, then it remains a failure unless it is fixed through the action surface or carries an owned, reasoned, unexpired disposition.
  Verify: the P1.1 command exits 0 only when every live gap is fixed or dispositioned.

### P3 — the strict publish

Requirement: one publish runs strict against the reconciled ledger and installs its own bytes as the pack.

- **P3.1** Given the reconciled ledger, when the publish runs with `CONFORMANCE_STRICT=1` (the default), then it reports `strict audit OK` and installs the pack.
  Verify: `docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh` with `GENERATED_AT` pinned and `HOMEPAGE` pointing at a scratch checkout carrying an empty `design/`.
- **P3.2** Given the publish output, when the fixpoint runs, then the gap register and the published data agree and `check-data` is green.
  Verify: `cmp docs/evidence/conformance-gap-register.json docs/design/data/conformance.json` and `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs`

### P4 — commit and ship

Requirement: the publish's bytes and the reconciled ledger land in one PR, and the site advances.

- **P4.1** Given the publish bytes and the reconciled ledger, when the PR merges, then the site's registers carry the new `generated_at` and the refresh's `design-pack` job is green.
  Verify: `curl https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/rework.json | jq -r .generated_at` advanced; `gh pr view <n> --json mergedAt`.

## Dependencies

- [x] Every reference resolves at `origin/main`.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no blocker.
- [x] One-PR scope: the reconciled ledger plus one publish's bytes.
- [x] Programme fields present and resolvable.

## Definition of done

- [x] P1.1–P4.1 pass at the PR head, each with a row in `Evidence at completion`.
- [x] `publish-data.sh` strict-green on the fresh live snapshot.
- [x] `check-data.cjs` green; `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` green.

## Out of scope

- The rework lane's replay and promotion (#526).
- Any change to the audit's rules; a wrong rule gets its own issue.
- The homepage repository's own verify and merge.

## Deployment prerequisite

No — the snapshot transaction is read-only against the live primary; the publish writes this repo's tree and the homepage staging tree.

## Open questions

None: the measurement decides, and a live gap that cannot be fixed in this unit is dispositioned with an owner and an expiry, never waived in prose.

| P9 `CLAUDE.md` role routing | ABSENT | `grep -n 'programme-manager' CLAUDE.md` → no route at baseline |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §4–§5 · study §5
Requirement: a project the live register marks proposed or unbuilt gets a P0 §4 brief and a P0 §5 analysis/architecture inception before any build issue; the live state is verified first because plans and assessments drift.

- **P1.1** Given a project the live register marks proposed or unbuilt, when a session follows the skill, then it verifies the live state, produces the brief and both inception documents, and refuses to create a build issue first.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/business-analyst/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/business-analyst/SKILL.md && grep -q 'live register' .claude/skills/business-analyst/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P2 — `programme-architect` role card

`docs/plans/T9-architecture-capability.md` §4–§5 · #395
Requirement: the Phase-A Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract are distinct; the design gate and Phase-G compliance review use the live delivery contract, with the full mandatory ADM artefact set.

- **P2.1** Given a project with a live SAW but no live delivery contract, when the Phase-G compliance review is requested, then the skill refuses to review the SAW and names the missing delivery contract.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/programme-architect/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/programme-architect/SKILL.md && grep -q 'delivery contract' .claude/skills/programme-architect/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P3 — `benefits-manager` role card

`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §6 · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3
Requirement: a benefit profile carries the six groups; realization needs a measured baseline and transition; a token-spend KPI is refused by the owner's 2026-11-25 decision.

- **P3.1** Given a request to define a token-spend benefit target, when a session follows the skill, then it refuses the token-spend KPI and points to the authorized benefits; given a shipped deliverable with no baseline, it reports `unmeasured`.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/benefits-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/benefits-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'token-spend' .claude/skills/benefits-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'unmeasured' .claude/skills/benefits-manager/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P4 — `programme-manager` role card

`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §7 · #302/#303
Requirement: tranches 4–13 are authorised by nine retrospective reviews (4–12 now, 13 when T12 delivers), each on evidence with an empty decision block; no consolidated review, no re-plan; a re-baseline goes through change control.

- **P4.1** Given a request to catch up tranches 4–13 in one consolidated review, when a session follows the skill, then it prepares the nine retrospective reviews and refuses the consolidated one.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/programme-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/programme-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'nine retrospective' .claude/skills/programme-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'change control' .claude/skills/programme-manager/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P5 — `release-manager` role card

#8 · `docs/evidence/2026-11-10-plan-audit.md` §V4
Requirement: a release receipt records the deployed SHA/image digest, the live probe, the rollback and the executed test counts per #8/V4; merge is not shipped, and an open PR is not a merge.

- **P5.1** Given an open or merged PR with no deployed identity, when a release is requested, then the skill refuses to declare it shipped and names the missing receipt fields.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/release-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/release-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'deployed' .claude/skills/release-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'V4' .claude/skills/release-manager/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P6 — `quality-manager` role card

`docs/design/README.md` (fixpoint) · #302 · #88
Requirement: conformance is claimed only after audit → publish → build-docs → publish → re-audit with both `--check` gates green and the output pages present; independent acceptance is dispatched, not self-attested.

- **P6.1** Given a stale standards pack, when conformance is claimed, then the skill runs the fixpoint with the snapshot's output pages, re-audits, and refuses a green claim while a declared output is absent.
  Verify: `bash -c "test -f .claude/skills/quality-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q '^## Refusals' .claude/skills/quality-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 're-audit' .claude/skills/quality-manager/SKILL.md && grep -q 'output pages' .claude/skills/quality-manager/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P7 — `issue-create` requires the Programme fields

`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract"
Requirement: every unit issue created through the skill carries non-empty `Tranche`, `Brief`, `ADM phase/plateau` and `Benefits` rows, each resolving to a live row/document or `pending #N`; an unready source hands to `business-analyst`.

- **P7.1** Given a draft issue body with a bare `—` in a Programme row, when `board.py --dor` runs, then it exits 1; given filled rows, it exits 0.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/ci/board.py --self-test` and `bash -c "grep -q 'Programme' .claude/skills/issue-create/SKILL.md && grep -q 'board.py' .claude/skills/issue-create/SKILL.md"`.

### P8 — `issue-deliver` requires an independent verdict for live/governance parts

`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Definition of done"
Requirement: a deployment-gated, end-to-end acceptance or governance-artefact part is verified by a fresh independent agent, not by the builder's own evidence.

- **P8.1** Given a deploy-gated part with a green local gate, when the builder reaches the DoD gate, then the skill dispatches an independent verifier rather than merging on self-attestation.
  Verify: `bash -c "grep -q 'independent' .claude/skills/issue-deliver/SKILL.md && grep -q 'quality-manager' .claude/skills/issue-deliver/SKILL.md"`; behavioural RED/GREEN in Evidence.

### P9 — `CLAUDE.md` role routing

`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §3 item 8
Requirement: the session entry contract routes the work to one role skill and states the separation-of-duties rule and the owner-only signatures.

- **P9.1** Given "which skill baselines a benefit?", when a session reads `CLAUDE.md`, then the routing table names `benefits-manager` and no branch is opened.
  Verify: `bash -c "grep -q 'benefits-manager' CLAUDE.md && grep -q 'programme-architect' CLAUDE.md"`; routing RED/GREEN in Evidence.

issues.body:
## Goal

The V2 programme's delivered slices and a delivered work product each carry a Lean-checked certificate that a third party can re-verify, and the programme release gate refuses to open without its bundle.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md` § What Lean can and cannot prove here, § Design 6 — created by #744.
- `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery/project-brief.md` — created by #744.
- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.3 (plan ≠ evidence), §5.4 (gates), §12 (the V2 slices and their gates).
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § Issue content contract.

**Written split (2026-11-26, 03-DELIVERY exception, 2 issues ≤ 5).** This is the deployment-gated
half: its live scenarios need the engine carrying `0076` (from #744) and a prover reachable from the
`conveyor` namespace, neither of which can be proven in that unit's PR.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `1` — authorised (`seed/programme-definition.json` tranches[1]); the programme certificates it produces are read by the T12 acceptance in tranche 4 |
| Brief | `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery/project-brief.md` — created by #744 |
| ADM phase/plateau | `G`; capability |
| Benefits | `B1 — Auditable decisions`, as the enabling evidence for its "every choice has a decision row" target; this unit adds the re-checkable certificate such a row cites |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/746-lean-corpus` |
| HEAD | `0db5b19a` |
| Session | claude-code on m4 |
| Updated | 2026-11-26T14:26Z |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.3, §5.4, §12 | main@9da0ed9c |
| Plan | `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md` | #744 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/proof/render.rs` — the facts renderer | to create |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/proof/mod.rs` — the certificate types | to create |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/pm/mod.rs:resolve_evidence` — the `lean_proof` arm #744 adds | #744 |
| Lean | `docs/spec/lean/DeliveryModel.lean` — the hand-written model | to create |
| Lean | `docs/spec/lean/README.md` — the grade vocabulary and the trust note | to create |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/lean_corpus.rs`, `proof_render.rs`, `proof_programme.rs`, `proof_package.rs` | to create |
| Evidence | `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` — the live certificate record | to create |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@9da0ed9c` · measured 2026-11-26
- Docs: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` blob `e63417a0` · `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` blob `6284617a`
- Prover: `apps/lean4-prover/lean/lean-toolchain` and `lake-manifest.json` at main name the toolchain and Mathlib revision every certificate records

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 measurement | ABSENT | no recorded `computation_time_ms` for a `by decide` proof over a conveyor snapshot |
| P2 Lean model | ABSENT | no `docs/spec/lean/` path at main; `apps/lean4-prover/lean/` holds only the project skeleton |
| P3 facts renderer | ABSENT | no renderer in `crates/actions` at main |
| P4 programme certificates | ABSENT | no `proof` rows and no bundle in the repo |
| P5 package manifests | ABSENT | no manifest type exists |
| P6 live gate | ABSENT | `lean_proof` evidence kind does not exist until #744 merges |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — measurement before anything depends on it

Requirement: the prover's real caps are measured against a conveyor-shaped snapshot, not assumed.

- **P1.1** Given a representative slice snapshot, when it is rendered and checked, then the record names the source character count, the `computation_time_ms`, the reduction used (`decide` or `native_decide`) and whether the 100 000-character and 120-second caps bind.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Measurement, with the raw response bodies attached (to create)

### P2 — the model and its universal theorems

Requirement: the delivery rules are formalised once, and their universal properties are proven for every state rather than for one record.

- **P2.1** Given the model file, when the prover checks it, then it is `valid` and the theorems `closed_is_terminal`, `no_self_transition` and `accepted_path_carries_evidence` are proven.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lean_corpus.rs::the_model_checks` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a deliberately wrong variant of the model, when it is checked, then the check is not `valid`, so the corpus cannot silently become vacuous.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lean_corpus.rs::a_wrong_model_is_refused` (to create)

### P3 — the facts renderer

Requirement: a certificate's Lean source is a pure function of canonical facts, so the Rust↔Lean binding is checkable without hashing inside Lean.

- **P3.1** Given the same facts read twice, when they are rendered, then the bytes are identical and `sha256(facts_canonical)` equals the stored `facts_sha256`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_render.rs::the_same_facts_render_byte_identical` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a snapshot with a missing evidence row, when the renderer builds the theorem, then the resulting check is not `proven` and the refusal names the offending item.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_render.rs::a_bad_snapshot_names_the_item` (to create)

### P4 — programme certificates

Requirement: every built V2 slice has a leaf certificate, and one bundle proves the set against the release spec hash.

- **P4.1** Given the built slices, when the programme proof runs, then each leaf certificate is `proven` on the pinned spec hash and the bundle proves the multiset of leaf certificate hashes.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_programme.rs::each_built_slice_has_a_certificate` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given the same bundle with one slice removed, when it is checked, then it is not `proven`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_programme.rs::the_bundle_fails_when_a_slice_is_dropped` (to create)

### P5 — work-product and package proofs

Requirement: any delivered package can carry a certificate about its own manifest.

- **P5.1** Given a package manifest whose migrations are paired, whose routes are a subset of the served OpenAPI paths and whose required checks all passed, when it is proved, then the certificate is `proven` and readable from the card that delivered it.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_package.rs::a_complete_package_is_proven` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given an unpaired migration or a route missing from the served document, when it is proved, then the result is not `proven` and names the item.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proof_package.rs::an_incomplete_package_names_the_item` (to create)

### P6 — the live gate

Requirement: the programme release gate requires the bundle, and the refusal path is real.

- **P6.1** (live, deployment-gated by #744's migration reaching the deployed engine and by the `conveyor`→`lean4-prover:8812` reachability change in the private infrastructure repository) Given the deployed engine, when a release gate is opened without the bundle, then it answers `422 gate_evidence_missing`; with the bundle it opens and the approval meta cites the certificates.
  Verify: the command and its output recorded in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Live gate (to create)
- **P6.2** (live) Given a tampered stored `facts_canonical`, when the gate is re-routed, then it refuses with the typed proof error and the audit row records the refusal.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § Tamper drill (to create)

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| acceptance-blocked-by | #744 | the store, the actions and the `lean_proof` arm must exist before a certificate can be stored or cited; construction of the corpus and renderer does not wait | open |
| related | #561 | the declared Lean actions and the toolkit seed the live calls use | closed |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref or is marked `to create`.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no `Blocker:` line, because `acceptance-blocked-by` never freezes construction.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from #744 (new paths under `docs/spec/lean/`, `crates/actions/src/proof/`, `docs/evidence/`).
- [x] Scope corrections applied: no old-system shutdown or parity work.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head.
- [ ] The live scenarios are recorded in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` with the response bodies.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Prover-side attestation and any claim that the certificate is signed rather than re-checkable.
- Rust-level verification (Verus/Kani) and refinement of the model to the implementation.
- Widening the requirement from the programme release gate to every card's Definition of Done — that is a later decision informed by one cycle of real refusals.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes. Two gates: the deployed engine must carry #744's migration, and the `conveyor` namespace must be reachable to `lean4-prover:8812` (rule change in the private infrastructure repository, opened 2026-11-26). Until both hold, P6 stays unproven and the issue does not close.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which built slices enter the first bundle? | implementation session | every slice the coverage record marks built, and no planned one |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |

## Goal

The four `analyse.*` verbs that SPEC V2 declares but the registry does not serve — app, brand, content and report — become read-only actions whose reports are deterministic functions of stored documents plus caller-supplied evidence, so a gate can cite them.

## Plan / audit source

## Baseline

- Docs: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` blob `e63417a0` · `docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json` blob `5aeaf6a0` · `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` blob `6284617a`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |

| P1 `analyse.app` | ABSENT | `grep -rn 'analyse\.app' crates/actions/src crates/actions/tests/registry.rs` → no hit; `crates/analysis/src/app/mod.rs:107` is a page critique over `PageEvidence`, not a route-coverage report |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — `analyse.app` reports §10.5 destination coverage

Requirement: with a caller-supplied route table and captured pages, the action reports every §10.5 destination whose route is absent, present but unserved, or unreachable from the supplied pages; the report is deterministic and writes nothing.

- **P1.1** Given a route table missing two §10.5 destinations and one destination recorded as unserved, when `analyse.app` runs, then the report carries `app-destination-missing` for each absent route and `app-destination-unserved` for the unserved one.
  Verify: `crates/analysis/tests/app.rs::the_destination_table_is_measured_against_the_route_table` (to create at `crates/analysis/tests/app.rs`)
- **P1.2** Given the same document bytes twice, when `analyse.app` runs twice, then the two reports serialise to identical bytes.
  Verify: `crates/analysis/tests/app.rs::the_same_evidence_twice_is_the_same_report` (to create)

### P2 — `analyse.brand` reports the page's consistency with supplied brand facts

Requirement: palette, typography and voice facts supplied by the caller are checked against one stored page; each declared fact the page does not express and each observed fact the brand does not declare is named.

- **P2.1** Given a page that uses one declared colour and an undeclared font, when `analyse.brand` runs, then the report names the missing palette entry and the undeclared family, and carries no finding for the declared fact it expresses.
  Verify: `crates/analysis/tests/brand.rs::the_page_is_measured_against_the_supplied_brand` (to create at `crates/analysis/tests/brand.rs`)
- **P2.2** Given a required voice term that the page never uses, when `analyse.brand` runs, then `brand-voice-term-missing` names the term.
  Verify: `crates/analysis/tests/brand.rs::a_missing_voice_term_is_named` (to create)

### P3 — `analyse.content` reports per-page heading, source and filler quality

Requirement: one stored page yields one report that joins the existing CRO/marketing findings with required-heading, source and filler checks; several page ids yield one report per page.

Requirement: a tenant-scoped, RLS-forced `proof` table whose row can be re-verified without trusting the writer.

  Verify: `crates/store/tests/s07_schema.rs` ledger + table list (to update), `crates/store/src/migrate.rs` (to update)

### P3 — the proof actions

Requirement: a certificate is built from the engine's own persisted invocation, never from a caller-supplied verdict.

- **P3.1** Given a completed `lean4.check` invocation, when `proofs.record` names its idempotency key, then the stored verdict, diagnostics and computation time are the persisted response's, and a verdict supplied in the input is ignored.

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/proofs_reverify.rs::a_tampered_source_fails`, `::a_replay_returns_the_first_certificate` (to create)

Requirement: a gate can pin a spec hash and refuse a proof that does not answer it.

- **P4.1** Given a gate opened with `pinned_spec_sha256` and a `lean_proof` evidence ref whose proof is `proven` on that spec, when the PM routes the gate, then the approval meta carries `{ "kind": "lean_proof", "id": <proof> }` and the gate opens.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/pm_gate_proof.rs::a_valid_proof_opens_the_gate` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a failed verdict, a proof on a different spec hash, a certificate hash that does not recompute, or a proof id in another tenant, when the gate is routed, then each is refused with a typed `422` naming which check failed; and a gate with no evidence and `require` still answers `gate_evidence_missing`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/pm_gate_proof.rs::every_bad_proof_is_refused`, `crates/actions/tests/pm_gate_evidence.rs` (extend, exists)

### P5 — the credential and the app row

Requirement: the prover credential is its own sealed secret, minted against its own catalogue app.

- **P5.1** Given an operator writes a BYO token with the new service value, when the row is written, then the sealed secret is `lean4.token` and the report names the secret, its source and no value; and a mint against an unknown catalogue app fails instead of silently succeeding.

## What

The `web` job fails a **different** test on almost every run, in specs the PR under test does not touch. Four measured instances, three environments, four different tests:

| Where | Instance | Result |
|---|---|---|
| PR #720 CI (`web`, run 45574780274, 2026-11-25T08:16Z) | `board.spec.ts:253 a label, a lane and an unarchive round-trip through the UI` | the run's only failure (30.9 s); **main's `web` on the merged tree (run 45581446543, 09:01Z) passed** |
| Local full suite, fresh seed (#572 session) | `board.spec.ts:8 keyboard moves a card between lanes` | re-ran alone: **1 passed in 1.2 s** |
| Local full suite, fresh seed, next run | `evals.spec.ts:91 the report is the server's…` — the `Variant` table is absent; the DB held **2 `queued` eval runs** | different test from the run before |
| PR #727 CI (`web`, run 45588657478, 09:46Z) | `evals.spec.ts:252` (same `Variant` table) **and** `tools.spec.ts:142` (panel not visible) | 2 failed |

A fifth, earlier instance is on record: #512 (closed) fixed a board refetch race after Add card / Save; the current `board.spec.ts:8/253` failures look like the same family.

## Why it matters

- Every lane sees a red `web` job that is not its change; the only recourse is a re-run, and the PR can still merge (the merge queue runs no `web` job), so a red check teaches the fleet to ignore it.
- The evals instance is not purely visual: the report reads `—` while eval runs are still `queued`, i.e. the test can read before the worker has drained the run.

## First step

Reproduce under load, not alone — `--repeat-each` on the exact job stack:

```
cargo leptos build --release --frontend-only --cargo-locked
BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8930 DEV_AUTH_TOKEN=dev:alice \
  npx playwright test board.spec.ts evals.spec.ts --repeat-each 10 --workers 1
```

Then read the trace of the first repeat that fails. For `evals.spec.ts`, assert on the **run's status** (`eval_runs.list`) before reading the report, instead of racing the worker; for the board, the #512 fix (wait for the refetch the mutation triggers) is the prior art to check.

## Acceptance

- `--repeat-each 10` on `board.spec.ts` and `evals.spec.ts` is green on the fixed stack.
- The evals test does not read the report until the run it asserts is `complete` (an explicit wait on the run's status, not a sleep).
- One PR, `Closes #<n>`; `web` green twice on CI.

## Out of scope

- The `tools.spec.ts:142` failure on #727 — that is #630's own tools-panel work, already being iterated on its lane.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — an accepted gate applies its draft

`S21-message-construction.md` §22 (deferred unit) · `v1-p77-1`'s sibling decision, ADR 0011 § Alternatives.
Requirement: `decision_policy.meta.on_accept ∈ {park, apply}` (absent = `park`, validated at authoring); an accepted L1 decision applies through the one `apply_draft_tx`; a cardless run applies nothing and says so.

- **P1.1** Given an `internal_agent` binding whose `gate.precheck` policy declares `on_accept=apply` and a draft that passes the threshold, when `run.execute` finishes the step, then the draft document is attached to the run's card, the run is `succeeded`, exactly one `gate.precheck` decision exists and exactly one `inference_call`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/internal_agent_runtime.rs::an_accepted_draft_is_applied_when_the_policy_says_apply` (to create)

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/internal_agent_runtime.rs::an_accepted_draft_parks_by_default` (to create)

- **P1.4** Given an `internal_agent` run whose card is cleared (the pre-guard shape), when it executes, then the dispatcher refuses it `capability_not_ready` before any model or laya call; the executor's `apply_skipped: no_card` branch remains defence in depth.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/internal_agent_runtime.rs::a_cardless_internal_agent_run_is_refused_before_any_call` (to create)

### P2 — no model call without compiled text and a 64-hex hash (`v1-p77-1`)

`v1-p77-1` · SPEC_V2 §7.7.
Requirement: an active `internal_agent` must name a resolvable prompt; readiness blocks without one; execution refuses before any call; every recorded call carries a 64-hex `prompt_sha256`.

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/capability.rs::an_active_agent_without_a_prompt_is_refused` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given an existing draft agent with no prompt, when `capability_agents.update` would make it active, then `422 prompt_ref_required`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/capability.rs::activating_an_agent_without_a_prompt_is_refused` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a row written before the guard (active, no prompt), when readiness is computed, then a `PromptNotConfigured` blocker is returned.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/capability.rs::readiness_blocks_an_agent_with_no_prompt` (to create)
- **P2.4** Given a workflow `agent.run` whose effective prompt is `None`, when it executes, then zero `inference_call` rows exist and the run refuses `409 capability_not_ready` naming the agent.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/agent_run_resolved.rs::a_run_with_no_compiled_prompt_makes_no_call` (to create)
- **P2.5** Given any completed `internal_agent` call, when the ledger is read, then `prompt_sha256` matches `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/internal_agent_runtime.rs::every_internal_agent_call_records_a_64_hex_hash` (to create)

### P3 — a recipe-level prompt budget is authorable (`v1-p77-2`)

`v1-p77-2` · SPEC_V2 §7.7.
Requirement: `prompt_recipes.create` accepts and writes `budget_chars`; the compile's measured refusal then becomes reachable at the recipe level; a new version changes the ceiling.

- **P3.1** Given `prompt_recipes.create` with `budget_chars=200` and sections that total more, when the recipe compiles, then it refuses `PromptOverBudget` with the measured size and makes no model call.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/prompt_recipes.rs::a_recipe_budget_is_written_and_refuses_measured` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a second version with a larger ceiling, when it is activated, then the same facts compile and the hash matches the unbounded compile.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/prompt_recipes.rs::a_new_version_changes_the_ceiling` (to create)
- **P3.3** Given `budget_chars=0`, when create is invoked, then `422`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/prompt_recipes.rs::a_zero_budget_is_refused` (to create)

### P4 — the release compiles its knowledge layers (`v1-w1a-2`, P0)

`v1-w1a-2` · SPEC_V2 §4.1.
Requirement: one `organisation_layer` table at base, industry, department archetype, each department in declared order and job; required tightens downward only; sibling disagreement refuses; the snapshot records value and source; the hash is deterministic.

- **P4.1** Given one kind set at base, industry, archetype and department and another at job, when the release compiles, then the job value wins and every value's level and source are named.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::the_release_resolves_layers_in_declared_order` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a department whose required kind resolves nowhere, when publish runs, then `409 release_not_ready` names the kind and the department and writes no release row.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::an_unresolved_required_kind_refuses_publish` (to create)
- **P4.3** Given two sibling departments setting one kind to different values with no job-layer row, when publish runs, then `422 department_conflict` names the departments; a job-layer row resolves it.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::sibling_departments_conflict_unless_the_job_resolves` (to create)
- **P4.4** Given `required=true` at an ancestor and `required=false` below, when resolved, then the result is required and the value still overrides; the reverse never loosens it.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::required_only_tightens_downward` (to create)
- **P4.5** Given two identical publishes, when hashed, then `release_hash` is identical byte-for-byte and the layer section is stable.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs::two_identical_publishes_hash_identically` (to create)
- **P4.6** Given `organisation_layers.set|list` over HTTP and MCP, when the parity sample runs, then both transports answer and the served-spec lock matches.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/parity_http_mcp.rs` + `served-spec.lock.json --check-lock` (exists)

### P5 — the live model/laya proof runs

`docs/evidence/S21-RUN.md` § Unblock · SPEC_V2 §7.2–§7.7.
Requirement: the owner provisions a licensed test caller; the two ignored proofs run against the real router and laya bridge and record measured rows — or the receipt records the exact blocker.

- **P5.1** (live, acceptance-gated by the owner-provisioned caller) Given the estate's inference router and laya bridge and a licensed caller's tokens in the local environment, when the two `#[ignore]`d proofs run, then the model call and the laya decision are recorded with real latency and a 64-hex prompt hash.

## Goal

`apps/research`'s media binary resolves its tenant from a licence bearer in `Authorization: Bearer`
when no `X-Tenant-Id` is present, so the conveyor's external action engine — which can send only
`Authorization` — can call the media read surface. The media toolkit then becomes declarable in a
follow-up unit.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/688-media-licence-bearer` |
| HEAD | `19bffc70` |
| Session | m4.local, 2026-11-25 |
| Updated | 2026-11-25 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## Plan / audit source

- #561's scope correction (2026-11-24): the media routes authenticate on `X-Tenant-Id`, which
  `HandlerRef::External` cannot send; the five `media.*` provenance rows are `DROP` for that reason.
- `apps/research/src/media/tenant.rs` — the tenant gate; #226 closed the bare-header trust, and this
  unit must not reopen it.
- `apps/inference-router/src/auth.rs:5` — the precedent: the bearer is read from `X-Tenant-Id`
  first, then `Authorization`.
- `crates/actions/src/spec.rs:652-679` — `HandlerRef::External` carries only `auth` (sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer`), with no custom-header field.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `4` — T14 (Estate toolkits), `seed/programme-definition.json` |
| Brief | `docs/plans/04-TOOL-ESTATE-INVENTORY.md` §1 |
| ADM phase/plateau | `—` (no architecture change; the service accepts the platform's existing bearer convention) |
| Benefits | `enabling — no direct benefit`: it clears the path for the media toolkit |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/research/src/media/tenant.rs` | origin/main@ca392a97 (blob `2dc99951`) |
| Code | `apps/inference-router/src/auth.rs` | origin/main@ca392a97 (blob `95ad5327`) |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/spec.rs` (`HandlerRef::External`) | origin/main@ca392a97 |
| Test | `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs` (the auth cases) | origin/main@ca392a97 |
| Seed | `seed/tool_provenance.json` rows `media.search|score|downloads|items|collections` (`DROP`) | origin/main@ca392a97 |
| Plan | `docs/plans/04-TOOL-ESTATE-INVENTORY.md` §1 | origin/main@ca392a97 (blob `1300acc6`) |
| Issue | #561 (the wave that measured the gap) | open |
| Issue | #226 (the bare-header trust this must not reinstate) | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `origin/main@ca392a97`, measured 2026-11-24.
- Docs: `tenant.rs` blob `2dc99951`; `auth.rs` blob `95ad5327`; inventory blob `1300acc6`.

## Current state

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 Authorization-only licence resolution | ABSENT | `tenant.rs` reads only `x-tenant-id`; a request without it is `401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` even when `Authorization` carries a valid licence |
| P2 the bare-header trust stays closed | DONE — must not regress | #226; a bare `X-Tenant-Id` requires a service vouch on `MEDIA_DISCOVERY_ONBEHALF_SUBJECTS` |
| P3 the media action declaration | OUT OF SCOPE — follow-up | #561 records the five operations as `DROP` in `seed/tool_provenance.json` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the Authorization licence path

The media service resolves the tenant from the licence in `Authorization` when `X-Tenant-Id` is
absent; the licence is introspected at `LICENSE_INTROSPECT_URL` exactly as the header-borne token is,
and the tenant is the one the ACTIVE licence names.

- **Given** an active licence token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and no `X-Tenant-Id`,
  **when** a `/api/*` request arrives, **then** the request proceeds with the licence's tenant.
  **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::a_licence_bearer_resolves_the_tenant` (to create).
- **Given** an expired or unknown licence in `Authorization`, **when** the request arrives,
  **then** the answer is `401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`.
  **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::an_invalid_licence_bearer_is_401` (to create).
- **Given** both headers, **when** they name different tenants, **then** the licence wins and the
  mismatch is recorded (the router's rule).
  **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::the_licence_tenant_wins_over_a_mismatched_header`
  (to create).

### P2 — the security review

The change must not reinstate the bare-header trust #226 closed: a bare `X-Tenant-Id` without a
vouch stays `401`, and `MEDIA_DISCOVERY_ONBEHALF_SUBJECTS` is unchanged.

- **Given** a bare `X-Tenant-Id` and no credential, **when** the request arrives, **then** the answer
  is `401` (unchanged).
  **Verify:** the existing #226 cases in `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs` stay green.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #561 | it measured the gap and recorded the `DROP` rows | open |
| blocks (follow-up) | the media toolkit declaration | the five operations become declarable once the bearer path exists | to create |
| related | #226 | the bare-header trust this unit must not reopen | closed |

No `blocked-by` is open; `status:ready`.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline and doc blob shas named; every cited path resolves at `origin/main@ca392a97`.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no open `blocked-by`.
- [x] No app route, table or schema changes beyond the auth extractor; the handlers are untouched.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head.
- [ ] `cargo test -p conveyor-research` and the `apps/research` contract/parity suites are green.
- [ ] The #226 cases stay green; the licence is introspected, never trusted on its face.
- [ ] One non-draft PR `Closes #<n>` merged; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the external action engine (`HandlerRef::External`) or to the conveyor's action
  declarations; the media toolkit is a follow-up.
- The downloads adapter (`POST /api/downloads` stays `501`) and the write routes (`score`,
  collections create/import/delete).
- Any change to the webscraper or the Lean prover.

## Deployment prerequisite

The change is in the research image; its live proof waits on the image publish and rollout, recorded
after merge.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Should `Authorization` resolve the tenant for every `/api/*` route, or reads only? | owner | every `/api/*` route — the extractor is the gate, and the write routes stay unused by the conveyor |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test tenant` -> `a_licence_bearer_resolves_the_tenant` | PASS | 19bffc70 |
| P1.2 | `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test tenant` -> `an_invalid_licence_bearer_is_401` | PASS | 19bffc70 |
| P1.3 | `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test tenant` -> `the_licence_tenant_wins_over_a_mismatched_header` | PASS | 19bffc70 |
| P2.1 | `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test tenant` -> the #226 cases (`a_service_token_scopes_the_tenant`, `no_credential_is_refused`, `a_malformed_tenant_is_a_400`, `a_licence_token_names_the_tenant`) | PASS (7/7 tenant suite) | 19bffc70 |

## Goal

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — The live governance chain

Generalise the T19 chain script into `scripts/governance-chain.py --project <id> --plan docs/plans/<dir>` (T19 invocation preserved); run the T19F chain: seven mandatory artefacts, seven links, the live SoAW, the phase-F delivery contract, two Phase-G reviews, the published `architecture-artifact` document, and a read-only B7 check (no baseline overwrite).

- **P1.1** Given the deployed engine carrying #683's merge, when the T19F chain check runs, then 7/7 artefacts are `approved`, two contracts are `live`, both Phase-G reviews are recorded and the `architecture-artifact` output is published.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/governance-chain.py --project T19F --check` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given B7's existing measured baseline, when the chain runs, then B7 is read and not overwritten.
  Verify: the chain's B7 assertion in `governance-chain.py --check` (to create)

### P2 — The live gate

`scripts/t19f-live-gate-check.py`: author a policy v2 through the authoring actions (intake → draft → review approval → publish), prove the meeting pinned at v1 still resolves v1; open a board sitting on a real subject and decide it `via='meeting'`; materialise a real cadence slot; read everything back through actions.

- **P2.1** Given the deployed engine, when the gate runs, then the policy v2 row exists and the in-flight v1 meeting still resolves v1.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/t19f-live-gate-check.py --check` (to create; evidence `docs/evidence/t19f/live-gate.json`)
- **P2.2** Given the gate's sitting, when the decisions are read back, then the board's per-seat `approval_decision` rows carry `via='meeting'` and the approval matches the rule.
  Verify: the gate's sitting assertion (to create)
- **P2.3** Given the gate's cadence, when the meeting is read back, then one non-cancelled meeting exists with the cadence row's type and slot.
  Verify: the gate's cadence assertion (to create)

### P3 — Programme publication

`migrate --seed --tenant nonagentic`, `programmes.refresh`, then the strict publish and the docs build to a fixed point; the regenerated pack is committed.

- **P3.1** Given the live tenant, when the seed and refresh run, then T19F, its board and the B7 link are live rows and the refresh reports no unexpected creates.
  Verify: the seed/refresh read-back recorded in `docs/evidence/t19f/` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given the live snapshot, when the strict publish runs, then there is no new T19F P0/P1 and `programme.json`, `msp.json`, `standards.json` and `conformance.json` carry T19F.
  Verify: `CONFORMANCE_STRICT=1 docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh` then `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot docs/design/data --strict --fail-on P0,P1 --baseline docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json`
- **P3.3** Given the published pack, when the docs build and checks run, then the T19F plan and its artefacts render under `docs/design/docs/` and the pack checks are clean.
  Verify: `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check && node docs/design/scripts/check-docs.cjs`

### P4 — The closure review and evidence

Publish `docs/plans/T19F/closure-review.md` and `docs/plans/T19F/evidence.md`; the review records acceptance met and **defers project closure to the tranche-6 review**; T19F stays `active`, so no unledgered P0 is manufactured.

- **P4.1** Given the acceptance evidence, when the closure review is published, then it records acceptance met and the deferral, and the live project row remains `active`.
  Verify: the documents read-back in `docs/evidence/t19f/` and `node docs/design/scripts/check-docs.cjs`
- **P4.2** Given the T19F project, when the conformance audit runs, then no `project_in_unauthorised_tranche` finding exists for T19F (it is not closed).
  Verify: the strict audit above (§P3.2)

## Goal

`docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh` must derive the docs index and the programme seed from the
data it installs, so a green publish never leaves the committed pack internally stale.

## Why now

Measured on #545 (2026-11-24). The live publish passed the strict gate and wrote the record,
register and pages, but left two derived artefacts inconsistent:

- it runs `build-docs.py` **before** installing `$tmp/data`, so `documents.js` hashed the
  pre-publish `docs/design/data/conformance.md`; `build-docs.py --check` failed with
