| P5 tests | ABSENT | no case covers an attachment under a publishable-but-unpublished parent, update publish/unpublish, the limbo transition gate, or restore-unpublish |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — every public reader agrees

`docs/design/README.md` § "The output standard" · audit F1.
Requirement: an attachment is public only when its parent is public; `publishable` alone serves nothing.

- **P1.1** Given a publishable-but-unpublished parent with an attachment, when `/design/docs/attachment-<id>` is requested, then `404` with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs::a_publishable_but_unpublished_parent_serves_no_attachment` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given the same parent, when the public outputs index is built, then neither the parent nor its attachments appear.
  Verify: same test, reading `/design/docs/outputs.js` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a published parent, when its attachments are requested, then `200` and the index carries them.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs` — the existing attachment case
- **P1.4** Given the design module contract, when read, then it names `published_at`, not `publishable`, as the filter.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'published_at' crates/api/src/design.rs`

### P2 — the publish gate reads publication

`docs/design/README.md` § "The output standard" · audit F2.
Requirement: the headings gate runs on every transition into public, including a publishable-but-unpublished row.

- **P2.1** Given a publishable-but-unpublished row missing a required heading, when `documents.publish {publish: true}`, then `409 output_incomplete` and `published_at` stays null.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_publishable_but_unpublished_row_is_checked_on_transition` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a complete publishable-but-unpublished row, when published, then `200` and `published_at` is set.
  Verify: same test (to create)
- **P2.3** Given an already-published row, when published again or edited, then the headings are not re-checked.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_complete_output_publishes_and_unpublish_never_blocks` (exists)

### P3 — compose and update write publication

`docs/design/README.md` § "The output standard" · audit F3.
Requirement: a compose or update that sets `publishable: true` is a public transition and sets `published_at`; setting it false unpublishes.

- **P3.1** Given `documents.compose` with `publishable: true` and a complete category body, when it returns, then `published_at` is set and the row is served publicly.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::an_output_composed_straight_to_public_is_checked` (extend)
- **P3.2** Given an incomplete body, when composed with `publishable: true`, then `409 output_incomplete`.
  Verify: same test (exists)
- **P3.3** Given a private complete row, when `documents.update {publishable: true}`, then `published_at` is set and the public page serves the row.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::update_publish_and_unpublish_move_published_at` (to create)
- **P3.4** Given a published row, when `documents.update {publishable: false}`, then `published_at` is null and the page, outputs index and attachments are absent.
  Verify: same test (to create)
- **P3.5** Given a published row, when an update changes the body without `publishable`, then `published_at` is unchanged and the row stays public.
  Verify: same test (to create)
- **P3.6** Given a publishable-but-unpublished row with incomplete headings, when `documents.update {publishable: true}`, then `409 output_incomplete`.
  Verify: same test (to create)

### P4 — history and permission checks read publication

Audit F4 and the F2/F3 class.
Requirement: only a public row is labelled published, locked from member edits, blocked from `request_publish`/`return`, or unpublishable without an admin.

- **P4.1** Given a publishable-but-unpublished row, when `documents.revision_list` is read, then its revision is `draft`, not `published`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_publishable_but_unpublished_row_is_not_history_published` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a publishable-but-unpublished row, when `documents.request_publish` or `documents.return` runs, then neither reports already-published/published-locked.
  Verify: same test (to create)
- **P4.3** Given a published row, when a member edits it, then `409 published_locked`.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::a_member_drafts_and_requests_an_admin_publishes_and_history_restores` (exists)
- **P4.4** Given a published row, when an admin restores an earlier revision, then the row is unpublished (`published_at` null) and absent from the public window.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::restoring_a_published_row_unpublishes_it` (to create)

### P5 — the contract and the regression set

Audit F5.
Requirement: the source states the invariant and no reader or writer is left on the old bit.

- **P5.1** Given the store and action docs, when read, then `DocumentPatch.publishable` and the design module state that publication is `published_at`.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'published_at' crates/store/src/document.rs crates/api/src/design.rs`
- **P5.2** Given the merged tree, when grepping the public readers, then no attachment reader filters on `p.publishable` alone.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'p.publishable' crates/store/src/document.rs` → no hits
- **P5.3** Given the merged tree, when the suite runs, then every existing publication test still passes unchanged.
  Verify: the PR's CI test shards at the PR head

<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->
## Goal

The worker claims up to eight jobs per tenant-tick in one scoped transaction with one `reap_exhausted`, instead of one transaction and one reap per job.

## Plan / audit source

- Cross-cutting performance unit from the 2026-11-21 static-analysis session (owner direction: static code analysis first; the deployed-cluster analysis is a later session). There is no slice plan; the measured state and the acceptance are in this issue.
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract" — the shape of this body.

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | `0` — cross-cutting engineering; no delivery tranche is authorised for it |
| Brief | `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` (the P0 definition set) |
| ADM phase/plateau | — (no architecture change) |
| Benefits | enabling — no direct benefit: it removes repeated database work from the worker's only continuous loop |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/536-worker-claim-batch` |
| HEAD | `70f24a24` |
| Session | m4 · Claude Code |
| Updated | 2026-11-21 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/store/src/jobs.rs:claim_with` (the claim CTE) and `:reap_exhausted` | main@7314a2d0 |
| Code | `apps/server/src/worker.rs:Worker::tick` (`BATCH_PER_TENANT`, `MAX_IN_FLIGHT_JOBS`, the per-claim loop) | main@7314a2d0 |
| Code | `crates/store/src/scope.rs:begin_scoped` (BEGIN + tenant GUC per call) | main@7314a2d0 |
| Code | `migrations/0001_platform.sql` (`job_claim_idx`, `job_lease_idx`, `job` RLS policy) | main@7314a2d0 |
| Test | `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs` (claim, reclaim, fencing, exhaustion) | main@7314a2d0 |
| Test | `apps/server/tests/common/mod.rs` (`TestDb::fresh`, runtime + superuser pools, real migrations and RLS) | main@7314a2d0 |
| Gate | `scripts/ci/gate.sh` | main@7314a2d0 |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@7314a2d0`, measured 2026-11-21.
- Docs: `03-DELIVERY.md` blob `65e4b5bf3eab`; `crates/store/src/jobs.rs` `5a7f240f2a02`; `apps/server/src/worker.rs` `5193c2b3216f`; `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs` `11865ed0aa44`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 one claim transaction per batch | ABSENT | `claim_with` opens `begin_scoped` and commits per call; `claim` delegates with no batch size |
| P2 one reap per batch | ABSENT | `reap_exhausted` runs inside every `claim_with`; the tick loop calls claim up to `BATCH_PER_TENANT` times |
| P3 tests and statement evidence | ABSENT | no batch API, no batch tests, no EXPLAIN evidence exists |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — batch claim in the store

Requirement: one scoped transaction claims up to `max` due jobs with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, preserving every claim clause (per-row token, lease, attempts/continuation, kind filter) and running the reap once before the claim.

- **P1.1** Given three due jobs and `max = 2`, when `claim_batch` runs, then it returns exactly two distinct jobs, both `running` with distinct lease tokens, and the third row stays `pending`.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::claim_batch_returns_at_most_max_and_leaves_the_rest` (to create at that path)
- **P1.2** Given two uncommitted `claim_batch_tx` calls on the same tenant, when both have run, then the second returns none of the rows the first locked.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::two_uncommitted_batches_pick_disjoint_rows` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given due pending rows, future-dated pending rows and a row of another kind, when a batch runs with a kind filter, then only due rows of the named kinds are returned.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::claim_batch_honours_kind_and_run_after` (to create)
- **P1.4** Given the existing single-claim callers, when the batch API lands, then `claim` and `claim_with` behave exactly as before (`max = 1`).
  Verify: `cargo-guard.py nextest run -p conveyor-store --test jobs` — the existing tests pass unchanged.

### P2 — the worker claims once per tenant-tick

Requirement: the tick resolves its claim budget from free permits, issues one `claim_batch`, and gives each returned job one held permit.

- **P2.1** Given five free permits and a non-empty queue, when the tick runs, then it claims at most `min(5, BATCH_PER_TENANT)` jobs in a single store call and spawns one task per job.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/worker.rs::claim_batch_tests::the_budget_is_capped_by_permits_and_the_tenant_batch` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given zero free permits, when the tick runs, then no claim is issued.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/worker.rs::claim_batch_tests::no_free_permit_means_no_budget` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a claim error, when the tick runs, then every permit it took is released and the loop continues to the next tenant.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/worker.rs::claim_batch_tests::dropping_the_budget_returns_the_permits` (to create)

### P3 — one reap, exactly-once dead-lettering

Requirement: the batch's single reap keeps the old exhaustion semantics.

- **P3.1** Given an expired, exhausted `running` row, when a batch claims, then the row is `dead` and is not returned in the batch.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::the_batch_reap_dead_letters_an_exhausted_row` (to create)

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #18 | the deployment gate named by the template; closed, and this unit's live verification is the next session's cluster analysis | closed |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the cited blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every code/test/gate reference resolves at `main@7314a2d0`; the two issue references resolve.
- [x] Every part has at least one scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete and typed; no `blocked-by`, so no `Blocker:` line.
- [x] One-PR scope; no other ready issue touches these files.

## Definition of done

- [x] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [x] `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` green at the exact head.
- [x] Tests added per part; none skipped.
- [x] No migration, no ledger, and `served-spec.lock.json` untouched (no route or action change).
- [x] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- The claim CTE's OR-arm plan (possible seq scan over retained `job` rows): recorded with a seeded EXPLAIN as PR evidence only; its own issue if the scan is confirmed.
- Eval report aggregation (`crates/actions/src/eval/report.rs`), organisation snapshot N+1 (`crates/store/src/organisation.rs`), dead `counts_tx` (`crates/store/src/jobs.rs`).
- Live-cluster profiling and `pg_stat_statements`.
- The audit's standing scope corrections: no old-system shutdown/freeze/dump, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity work.

## Deployment prerequisite

No. Code-only; the deployed worker picks the change up on the normal image promotion. Live verification belongs to the next session's cluster analysis, not to this issue.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Is the single-claim CTE already index-backed at scale, or does it seq-scan the retained `job` rows? | next session | No SQL change here; seed a local fixture, record EXPLAIN, file its own issue if the scan is real |

## Evidence at completion

PR #539, `Closes #536`, merged 2026-11-21T18:38:32Z as `abe27233`. Local gate
`bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` at the PR head: 3542/3542 passed, `gate: OK`, exit 0.

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::claim_batch_returns_at_most_max_and_leaves_the_rest` | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P1.2 | `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::two_uncommitted_batches_pick_disjoint_rows` — 2 of 3 rows locked; the second open claim takes exactly the skipped row | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P1.3 | `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::claim_batch_honours_kind_and_run_after` | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P1.4 | `cargo-guard.py nextest run -p conveyor-store --test jobs` — 13/13 (7 existing unchanged, 6 new) | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P2.1 | `apps/server/src/worker.rs::tick_claim_tests::one_tick_claims_exactly_the_free_permit_budget` — 5 free permits, 8 due → 5 claimed, 3 pending, all 5 succeeded; plus the budget helper unit test | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P2.2 | `apps/server/src/worker.rs::tick_claim_tests::a_tick_with_no_free_permit_claims_nothing` — all 8 permits held → both jobs stay pending; plus the helper unit test | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P2.3 | `apps/server/src/worker.rs::tick_claim_tests::a_claim_error_releases_the_budget_and_the_tick_survives` — the claim error returns the whole budget and the tick returns Ok | pass | `41dd9a2c` |
| P3.1 | `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs::the_batch_reap_dead_letters_an_exhausted_row` | pass | `41dd9a2c` |

Note on P2: the tick tests prove the observable contract (claim sized by free permits, one task
per claimed job, zero budget → no claim, claim error → budget released, tick survives). "In a
single store call" is structural — `tick` has one `claim_batch` call site and no claim loop — a
behavioural test cannot count round trips without instrumenting production code. The P2.3
"continues to the next tenant" half is likewise structural: the error arm has no `?`/`break`.

### Open question 1 (answered)

A 20k-row seeded fixture (retained `succeeded` history + 3 due rows, `ANALYZE`) produced, for
the old single-claim statement and the batch statement, `Index Scan using job_live_dedupe_key`
with a filter on the OR arms and no `Seq Scan` on `job`; both plans ~0.1–0.2 ms. The partial
live-jobs index excludes retained history, so no index or SQL change was needed. The fixture was
temporary and is not retained; the EXPLAIN summary is in PR #539.

## Goal

The public design pack renders the tenant's delivery work at four levels — a portfolio Gantt (programmes plus standalone change initiatives), a programme Gantt, a project kanban of work packages and cards, and a work package's own kanban — with in-progress vs completed state and token cost per row. - **P17.1** Given a candidate finding, when `verify-findings.py` runs, then every cited path exists, the line is in range and the quoted text is the raw line; a stale or invented quote fails the gate.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/verify-findings.py docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json`
- **P17.2** Given the admitted findings, when the register is generated, then every finding is a package or carries `duplicate_of`; the scorecard's denominators still come from the standard.
  Verify: the register two-run `cmp` + `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test`
- **P17.3** Given the external programme assessment, when a claim is admitted, then its evidence was re-read in the tree; an unverifiable claim is rejected, not paraphrased.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/verify-findings.py` (the ledger contains no unverified quote)

### P18 — Merge, materialise, publish, live verify
`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § Definition of done
Requirement: the unit merges only on a green local gate and one CI run; the merged binary materialises the packages and the read-only publish regenerates the pack from the post-write database.

- **P18.1** Given the branch head, when the acceptance command runs, then every gate passes and the PR's CI is green at that head.
  Verify: the acceptance command below + the PR's checks
- **P18.2** Given the merged image, when the materialiser runs dry first and then `--apply` by severity, then each open package becomes one card with `meta.rework_key` and the receipt records it.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/materialise-rework.py --self-test` + the post-merge receipt
- **P18.3** Given the post-write database, when `publish-data.sh` runs, then the live `snapshot.js` carries `rework`, `data/standards.json` and the artefact pages are served, and the four levels render them.
  Verify: live `curl` + a Playwright pass on `https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/#portfolio`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #435 | the SPEC_V2 programme this surface reports on | open |
| related | #526 | the tranche-0 rework batch records projects; the pre-publish audit in P4.3 must see its rows | open |
| related | #524 | the strict programme gates change the same programme rows; no file overlap with this pack work | open |


## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the plan/audit blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/design/code/test reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `blocked-by`; the external #193 flake was
  re-tested on the rebased head rather than fixed in this lane.
- [x] One-PR scope; the pack files and the store files are disjoint from #524/#526.
- [x] Scope corrections applied: no old-system shutdown/parity work, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head; Rust verdict from the GitHub preflight, design-pack job green.
- [ ] Tests added/updated per part; none skipped.
- [ ] Docs updated (`docs/design/README.md`, `STUDIO-SPEC.md`, the snapshot module docs).
- [ ] The publish recorded with the live check from P4.3.
- [ ] P7–P12 have one Evidence-at-completion row each, at the exact head.
- [ ] The acceptance command is green at the exact head (see below).
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

### Acceptance command

```
python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py --self-test \
  && python3 scripts/generate-standards.py --self-test \
  && python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test \
  && python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --check-standard \
  && python3 scripts/verify-findings.py docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json \
  && python3 scripts/generate-standards.py --check --snapshot docs/design/data \
  && python3 scripts/materialise-rework.py --self-test \
  && node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs \
  && node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs \
  && node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs \
  && node docs/design/scripts/check-standards.cjs \
  && python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check
```

## Out of scope

- ~~Authoring work packages (creating parent/child cards)~~ — **superseded 2026-11-21**: findings must create rework packages (P9). Planned dates are still never invented; the view reads `meta.plan_start`/`meta.plan_end` when present.
- Any Leptos implementation — this pack is the design mock for the future Leptos UI.
- Real-time updates; the site stays snapshot-driven.
- Changing any programme/tranche/benefit row **in place**, including the #526 rework records. Rework cards are new rows; they never rewrite the record they report on.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes, post-merge only: the image must be rebuilt before `publish-data.sh` can regenerate `data/*.json`. No blocking issue; the code PR does not wait on it.

- **P6.3** Given the five projects, when `documents.list` filters `publishable:true`, then each returns 0 rows.
  Verify: `for id in 01a1d039-0d34-73db-975e-5d178d729cef 01a1d039-0d34-7973-8989-0b83246fc888 01a1d039-0d36-7de8-891c-4d3dcf110cf5 01a1d039-0d37-7f20-9959-979c31daeb5e 01a1d039-0d38-7db1-b685-d76bd4cebf47; do echo "{\"project_id\":\"$id\",\"publishable\":true}" | ssh -i "$CONVEYOR_SSH_KEY" "$CONVEYOR_HOST" "sudo KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml kubectl -n conveyor exec -i deploy/conveyor -- conveyor admin action invoke --tenant nonagentic --name documents.list --input /dev/stdin" | python3 -c "import json,sys;s=sys.stdin.read();d=json.loads(s[s.find('{'):]);assert len(d.get('items',[]))==0,d" || exit 1; done`
- **P6.4** Given the checked-in snapshot, when the conformance audit runs before and after, then the gap registers have no new P0/P1 and the same ledger count. The fresh-snapshot audit is `CANNOT ASSESS` (read-only pod filesystem; no cluster change).
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot docs/design/data --out .audit/before --report && python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot docs/design/data --out .audit/after --report && python3 -c "import json;a=json.load(open('.audit/before/conformance-gap-register.json'));b=json.load(open('.audit/after/conformance-gap-register.json'));assert a==b"`.
- **P6.5** Given the 16 new files, when `docs/design/data/documents.json` is read, then every file is indexed once.
  Verify: `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('docs/design/docs/documents.json'));idx={x.get('source') for x in d.get('documents',[])};need={f'docs/plans/inception/{k}/{n}' for k in ('T5','T6','T12','T15','T17') for n in ('00-project-brief.md','01-inception-analysis.md','02-architecture-design.md')}|{'docs/plans/inception/README.md'};missing=need-idx;print(missing);raise SystemExit(1 if missing else 0)"`.

### P7 — Publish the five sets

- **P7.1** Given the 15 rows at v3 carrying the published metadata, when `documents.publish` runs with `publish: true` and `--if-match 3`, then each row reads `publishable = true`, `published_at` non-null, version 3.
  Verify: `documents.get` per id; assert the three fields and the file hash.
- **P7.2** Given the five projects, when their published categories are read, then `inception-analysis` and `architecture-design` are both present and `assert_inception_published` passes.
  Verify: `documents.list {project_id}` → the categories with `published_at` include the pair.

### P8 — The public window reads `published_at`

- **P8.1** Given a document with `publishable = true` and `published_at = null`, when the snapshot and the outputs index are generated, then it is absent, while a published document is present.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/snapshot_outputs.rs::only_published_outputs_are_public_and_rendered_safely` (CI, and the preflight workflow).
- **P8.2** Given the deterministic snapshot fixture publishes its live output, when the snapshot runs, then the document projection and the outputs index carry only published rows.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/snapshot_deterministic.rs` (CI, and the preflight workflow).

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #347 | prior unit; closed 2026-11-18 on `publishable`; this unit corrects the record | closed |
| related | #77, #80, #86, #88 | the five projects' delivery units; blocked; their target tranches are recorded, not authorised | open |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #87 | T17's live rows are shared with its claimed session; the repo files proceed, the row stops on a version move | open |
| related | #524, #526 | the strict-gates and tranche-0 rework lanes; not touched | open |

No `blocked-by`; no `Blocker:` line.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/standard/code reference resolves at `main@70d31773`; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has at least one scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `blocked-by`, so `status:ready`.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from the open lanes; T17's issue and branch untouched.
- [x] Scope corrections: none of the legacy corrections apply (no old-system freeze, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Docs gate green at the exact head: `build-docs.py`, `check-docs.cjs`, `check-data.cjs`, `build-coverage.py --check`, `check-programme-definition.py`, `no-private-refs.sh`.
- [ ] No test is added or skipped; no migration and no Rust build.
- [ ] Docs updated and the generated pack committed.
- [ ] Live verification recorded: 15 read-backs, the live predicate, the audit diff.
- [ ] #77, #80, #86, #87, #88 untouched.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

Tranche authorisation; `statement-of-architecture-work` (T9-only); #524/#525/#526; T17's issue/branch/status; the assessment lane; Wave 2 and the other seven #347 projects. Publication and the snapshot/outputs filter fix are in scope and delivered in this unit.

## Deployment prerequisite

No. The engine is deployed; the live writes are verification, not a deployment gate.

## Open questions

| 2 | If T17's claimed session moves a row, does the unit wait or exclude it? | owner | Stop that row, finish the other four, report |

<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->

## Goal

The seven tranche-0 projects (P0, PLATFORM, DESIGN-PUBLISH, SPEC-V2, S00, S01, T0) are reworked by the
reconstituted lifecycle — reopened where closed, chartered, put under a contract, given A–D artefacts, a
baseline and a green acceptance manifest, reviewed at Phase G and re-closed through #524's gate — and the
verifier that proves it (`scripts/verify-project.py` + `acceptance/programme/<KEY>.toml`) exists and is
re-runnable.

## Scope change — 2026-11-21 (owner directive)

The owner directed that the rework is one continuous exercise: if a project still has a point, its
missing artefacts are provided retroactively and the project is reworked from start to finish by the
book; the work uses the **fewest PRs possible on one branch**, and the PR is **merged only when the
whole programme is correct and fully implemented**. The owner also requires **MSP, TOGAF *and* SAFe**
to be applied, with their necessary artefacts.

#526 is therefore the programme rework unit. It carries U5a (below), the remaining tranches (U5b–U5h),
the SAFe cadence (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 — currently the least implemented standard: no rules, no
output categories, no demo/lesson actions), benefit measurement (U6) and the viability gate plus
republish (U7). Slice issues are not created; the batches are parts of this issue, and each batch ends
with its tranche review and the authorisation of the next tranche. This is a recorded scope change, not
a silent widening.

## Scope change — 2026-11-27 (owner directive)

The owner directed that this lane lands now, superseding the 2026-11-21 instruction that the PR wait
until the whole programme is complete. #526 lands **tranches 0–5 reworked and green, plus the
tranche-6 governance** (cadences, refinement WSJF, PI plan/objectives, S06a retirement decision). The
tranche-6 member packs (S06b, S06a receipt, S10, S11, T19F), the tranche-6 exit and review, and the
remaining tranches (7–13), benefits (U6) and the viability gate (U7) continue in **#838** and its
successors. The one-PR-per-unit rule still holds; the unit boundary moved, recorded here.

## Plan / audit source

The adopted rework plan (2026-11-21), U5a row. Its instrument and enablers are in the repository:
`governance/conformance.json`, `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py`,
`docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json`, `scripts/programme-record.py` (U1–U3: #504, #510, #519; U4: #524).
The standards it applies are `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (TOGAF ADM), §8.2 (SAFe cadence), §8.3 (MSP) and §12,
`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §§3–8, and `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract".

## Current state (measured)

| P1b harness + reviews read path | DONE on branch | full lifecycle read-back map (self-test 11/11), `architecture.reviews_get`, `actions.json` and `served-spec.lock.json` regenerated — deploy-bound probe |
| P1c snapshot fields | ABSENT | `crates/store/src/snapshot.rs` contracts select omits `requested_by`; compliance_reviews omits `evidence` |
| P1 verifier + manifests | DONE on branch | `scripts/verify-project.py` + seven `acceptance/programme/<KEY>.toml` |
| P2 P0 | PARTIAL — 7/9 | reopened, chartered, scope baseline approved, SoAW, seven A–D artefacts, delivery contract, Phase-G review, closure output; the two failing checks are P1c's snapshot fields |
| P3 PLATFORM | DONE | standing row: charter and approved baseline; manifest 3/3; no closure attempted |
| P4 DESIGN-PUBLISH | PARTIAL | closed; 1 P0 `closed_without_closure_review` + 1 P1 `unpublished_declared_output` |
| P5 SPEC-V2 | PARTIAL | closed; 2 P1 `closed_without_closure_review`, `closure_outputs_undeclared` |
| P6 S00 | PARTIAL | closed; 3 P1 `closed_without_closure_review`, `closure_outputs_undeclared`, `mandatory_artefacts` |
| P7 S01 | PARTIAL | closed; 3 P1 `closed_without_closure_review`, `closure_outputs_undeclared`, `mandatory_artefacts` |
| P8 T0 | PARTIAL | closed; 1 P1 `mandatory_artefacts` |
| P9 batch audit + ledger shrink | OPEN | no `docs/evidence/rework/` yet; the batch's 12 entries are still in the v3 ledger |
| P10 SAFe cadence | ABSENT | 0 SAFe rules, 0 SAFe output categories, no demo/lesson actions (`credit_demo_tx`/`propose_lesson_tx` exist with store tests but no action), no live cadence/WBS/demo/lesson rows |
| P11 remaining tranches | ABSENT | U5b–U5h: 41 projects across tranches 1–13 |
| P12 benefits (U6) | ABSENT | 6 profiles, 0 transitions; 6 placeholder baselines |
| P13 viability + republish (U7) | ABSENT | the pack is the frozen `a33e656`; no viability assertion reads the live register |

Ledger total for the batch: **12 entries — 1 P0 + 11 P1** (subjects P0, DESIGN-PUBLISH, SPEC-V2, S00,
S01, T0; PLATFORM carries none). The committed ledger is **v3, 146 P0/P1 — 27 P0 / 119 P1**, accepted
2026-11-21T11:08Z under the standing delegation and strict-green. P9 deletes this batch's twelve entries
as it fixes them; the new SAFe rules will add honest entries, which the batches burn down and U7
requires at zero unwaived.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1a — the ledger bootstrap (before any project record)

- Given the committed ledger is the 153-entry pre-U4 derivation and strict publish is on, when the unit
  takes an out-of-band fresh snapshot in a retained directory and runs the auditor with `--report`, then
  it produces the ledger and register there, the acceptance is recorded as a delegated decision under P0,
  the ledger header carries the acceptance, the twelve orphaned P1s are deleted and the five new P0s are
  accepted with owner/expiry, and the commit precedes any `publish-data.sh` run.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot <retained> --strict --fail-on P0,P1 --baseline docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json`; `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --check` on the acceptance document; `publish-data.sh` strict passes after the commit and would have failed before it.

### P1 — the verifier and the manifests

- Given no verifier exists, when `scripts/verify-project.py` is added, then it reads
  `acceptance/programme/<KEY>.toml`, runs each clause's `Verify:` command, writes
  `docs/evidence/rework/<KEY>.json` (SHA, command, exit, captured result), and carries the negative
  checks — no placeholder baseline, `closure_outputs` non-empty and published, contract `approval_id`
  non-null and requester ≠ approver, closure gate approved by a distinct actor, `delegation_ref` present
  and resolvable, zero invalid waivers, and no closure on a red manifest.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --self-test` (to create)
- Given a clause fails, when the verifier runs for that project, then the result is red and the project
  cannot close.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project <KEY>` exits non-zero (to create)

### P1b — the record harness and the reviews read path

- Given the lifecycle writes `projects.close`, `projects.baseline`, `architecture.contracts_request|approve`,
  `architecture.artifacts_create|approve`, `architecture.reviews_record`, `documents.create|update` and
  `pm.plan`, when `scripts/programme-record.py` runs each write, then it resolves a row-specific read-back
  (with the read input the write input does not supply) and the self-test covers every mapping.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --self-test` (to extend)
- Given `architecture.reviews_record` has no read action, when the unit adds `architecture.reviews_get`,
  then a written Phase-G review reads back with `reviewed_by`, `evidence.delegation_ref` and the manifest
  result, and the action is registered.
  **Verify:** `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry` (CI preflight); a live probe at the deployed image returns the review by id.

### P1c — the public record carries the requester and the delegation

- Given the snapshot's `contracts` projection omits `requested_by` and `compliance_reviews` omits
  `evidence`, when the projection is extended, then a fresh snapshot carries each contract's requester and
  each review's delegation and manifest fields, and the conformance audit can test requester ≠ approver.
  **Verify:** `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test snapshot_conformance` (CI preflight); a fresh-snapshot check shows the new fields.

### P2 — P0

- Given P0's 1 P1 entry, when the lifecycle re-runs, then its Statement of Architecture Work, A–D set,
  contract, manifest and Phase-G review exist, U3's charter and baseline are verified rather than
  duplicated, and the entry is gone.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project P0`; `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --strict --fail-on P0,P1` on a fresh snapshot shows no P0/P1 entry for P0.

### P3 — PLATFORM

- Given the standing row has no charter or baseline, when the unit runs, then `projects.charter` and
  `projects.baseline` exist and read back, and no closure is attempted.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --check` on both rows; `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project PLATFORM`.

### P4 — DESIGN-PUBLISH

- Given the P0 `closed_without_closure_review` and the P1 `unpublished_declared_output`, when the project
  is reopened, reworked and re-closed through #524's gate, then both entries are gone and the closure
  review and the declared output are published.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project DESIGN-PUBLISH`; the strict audit above.

### P5 — SPEC-V2

- Given its 2 P1 entries, when the lifecycle re-runs, then the closure review exists and the declared
  outputs are published; both entries are gone.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project SPEC-V2`; the strict audit.

### P6 — S00

- Given its 3 P1 entries, when the lifecycle re-runs, then the A–D artefacts exist, the closure review
  exists and the declared outputs are published; all three entries are gone.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project S00`; the strict audit.

### P7 — S01

- Given its 3 P1 entries and a decision project whose subject no longer exists, when it is reopened and
  reworked, then the decision record carries the measured numbers still observable, anything unrecoverable
  is marked `not recoverable`, and the project closes with that record; all three entries are gone.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project S01`; the strict audit.

### P8 — T0

- Given its 1 P1 `mandatory_artefacts` entry, when the lifecycle re-runs, then the A–D set exists and is
  approved; the entry is gone.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project T0`; the strict audit.

### P9 — the batch audit and the ledger shrink

- Given the seven projects, when the fresh-snapshot strict audit runs, then zero P0/P1 entries remain for
  the batch and the 12 entries are deleted from the ledger, not re-dated.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --strict --fail-on P0,P1` on a fresh temp
  snapshot; `git diff -- docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` shows 12 deletions and no re-dating.

### P10 — the SAFe cadence, made operable and enforced

- Given `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 adopts SAFe as the programme cadence, when the unit runs, then the product
  exposes demo credits and lessons (`cadences.credit_demo`, `cadences.credit_list`, `lessons.propose`,
  `lessons.list` over the existing `credit_demo_tx`/`propose_lesson_tx`), the snapshot projects
  `demo_credits` and `lessons`, and the conformance standard carries SAFe rules
  (`pi_cadence_missing`, `pi_plan_missing`, `pi_objectives_missing`, `demo_credit_missing`,
  `retro_lesson_missing`, `wsjf_inputs_missing`, `backlog_refinement_missing`).
  **Verify:** the action/registry tests via the GitHub preflight; `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --self-test`;
  `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test`.
- Given each PI (= tranche), when its batch closes it, then a `pi` cadence row, published `pi-plan` and
  `pi-objectives` outputs, WBS deliverables carrying the four WSJF integers, a `demo` cadence with one
  credit per accepted deliverable carrying its evidence, a `retro` cadence with one lesson per finding,
  and a `refinement` row exist and read back.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --check` on each row; the strict audit shows no SAFe
  rule for that tranche; `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project <KEY>` includes the project's PI
  objective and demo credit.
- Given `governance/standards-coverage.json`, when the auditor self-test runs, then every mandatory clause
  of TOGAF §8.1, SAFe §8.2 and MSP §8.3 maps to at least one rule, output category, live row type and
  verifier check, and no rule is orphaned.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test`.

### P11 — the remaining tranches (U5b–U5h), by the book

- Given each project in the batch table, when its tranche is reworked, then it runs the full lifecycle
  (reopen where closed → charter → SoAW → A–D → contract → PI/WBS + acceptance → Phase-G → baseline →
  closure request → distinct-actor decision → close), its manifest is green at a named SHA, and its
  ledger entries are deleted, not re-dated.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --all`; the strict audit on a fresh snapshot shows no
  P0/P1 for the batch; `git diff -- docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` shows deletions only.
- Given each batch's tranche review, when the rework evidence is presented, then the review records
  continue/pause/stop, its retro produces lessons, and a `continue` authorises the next tranche.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --check` on the review and the authorisation;
  `tranches.list` shows the next tranche authorised.

| Batch | Tranches | Projects |
|---|---|---|
| U5b | 1 | S02, T1, T11 |
| U5c | 2–3 | S03, T2, S04, T13, T3 |
| U5d | 4 | S05, S07, S09, T10, T14, T4, T9, T16 |
| U5e | 5–6 | S08, S06, S17, T17, T7, S06a (fold), S06b, S10, S11 |
| U5f | 7–8 | S06c, S16, S15, S06d, S13, S19 |
| U5g | 9–11 | S18, S20, S21, S12, S14, T5, T6, T8 |
| U5h | 12–13 | T15, T12 |

Demotion to `close by decision` follows the stated policy only (no live surface, no open issue, no
unpublished declared output). S06a is the one fold; S14 is rework (#29 joins it, never duplicated);
#395 is executed; #17's CI archetype is untouched.

### P12 — benefit measurement (U6)

- Given the six benefit profiles, when U6 runs, then every profile's six field groups are complete, no
  placeholder remains, each benefit has a baseline measured before its transition and a post-transition
  measurement with attribution and evidence; a baseline that cannot be observed is recorded
  `baseline_status: unavailable` (never claimed `realized`); one full transition is exercised end to end.
  **Verify:** `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --strict --fail-on P0,P1`; the profiles and
  transitions read back through `benefits.get` / `benefits.transition_list`.
- Given the owner's KPI, when U6 runs, then **token spend per accepted deliverable** is defined with a
  comparison basis and target, baselined before the T5/T6 improvement transition and measured after, from
  the inference ledger and accepted outputs.
  **Verify:** the KPI's baseline and post rows read back with their evidence; a measured delta is recorded.

### P13 — the viability gate and the republish (U7)

- Given the whole programme, when U7 runs, then "viable" holds all at once: zero unwaived P0/P1; every
  project has a verdict and every `rework` project a Phase-G review with a green manifest at the published
  SHA; every delivery project an approved SoAW and delivery contract (requester ≠ approver, delegation
  cited); every closed project its declared outputs published and an approved closure review; every PI its
  cadence, plan, objectives, demo credits and lessons; one benefit measured before and after with an
  attributable delta including token spend; and the public pack republished from live rows, so the
  programme table derives from records, not seed claims.
  **Verify:** the T12 acceptance extension (#88); `publish-data.sh` strict with the branch binary; the
  republished snapshot matches the live rows; the viability assertion exits 0.

## Goal

After this lands, a project cannot close, a tranche cannot be reviewed or continued, and a contract, review or waiver cannot be approved except through one gated path that requires the missing prerequisite, a distinct approver and a cited standing delegation; publication is strict against a re-derived burn-down ledger, so a new or worsened conformance gap stops the publish.

## Plan / audit source

The owner's approved retrospective rework plan, U4 · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (ADM gates and compliance) and §8.3 (MSP tranche review, closure, benefits) · `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §§6–8 · `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract" · the U3 evidence comment in #511 · the gap register and ledger that landed with #501/#511.

## Programme

| Tranche | `0` — corrective assurance and the gate instrument; no delivery project starts under it |
| Brief | `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §8 (P0 acceptance) |
| ADM phase/plateau | `Preliminary` / `PSA` — the governance write path and gate; no architecture change of its own |
| Benefits | `B6` — Predictable delivery (`seed/programme-definition.json`) |

## Claim

- Docs: `SPEC_V2.md` blob `c86d8f2a` · `P0-programme-definition.md` blob `91b744d9` · `03-DELIVERY.md` blob `65e4b5bf` · `governance/conformance.json` blob `e5f11573` · `docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` blob `6c3c3303` · `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` blob `8ac49005`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 one close gate | ABSENT | `board/projects.rs:projects_close` calls only `programme::assert_closure_outputs_published`; `pm/mod.rs:pm_close` checks an approved `closure` gate and never the published outputs. Neither checks the tranche, charter, baseline, design gate or Phase-G. |
| P2 request → decision → close | ABSENT | `pm/mod.rs:pm_close` calls `approve_asset(..., ctx.actor_id)` on the closure asset it just wrote; the asset's author approves it. |
| P3 tranche review gate | PARTIAL | `store/src/spine.rs:review_tranche_tx` requires evidence and authorises the next tranche on `continue`; it does not check the reviewed tranche's state, refuse a second review, or refuse a `continue` with no planned next tranche. `spine/mod.rs:tranches_review` writes `reviewed_by = ctx.actor_id`. |
| P4 dual control + delegation | PARTIAL | `store/src/approval.rs:record_decision_tx` refuses requester = approver; `architecture.rs:architecture_contracts_approve` refuses requester = approver. `architecture_reviews_record`, `architecture_reviews_waive` and `tranches_review` have no distinct approver and no `delegation_ref`; no action input carries a delegation field. |

U3's live acts in #511 already close at least `tranche_review_without_authorisation` (1), `programme_baselines` (3), `board_not_approved` (1) and tranche-1 entries, so strict mode reports "ledger grew" until it is re-derived. |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — one close gate
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (Phase G) · §8.3 (project closure) · `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §§6–8.
Requirement: every writer that reaches `closed` calls one gate that requires the project's tranche, its declared closure outputs, its approved closure decision, and for a delivery project its charter, baseline, design gate and Phase-G review (or a valid waiver).

- **P1.1** Given a project whose tranche is `planned`, when either close path runs, then it answers `409` naming the tranche and writes no status change.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/closure_gate.rs::close_refuses_an_unauthorised_tranche` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given an approved `closure` gate decided by the closure asset's author or by the actor requesting the close, when close runs, then it refuses and writes nothing.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/closure_gate.rs::close_refuses_a_self_approved_closure` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a delivery project with no live, board-approved delivery contract or no Phase-G compliance review, when close runs, then it refuses; with an active waiver for a non-conformant review, then it passes.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_close.rs::close_refuses_without_a_contract` and `::close_refuses_a_pending_closure` (to create), plus the full path in `::a_programme_project_closes_through_the_one_gate`.
- **P1.4** Given every prerequisite met, when close runs, then the project reads `closed` and the closure row exists.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_close.rs::a_programme_project_closes_through_the_one_gate` (to create); the existing `closure_gate.rs` non-programme tests stay green.
- **P1.5** Given `projects.close` or `pm.close`, when either runs, then both pass the same gate; the programme's request is `projects.close_request`, not a status edit.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_close.rs::close_request_refuses_a_standalone_project` and the full path above.

### P2 — request → decision → close
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 Phase G · §8.3 closure.
Requirement: the closure is written as a draft, decided by a different actor, and only then closed; the author never approves their own closure asset.

- **P2.1** Given `projects.close_request`, when it runs, then the closure asset is `draft`, no project status changes, and a `closure` gate naming `closure_asset_id` and the acceptance manifest is open. `projects.close` and `pm.close` then pass the one gate.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_close.rs::close_refuses_without_a_closure_gate` and `::close_refuses_a_pending_closure` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given the closure gate, when its requester decides it, then the decision is refused and no decision row is written.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/approval_standalone.rs::a_second_principal_decides_a_gate_the_first_requested` (exists); `crates/actions/tests/closure_gate.rs::closure_gate_refuses_the_requester` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a distinct approver decides the closure gate, then the closure asset is approved by that approver, not by its author.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/closure_gate.rs::closure_asset_is_approved_by_the_decider` (to create)
- **P2.4** Given a draft closure asset, when any close path runs, then it refuses.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/closure_gate.rs::close_refuses_a_draft_closure_asset` (to create)

### P3 — the tranche review is a gate
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 · `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs`.
Requirement: a review is possible only on a reviewable tranche, once per close, and a `continue` requires a planned next tranche it can authorise.

- **P3.1** Given a `planned` tranche, when a review runs, then it refuses and writes no review row.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::review_refuses_a_planned_tranche` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given an authorised tranche already reviewed, when a second review runs, then it refuses.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::review_refuses_a_second_review` (to create)
- **P3.3** Given a `continue` with no next tranche or a next tranche not `planned`, then it refuses and writes no row.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::continue_refuses_a_missing_next_tranche` and `::continue_refuses_a_next_tranche_not_planned` (to create)
- **P3.4** Given `pause` or `stop`, when no next tranche exists, then the review is recorded.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::pause_and_stop_do_not_need_a_next_tranche` (to create)
- **P3.5** Given a conformant `continue`, then the next tranche reads `authorised` with the review id (the existing behaviour stays).
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_review_records_continue_pause_or_stop` (exists)

### P4 — dual control and the delegation citation
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1/§8.3 · `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract".
Requirement: `tranches.review`, `architecture.contracts_approve`, `architecture.reviews_record`, `architecture.reviews_waive` and the `pm.close` closure gate carry a resolvable `delegation_ref` (the published P0 standing-delegation decision output), and the deciding/reviewing actor is distinct from the requester/executor.

- **P4.1** Given a delegated act with no `delegation_ref`, then it refuses `422` and writes no row.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/delegation.rs::delegated_acts_require_a_delegation_ref` (to create at path)
- **P4.2** Given a `delegation_ref` that is unknown, unpublished or not under P0, then it refuses and names the ref.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/delegation.rs::delegation_ref_must_resolve_to_the_published_p0_output` (to create)
- **P4.3** Given the reviewer/approver is the requester/executor, then it refuses; given a distinct delegate, then the row records both the delegation and the distinct actor.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/delegation.rs::delegated_acts_are_dual_controlled` (to create); `crates/actions/tests/approval_standalone.rs::a_second_principal_decides_a_gate_the_first_requested` (exists)
- **P4.4** Given a gate whose policy requires `kind='human'`, when a non-human actor attempts it, then it refuses; the delegated act records the actual decider kind, never a fabricated human.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/approval_race.rs` / the existing human-only gate test (exists); `crates/actions/tests/delegation.rs::a_human_only_gate_refuses_the_delegate` (to create)

### P5 — ledger v3 and strict publish
`governance/conformance.json` · `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` · `docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh`.
Requirement: the ledger is re-derived from the live post-U3 snapshot, accepted with disposition/owner/expiry, and publication fails on a new, worsened, expired or vanished entry.

- **P5.1** Given a fresh post-U3 snapshot, when the audit runs in report mode, then the regenerated ledger deletes the entries U3 fixed and keeps the rest with the same discipline.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot <fresh> --report --out <tmp>`; `git diff --exit-code docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` after the acceptance write (deployment-gated).
- **P5.2** Given ledger v3, when strict runs on the fresh snapshot, then there are zero failures.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot <fresh> --strict --fail-on P0,P1 --baseline docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` (deployment-gated).
- **P5.3** Given a new closure gap not in the ledger, when a dry-run publish runs, then it fails and names the project.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` case `closed_status_unconformant` (to create); a dry-run publish with a seeded gap (deployment-gated).
- **P5.4** Given `CONFORMANCE_STRICT` unset, when `publish-data.sh` runs, then strict is the default.
  Verify: `bash -n docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh`; the self-test/CI assertion that the default is `1`.

## Design corrections found while implementing

The first tranche starts `planned`; its review is what closes it and authorises the next one, so the review guard refuses only `closed | retired` and the one-review check catches duplicates. `pm.close` cannot be the programme's request (it requires a PM binding), so `projects.close_request` writes the draft asset and gate; `pm.close` remains the PM-bound closer and passes the same gate. The PM's `design` gate is PM-binding-only; the board-approved live delivery contract is the design authority at programme level, so the close gate checks that contract plus its Phase-G review.

- [x] Baseline named; doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies complete and typed; no open `blocked-by`, so `status:ready`.

- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head; no local compiling `cargo` (preflight for the Rust verdict, PR CI final).
- [ ] Every refusal has a test that asserts no row was written; the conformant paths stay green.
- [ ] The auditor self-test covers the derived-status case; ledger v3 is committed with its acceptance record.
- [ ] `publish-data.sh` is strict by default; a dry-run publish with a seeded new gap fails and names the project.
- [ ] After deploy, the live negative probes pass; the fresh-snapshot strict audit is green.

## Out of scope

- The per-project retrospective rework and its acceptance manifests (U5a–U5h).
- Benefit measurement, including token spend per accepted deliverable (U6).
- The viability gate and the public republish (U7).
- Any SQL backfill or seed write that sets state or timestamps; records go through actions.

## Goal

The conformance standard is corrected to the profile it claims to apply, a record harness can write and read back live governance rows, the product gains the five capabilities the retro proved missing (a programme-baseline writer, a charter writer for an existing project, a reopen path, an operator actor selector so a delegate can act as itself, and an `--if-match` selector for the version-guarded writes), and the programme's authority record is repaired under the owner's recorded delegation: tranche 1 authorised from the existing review, the board active, the programme baselines recorded, the out-of-sequence closures accepted as exceptions, and baseline v2 accepted as a burn-down ledger.

## Plan / audit source

The owner's approved retrospective rework plan, U3 · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (Preliminary vs per-project sets) and §8.3 (tranche authorisation, programme baselines) · `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §§6–8 · the gap register that landed with #501 (`docs/evidence/conformance-gap-register.{json,md}`) · the U2 write path (#508).

| Benefits | `B6` — the seed, coverage and published checklist agree at every tranche review |

## Claim

## Baseline

The register's snapshot is `a33e656`; a fresh snapshot is taken at the acts and the register regenerated.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A1 Preliminary requirements are per project | ABSENT | `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py` unions every phase's requirements up to the project's phase; all 48 projects receive the Preliminary capability set (48 × 3 spurious) |
| A2 Artefact severity by adoption date | ABSENT | the same file: `P2` before adoption and `P1` after, regardless of whether the capability is live |
| A3 Empty closure-output declaration | ABSENT | all 26 S-track projects declare zero closure outputs, so `closed_without_closure_review` passes vacuously for 13 closed projects |
| A4 #435's stated derivation | ABSENT | #435 names `scripts/programme_state.py`, which does not exist; the generator is `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` |
| B1 record harness | ABSENT | no helper writes programme/architecture actions; the only live path is the admin CLI in `scripts/ops-live-proof.sh` |
| D tranche 1 authorisation | ABSENT | live `tranches.list`: tranche 0 `closed`, tranche 1 `planned`; review `01a1ed84-e111-7082-9fa8-7fe77ccc9024` says `continue` |
| D board | ABSENT | live `architecture.board_get`: `conveyor-architecture-board` is `draft` |
| D programme baselines | ABSENT | `msp.json`: 0 programme baselines, 0 register items, 0 project baselines |
| D exceptions | ABSENT | 19 closed projects in tranches 1–8 are recorded in the gap register, not in a governance record |
| C programme-baseline writer | ABSENT | `programme_baseline` has no action; `baselines.take` is project-only and a test fixture is the only inserter |
| C charter-on-existing | ABSENT | `pm.charter` inserts a new project; no action writes a charter for an existing one |
| C reopen | ABSENT | `projects.activate` excludes `closed`; `pm.close` requires an open project |
| C actor selection | ABSENT | `conveyor admin action invoke` always acts as the tenant's first active member; there is no `--actor-id` |
| C precondition | ABSENT | the admin CLI passes `precondition: None`; version-guarded actions (`projects.programme_meta`, `documents.publish`) answer 412 on every write |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### A — the standard corrected
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1.
Requirement: the auditor checks what the adopted profile requires — capability artefacts once, per-project sets from A — and its severity follows the disposition, not the project's age.

- **A.1** Given a conformant capability and 48 delivery projects, when the audit runs, then the Preliminary set is checked once and no project is required to own it.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` (a fixture with the capability set and projects without it yields zero `mandatory_artefacts`).
- **A.2** Given a live project closed before adoption, when its mandatory set is missing, then the gap is `P1`; given a `close-by-decision` project, then the rule does not apply.
  Verify: the self-test's pass/fail fixtures for `mandatory_artefacts`.
- **A.3** Given a closed project with `closure_outputs: []`, when the audit runs, then `closure_outputs_undeclared` is `P1`.
  Verify: the self-test fixture; the regenerated register lists the affected projects.
- **A.4** Given #435's body, when the derivation is read, then the named script exists (`scripts/programme_state.py`, added in `7c76377a`); a redacted issue-registry body is recorded `unprovable` as P2, never as a missing-script gap. `derivation_missing` is zero at P0/P1.
  Verify: `test -f scripts/programme_state.py`; `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --report` → `derivation_missing` only as P2/`unprovable` with the redaction reason.
- **A.5** Given the golden snapshot, when the audit runs twice, then the outputs are byte-identical and every rule has a pass and a fail fixture.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` and `--snapshot <golden> --report` twice, `cmp` the files.
- **A.6** Given baseline v2, when an entry expires or a new fingerprint appears, then strict mode fails with the entry named; the ledger never grows.
  Verify: a self-test case for an expired entry and for a new gap id.

### B — the record harness
`scripts/ops-live-proof.sh` (the admin-CLI write path).
Requirement: a session can perform and verify one governance write without hand-built SSH, and cannot claim a write it did not read back.

- **B.1** Given an action, input and evidence path, when `programme-record.py` runs without `--dry-run`, then it invokes the action, reads the row back and prints both; when the evidence path is absent, it refuses before invoking.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --action tranches.list --input '{"programme_id":"01a1d039-0d24-7d16-ae52-4841e96ccfac"}' --check` → the live rows.
- **B.2** Given `--dry-run` on a write action, then no write occurs and the planned call is printed.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/programme-record.py --action tranches.authorise --input '{"review_id":"…"}' --dry-run` → no state change on a read-back.

### C — the rework path (product enablers)
`crates/actions/src/portfolio/programmes.rs`, `crates/actions/src/board/projects.rs`, `crates/actions/src/pm/mod.rs`, `crates/store/src/portfolio.rs`.
Requirement: the product can record the programme baselines and can re-run an existing project's lifecycle. These are the gaps the retro found; without them D.5, D.6 and every U5 batch are impossible.

- **C.1** Given the three MSP kinds, when `programmes.baseline` takes a baseline, then the row reads `taken_by` and a frozen snapshot; a non-MSP kind is refused. Given a second actor, when `programmes.baseline_approve` runs, then `approved_by` is set; the taker approving its own baseline is refused, and a second approval is refused.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_baseline.rs` and `crates/store/tests/programme_baseline.rs`; after deploy, a live take + a refused self-approval.
- **C.2** Given an existing project with no approved charter, when `projects.charter` runs, then the charter asset and gate exist on that project and `projects.baseline` accepts it; a second charter is refused.
  Verify: the action test; after deploy, `projects.charter` on an existing project then an approved gate.
- **C.3** Given a closed project, when `projects.reopen` runs with the rework verdict cited, then it reads `active`; archived and non-closed projects are refused, and the old closure asset remains.
  Verify: the action test; after deploy, a live reopen of one closed project.
- **C.4** Given a project, when its verdict is written through `projects.programme_meta`, then `meta.viability` reads `rework|fold` with its evidence; an unknown meta key is still refused.
  Verify: the action test; a read-back of all 48 verdicts.
- **C.5** Given the tenant has distinct members, when `conveyor admin action invoke --actor-id <uuid>` runs, then the write is attributed to that member; a user with no active membership is refused. The harness uses it to act as the executor and as the delegate.
  Verify: an admin test for member/non-member; after deploy, a write as `conveyor-approver` reads back that actor id.
- **C.6** Given a version-guarded action, when the operator invokes it with `--if-match <version>`, then the call is made against that version; a stale version is refused 412. The harness passes the version on the write and never on the read-back.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/admin_actor.rs` (current version writes, stale refused); `programme-record.py --self-test` case `if-match is passed to the write only`.

### D — the delegated acts
The owner's instruction of 2026-11-20 (this programme's standing delegation) · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3.
Requirement: the authority record is repaired with dated, delegated acts that link the evidence actually available; history is not rewritten.

- **D.1** Given the owner's delegation, when the act is recorded, then the decision output names the delegate identity, its scope and the date, and every later act cites it.
  Verify: `programme-record.py --check` on the delegation output; the acts' evidence names it.
- **D.2** Given the rework mandate and the triage, when they are recorded, then every project carries a verdict (`rework | fold`) with its evidence: 47 rework (42 backfill-and-verify, 5 inception), 1 fold (S06a — superseded by S06b), 0 close-by-decision. S01 (the decision record with the measured numbers that remain observable) and S14 (the release receipt and acceptance harness) are rework; a project with a live surface or an open issue is never closed by decision.
  Verify: the triage output read back; `meta.viability` resolves for all 48 projects through `projects.programme_meta`.
- **D.3** Given review `01a1ed84-e111-7082-9fa8-7fe77ccc9024` (`continue` on tranche 0), when `tranches.authorise` runs, then tranche 1 reads `authorised` with that review id.
  Verify: `tranches.list` → tranche 1 `authorised`, `authorisation_review_id` = the review.
- **D.4** Given the board `01a1f2c0-b22a-7e27-a6cc-1a8e48db327e`, when `architecture.board_decide` records an approved decision about the board, then it reads `active`; the Preliminary artefact set is approved under the same act.
  Verify: `architecture.board_get` → `active`; `architecture.artifacts_list` → the three Preliminary artefacts `approved`.
- **D.5** Given the programme, when the three programme baselines and the register items are recorded, then `baselines.list`/the MSP read shows management, governance and boundary.
  Verify: `baselines.list` → the three kinds; a read-back of the register items.
- **D.6** Given the 19 out-of-sequence closures, when the exception record is written, then each names the project, tranche, date, benefit impact and the control that prevents recurrence; no project is moved between tranches.
  Verify: the exception output read back; `project_in_unauthorised_tranche` remains until each project's rework batch, never "fixed" by moving rows.
- **D.7** Given baseline v2, when accepted, then each entry carries a disposition, owner and expiry, and the forward plan (tranches 9–13) is re-baselined through change control.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` read back; strict mode passes with the ledger; the plan output read back.

## Dependencies

| blocked-by | #508 | merged in PR #510 (`044f1093`); the issue is closed | closed |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #508's deployment | deployed: image `a8ea1f2f` rolled out; `tranches.authorise`, `projects.programme_meta` and `projects.activate` verified live | done |
| related | #502, #503 | merged in #505; their gates/seed data are inputs | closed |

| related | #395 | the contract-per-project work the rework batches execute | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies complete and typed; one `blocked-by` (#508).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head; no local compiling `cargo`.

`benefits.update` accepting `realized` is **not** this unit — it is #502.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### A — project status and programme-owned metadata
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 (a project starts inside an authorised tranche) · `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §7.
Requirement: status and programme-owned metadata change only through gated actions, never through a general edit. The programme's own write path is `projects.programme_meta` (`portfolio:write`); the console's class, tranche and plan edit uses it, and status moves to explicit Activate/Pause/Archive/Close controls.

- **A.1** Given a project with a `programme_id` created without a status, when `projects.create` runs, then the row is `draft`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::project_born_draft_in_a_programme` (to create)
- **A.2** Given any project, when `projects.update` supplies `status`, then it is refused `422 status_not_editable` and no column changes.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::update_refuses_status` (to create)
- **A.3** Given a project whose meta carries `tranche`, `adm_phase`, `plateau`, `expected_outputs`, `closure_outputs`, `depends_on`, `plan`, `plan_status` or `status_source`, when `projects.update` supplies any of them, then it is refused and every prior value is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::update_refuses_programme_meta` (to create)
- **A.4** Given a draft project, when `projects.activate` runs, then it becomes `active` only if its tranche is `authorised` or `closed`; otherwise `409 tranche_not_authorised` and nothing is written. A programme project with no tranche row at all is refused the same way (fail closed).
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::activate_requires_authorised_tranche` (to create)
- **A.5** Given an active project, `projects.pause` moves it to `paused`; given a closed project, `projects.archive` moves it to `archived`; neither state is reachable through `projects.update`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::pause_and_archive_are_gated` (to create)
- **A.6** Given a project and a programme-owned key, when `projects.programme_meta` runs under `portfolio:write`, then the key merges; a key the programme does not own is refused `422 meta_key_not_programme`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::programme_meta_is_the_programme_write_path` (to create)

### B — contract requester identity
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (a contract is a gate object; approval is a decision) · #395.
Requirement: a contract records who requested it, immutably, and that actor cannot approve it.

- **B.1** Given actor X requests a contract, when the row is read back, then `requested_by = X`; no later action changes it.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::contract_records_requester` (to create) + migration (to create)
- **B.2** Given a contract requested by X, when X calls `architecture.contracts_approve`, then `409 requester_is_approver` and no approval row is written.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::contract_cannot_self_approve` (to create)
- **B.3** Given a pre-existing contract with `requested_by` null, when it is approved without a board decision, then it is refused `409 requester_unknown`; with a board decision it approves, reads `requester_unknown: true`, and stores the decision's `approval_id`. The requester is never backfilled with a guess.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::legacy_contract_requester_flagged` (to create)

### C — tranche authorisation
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 (a review is an approval; the next tranche starts only when authorised).
Requirement: the authorisation is a live row linked to an existing `continue` review. The normal path already does this inside `tranches.review`; `tranches.authorise` is the **repair** path for a review that never produced it — it cannot manufacture a review, and it cannot authorise a tranche whose predecessor has no `continue` review. Placed in `crates/actions/src/spine/mod.rs` beside `tranches.review`: the module owns the tranche actions. The duplicate-PR intent is satisfied — this branch and #505 (merged) overlap only on `crates/store/src/spine.rs`, below the two-file threshold.

- **C.1** Given tranche N with an existing `continue` review and tranche N+1 `planned`, when `tranches.authorise` runs, then N+1 becomes `authorised` with `authorised_at` set and `authorisation_review_id` naming that review.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::tranche_authorise_links_review` (to create)
- **C.2** Given no review, an unknown review, or a decision other than `continue`, when `tranches.authorise` runs, then it is refused and nothing is written. The review itself determines the tranche it authorises, so there is no separate target to mismatch.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::tranche_authorise_refuses_absent_or_noncontinue` (to create)
- **C.3** Given an already-authorised tranche, a repeat call returns the same review link and writes no second row.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::tranche_authorise_is_idempotent` (to create)

### D — board decision record
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (the board's charter, authority and decisions are rows, not prose).
Requirement: `architecture.board_decide` writes a typed decision with its evidence, and the board's active state is derived from that decision.

- **D.1** Given an architecture board, when `board_decide` runs, then a decision row carries body, decision, evidence, actor and timestamp, and its id is returned.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::board_decision_is_a_row` (to create)
- **D.2** Given a decision `active`, the board reads `active`; with no such decision, a direct status write is refused.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::board_status_derives_from_decision` (to create)
- **D.3** Given a contract approval, the approving decision id is linked to the contract (`approval_id` non-null).
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::contract_approval_links_decision` (to create)

### E — standalone project baseline
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.4 (the PMP baseline) · `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §7.
Requirement: a programme actor can baseline a chartered project without a PM job binding; the charter gate and the baseline approval stay.

- **E.1** Given a project with an approved charter, when `projects.baseline` runs, then the WBS nodes and a `project_baseline` row are written and the baseline approval opens.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::baseline_without_pm_binding` (to create)
- **E.2** Given a project without an approved charter, when `projects.baseline` runs, then `409 charter_not_approved` and nothing is written.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/write_path.rs::baseline_requires_charter` (to create)
- **E.3** Given `pm.plan` with a PM job binding, its behaviour is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/plan_spine.rs` (existing pm.plan tests)

### F — regression
Requirement: each invariant above has a test that fails at `main@0a8a6e95` and passes at the PR head; the compile/lint verdict comes from preflight.

## Goal

An automated publish must commit only the files it generates. Today it also commits every hand-authored file of the **deployed image's** pack, so a publish PR silently reverts whatever main changed since that image was built.

## Measured 2026-11-20 (publish PR #475, job `01a1f7e0-17ca-7bb0-971e-8d3461931aa4`)

- `design-pack` fails at the data step: `coverage: ... is STALE`.
- A side-by-side build of the branch's pack vs the committed `coverage.json` shows **only line-number drift**: every `actions_invoked[*].line` is 9 lower than the committed value.
- The branch's `docs/design/v2.js` is the **deployed image's** copy (built at `d86c5e5b`), not main's (`81c2c2c5`, which carries #469's +6-line hook and other changes). The publish therefore reverts main's `v2.js`, and the committed coverage no longer matches the reverted file.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/server/src/publish.rs:154` — `collect_pack(&pack_root, &temp.0)` | main@81c2c2c5 |
| Code | `apps/server/src/publish.rs:383-402` — `collect_pack` walks the whole image pack and only excludes scripts/legacy/data, Markdown and output pages | main@81c2c2c5 |
| Code | `apps/server/src/publish.rs:336-352` — `GENERATED_DATA` and the deletion rule already define what a publish owns | main@81c2c2c5 |
| Check | `scripts/build-coverage.py:--check` — the data step that failed | main@81c2c2c5 |
| PR | #475 (a proof run; not a publication candidate) | open |
| Issue | #400 (the publish DoD) | open |

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — a publish commits only its generated files | **ABSENT** | `collect_pack` returns the image's `v2.js`, `studio.html`, docs and data, then overlays the temp; the branch's `v2.js` is 9 lines behind main and the coverage drifts |
| The generated set it should commit | **DONE** | `GENERATED_DATA` + the output pages + the temp data/docs; the deletion rule already excludes hand-authored files |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the publish's file set is the generated set

Given a repository whose main has moved since the deployed image was built, when a publish runs, then the commit touches only generated files: the snapshot data, the published output pages and the documents index. Hand-authored pack files (`v2.js`, `studio.html`, scripts, decisions, Markdown) are never in the diff, and a hand-authored file absent from the image is never deleted.

Verify: unit test — `collect_pack` over a temp dir returns exactly the temp's data/docs entries; a file present only in the pack root is absent. Then a live publish from the fixed worker: the PR's diff lists only `docs/design/data/*` and `docs/design/docs/*` generated files, and its `design-pack` data step is green.

## Measured

Full-suite nextest gate (rbuild, run `s1-20261120T072645Z-46482`, m1) on `origin/main@7ff187ff`:

```
FAIL conveyor-api::copilot_rounds a_turn_that_never_stops_calling_tools_is_refused_at_the_round_cap
panicked at crates/api/tests/copilot_rounds.rs:37:5:
the turn is recorded, not rejected: {"detail":"inference answered 502 (turn … recorded as failed)", "status":502, "type":"action-upstream-failed"}
```

1254/1255 passed; the binary aborted the run (fail-fast), so 2196 tests were not run. The same test passed alone in an earlier session and in CI; this is the second observation of this flake under full-suite load (first recorded 2026-11-19, observed not filed).

## Why it is a harness race, not the product

- The stub (`crates/api/tests/copilot/mod.rs::Model::start`) binds `127.0.0.1:0` and never answers 5xx.
- `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` maps ANY transport error from an external call to `upstream_failed(service, 502)` (line ~1368): the 502 is the conveyor failing to reach the stub, not the stub replying.
- Under nextest's process-per-test load the stub (same 2-thread runtime as the test) and/or a pooled keep-alive connection are starved/reset.

## Suggested fix (one unit)

Run the stub server on its own OS thread with its own runtime (or disable keep-alive on the test client), so CPU saturation cannot starve the accept/serve task; optionally retry the transport error once in the test client. Acceptance: the full suite passes 3 consecutive runs on m1 under load, and the test still fails when the round cap is removed (negative control).

Not filed as a `unit` because no issue contract was drafted; promote if it becomes work.
