## Goal

The Admin **Workers and Billing** tabs must render the conveyor's own data (the durable queue +
host registry; the ledger summary). It currently calls the local `workers.list` through the generic "external service"
panel, whose copy says an unconfigured service is an error — and `admin.spec.ts` still asserts the
removed external failure, so the dev suite is red on main.

## Measured 2026-11-20 (main@7ff187ff)

- `crates/actions/src/workers.rs:2,64` — `workers.list` is an **internal** action over
  `store::jobs::counts_tx` and the `host_registry`; the Python service it once named is legacy.
- `crates/actions/src/metrics/mod.rs:855` — `billing.summary` is an **internal** ledger read
  (200 with `{from,to,inference_calls,tool_calls,total_usd}`), also not the external Python service.
- `apps/web/src/screens/admin.rs:202` — `Tab::Workers => Ok(TabData::External(...))`, rendering the
  panel at `:471` whose copy says "This tab reads an external service… An unconfigured service is
  an error, not an empty list."
- `apps/web/e2e/admin.spec.ts:44-46` — clicks Workers and expects `.problem` containing
  `no base URL is configured`; the local action answers 200 with `{hosts:[], queue:[…]}`, so the
  test fails deterministically (11.4 s) and the full dev suite is 76/77.
- Main's last `web` run is green only because the workers.list change landed in a server path and
  the UI-path-filtered workflow did not run; this is the first suite to see it.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Action | `crates/actions/src/workers.rs:64` — internal `workers.list` | main@7ff187ff |
| Screen | `apps/web/src/screens/admin.rs:202,471` | main@7ff187ff |
| Spec | `apps/web/e2e/admin.spec.ts:15-46` | main@7ff187ff |

## Claim

| Session | `m4/finish-conveyor-leftovers (claim nonce 21D5DF19-2281-44DB-A7E0-94DD9168A6F6)` |
| Updated | `2026-11-20` |

## Part P1 — the tab is the local inventory

Given a tenant with queue rows, when the operator opens Admin → Workers, then the tab renders the
durable queue (kind, status, count) and an honest empty-host state; when they open Billing, then it

## Goal

The live programme stops lagging the repository. `seed/programme.json` is generated in the repo and compiled into the image, but the tenant's programme rows are only refreshed by an operator running `migrate --seed` in a pod after an image roll. Measured 2026-11-19: the live app shows **T11, T14 and T16 as `proposed`** while the repo's seed says `built`. This unit exposes the same seed application as an operator action and a control on the Programme page, so the app publishes its own programme truth without a pod step.

## Why this is a separate unit

#448 is the Procedures destination; this is the programme store and its console control. The change touches `crates/store` (the seed's shape), `crates/actions` (a new action), `docs/design/v2.js`, `check-console.cjs` and the generated action data — a different artefact and a different gate.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-19, origin/main `ddd02789`)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The seed is embedded and idempotent | YES | `crates/store/src/seed_programme.rs:36` `PROGRAMME_EXPORT = include_str!("../../../seed/programme.json")`; `seed_programme(pool, tenant)` at `:110`; the internals (`upsert_programme`, `upsert_project`, `ensure_project_board`, `board_lanes`) already take `&mut PgConnection` |
| An operator action exists | ABSENT | `git grep -n "programmes.refresh\|programme.refresh" -- crates/actions/src` → 0 hits |
| The page has a refresh control | ABSENT | `docs/design/v2.js` Programme tabs have no refresh action |
| The live programme lags | MEASURED | live `/design/data/snapshot.js` `programme.projects[].meta.measured_status`: T11/T14/T16 = `proposed`; `seed/programme.json` on main: `built` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the store exposes a connection-scoped seed application

- **P1** Given a tenant and a scoped transaction, when `seed_programme_tx` runs twice, then the first returns the created counts and the second returns every row skipped (no version bump, no `updated_at` change); `seed_programme(pool, tenant)` keeps its targets/transaction loop over it.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/seed_programme.rs` (a new case over the tx variant; created 49 / skipped 49 — the programme row plus 48 projects).

### P2 — the action

- **P2** Given a caller holding `portfolio:write` (the `programmes.*` family scope), when `programmes.refresh` is invoked, then it applies the image's embedded seed to the caller's tenant and returns `{created, updated, skipped, boards_created}`; a second call is all-skipped; another tenant's rows are untouched; a role without the scope is refused 403.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/programme_refresh.rs` (board fixture; the scope-refusal case uses a member role).

### P3 — the page publishes it

- **P3** Given a signed-in operator on the Programme page, when they click Refresh, then the page calls `programmes.refresh`, re-reads the programme and re-renders, and the toast names the counts; the control is hidden when `C.can("programmes.refresh")` is false and absent on the public snapshot.
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` (a new signed-in case asserting the wire and the counts; the snapshot case asserts the control is absent).

### P4 — the generated data stays current

- **P4** Given the new action, when the pack regenerates, then `docs/design/data/actions.json`, the served-spec lock, coverage and docs are current and every design-pack check is green.
  Verify: the actions dump, `--print-openapi --write-lock`, `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check`, `node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs --self-test`, `check-data.cjs`, `check-docs.cjs`, `build-docs.py --check`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #448 | both publish programme state from the console | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named; every path resolves at `ddd02789`.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] Dependencies typed; none blocks this unit.
- [x] One PR scope: `crates/store/src/seed_programme.rs`, `crates/actions/src/portfolio/programmes.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/programme_refresh.rs`, `docs/design/v2.js`, `check-console.cjs`, the generated action/coverage/docs data.

Requirement: the three dead seed manifests are gone, the inventory test classifies every External
service and its runtime, and every counted figure is regenerated.

- **P4.1** Given the External services in the registry, when the inventory test runs, then each
  one has a classification row naming its runtime and the date it was read; an unclassified
  service fails the test.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions external_inventory::`

### P5 — live proof on the deployed image (deployment-gated)

  200 with no `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_*` URL set for its old service.

actions are registered after the merge's image roll; the design pack's `procedures` screen class is

- **P1** Given the published process of a converted SOP, when `processes.get` is called, then the answer carries `source_asset_id`, `knowledge_pack_ref`, `converter_version`, `approval_id` and each step's `action_text`/`pddl_preconditions`/`pddl_effects`.

The mock UI's `operations` screen stops being a ribbon and reads the live incident record that #78 (T7) now writes: incidents (service, severity, state, detected_at, mitigated_at, resolved_at), their runbook selection and their linked postmortem. Read-only — the owner's 2026-11-19 decision keeps the console an operator read surface, so no write path is added.

## Why this is a separate unit
#78 built the engine (the five §10.4 `ops.*` actions, the postmortem governed asset, `ops.flag_flip`). The console half needs a public-snapshot section and a `v2.js` live branch — the #385 architecture precedent — which is a different artefact and a different gate.

## Acceptance
- `snapshot_tx`/`site_view` expose an `ops` section: incident cards with their meta, programme-bound only (#382's filter), no private fields.
- `docs/design/v2.js`'s `operations` page renders the rows and contains no `ribbon(`/`consoleRibbon(`; `scripts/build-coverage.py` moves it from `proposed` to `live` (its `gap` cleared).
- The design-pack job (`build-coverage.py --check`, `check-data.cjs`, `check-coverage.cjs`) is green; `/design/` 200.

## Out of scope
Any write path from the browser; the on-call stack; the other six proposed screens.

<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->

## Goal

A contributor can answer "where does the SPEC_V2 programme stand, and can I download that answer?"
from one public URL and one tracked GitHub issue, both generated from the same rows — instead of
from five registers that disagree.

## Plan / audit source

No slice plan exists for this unit; this issue is the brief. Sources: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12 (the
tranche gates), `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` (the unit protocol), and the measured state below.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/433-programme-record` |
| HEAD | `d5e6b4541e8c3aac33da761c5a6b11ac20d257da` |
| Session | mini3/claude (claim nonce 3F3A0ED9-6211-4E68-B37E-119C27062C21) |
| Updated | 2026-11-19 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12 — blob `73df92c3` | main@6c46d92e |
| Protocol | `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` — blob `67dda4f3` | main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs` — writes `programme.json` … `manifest.json` | main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `crates/pack/src/live.rs:SiteView` — the served view (snapshot.js only) | main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `crates/api/src/design.rs:live_path` — the four served live paths | main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `scripts/build-programme-seed.py:build` — the status derivation | main@6c46d92e |
| UI | `docs/design/v2.js:509` — `snapshotProjects` renders `programme.projects` | main@6c46d92e |
| Gate | `docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs` — blob `26120612` · `check-data.cjs` | main@6c46d92e |
| Data | `docs/design/data/coverage.json`, `docs/design/data/issues.json` | main@6c46d92e |
| Issue | #427 · #394 · #62 · #8 | open/closed per Dependencies |
| Path | `scripts/programme_state.py`, `scripts/build-programme-view.py`, `crates/pack/src/live.rs::programme_csv` (test inline), `/design/data/programme.csv` (served) | to create |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@6c46d92e603f2efe70bd30010c6753033e5ac523`, measured 2026-11-19.
- Docs: SPEC_V2 blob `73df92c3878a449ed38bb280ad44ba4262174ed4` · 03-DELIVERY blob
  `67dda4f373f14fc17805cb0bbf491c4125308b15` · check-coverage.cjs blob
  `2612061293f0997c480fd1e33a0d42830cffba23`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 the programme is downloadable as JSON | ABSENT | `conveyor snapshot` writes `programme.json` (`crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs` file list) but it is not committed (`git ls-tree origin/main docs/design/data/` lists six files, none of them `programme.json`) and `crates/api/src/design.rs:live_path` answers only `snapshot.js`/`outputs.js`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/programme.json` → `404` |
| P2 CSV | ABSENT | no CSV writer in the snapshot; `/design/data/programme.csv` → `404` |
| P3 one delivery-status derivation | PARTIAL | `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` ranks plan frontmatter over GitHub issue state: T11's issue #84 is closed (merged #404) yet `seed/programme.json` says `"status": "draft"`, `"measured_status": "proposed"` |
| P4 one tracked issue | ABSENT | `gh issue list --label programme` → empty; `gh issue list --search 'conveyor-buildout in:title' --state all` → only closed #62 |
| P5 page download + one prose source | PARTIAL | `docs/design/v2.js:509` renders the programme's projects from `CONVEYOR_SNAPSHOT`; no download link; `docs/plans/00-INDEX.md` carries dated live-status prose (`grep -n 'Status 2026-11-07'`) |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — serve the snapshot's programme file
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12 · `crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs` · `crates/api/src/design.rs`
Requirement: the public tenant's programme and project rows are downloadable as JSON at
`/design/data/programme.json`, built from the same `SiteView` the page uses, with the same
`no-store` discipline as `snapshot.js`.

- **P1.1** Given the public tenant, when `GET /design/data/programme.json`, then `200
  application/json` and `.projects|length == 48`.
  Verify: `curl -s https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/programme.json | jq '.projects|length'` → `48` (live, after merge + reconcile)
- **P1.2** Given no public tenant is configured, when the path is requested, then `404 no-store`.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs::no_public_tenant_is_a_closed_window` (extended with the two paths)
- **P1.3** Given the same request, then the payload carries `schema`, `generated_at`, `projects`
  and the `issue_registry` the page joins against.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs::the_programme_is_downloadable_as_json_and_csv` (to create)

### P2 — CSV download
`crates/pack/src/snapshot.rs`
Requirement: the same rows are offered as CSV with a stable header, so a reader can open them
without the site.

- **P2.1** Given the public tenant, when `GET /design/data/programme.csv`, then `200 text/csv` and
  49 lines (header + 48 projects).
  Verify: `curl -s https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/programme.csv | wc -l` → `49`
- **P2.2** Given the CSV's first line, then it is exactly
  `key,name,tranche,status,blocked_by,units_open,units_claimed,issues,plan`.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-pack live::tests::the_programme_csv_names_the_blockers_and_counts_the_units`

### P3 — one delivery-status derivation
`scripts/build-programme-seed.py`
Requirement: delivery status is derived once, with GitHub issue state as the highest authority —
issue closed + a merged PR → `closed`; an open blocker issue → `blocked`; code present → `built`;
otherwise `proposed` — and plan frontmatter can never override a closed issue.

- **P3.1** Given T11's issue #84 is closed and #404 merged, when the seed is generated, then T11's
  status is `closed` despite `plan_status: draft`.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/programme_state.py --project T11` → `closed`; `jq -r '.projects[]|select(.key=="T11")|.status' seed/programme.json` → `closed`
- **P3.2** Given a project whose blocker issue is open, when generated, then its status is
  `blocked` and never `closed`.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/programme_state.py --self-test`
- **P3.3** Given no input change, when the generator runs twice, then the seed is byte-identical.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py && sha256sum seed/programme.json` twice → equal

### P4 — one tracked issue
`.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml`
Requirement: one pinned issue, `conveyor-buildout — the SPEC_V2 programme`, carries the generated
table of every project (status, tranche, blocked-by, units, issue/PR links) and is refreshed by the
registry job on every run.

- **P4.1** Given the programme rows, when the job runs, then the tracked issue's body equals the
  generated body.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-programme-view.py --check-issue 435` → exit 0
- **P4.2** Given a merged unit PR, when the next refresh runs, then the tracked issue's row for that
  project changes state and the run summary names the changed projects.
  Verify: `gh run view <issue-registry run> --json jobs` summary text

### P5 — page download + one source of prose
`docs/design/v2.js` · `docs/plans/00-INDEX.md`
Requirement: the programme page offers the JSON and CSV downloads and shows delivery status beside
pack coverage; `00-INDEX.md`'s live-status prose is banner-marked as a build record pointing at the
tracked issue.

- **P5.1** Given the design pack, when the programme page renders, then it carries links to
  `data/programme.json` and `data/programme.csv` and both status columns.
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` (extended case, to create)
- **P5.2** Given `docs/plans/00-INDEX.md`, then the S-table is preceded by a build-record banner
  linking the tracked issue.
  Verify: `git grep -c 'build record' docs/plans/00-INDEX.md` → ≥ `1`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #427 | the design-pack's T11 coverage row — a different status from delivery status; this unit publishes both side by side, it does not fix #427 | claimed, PR #429 open |
| related | #394 | both edit `scripts/build-programme-seed.py`; no ordering — whichever lands second rebases | ready |
| related | #62 | prior art: the programme's plan state reads GitHub issues + conveyor rows (closed) | closed |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #8 | the live `curl` scenarios verify after the merge deploys; construction is not blocked | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the doc blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/code/test reference resolves at `main@6c46d92e`; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `blocked-by`, so no `Blocker:` line.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from #427 and sequenced against #394 on one file.
- [x] Scope corrections applied (no old-system shutdown/parity, no ledger import).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`scripts/ci/gate.sh`).
- [ ] Tests added/updated per part; none skipped.
- [ ] Docs updated; migrations and `--check-lock` untouched (none expected).
- [ ] Live verification recorded after merge + Flux reconcile.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- **Auto-merging the generated registry PR.** The workflow deliberately never merges; `design-pack`
  is not a required check (measured: #423 merged red), so auto-merge would reproduce that trap, and
  making it required is a repository-admin change the token cannot perform.
- #427's T11 pack-coverage declaration and #394's seed definition payload.
- `~/.claude/plans/program/LEDGER.md` (outside this repository) — the PR records the follow-up line,
  it does not edit that file.
- AHTAPol and w2v product builds (`docs/SPEC_LEGACY_KAG.md`).

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes — P1.1/P2.1's live `curl` scenarios run after merge and Flux reconcile. No separate blocker.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What the page shows when delivery status and pack coverage disagree | owner | show both, labelled; never reconcile silently |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.2 no public tenant is a closed window | `conveyor-api --test design_live` | PASS — 10 passed, incl. both programme paths | eee1191a |
| P1.3 the programme is downloadable | `design_live::the_programme_is_downloadable_as_json_and_csv` | PASS — 200 JSON, schema, projects, issue_registry; CSV header | eee1191a |
| P2.2 CSV header and escaping | `conveyor-pack --lib` → `live::tests::the_programme_csv_names_the_blockers_and_counts_the_units` | PASS — 11 passed | eee1191a |
| P3.1 T11 reads closed | `python3 scripts/programme_state.py --project T11` | `closed`; seed `["closed"]` | eee1191a |
| P3.2 precedence cases | `python3 scripts/programme_state.py --self-test` | 7/7 cases | eee1191a |
| P3.3 determinism | `build-programme-seed.py` twice → sha256 | identical (`cc35aa2a…` on the pre-rebase tree) | eee1191a |
| P4.1 tracked issue matches the seed | `python3 scripts/build-programme-view.py --check-issue 435` | exit 0 | eee1191a |
| P4.2 a refresh names the rows it moved | `python3 scripts/build-programme-view.py --update 435` | `no project row changed`; teed into the job summary | eee1191a |
| P5.1 downloads are linked | `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` + one link removed | exit 0 / exit 1 FAIL — the gate can fail | eee1191a |
| P5.2 one prose source | `git grep -c 'build record' docs/plans/00-INDEX.md` | 4 (≥1) | eee1191a |
| P1.1/P2.1 live 200s | `curl …/design/data/programme.json` / `.csv` | after merge + reconcile (acceptance-blocked-by #8) | — |

## Goal
`S14-cutover.md` stops instructing an operator to query or assert objects that have been deleted: the plan records the executed sweep and the n8n decommission, and the checks that named those objects assert absence.

## Plan / audit source
Measured defect, 2026-11-19 — the slice plan itself (`docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md`); no other plan owns it.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | issue/430-s14-n8n-doc |
| HEAD | 826aea60 |
| Session | mini3 / cluster-cleanup R12 |
| Updated | 2026-11-19 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References
| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Doc | `docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md` | main@6c46d92e (blob 77e49b86) |
| Evidence | gitops-production `docs/archive/retired-services-2026-11-16/README.md` § Round 9 — the S14 sweep executed early | gitops main, measured 2026-11-19 |
| Live | `psql -d n8n` → database absent; `kubectl get ns n8n` → NotFound | measured 2026-11-19 |

## Baseline
- Code: `main@6c46d92e` · measured 2026-11-19

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — the P1 precondition | STALE | `sudo -u postgres psql -At -c "select datname from pg_database where datname='n8n'"` → no row |
| P2 — the §3 OUT statement | STALE | says "the idle process stays" |
| P3 — exit criterion #4 | STALE | `kubectl -n n8n get deploy n8n-worker` → namespace NotFound |
| P4 — §9.9 | STALE | says the deployment "stays idle, undecommissioned" |
| P5 — frontmatter | PARTIAL | `status: planned` on an executed slice |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the precondition is a historical record
Requirement: P1 states the n8n DB was dumped at T+14 and deleted with the namespace; it no longer issues a live query.

- **P1.1** Given the plan, when an operator reads P1, then no line asks them to query the deleted database.
  Verify: `! grep -q 'psql -d n8n' docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md`

### P2 — the scoping statements match reality
Requirement: §3 OUT and §9.9 record n8n as decommissioned (namespace and DB absent), not idle.

- **P2.1** Given the plan, when read, then neither line claims the deployment stays.
  Verify: `! grep -q 'the idle process stays' docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md && ! grep -q 'stays idle, undecommissioned' docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md`

### P3 — the exit criterion asserts absence
Requirement: the exit criterion that named the n8n Deployment asserts the namespace is gone.

- **P3.1** Given the gate block, when run today, then step 4 passes against the decommissioned state.
  Verify: `grep -q 'kubectl get ns n8n --ignore-not-found' docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md`

### P4 — the frontmatter records the execution
Requirement: the status names the execution date and the evidence, replacing `planned`.

- **P4.1** Given the frontmatter, when parsed, then it says executed with the date.
  Verify: `grep -q '^status: executed' docs/plans/slices/S14-cutover.md`

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | — | the sweep itself ran in gitops-production #5333 (another repository) | merged |

## Definition of ready
- Baseline sha recorded; the doc path resolves; each part carries a Verify command.
- No blocker open.

## Definition of done
- A docs-only PR with `Closes #<this>`; its checks green; merged through the queue.
- The four greps in P1–P4 pass on `main`.

## Out of scope
- Re-running any S14 check or touching the cluster.
- The gitops archive README (it already records the sweep).
- Any code, image or deployment change.

## Deployment prerequisite
None — docs only; no image is built and nothing rolls.

## Open questions
None.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | — |

## Goal

T11's coverage row must reflect what #84 built. Every registry refresh is born red because
`docs/design/data/coverage.json` still says T11 is `proposed` with `measured {actions:[0,0],
modules:[0,0], tables:[0,0]}`, so `check-coverage` lists it under `summary.projects.uncovered`
and the `design-pack` job fails.

## Measured 2026-11-19 (after #404/#84 merged at 12:49Z)

- Refresh PR #423 at `a0b6b87e` (regenerated 13:51:30Z, after #424 fixed T14):
  `uncovered: ["T11"]`; T11 `status: proposed`, `measured [0,0]×3`, `units.open: 0` (`numbers: [84]`).
- `design-pack` fails on that sha: `check-coverage.cjs:223` —
  `AssertionError: a non-built project has no open unit`, `actual ['T11']` vs `expected []`.
- #416 fixed the identical defect for T14 by declaring the merged artefacts in
  `scripts/v2-slice-artefacts.json`; T11's declaration still carries only `evidence` + `gap`, so
  `measure_v2` returns the curated `proposed` row (`scripts/build-coverage.py:543-548`).
- T11's row never was authored wrong — it was never re-declared after #404 landed the code.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Generator | `scripts/build-coverage.py` `measure_v2` + `v2_artefacts` | main@866750e9 |
| Declaration | `scripts/v2-slice-artefacts.json` — T11 | main@866750e9 |
| Check | `docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs:219-223` | main@866750e9 |
| Prior fix of the same class | #416 / PR #424 (T14) | merged 13:51:17Z |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — T11 measures as built

Given the merged #84 code and the closed issue, when the coverage generator runs, then T11's row
is `built` and `summary.projects.uncovered` is empty.

Verify: `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py && node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs` exits 0,
and the next registry-refresh PR's `design-pack` job is green.

## Dependencies

| Kind | Issue | State |

| related | #84 | closed by #404 (merged 12:49Z); the build this row must reflect |
| related | #416 | closed; the same fix applied to T14 |

- [x] One part with a `Verify:`.
- [x] One-PR scope: the declaration and its regenerated data; no hand-edit of the generator.

## Definition of done

## Goal

A push to `nonagenticai/conveyor` either passes the pre-push gate or is refused; today it can report
`PUSH BLOCKED` and let the push through, after spending 30 minutes per attempt.

## Plan / audit source

The pre-push hook installed 2026-11-19 09:56 (`.git/hooks/pre-push`, `lib-rust-gate.sh`, from
`gitops-production/scripts/hooks/`). Measured while pushing the #409/#422 branches:
`.local-ci-push.txt` in the worktree.

## Baseline

`main@8fb6a81b` (PR #425 merged) — hook installed, `lib-rust-gate.sh` submits a coding job that
runs `cargo build` then `cargo test` on the pushed HEAD.

## Current state (measured)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Each push spends 10-30 minutes in the gate | pushes to `issue/409-*` and `issue/422-*`; the #422 retry log: `[896.0s] succeeded` then a second attempt `verdict: failed — the runner pod did not finish within 1800s` |
| The gate reports a failure it cannot explain | `.local-ci-push.txt`: `FAIL cargo test (exit 101)`, and the captured log holds a truncated rustc command line with no error text; the same HEAD compiles here (`cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test estate_toolkits --no-run` → Finished, exit 0) and CI's own suite passed |
| A blocked verdict still lets the push land | `verdict: 1 of 1 checks failed` + `❌ PUSH BLOCKED` printed, then the ref was updated (`git ls-remote` shows the branch at the pushed SHA). The hook fails open on anything but exit 1 |
| Two gate runs blocked the same branch twice | 1800 s timeouts on `issue/422-in-flight-test` |

Two defects: the gate's own output is truncated to the point of being unactionable, and its verdict
and its exit status disagree — a hook that says "BLOCKED" and pushes anyway trains people to ignore it.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the gate either blocks the push or does not claim to
- **P1.1** Given a failing gate result, when the hook exits, then the push is refused (exit 1) and the log says which check failed and why.
  Verify: a deliberately broken branch push is refused, and `.local-ci-push.txt` carries the compiler/test error text.

### P2 — the gate's log carries the failure, not a truncated command line
- **P2.1** Given `FAIL cargo test`, when the log is read, then the first error (file, line, message) is present.
  Verify: the log for a failing run contains a `-->` location line and the error message.

### P3 — the gate's runtime is bounded well below the push timeout
- **P3.1** Given a green tree, when a push runs the gate, then it completes inside a stated budget (the measured 896 s for a successful run is the current baseline; a 1800 s timeout that fires twice is not a budget).
  Verify: the recorded durations of ten consecutive pushes.

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| relates | #22 | CI cost measurement lives there; this is the local push gate | OPEN |

## Definition of ready
- [x] Baseline named; each claim measured from a real push log.

## Definition of done
- [ ] The three scenarios pass; one PR `Closes #<n>` MERGED (the hook lives under `.git/hooks`,
      so the fix lands in `gitops-production/scripts/hooks/` and is installed from there).

## Out of scope
The coding service itself and the CI workflows.

## Goal

`conveyor-actions::estate_toolkits::an_in_flight_run_finishes_after_the_unbind` is deterministic: the
unbind waits until the destination has received the call instead of sleeping a fixed 120 ms.

## Plan / audit source

PR #415's first CI run (job 135513313257): `FAIL [ 2.248s] … an_in_flight_run_finishes_after_the_unbind`
at `estate_toolkits.rs:453` — `code` was not 200. The same tree passed locally (5/5) and the re-run
passed, so it is a timing race, not a code defect.

## Baseline

`main@2ed9a1ef` (the #409 merge) — the test sleeps 120 ms after starting the call and assumes the
broker has resolved by then.

## Current state (measured)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The test fails when the unbind beats the broker's resolve | CI job 135513313257, assertion at `estate_toolkits.rs:453` |
| It passes alone, repeatedly, on an idle box | 5/5 runs of the single test through the build guard |
| The stub counts a hit before its delay | `estate_toolkits.rs` `answer()` — a hit proves the broker is inside the dispatch |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the unbind is ordered by the destination, not by wall clock
- **P1.1** Given the call in flight, when the destination has received it, then the unbind runs and the call still answers 200 with its ledger row.
  Verify: the single test run 5 consecutive times through `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py nextest run -p conveyor-actions --test estate_toolkits -E 'test(an_in_flight_run_finishes_after_the_unbind)'`

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| follows | #409 | the test shipped with the T14 proof script | CLOSED |

## Definition of ready
- [x] Baseline named; the failure and its non-reproduction are both measured.

## Definition of done
- [ ] The scenario passes 5/5 locally and in CI; one PR `Closes #<n>` MERGED.

## Goal
A metered external call (inference/audio/imagegen) that is cut off by the action timeout or by a cancelled run is read to its terminal chunk in the background, so the inference-router completes the request and books its usage instead of losing an already-prefilled prompt.

## Plan / audit source
Measured defect, 2026-11-19 — no slice plan owns it. Evidence and code refs below; the contract shape is `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Issue content contract".

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | issue/412-metered-call-drain |
| HEAD | 8b3c9a85 |
| Session | mini3 / cluster-cleanup R12 |
| Updated | 2026-11-19 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References
| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs:invoke_external` | main@36b9b60d |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs` (`inference.chat`, `captures_usage: true`) | main@36b9b60d |
| Code | `apps/inference-router/src/ledger.rs` (a failed/aborted attempt books a zero cost event) | main@36b9b60d |
| Test | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs::tests::a_metered_call_drains_its_body_after_the_action_timeout` | issue/412-metered-call-drain |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/inference_call_drain.rs::a_cancelled_metered_call_is_read_to_completion` | issue/412-metered-call-drain |
| Test | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs::tests::an_unmetered_call_is_abandoned_when_its_caller_leaves` | issue/412-metered-call-drain |

## Baseline
- Code: `main@36b9b60d` · measured 2026-11-19 (live cluster, tenant `nonagentic-conveyor`, licence `01a1e15d-…`)

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — metered action call survives a timeout/cancel | ABSENT | `invoke.rs:1273` wraps `builder.send()` in `tokio::time::timeout`; `invoke.rs:955` wraps the whole action. Dropping either future closes the connection mid-generation. |
| P2 — the router books an aborted attempt | ABSENT by design | `ledger.rs`: an attempt without usage books a zero event, so vLLM's counted prefill reaches no billing row. |

Measured 2026-11-19 (burst 10:27–10:36Z, the same tenant):
- `inference_router_tokens_total{kind="prompt"}` = 191,979 vs `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` = 254,984.
- `vllm:request_prompt_tokens_sum` (completed requests only) = 193,152 → **~61,800 prompt tokens belong to requests that never completed**.
- `billing_cost_events` has 16 rows / 191,179 input tokens for the burst; the aborted attempts have no row.
- Two `run` rows were `cancelled` in the window (`01a1f35e-e063-761a-a168-9294a9591967`, cancelled 11:28:19→11:31:45+01; `01a1f354-…` family), and `inference_router_provider_attempt_seconds_total` stepped +89.4 s at the cancel. `action_invocation` has no row for those attempts (all recorded `inference.chat` rows are `ok`).
- The cost-event actor is the router's Keycloak service account (the fallback when the caller sends no `X-Actor-Id`); the caller is the conveyor's `inference.chat` action.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — drain a metered external call on timeout/cancel
Requirement: when `spec.captures_usage` is true, run the HTTP send and the body read in a task of its own, so the request reaches its terminal chunk even when the caller's future is dropped; the action still honours `spec.timeout_ms` and still returns its timeout error.

- **P1.1** Given a metered upstream that streams slowly, when the action timeout elapses, then the upstream body is read to its last chunk and the action returns its timeout error.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --lib tests::a_metered_call_drains_its_body_after_the_action_timeout`
- **P1.2** Given a metered call in flight, when the caller's future is dropped (a cancelled run), then the upstream body still reaches its last chunk.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test inference_call_drain a_cancelled_metered_call_is_read_to_completion`
- **P1.3** Given a non-metered external action, when its timeout elapses, then the request is still abandoned as today (no background spend).
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --lib tests::an_unmetered_call_is_abandoned_when_its_caller_leaves`

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #235 | the router's actor/attribution contract this call rides on | merged |

## Definition of ready
- Baseline sha recorded; every code path cited resolves at it.
- Both acceptance tests defined with a Verify command.
- No blocker open.

## Definition of done
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p conveyor-actions --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the crate's tests pass locally through the sanctioned Rust route.
- One PR with `Closes #<this>`, its checks green, squash-merged.
- The conveyor image is published and Flux applies the digest; the worker and server roll Ready.
- Live: a cancelled run's `inference.chat` attempt lands in `billing_cost_events`, and `local_llm:metering_coverage_ratio:1h` stays ≥ 0.99 across a burst containing a cancellation; `LocalLlmMeteringCoverageLow` does not fire.

## Out of scope
- The router's zero-cost-event policy for an attempt with no usage (`apps/inference-router/src/ledger.rs`).
- Non-metered external actions' cancellation semantics.
- The direct `produce.script` transport (`crates/actions/src/produce.rs`), which owns its own request; no `produce.script` invocation appeared in the measured burst, so no abort signature was observed there. If one appears, it takes the same drain on its own evidence.
- The alert rule's thresholds (`LocalLlmMeteringCoverageLow`); its history forbids threshold fitting.

The conveyor image builds on merge and Flux ImagePolicy `conveyor`/`conveyor-worker` auto-updates the digest; the live scenario is verified after that rollout (no manual pin).

None.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | — |

- **P1.2** Given the branch is not queued, when the refresh runs, then it behaves exactly as today (push, then open/update the one PR).

- **P2.1** Given the push is refused with `GH006 … merge queue` (the race between the check and the push), when the step runs, then it records the reason, exits 0, and any other push failure still fails the step.

| — | — | self-contained | — |

## Goal

The deployed (OIDC) Playwright suite must run from a clean checkout: the setup project must create
the state it uses, and the harness must give every page the bearer the app's memory-only token
policy (ADR 0001) deliberately does not persist. **Owner decision 2026-11-20: harness-owned
bearer (option B).** The app's token policy is untouched.

## Measured 2026-11-19/20 (deployed console, main@7ff187ff)

1. **The setup project cannot start from a clean checkout.**
   `BASE_URL=https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai E2E_USER=conveyor-e2e E2E_PASS=… npx playwright test e2e/oidc.setup.ts`
   fails with `Error reading storage state from test-results/oidc-state.json: ENOENT`.
   `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` sets `use.storageState` globally, so the `oidc` setup project
   is asked to read the file it exists to write; Playwright clears `test-results/` at run start.
2. **A later page load has no bearer.** `apps/web/src/auth.rs` keeps the access token in memory
   and completes a login only on a `?code=` callback. A fresh context with the Keycloak SSO
   cookies loads `/` and sees **Sign in**.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Config | `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` — OIDC projects, storageState | main@7ff187ff |
| Setup | `apps/web/e2e/oidc.setup.ts` — login, token and state files | main@7ff187ff |
| Helpers | `apps/web/e2e/helpers.ts` — `authFor`/`invoke` (API requests) | main@7ff187ff |
| App policy | `apps/web/src/auth.rs` — memory-only token | main@7ff187ff |
| Plan | `docs/plans/slices/S12-ui-buildout.md` §6 step 0 | main@7ff187ff |

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/391-deployed-oidc-bearer` |
| HEAD | `9543a3e0` |
| Session | `m4/finish-conveyor-leftovers (claim nonce B3357CE4-40D8-4BE3-9738-4910FDB53560)` |
| Updated | `2026-11-20` |
| Adopted-from | — |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the setup runs from a clean checkout

Given no `apps/web/test-results/`, when the `oidc` setup project runs against the deployed app,
then it exits 0 and writes the token and storage-state files; the app project depends on it and is
the only project that reads the state file.

Verify: `rm -rf apps/web/test-results && cd apps/web && BASE_URL=https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai E2E_USER=… E2E_PASS=… npx playwright test e2e/oidc.setup.ts` exits 0 and both files exist.

### P2 — the harness injects the bearer

Given a page in the app project under OIDC mode, when the app calls `/api/**`, then the request
carries `Authorization: Bearer <setup token>` at the network layer; the app's memory-only token
policy is unchanged. The route is installed only when `BASE_URL` is set and `DEV_AUTH_TOKEN` is
not (dev mode is untouched).

Verify: a deployed smoke (`BASE_URL=… E2E_USER=… E2E_PASS=… npx playwright test e2e/shell-login.spec.ts -g "a credential lands on Today"` or a dedicated `deployed.spec.ts`) reaches the signed-in shell without a click.

### P3 — dev mode is unchanged

Given `DEV_AUTH_TOKEN=dev:alice` locally, when the whole suite runs, then the fixture installs no
route and the 75-test dev suite is green.

Verify: `cd apps/web && DEV_AUTH_TOKEN=dev:alice BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8930 npx playwright test --reporter=line` → 75 passed.

## Goal

`/boards` currently costs one `GET /api/projects/{id}` per project on the first page
(`load_projects`: `GET /api/projects?limit=50`, then a detail read per row). With 50 projects the
screen sits on "Loading projects…" for tens of seconds and the tenant's whole project history is
read one row at a time. Make one page one request (or one small bounded batch).

Measured 2026-11-19 on the deployed console (`sha256:36953744…`): `/api/projects?limit=50`
returns 50 items; the browser then issues 50 sequential `/api/projects/{id}` reads and the screen

## Goal

`scripts/ci/gate.sh` builds into a per-worktree `target/` (48 GB measured on `.worktrees/issue-366`

escapes the disk-floor and slot limits `cargo-guard` exists to enforce.

### P1 — The gate builds through the sanctioned route

<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->
## Goal

`.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` must generate its seed from the same registry it ships, and a closed generated PR must never wedge the automation. Two defects, both measured:

1. **Inconsistent sources.** The workflow runs `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` → `docs/design/data/issues.json`, then regenerates the seed. `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` does not read that file — it calls `gh issue list` again (`gh_issues()`, line ~295). The committed pair therefore comes from two reads seconds apart, and `crates/store/tests/seed_programme.rs::seed_programme_links_the_registered_issues` refuses the mismatch. Fix the generator to consume the fetched registry (`--issues-file`, or by default when `docs/design/data/issues.json` exists) so the pair is consistent by construction.
2. **The closed-PR reopen wedge.** When the generated PR is closed without merging and the next run force-pushes its branch, GitHub refuses both `gh pr reopen` and `PATCH /pulls/{n} {state:open}` with *"the branch was force-pushed or recreated"*, so every subsequent run fails at that step. Measured twice (PR #355 and PR #367). The workflow must never depend on reopening: when no open PR exists for its head, push a fresh branch (`automation/issue-registry-<timestamp>`) and open a new PR from it.

## Plan / audit source

The issue is its own audit; the measured sources are the workflow, the fetch script, the generator and the store test, all cited below at `main@f14b7d36`.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:69-70` (fetch), `:150-170` (fixed head, force-push, reopen) | main@f14b7d36 |
| Code | `scripts/build-programme-seed.py:295-316` (`gh_issues()` — the second live read), `:392` (its call) | main@f14b7d36 |
| Code | `scripts/fetch-issues.sh:25-29` (the registry fetch) | main@f14b7d36 |
| Test | `crates/store/tests/seed_programme.rs::seed_programme_links_the_registered_issues` | main@f14b7d36 |
| Issue | #367, #355 — the two wedge incidents | closed / merged |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@f14b7d36`, measured 2026-11-19.
- Workflow: run 44446030449 (`issue-registry`) succeeded 2026-11-19T02:40Z. It is green **by luck**: no issue changed between the two reads, so the committed pair agreed. The structural defect is present in the source.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-19)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 one source for the seed and the registry | PRESENT | `build-programme-seed.py:392` calls `gh_issues()`; the workflow fetches `issues.json` first at line 70. Two live reads, seconds apart. |
| P2 a closed generated PR never wedges the automation | PRESENT | Workflow lines 156-170: fixed head `automation/issue-registry`, force-push at line 150, then `gh pr reopen`. |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — one source for the seed and the registry

- **P1.1** Given the fetched `issues.json`, when the seed is regenerated, then its issue links and states come from that file, and a second run is byte-identical.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test seed_programme seed_programme_links_the_registered_issues`
- **P1.2** Given a live issue created between the fetch and the generation, when the workflow runs, then the committed pair still agrees (the live list is read once).
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py --check` after a fetch with a modified file.

### P2 — a closed generated PR never wedges the automation

- **P2.1** Given no open generated PR and a closed one whose branch was force-pushed, when the workflow runs, then it opens a NEW PR from a fresh timestamped branch and never calls `gh pr reopen`.
  Verify: `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml | grep -c 'gh pr reopen'` is 0, and the workflow's next run after the merge completes green (`gh run list --workflow issue-registry.yml`).
- **P2.2** Given an open generated PR (fixed or timestamped head), when the workflow runs with changed data, then it updates that one PR and no second generated PR appears.
  Verify: `gh pr list --state open --search 'docs: refresh the public issue registry in:title'` returns at most one.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #367, #355 | the two wedge incidents | measured |
| related | #381 | the last generated PR merger; the current green posture | merged |

## Programme

| Benefits | enabling — keeps the programme ledger consistent; no direct benefit |

- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no `blocked-by`, so no `Blocker:` line.
- [x] One-PR scope: the generator's issue source and the workflow's PR-creation branch logic.
- [x] Programme section present (this issue was created 2026-11-18, so the forward-only exemption does not apply).

## Definition of done

- Both parts pass at the PR head; the evidence table carries one row per scenario.
- Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate`).
- One PR `Closes #372` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.
- The next push to `main` runs `issue-registry` green; when data changed it opens or updates exactly one generated PR, and it never reopens a closed one.

## Out of scope

- Changing the registry's content or redaction rules (`scripts/fetch-issues.sh`).
- Fixing the board/coverage generators beyond what P1 requires.
- Manually closing or reopening generated PRs.

| P5 live | ABSENT | `kubectl get deploy -A` → no sheets workload; the actions are in-process and ship with the `conveyor` image |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — Deterministic XLSX writer

`docs/decisions/0007-tool-estate-conveyor-and-coding.md` §1 (the `apps/server` row).

- **P1.1** Given one workbook, when it is exported twice, then the two byte strings are equal, every zip entry is stored, and every entry carries the same fixed timestamp.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/determinism.rs::two_exports_are_byte_identical` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given text repeated across cells, when exported, then each distinct string appears once in `sharedStrings.xml`, in first-seen order.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/determinism.rs::shared_strings_are_first_seen_and_deduped` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given the extracted archive writer, when `crates/deck` runs its existing tests, then `deck::zip_parts` produces the same deck it did before the extraction.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-deck` (exists)
- **P1.4** Given a workbook whose produced bytes exceed 10 MiB, when exported, then the refusal is `too_large` naming `bytes` and the limit, never a downstream 413.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/limits.rs::export_over_the_byte_ceiling_is_a_typed_refusal` (to create)

### P2 — Reader

`docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` (grouping by runtime shape: pure-CPU work stays in the workspace).

- **P2.1** Given a workbook carrying text, number, bool, date and formula-with-cached-value cells, when export then import is applied, then the canonical workbook equals the input.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/roundtrip.rs::export_import_equals_workbook` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a workbook written by a different producer (deflated parts, styles, merged ranges), when imported, then formulas, dates and merged ranges survive and only the top-left cell of each merge is valued.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/real_world_import.rs::imports_formulas_dates_and_merged_cells` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given input beyond a stated cap (sheets, rows, columns, cells, text length, decoded bytes), when imported or exported, then the refusal is `too_large` naming the capped thing, its count and the limit.
  Verify: `crates/sheets/tests/limits.rs::oversized_cell_count_is_a_typed_refusal` (to create)

### P3 — Actions

`crates/actions/src/deck.rs` (the artefact shape) · `crates/actions/src/documents/actions.rs` (the storage path).

- **P3.1** Given a matrix request, when `sheets.export` runs with the default inline mode, then the response carries `media_type`, `bytes`, `sha256` and base64 whose decoded length and recomputed hash equal the reported values.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/sheets.rs::export_returns_verified_inline_artefact` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given `as:"document"`, when `sheets.export` runs, then exactly one document row and one object exist, and the returned `sha256` equals the object's digest.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/sheets.rs::export_as_document_stores_one_object` (to create)
- **P3.3** Given bytes of a workbook, when `sheets.import` runs, then a canonical workbook is returned and re-exporting it reproduces the same cells.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/sheets.rs::import_then_export_roundtrips` (to create)
- **P3.4** Given a workbook above the inline cap, when `sheets.export` runs in inline mode, then the refusal names the document mode as the route.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/sheets.rs::export_over_inline_cap_is_refused` (to create)
- **P3.5** Given the spreadsheet media type, when a document is created from xlsx bytes, then the type gate accepts it and a non-ZIP body is still refused.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/documents/actions.rs::xlsx_is_an_allowed_document_type` (to create)

### P4 — Registry, lock and design pack

`served-spec.lock.json` · `docs/design/` (the pack the console serves).

- **P4.1** Given the two registered actions, when the served lock is regenerated, then it holds 493 operations and 462 action routes, and the check passes at the head.
  Verify: `cargo run -p conveyor-server -- --print-openapi --check-lock`
- **P4.2** Given the counted registry tests, when the suite runs, then the operation and action-route counts match the lock.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry`
- **P4.3** Given the design pack, when its checks run, then they pass with the two new action rows present.
  Verify: `for f in docs/design/scripts/check-*.cjs; do node "$f"; done` and `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check`

### P5 — Live proof (deployment-gated)

The proof waits on the image built from this merge rolling out; construction does not. No open deployment issue exists (#18 is closed), so the rollout is this unit's own step.

- **P5.1** Given the deployed conveyor, when `sheets.export` is invoked on a three-sheet workbook (typed cells, a date, a formula with a cached value), then the decoded bytes hash to the reported `sha256`.
  Verify: invocation recorded on this issue with its command and response
- **P5.2** Given the same workbook with `as:"document"`, when exported then imported, then the stored object's digest equals the response's and the imported matrices equal the input.
  Verify: `mc cat <object> | sha256sum` plus `sheets.import` response, recorded

## Goal

The console never offers a decision the store will refuse. A gate whose requester is the caller
cannot be self-decided under the default `self_approval: forbidden` (#282), yet the cockpit and the
eval sign-off tabs still render an enabled **Approve** button for exactly that gate. Clicking it
answers `409 the requester cannot decide their own gate`, and the pill stays `pending` with no
explanation.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-18)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The refusal is real | `POST /api/actions/approvals.decide` as the gate's requester → `409 {"detail":"the requester cannot decide their own gate"}` (reproduced against the deployed console) |
| The cockpit offers it anyway | `apps/web/src/screens/cockpit.rs` renders the decide control for every pending gate on the card, with no requester check |
| The eval tab offers it too | `apps/web/src/screens/evals.rs` (the sign-off rows) renders the same control |
| Two specs already fail on it | `apps/web/e2e/cockpit.spec.ts` (`the cockpit claims, starts a run and approves a gate`) and `apps/web/e2e/evals.spec.ts` (`cases, sign-off and climb tabs read their real actions`), both on `origin/main` |
| The good pattern already exists | `/approvals` (#285) disables the control **with the reason** when the caller requested the gate and the policy forbids self-approval |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/store/src/approval.rs:842-860` — `record_decision_tx`'s `RequesterCannotDecide` | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/control/policies.rs:110-124` — the policy vocabulary (destructive actions only) | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `apps/web/src/screens/approvals.rs:45-82,165-176` — the load-one-policy-per-gate and disable-with-reason pattern | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `apps/web/src/screens/cockpit.rs:290-320` — the decide render | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `apps/web/src/screens/evals.rs:2779` — the sign-off decide render | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `crates/store/src/seed.rs:55-59` — the dev seed's member list | main@c8204432 |
| Code | `crates/actions/tests/support/mod.rs:291-355` — the existing `dev:reviewer` fixture | main@c8204432 |
| Test | `apps/web/e2e/cockpit.spec.ts`, `apps/web/e2e/evals.spec.ts` | main@c8204432 |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/approval_standalone.rs` (the review-decides scenario) | main@c8204432 |

## Baseline

## Claim

| Branch | `issue/357-console-self-gate` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the control follows the policy, and says why

- **P1.1** Given a pending gate the caller requested, when the cockpit or the eval tab renders it under `self_approval: forbidden`, then the decide control is **disabled with the reason** (as `/approvals` does), not hidden and not enabled.
  Verify: `apps/web/e2e/cockpit.spec.ts::a_self_gate_is_shown_but_not_decidable_in_the_cockpit`
- **P1.2** Given the tenant allows self-approval for that action, when the caller clicks Approve, then the decision is recorded and the pill moves off `pending`.

### P2 — the dev fixture can exercise dual control

The dev seed has **one** principal per tenant, so no spec can drive the two-person path that §5.4
actually requires.

### P1 — the READY process composes the draft artefact from the agent's answer
Requirement: a computed `documents.compose` step follows the agent step and stores `steps.1.output.output` as the document body with the card and project attached.

- **P1.1** Given a published process whose step 1 is an agent and step 2 is a computed `documents.compose` templated from `{{steps.1.output.output}}`, when the step runs, then a document exists whose body is the agent's answer and the step output carries its id.

  Verify: `runs.get` judge criteria on the proof run

issues.body:
## Symptom

`design-pack` fails on **every** push to main since `d011edb` ("docs: refresh the public issue registry and its derived data", #309). Measured 2026-11-18:

- main runs `44192734080` (`d011edb`) and `44194863888` (`c10d759`) — `design-pack` failure; run `44196440372` (`b7381ae`, current head) — same.
- Locally on the merged tree: `node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs` →
  `AssertionError: a non-built project has no open unit. + actual ['P0'] - expected []`.
- `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py` reproduces it: `uncovered=1`.

## Cause (measured)

The generator defines `uncovered` as a project whose status is NOT `built|archived|standing` AND whose open-unit count is 0 (`scripts/build-coverage.py:696-701`). P0 is the programme-definition project:

- its three units are now **CLOSED**: #120 (definition project and gate), #121 (author the definition set), #122 (the reuse map, architecture/analysis pack, inception standard);
- the refresh `d011edb` recomputed P0 to `units.open: 0` and `summary.projects.uncovered: ["P0"]`;
- P0's project status in the design data is not `built`/`standing`, so the assertion fires.

This blocks every PR in the repository (design-pack is a required check). It is a **design-data content decision**, not a code defect in the manifest pack: either

1. P0's status is updated (it is a *definition* project; `standing` or `built` may be the honest status now its three units are closed) — the data owner's call; or
2. the generator/check rule is amended for definition-only projects.

## Not caused by

Any open PR: `conveyor#318` (the scientific tenant gate) touches `apps/scientific` only; its `design-pack` red is this one, and its branch carries the merge of `b7381ae`.

## Goal

`apps/scientific` also owns the evidence-review family: a protocol-locked review with two blinded
reviewers, append-only decisions, a derived flow ledger and a hash-sealed inclusion-set export —
Rust, in this workspace, behind the same action registry and the same deployment.

## Plan / audit source

- ADR 0006 §Decision: `apps/scientific` absorbs the scientific research service (:8808) **and the
  evidence-review service (:8810)** — one evidence family, CPU-bound, one deployable, one database.
- ADR 0007 §1/§5: the estate completes in this workspace; analysis-shaped work is library code, and
  a stateful service keeps its own schema, database and role.
- The absorbed service's own README states the scope: `ER-001..ER-005` plus the `OUT-001` export
  contract, three invariants (a machine cannot decide; reviewer B cannot see reviewer A; history is
  append-only), 26 tables, and a canonical-hash seal.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` | main@c10d759 (blob 18afa65b) |
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0007-tool-estate-conveyor-and-coding.md` | main@c10d759 (blob 381f5091) |
| Plan | `docs/plans/04-TOOL-ESTATE-INVENTORY.md` §1/§5 | main@c10d759 (blob 8da5924b) |
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.4 (`analyse.*` boundary) | main@c10d759 (blob a8d2b66a) |
| Code | `apps/scientific/src/router/mod.rs` (the pattern for a tenant-gated route) | main@c10d759 |
| Code | `apps/scientific/tests/` (the crate's own test shape) | main@c10d759 |
| Capture | `docs/evidence/evidence-review-capture-2026-11-18.md` | `issue/319-evidence-review` @ `23fd7ab` |
| Source | the evidence-review service, revision `bac4f66` (2026-11-18) — identity recorded in the capture, not by repository path | private; recorded in P1 |

## Baseline

`main@c10d759` · measured 2026-11-17. The absorbed service was read at revision `bac4f66`
(2026-11-18; the issue's baseline commit `5e3a868` differs only in `uv.lock`): **60 operations**
over 10 route-bearing modules, **28 migrations**, and **47 tables** at the migration head. The 26
tables the retired production database held were measured before migrations `0019`–`0028`, which
add the outbox/jobs tables the README says never existed; the capture records the correction. The
repository is retired and its database roles were deleted on 2026-10-30, so the port creates the
schema and role it needs rather than inheriting them.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 capture | **landed** on `issue/319-evidence-review` @ `23fd7ab` | `docs/evidence/evidence-review-capture-2026-11-18.md`: 60 operations, 4 transport, 56 deferred, 0 ported; 47 tables |
| P2 schema | **landed** on `issue/319-evidence-review` @ `60f357f` | `apps/scientific/migrations/0001_evidence_review.sql` (47 tables, RLS, append-only) + `tests/evidence_review_schema.rs` — 4 tests green on Postgres 18 |
| P3 routes + invariants | ABSENT | no route, no actor seam, no blinding layers in `apps/scientific` |
| P4 export and seal | ABSENT | no inclusion-set export, no canonical-hash seal in Rust |
| P5 contract lock + parity | ABSENT | no operation is in the served lock; no parity table |
| P6 deploy | ABSENT | no Deployment anywhere runs the service; the namespace does not hold it |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the capture and the drop table
- **P1.1** Given the source at `5e3a868`, when the capture is written, then every operation carries
  its method, path, request/response schema and one state (`ported` / `dropped: transport` /
  `dropped: no consumer` / `dropped: deferred`) with a checkable ground.
  Verify: `ls docs/evidence/evidence-review-*.md` and
  `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_capture`.
- **P1.2** Given an operation that is not ported, when its row is read, then it names the conveyor
  surface that replaces it, the measured caller, or the decision that retired it — never an empty
  cell. Verify: the same capture test fails on an unaccounted or reasonless row.

### P2 — the schema, its RLS and its append-only history
- **P2.1** Given a fresh `evidence_review` database and its non-owner runtime role, when the
  migrations run, then the 47 tables exist, RLS is forced on every tenant table, and the runtime
  role cannot read another tenant's rows by naming it.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_schema -- rls`.
- **P2.2** Given an existing decision, when an `UPDATE` or `DELETE` reaches it through the runtime
  role, then the trigger raises and the row is unchanged.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_schema -- append_only`.

### P3 — the routes, the actor seam and the six blinding layers
- **P3.1** Given a caller presenting a tenant but no subject, when any decision route is invoked,
  then it is refused — no code path writes a decision without an authenticated human.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_reviews -- machine_cannot_decide`.
- **P3.2** Given reviewer B who owes a decision, when they read a queue, an aggregate, a count or a
  cursor derived from reviewer A's work, then they see their own assignments only; a missing record
  answers 404, never 403.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_reviews -- blinding`.
- **P3.3** Given an adjudication conflict, when a lead unbinds it, then an audit row is written
  before the resolution is returned. Verify: the same suite's `unblinding_writes_audit_first`.

### P4 — the inclusion-set export and its seal
- **P4.1** Given the same inclusion set, when the export is sealed twice, then the canonical hash is
  identical (RFC 8785), and a changed record changes the seal.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_exports -- seal`.
- **P4.2** Given an export read, when the ledger it cites has moved, then the read still serves the
  sealed bytes it recorded, not a re-derivation.
  Verify: the same suite's `a_seal_is_append_only`.

### P5 — the served contract and the parity gate
- **P5.1** Given the captured operations, when the served document is written, then every ported
  operation is in `served-spec.lock.json` and every dropped row carries its reason.
  Verify: `cargo run -p conveyor-scientific -- --print-openapi --check-lock` and the P1 test.
- **P5.2** Given one recorded review lifecycle, when it is replayed over the Rust routes, then the
  decisions, flow counts and export seal equal the recorded responses.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-scientific --test evidence_review_parity`.

### P6 — deployed and live
- **P6.1** Given the merged service, when it is deployed at one replica, then `/health/ready` is 200,
  a licence token names the tenant, and a bare `X-Tenant-Id` without a vouch is refused.
  Verify: the deployment's `kubectl` checks plus the recorded responses in the evidence document.
- **P6.2** Given the deployed service, when one review runs end to end, then two blinded reviewers,
  one conflict, one adjudication and one sealed export are recorded.
  Verify: `docs/evidence/2026-11-18-evidence-review-cutover.md` (one row per Verify, command and output).

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #212 | same app and deployment; this unit adds its own namespace/database | open |
| related | #154 | the analysis library the review family will call for content checks | open |

## Definition of ready

Baseline `main@c10d759` and the doc blob shas are named; every path resolves at that ref except the
capture (marked to create); every part has a BDD scenario with a `Verify:`; the two related issues
resolve; no `blocked-by` exists, so the state is `status:ready`; one PR scope — the library and its
tests are file-disjoint from every open unit (a new `apps/scientific/src/evidence_review/` subtree,
its own migrations and tests).

## Definition of done

Every scenario passes at the PR head with a row in `Evidence at completion`; the repo gate is green
at the exact head; tests added per part, none skipped; the capture and the cutover document are
committed; the migration ledger and `--check-lock` are handled; live verification (after the deploy)
is recorded; one PR `Closes #<this issue>` MERGED, issue closed, branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- XLSX import, automatic exclusion ranking, the proposal lane, appraisals and any regulatory
  canonical surface — all deliberately absent from the source's own README; not restored here.
- The `8811` research-output service and the outbox/durable-jobs packages — separate packages, not
  this service's tables.
- Any change to the conductor, the action registry or the UI — the family is served by this app.

## Deployment prerequisite

A fresh `evidence_review` database and a non-owner runtime role (the old role was deleted
2026-10-30), created with `gitops-production/scripts/host-configs/worker4/postgres/provision-service-db.sh`
(born-locked), and a namespace/Deployment in the `apps/scientific` group's manifests.

## Open questions

1. The source mounted `:8810` as a second process; the group is one deployable and one image, so
   this port mounts the review routes on the same service rather than a second port. Confirm at P5.
2. The blinding layers are properties of queries and of one read function, not of a role; the port
   keeps them as structural tests, not as a comment. Recorded in P3.

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Scenario | Command / test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

| Part | State | Evidence |

| The compose failure is a 500 store error | BROKEN | worker log: `store failure: … insert or update on table "document" violates foreign key constraint "document_created_by_fk"` |

passes on a live run: `documents.compose` succeeds, the judge accepts, the card moves.

<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->

## Goal

A capability-agent run finishes inside its 300 s contract budget, fails typed when it does not, and
delivers its artefact by calling a tool — instead of answering in text and passing.

## Plan / audit source

`docs/plans/01-CONTRACT.md` §17 (caps: 8/20 turns, 20/50 tool calls, 300 s; typed failures),
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.4 (action families) and §12 T13 (the tool spine is where a job calls tools),
`docs/evidence/2026-11-10-plan-audit.md` (the engine's measured ceiling).

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/307-engine-budget` |
| HEAD | `85778be` |
| Session | claude-code (mini3) — engine budget |
| Updated | 2026-11-17 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Contract | `docs/plans/01-CONTRACT.md` §17 (caps, typed failures) | `origin/main` |
| Code | `crates/workflow/src/agent.rs` `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`, `Reply::Elapsed` | `origin/main` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/workflow/agent.rs:541` `drive()` — the loop; the deadline is checked only at the top of an iteration | `origin/main` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs:113` `timeout_ms: 300_000` — equal to the agent cap | `origin/main` |
| Code | `crates/store/src/prompts/agent_v1.md` — the executor instruction | `origin/main` |
| Code | `crates/store/src/prompts/mod.rs` `BUILTIN_PROMPTS` — a change is a new version | `origin/main` |
| Issue | #97 (the A5 live engine proof, needs-human) | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `origin/main`, measured 2026-11-17.
- Live: 50 capability agents, all `local-llm`, 300 s / 12 turns; 0 runs in flight at measurement.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-17, 17:34–19:23Z)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| The cap is not a wall clock | BROKEN | a run reported `agent.timeout: the agent ran 347753 ms; its cap is 300000 ms`; a second run was still `running` 353 s after its step started |
| Per-call timeout equals the agent cap | BROKEN | the inference action declares `timeout_ms: 300_000`, so one slow call can consume the whole budget |
| Turns × latency exceed the budget | MEASURED | 12–17 inference calls per run, every call `outcome=ok`, 20–60 s each (max 114 s), prompt 31–51 k tokens, `cache_status=miss` |
| A text-only answer passes | MEASURED | all seven succeeded runs: `turns=1`, `tool_calls=[]`; the acceptance is a text judgement |
| A hung step holds the single worker | MEASURED | `deploy/conveyor-worker` is 1/1; while one step ran, no scheduled job materialised and a second run's step stayed `queued` |
| An in-flight call ignores the cap | MEASURED | a run whose step began 19:23:26 was still `running` at 405 s and was cancelled at 593 s; its 300 s cap passed at 19:28:26 and nothing stopped it |
| The cap is per attempt, not per run | MEASURED | the same run lived 938 s in total: each retryable 5xx starts a fresh loop and a fresh 300 s, and no run-level deadline exists |
| A rollout orphans a step's idempotency claim | MEASURED | a run failed `idempotency-conflict: a request with this Idempotency-Key is still running` after the worker was replaced mid-call |

## The live failure underneath (measured 2026-11-17 19:27–19:33Z)

The worker log names the upstream, not the loop:

```
job failed  kind=process.step  permanent=false  failure="action-upstream-failed: inference answered 524"
```

It repeats every ~4 minutes, and the run never reaches a terminal state: a retryable 5xx leaves
the step `running` for the job to retry, and a run has no total deadline. A direct GET to
`api.nonagentic.ai/inference-router` answers **401 in 0.14–0.23 s**, so the service is up — the
model call itself runs past the CDN's response window and is cut as 524.

Consequence for this unit: the wall-clock guard below is necessary but not sufficient. With the
upstream returning 524, a run cannot finish at all; that is an inference-router/edge concern
(streaming, a direct origin path, or a faster model), not an `agent.run` one. It is recorded here
so the guard is never mistaken for a fix of the 524.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the budget is a wall clock, not a between-turns check

Wrap each model call and each tool call in `drive()` (`crates/actions/src/workflow/agent.rs`) in a
`tokio::time::timeout` over the **remaining** budget, so an in-flight call cannot outlive the cap.

- Acceptance: a slow model call returns `agent.timeout` at the cap, not after it, and the error
  names elapsed ≤ cap + one poll.
- `Verify:` the new unit test with a fake model that sleeps past the cap asserts the typed error.
- `Verify:` a live run terminates at or before 300 s (+ 10 s of poll grace).

### P2 — one call cannot consume the agent budget (decided: not by lowering the timeout)

Analysed after the measurement: lowering the inference action's `timeout_ms` would turn a
slow-but-successful call into a retryable 5xx, and the executor retries a 5xx under the same
idempotency key — a re-buy loop, not a fix. P1's wall-clock guard already bounds an in-flight call
by the remaining budget, so the per-call timeout stays at the agent ceiling; the measured slow
calls (max 114 s) are not the failure mode.

- Acceptance: no change to `inference.chat`'s spec; the guard in P1 is what bounds a call.
- `Verify:` the P1 test covers the in-flight case.

### P3 — the acceptance requires the artefact

The loop's output carries `tool_calls`, and the judge reads it; make the acceptance use it:

- publish `agent@2` (a **new** version of the executor prompt: the step's work is done with the
  tools it names, and a final summary is valid only after the required calls) and point the
  capability agents' `prompt_ref` at it;
- publish `architecture_task.ready@10` with an acceptance criterion and DoD check that name the
  `documents.compose` call, so a text-only answer is rejected.

- Acceptance: a run whose model answers in text with zero tool calls is **rejected**; a run that
  calls `documents.compose` and answers is accepted.
- `Verify:` `procedures.get` shows the new acceptance criteria at the published version;
  `capability_agents.get` shows `prompt_ref = agent@2`.
- The seed never edits a published row: `agent@1` and `architecture_task.ready@9` stay readable.

### P4 — the proof

One live run on a scratch project: ≥1 recorded tool call (`documents.compose`), judge accept, card
moved, scratch project closed. Evidence rows (run time, turns, tool names, judge score) go in the
issue; the ids stay on the card, never in this public repository.

## Dependencies

None. This is engine content and a code path; no programme project gates it. #97 is related, not
a blocker. It does not change a CONTRACT §17 number.

## Definition of done

- [ ] P1 and P2 merged with tests; `scripts/ci/gate.sh` green locally and CI green at the PR head.
- [ ] P3 published as new versions, live agents repointed, both old versions still readable.
- [ ] P4's run recorded here and on its card; a zero-tool run is demonstrably rejected.
- [ ] The scratch project is closed; no live id appears in this repository.

## Goal

The programme's structured intermediate outputs — the definition set, benefit profiles and the
benefits map, tranche plans and reviews, stakeholder profiles, benefit realization, WBS, baselines,
registers, cadence and typed project dependencies — can be created, read, updated and removed in the
console, and are served read-only on the public design site. P0's first-tranche authorisation is
recorded and P0 is closed, so T1–T17's build units are no longer gated.

## Plan / audit source

  the upsert is refused.

Requirement: the unauthenticated snapshot carries the tenant's structured programme rows, with

  Verify: `apps/server/tests/snapshot_deterministic.rs` (redaction case)
- **P2.3** Live: `GET https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/data/snapshot.js` returns an `msp`
  object with the live benefits, tranches, stakeholders, links, baselines, WBS, registers and
  cadences.
  Verify: `curl … | jq '.msp | keys'`

### P3 — the console surfaces are live and public

`docs/design/README.md` · `docs/design/v2.js`
Requirement: the Programme definition page (five tabs), the Plan MSP tabs and the Portfolio
programme/dependency surfaces read the live store signed in, write through actions, and render the
snapshot read-only when signed out — with zero `/api/` requests.

- **P3.1** Signed in, a benefit can be created, edited, linked, unlinked and deleted from the
  Programme definition page; each write re-reads the row.

  review dialog names the published `tranche-review` document.

  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` (the plan/portfolio wire cases).

  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` (signed-out zero-request assertion)

  change.
  Verify: `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check && node docs/design/scripts/check-coverage.cjs`

### P1 — a declared expected output blocks close until it is published

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.4 · §10.3 — Requirement: `projects.close` reads the project's `meta.expected_outputs`, resolves each category to a published active document on that project, and refuses with `409 closure_outputs_missing` naming every category that is not published; nothing is written on refusal.

- **P1.1** Given a project whose `meta.expected_outputs` names a category with no published active document, when `projects.close` is called, then it returns 409 `closure_outputs_missing` naming that category and the project stays active.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test --locked -p conveyor-actions --test closure_gate an_expected_output_blocks_close` (to create)

  Verify: `rbuild -- test --locked -p conveyor-actions --test closure_gate a_project_without_a_declaration_is_unchanged`

  Verify: `rbuild -- test --locked -p conveyor-actions --test closure_gate a_draft_deleted_or_foreign_output_does_not_count`

### P2 — the class's closure outputs are required too

`seed/output-standard.json` — Requirement: the same read applies to `meta.closure_outputs` (e.g. `evidence`, `closure-review`), so a class that declares a closure review cannot close without it published.

  Verify: `rbuild -- test --locked -p conveyor-actions --test closure_gate a_missing_closure_review_blocks_close`

  Verify: `rbuild -- test --locked -p conveyor-actions --test closure_gate a_class_without_closure_outputs_is_unchanged`

### P3 — the refusal is a gate, not a report

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.4 — Requirement: the refusal writes no project status change, no run and no approval, and it names each missing category (not a count); P0's class is the worked example because its only missing output today is the owner's `tranche-review`.
