## Goal

A PR that belongs to us never asks a human for a review it does not need, and a workflow run parked
at `action_required` is approved — or listed as unattributable — without a human; queue builds are
neither cancelled by concurrency nor delayed by the 20-minute `design-pack`.

## Plan / audit source

Owner-approved delivery design, 2026-11-17 (hybrid: a repo-native workflow owns review requests and
parked runs; the fleet janitor keeps merge authority). In-repo contract:
`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "The PR — exactly one". Precedent:
`issue-registry.yml`'s self-approval of its own parked run. The design document is held with the
session plans and is deliberately not committed.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/300-delivery-approvals` |
| HEAD | `042e9e7cd1812504b7bc32e93faa80f709ad4659` |
| Session | `m4/georgedekker (claim nonce 93900AE1-E356-4CF0-B315-0AA0D6A9B3E8)` |
| Updated | `2026-11-17` |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "The PR — exactly one" | main@a686519 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `on` / `concurrency` / `design-pack` | main@a686519 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` step "approve the parked run" | main@a686519 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/delivery.yml` | to create (PR head `042e9e7`) |
| Code | `.github/CODEOWNERS` | main@a686519 |
| Issue | #207 — the `merge_group` trigger; merged by the queue itself | closed |
| Issue | #292 — a parked run that needed a hand approval | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@a686519ee4f15efe2393f4f38cb1426c0f985681`, measured 2026-11-17
- Docs: `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` blob `d71ff017606c72fe56178a8b11b51bc1e0ef3763` ·
  `ci-public.yml` blob `baa0172b0c27d31e913922a695017b79218437e1` ·
  `issue-registry.yml` blob `febea2eed6dc11b0dae9a9b93989737dba51bb1b` ·
  `.github/CODEOWNERS` blob `ddfee7be0c763e969c9c10d529727aa7081a478b` (at head `042e9e7`)

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 review requests cleared | ABSENT | no workflow dismisses a request; the request that actually reached the inbox is CODEOWNERS' `*` line (see P1.4) |
| P2 parked runs swept | ABSENT | `issue-registry.yml` approves only its own run; #292's run waited ~18 h on 2026-11-16 |
| P3 queue builds not cancelled | ABSENT | `ci-public.yml:37` was true for every `merge_group` ref |
| P4 design-pack off the queue path | ABSENT | `ci-public.yml:213-214` guard was only `!github.event.repository.private` |
| P5 policy text | ABSENT | `03-DELIVERY.md:288-309` had no queue rule and no review-request rule |
| P1.4 blanket CODEOWNERS request | ABSENT | `.github/CODEOWNERS:9` `* @nonagenticai/maintainers` requested the team on **every** PR while `require_code_owner_review: false`; the Actions token cannot resolve the team node, so nothing could dismiss it (DELETE → 422 "Could not resolve to a node") |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — Review requests are cleared automatically

`docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "The PR — exactly one" · design A2 (dismiss job)

Requirement: a review request on one of our PRs is deleted unless a human decision is pending.

- **P1.1** Given an open PR authored by one of ours from a same-repo head, with a requested
  reviewer and no `status:needs-human` label, when `delivery` runs, then `reviewRequests` is empty
  and the job summary names what was removed.
  Verify: `gh pr view <n> -R nonagenticai/conveyor --json reviewRequests --jq '.reviewRequests|length'` → `0`
- **P1.2** Given a PR carrying `status:needs-human`, when `delivery` runs, then its review requests
  are untouched.
  Verify: `gh pr view <n> -R nonagenticai/conveyor --json labels,reviewRequests` → request still present
- **P1.3** Given a PR whose head is a fork, when `delivery` runs, then nothing is changed.
  Verify: `gh pr view <n> -R nonagenticai/conveyor --json headRepositoryOwner,reviewRequests` → unchanged
- **P1.4** Given the CODEOWNERS file with no catch-all line, when a PR that touches no owned path
  opens, then it carries no review request at all.
  Verify: `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token -u georgiedekker) gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"nonagenticai",name:"conveyor"){pullRequest(number:<n>){reviewRequests{totalCount}}}}'` → `0`
- **P1.5** Given a PR that **does** touch an owned path, when `delivery` runs, then the CODEOWNERS
  request is named and left in place, and the job does not fail.
  Verify: the run summary shows `kept — a CODEOWNERS team request needs a human`; step conclusion success.

### P2 — Parked runs are approved, or named and left alone

design A2 (sweep job) · precedent `issue-registry.yml`

Requirement: an `action_required` run of this repo's workflow, for this repo's open PR by an allowed
author, is approved hourly; anything unattributable is listed and never approved.

- **P2.1** Given a same-repo `pull_request` run of one of this repo's workflows parked at
  `action_required` for an open PR by an allowed author, when the hourly sweep runs, then the run is
  approved and the summary names it.
  Verify: `gh run view <id> -R nonagenticai/conveyor --json status,conclusion` → not `action_required`
- **P2.2** Given a parked run whose head repository is not this repo, when the sweep runs, then the
  run stays `action_required` and the summary lists it as unattributable.
  Verify: `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs/<id> --jq .status` → `action_required`

### P3 — A queue build is never cancelled by concurrency

`ci-public.yml:35-37`

- **P3.1** Given a `merge_group` run in progress, when a second run for the same ref is requested,
  then the first is not cancelled.
  Verify: `gh api 'repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs?event=merge_group' --jq '[.workflow_runs[]|select(.conclusion=="cancelled")]|length'` → `0`

### P4 — design-pack is off the queue's critical path

`ci-public.yml:213-214`

- **P4.1** Given a queue build, when it runs, then `design-pack` is skipped and the six required
  contexts still report.
  Verify: `gh run view <id> -R nonagenticai/conveyor --json jobs --jq '[.jobs[].name]|map(select(.=="design-pack"))|length'` → `0`

### P5 — the policy is written down

`03-DELIVERY.md` § "The PR — exactly one" · `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "Accept"

- **P5.1** Given the documents at the PR head, when read, then they state the enqueue rule (never
  `--delete-branch`; confirm with `isInMergeQueue` or `state`, never an exit code) and the
  review-request rule (`status:needs-human` is the only way a human is asked).
  Verify: `git show <head>:docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md | grep -c 'status:needs-human'` → ≥ `1`

## Dependencies

- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `Blocker:` line (this issue is not blocked).
- [x] One-PR scope: one new workflow, two lines in `ci-public.yml`, CODEOWNERS, two docs.
- [x] Scope corrections: none apply (no old-system work in this unit).

## Definition of done

## Out of scope

  outstanding requests, and a bot cannot approve its own PR.

## Goal

`apps/scientific` resolves the caller's tenant from a bare `X-Tenant-Id` with no credential. The reference it replaces ran `ENABLE_AUTH=true` and introspected licence tokens (`LICENSE_INTROSPECT_URL`, `SCIENTIFIC_PROCESSOR_ONBEHALF_SUBJECTS` are both already in its Deployment env). Until the gate is restored, the Rust service cannot serve production traffic: `scientific-processor`'s NetworkPolicy admits the whole pod CIDR (10.42.0.0/16) to 8808, so any in-cluster pod can partition — and read or clear — another tenant's cached results by naming it.

Same class as #226 (media); found while deploying #212.

## Measured state (2026-11-17)

- `apps/scientific/src/router/mod.rs::caller_tenant` reads `x-tenant-id`, validates only its shape (`safe_segment`), and returns it. No `Authorization`, no introspection, no vouch.
- The tenant scopes the process-global cache (`router/cache.rs`, `cache::key_tenant`): a caller naming another tenant can read or clear that tenant's entries. The service has no database (nothing surviving writes a row), so no persistent rows are exposed — the impact is cache contents and compute.
- The reference's gate: licence tokens travel in `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <token>` (introspected); a bare tenant needs an allowlisted service-token vouch (`src/auth/vouch.py`); no default tenant. The Rust port has none of it.
- NetworkPolicy `scientific-processor`: ingress from `10.42.0.0/16` on 8808.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the reference's gate, restored (mirror #226)
- **P1.1** Given no credential, when a tenant-scoped operation is served, then 401 and nothing cached or returned. **Verify:** `apps/scientific/tests/tenant.rs::no_credential_is_refused` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <licence>`, when served, then the tenant is the active licence's own; inactive/unknown → 401. **Verify:** `tests/tenant.rs::a_licence_token_names_the_tenant` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a bare `X-Tenant-Id`, when served without an allowlisted service token, then 401/403; with one, the NAMED tenant (never the licence's). **Verify:** `tests/tenant.rs::a_service_token_scopes_the_tenant` (to create)

### P2 — the deployment runs
- **P2.1** Given the merged gate, when the image is deployed at 1 replica, then `/health/ready` is 200 and the three credential shapes answer as the tests pin. **Verify:** the deployment repo's `kubectl` checks + the recorded responses.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocks | #212 | the deployment cannot run live (P2.2/P2.3) before this | open |

## Definition of done

- The three scenarios pass at the merged head; the image is published and deployed at 1 replica; #212's blocked live scenarios are unblocked and recorded there.
- Integration test harness: the #226 introspection stub pattern (`apps/research/tests/common`) is reusable.

## Out of scope

- The media and licences services (their own gates are done / #261).
- Any change to the 18 surviving operations or their contract.

issues.body:
## Goal

Every `effect = destructive` action in the registry is refused without an approved approval that names **that exact object**, unless the tenant's policy waives it — enforced once, at the invoke boundary, instead of by a hand-written call in three handlers. The gate becomes **spec-declared and policy-driven**, so a new destructive action cannot ship ungated and a tenant can decide which ones need four eyes.

Owner ruling 2026-11-17: gate **all 27** ungated destructive actions, and make it **policy-driven** — no hardcoded per-action exceptions.

## Plan / audit source

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.4 (effect classes: destructive = approval + dry-run + dual control), §5.4 (a requester cannot decide the gate that judges their own work), §10.4 (`approvals` and `approval_policies.list|get|set` families).

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/282-destructive-gate` |
| HEAD | `54d69f9` |
| Session | claude-code (m4) |
| Updated | 2026-11-17 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.4, §5.4, §10.4 | main@c33b403 (`06acbac`) |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/spec.rs:ActionSpec` / `Effect` (`58363e6`) — the spec the gate reads | main@c33b403 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs::require_approval_tx` (`c76c951`) — today's hand-called gate | main@c33b403 |
| Code | `crates/store/src/approval.rs:808-817` (`baa4120`) — the unconditional self-approval refusal | main@c33b403 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs:702` (`a9273b6`) — the one path every action takes | main@c33b403 |
| Code | `crates/actions-derive/src/lib.rs` — the `#[crate::action]` attributes | main@c33b403 |
| Issue | `#171` — the gate this generalises; `#172` — the first destructive family to migrate | closed |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/destructive_gate.rs` · `crates/actions/tests/approval_policies.rs` | to create |

## Baseline

Code `main@c33b403`, measured 2026-11-17.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 the gate's placement | PARTIAL | `require_approval_tx` is called by exactly 3 handlers (`ops.restart`, `ops.scale`, `ops.rollback`); **27 other actions declare `effect = "destructive"` and call nothing** |
| P2 the policy layer | ABSENT | `git grep approval_polic` over `crates/` and `migrations/` → 0; §10.4 declares `approval_policies.list\|get\|set` |
| P3 self-approval | HARDCODED | `store/approval.rs:808-817` refuses the requester unconditionally, with no policy consulted |
| P4 the target | PER-ACTION, HAND-WRITTEN | `ops` builds `namespace/deployment/name/op` in `writes.rs::target_of`; no other destructive action has one |
| P5 `approvals.request` | PARTIAL | takes a caller-supplied `target` string (`approvals.rs:322-334`); a caller that cannot compute one has no path |

## Design note — the approval is a property of the CALL, not the payload

Every action input is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, so a generic gate cannot add an `approval_id`
to the payload of the 27: their schemas would reject it, and adding the field to each struct is the
per-action work this unit exists to avoid. The id therefore moves **out of `input`** into the call:

- `InvokeRequest` gains `approval_id: Option<Uuid>`; `HandlerCtx` exposes it.
- The HTTP body becomes `{"input": …, "approval_id": "…"}` (`POST /api/actions/{name}/invocations`);
  MCP carries it the same way. Both are additions, not renames — an old body still parses.
- `ops.restart`, `ops.scale`, `ops.rollback` and `ops.host_restart_unit` lose `approval_id` from
  their input structs and read `ctx.approval_id`; their tests move with them.

This is the reason this unit is more than a macro change, and it is why it lands before the 27.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the spec-declared target, enforced at the invoke boundary

Requirement: `ActionSpec` carries an `approval_target` — a function from the input to the canonical target string — declared by the action macro. `invoke()` refuses every `Effect::Destructive` action that arrives without a matching approved approval, **before dispatch**, so the gate cannot be forgotten by a handler.

- **P1.1** Given any registered action whose `effect` is `destructive`, when it is invoked with no `approval_id`, then it answers `403 approval_required` and no backend is touched.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/destructive_gate.rs::every_destructive_action_is_refused_without_an_approval`
- **P1.2** Given an approved approval whose target names another object, when the action runs, then it answers `403 approval_wrong_target`.
  Verify: same file → `::an_approval_for_another_target_is_refused`
- **P1.3** Given the registry, when the guard runs, then every destructive action WITH a declared target is gated, and every destructive action without one is listed explicitly in a burn-down constant — so the remaining 27 are visible rather than silent. The strict form (no list at all) is #283's, once the targets exist.
  Verify: same file → `::the_ungated_destructive_set_is_exactly_the_burn_down_list`
- **P1.4** Given a target function, when it is called twice with the same input, then the string is identical (the approval is deterministic, never clock- or id-derived).
  Verify: same file → `::the_target_is_deterministic`

### P2 — the policy layer

Requirement: an `approval_policy` row per (tenant, action) with `approval: required|waived` (default **required**) and `self_approval: forbidden|allowed` (default **forbidden**), managed by `approval_policies.list|get|set`. `approvals.request` computes the target server-side when given an action + input, so no caller types a target string.

- **P2.1** Given a tenant with no policy rows, when a destructive action is invoked with an approved approval, then it runs; when invoked with none, then it is refused — the default is `required`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/approval_policies.rs::the_default_policy_is_required`
- **P2.2** Given a policy set to `waived` for one action, when that action is invoked with no approval, then it runs and every other destructive action is still refused.
  Verify: same file → `::a_waived_policy_covers_only_its_action`
- **P2.3** Given `self_approval: allowed`, when the requester decides their own gate, then the decision is recorded; with the default `forbidden` the same call answers `403` (§5.4 preserved as a default, not a hardcode).
  Verify: same file → `::self_approval_is_a_policy_never_a_hardcode`
- **P2.4** Given `approvals.request` with `action` + `input`, when it returns, then `meta.target` is the spec-computed target and the caller never supplied it.
  Verify: same file → `::a_request_computes_the_target_it_will_need`
- **P2.5** `approval_policies.set|get|list` round-trip within the tenant and are invisible across tenants.
  Verify: same file → `::policies_are_tenant_scoped`

## Dependencies

| Kind | Issue | State |
|---|---|---|
| related | #171 | closed — the gate being generalised |
| related | #172 | the first family that will move onto it |
| blocks | the 27-action adoption | created when this issue is claimed |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline `main@c33b403` and blob shas for every cited file.
- [x] Every part carries a `Verify:` naming a test that will exist.
- [x] Dependencies typed: no `blocked-by` — this is the mechanism, and nothing constructs before it.
- [x] One-PR scope: the spec attribute + macro, the invoke-boundary gate, migration `0048_approval_policies.sql`, the three policy actions, the `approvals.request` target computation, the `approvals.decide` policy check, and their tests.
- [x] The migration number is `0048`: `0046` is T2's `decision_ladder` and `0047` is #172's `host_registry` (measured 2026-11-17).
- [x] The default is stated and safe: `required` + `self_approval: forbidden` — the §11.4 rule survives as the default, and a tenant opts out per action.
- [x] Not in this PR, and named: the 27 handlers' target declarations (the adoption issue) and the web UI's destructive flow (its own issue).

## Definition of done

- P1–P2 accepted, local gate green, one PR.
- The `ops.*` writes and `ops.host_restart_unit` lose their hand-written gate calls and behave identically (their tests stay green unchanged).
- A live proof after merge: one `ops.restart` refused with no approval, allowed with one, and refused again under a `waived` policy temporarily set and then restored.

## Out of scope

- Declaring targets for the 27 pre-existing destructive actions (the adoption issue).
- The web UI's request→decide→invoke flow (its own issue).
- The copilot proposal binding (its own issue).

## Goal

A generated registry pull request arrives with its required checks actually running, without a
maintainer having to find and approve the parked run by hand.

## Current state (measured)

`main@03472af`, measured 2026-11-17.

- `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:175-183` polls six times, 5 s apart, for a `pull_request`
  run whose `conclusion` is already `action_required`.
- Run 44058943794 pushed `39223b9` at 09:49:51Z. The `pull_request` run 44059172812 was created at
  09:49:56Z, but it had not settled to `action_required` before the last poll (~09:50:23Z), so the
  step took its fallback and dispatched `ci` (run 44059254592) — whose checks do **not** associate
  with the pull request. PR #271 therefore had no required contexts and could not merge.
- The run remained approvable afterwards: `POST repos/.../actions/runs/44059172812/approve`
  returned `{}` and the run moved to `queued`. The approval API is fine; only the window is short.
- The failure is not rare by accident: with `on.push` every merge to `main` can now produce a
  generated PR, so the race is exercised on every issue-closing merge.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:175-183` — the poll | main@03472af (blob `d04dcf7`) |
| Run | `44058943794` — pushed `39223b9` at 09:49:51Z, fallback dispatch at 09:50:27Z | — |
| Run | `44059172812` — the parked run, created 09:49:56Z, approved manually later | — |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the poll outlives the run's settling time

Widen the window to at least three minutes (the run settles in well under one) and keep the same
match, so the same approval path runs without a human.

- **P1.1** Given a generated pull request, when its `pull_request` run settles, then the step
  approves it and its summary says `Approved the parked pull_request run`.
  Verify: the run's step summary, and `gh pr checks <generated>` shows the required contexts.
- **P1.2** Given the workflow file, when the poll is read, then its iterations × interval are at
  least 180 s.
  Verify: `sed -n '/parked=""/,/^          if \[ -n "\$parked" \]/p' .github/workflows/issue-registry.yml`
- **P1.3** Given the change, when the workflow is linted, then actionlint 1.7.12 reports nothing and
  the patch has no whitespace error.
  Verify: `actionlint .github/workflows/issue-registry.yml && git diff --check`

## Dependencies

None. One file.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named: `main@03472af`, measured 2026-11-17.
- [x] Every reference resolves at `main@03472af`.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] No dependencies; one-file scope.

## Definition of done

- [ ] P1.1–P1.3 pass at the PR head, each with a row.
- [ ] CI `lint` and `checks` green at the PR head.
- [ ] One PR with `Closes #<n>` merged; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- The cost of the generated PR's full Rust suite (`seed/programme.json` is not docs-only, and
  `crates/store/tests/seed_programme.rs` reads it, so it must not be reclassified). Owner decision.

## Claim

## Goal

conveyor builds on Rust **1.100.0** — the owner's estate-wide pin — so its compiler matches every other Rust repo, and the Dockerfiles stop claiming 1.99.0.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-17)

- `rust-toolchain.toml` channel = `1.99.0`; `Dockerfile:11` and `docker/Dockerfile.service:10` pin `ARG RUST_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.0`.
- The `checks` job in `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` **asserts** the root Dockerfile's ARG equals `rust-toolchain.toml`, so the pin and the ARG must move together or CI fails on a mismatch.
- Owner direction, 2026-11-17: *"we use 1.100.x rust now, for all rust repos"*. `1.100.0` is the only release in that line (`channel-rust-1.100.1` and `-1.100.2` are 404), and `agent`, `strata_ingest`, `strata_rag`, `care-bus-agents`, `nonagenticai_mcp_server` already pin exactly it.
- m1 (the build host) has `1.100.0` installed with rustfmt + clippy; `rbuild --gate` on this branch ran under it.

## Acceptance (BDD)

Given the branch's `rust-toolchain.toml` names `1.100.0`
When `rbuild --gate` runs on m1
Then fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, nextest + doctests and `cargo audit` all pass under that compiler.

Given the branch is pushed
When the `checks` job runs
Then the Dockerfile ARG assertion passes (pin and both Dockerfiles agree).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `rust-toolchain.toml`, `Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.service` all say `1.100.0`
- [ ] `rbuild --gate` green on the branch
- [ ] CI `checks` job green on the PR
- [ ] one PR, `Closes #<this issue>`

## Goal

A capability agent whose row allows a 300-second turn actually gets it: `inference.chat`'s action bound must not be shorter than the agent's own timeout, or every slow model turn is rolled back at 60 seconds and the agent's bound is unreachable.

## Plan / audit source

- `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs` — `chat_spec` sets `timeout_ms: 60_000`; three unit tests assert that value.
- `crates/actions/src/workflow/agent.rs` — the loop's bound is `capability_agent.timeout_secs * 1000` (database allows 1..=300), and it checks elapsed time between turns; a single model call is bounded by the action's own timeout.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/270-inference-timeout` |
| HEAD | `0299adf` |
| Session | claude-code (mini3) |
| Updated | 2026-11-17 |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs::chat_spec` | main@87639c0 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/workflow/agent.rs::resolve` (`bound_timeout_ms`) | main@87639c0 |
| Test | `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs` `#[cfg(test)]` (the 60_000 assertions) | main@87639c0 |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@87639c0`, measured 2026-11-17.
- Live: the tenant's agents were raised to `timeout_secs = 300`; the served model generates at 2–8 tokens/s. Worker logs record `action-timeout: "inference.chat" did not finish within 60000 ms; the transaction was rolled back` on every agent turn that runs longer than a minute. The agent's 300-second bound is therefore unreachable, and a turn cannot persist anything.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — the action bound matches the agent bound | ABSENT | `chat_spec` hard-codes 60_000; the agent row allows 300_000 |
| P2 — a slow turn completes | BLOCKED by P1 | the worker rolls the invocation back at 60 s and retries; no tool call or artefact can land |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — one bound for the model call
Requirement: `inference.chat`'s action timeout is 300 000 ms — the maximum an agent row may declare — so the agent's own bound governs the loop and the action protects only against a hung call.
- **P1.1** Given the action spec, when it is built, then `timeout_ms` is 300 000 and the existing assertions agree.
  Verify: `rbuild -- nextest -p conveyor-actions --lib integrations::inference`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #177 | the same loop's tool surface (closed) | closed |
| related | #198 | the same loop's judge request (closed) | closed |
| blocks | — | the SOP acceptance rollout waits on this | — |

## Definition of ready

- [x] The scenario has a `Verify:` command and a test target.
- [x] References resolve at the named commit.
- [x] One-PR scope: one constant and its assertions.

## Definition of done

- [ ] The scenario passes at the PR head; one evidence row.
- [ ] The repo gate is green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate`).
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` merged; branch deleted.
- [ ] A live agent turn longer than 60 s completes and records its output (evidence on this issue, no live ids in the repo).

## Out of scope

- The model's throughput, the router's ladder, and the vLLM parser (a separate serving-layer change).
- Per-action or per-tenant timeout configuration; this is the single shared bound.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the price catalogue carries a unit
- **P1.1** Given a price row, when its unit is `token`, then its token rates are set and `unit_usd`
  is NULL; when its unit is `image`, `character` or `second`, then `unit_usd` is set and the token
  rates are 0.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test inference_`
- **P1.2** Given the migration, when it runs on an existing database, then `local-llm` keeps its
  0.14/0.28 rates and unit `token`, and the three media rows are seeded with a dated source.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test s16_schema --test s07_schema` and the
  embedded-set assertion in `crates/store/src/migrate.rs`

### P2 — the ledger names the surface
- **P2.1** Given a successful `media.generate_image`, `produce.speech` or `media.transcribe`, when the
  engine captures the call, then the ledger row's `model` is `image_gen`, `tts` or `asr` respectively
  (never `unrouted`), and `served_model` is NULL.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test generate_image --test speech_transcribe`
- **P2.2** Given a token `completions.create`, when it is captured, then its model identity is
  unchanged (`coalesce(served_model, model)` exactly as today).
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test inference_capture --test inference`

### P3 — the unit is recorded
- **P3.1** Given image generation, when it succeeds, then `usage_unit='image'` and
  `usage_units = data.len()`.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test generate_image`
- **P3.2** Given speech synthesis, when it succeeds, then `usage_unit='character'` and
  `usage_units = input.text.chars().count()`.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test speech_transcribe`
- **P3.3** Given transcription of a WAV, when it succeeds, then `usage_unit='second'` and
  `usage_units` is the WAV duration; given a non-WAV upload, then `usage_units` is NULL (unpriced,
  never $0).
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test speech_transcribe` plus the pure
  `wav_duration_secs` unit test

### P4 — the report prices the unit
- **P4.1** Given a media call with a price row and `usage_units`, when the report runs, then
  `cost_usd = usage_units × unit_usd`, it counts in `priced_calls`, and not in `unpriced_calls`.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test inference_`
- **P4.2** Given a media call with NULL units (non-WAV) or no price row, when the report runs, then
  it is `unpriced_calls` and contributes zero to `cost_usd`.
  Verify: same
- **P4.3** Given a bucket that mixes token and non-token calls, when the report runs, then the USD
  sum is exact and the bucket's `unit`/`units` are NULL (no fake unit total).
  Verify: same
- **P4.4** Given a uniform non-token bucket, when the report runs, then it carries the bucket's
  `unit` and the summed `units`.
  Verify: same

### P5 — the console shows it
- **P5.1** Given the usage screen, when a bucket has units, then a Units column renders the kind and
  count; when a call is unpriced, then it reads "unpriced", never $0.
  Verify: `cd apps/web && npm run e2e -- e2e/usage.spec.ts`

### P6 — the deployed report keeps its token figures and carries the new fields

## Goal

The inception standard is a **gate, not advice**: a delivery project's build run cannot start until
its `analysis` and `architecture` outputs are published (P0's per-project inception standard). The
buildout's own T1–T17 projects and every tenant delivery project are subject to it, so TOGAF's
"analysis, then architecture, then build" order is enforced by the engine and not by a session's
memory.

## Plan / audit source

`docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §5 (the inception standard) · `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (a
delivery project's design gate needs the contract governing it) · §12 T12 · `seed/programme.json`
`meta.expected_outputs` (T projects carry `project-brief`, `inception-analysis` and
`architecture-design` once #221 / PR #262 lands).

Measured 2026-11-17 on `main@87639c0`:

- `crates/actions/src/programme.rs:assert_dependencies_met` enforces only `meta.depends_on`; the two
  run-start paths (`process_runs.start`, `projects.execute`) call it and nothing else.
- `git grep -n 'inception' -- crates apps` → no gate.
- The live programme: 47 of 48 projects carry a `project-brief`; none carries `analysis` or
  `architecture` (conveyor-program measurement, 2026-11-16).

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/264-inception-gate` |
| HEAD | `7586ed6a1bf0a298f02aa41057bfbcc58d129da1` |
| Session | claude-code (mini3) — inception gate |
| Updated | 2026-11-17 |
| Adopted-from | — (new unit) |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1, §8.5, §12 T12 | `main@87639c0` |
| Plan | `docs/plans/P0-programme-definition.md` §5 | `main@87639c0` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/programme.rs:assert_dependencies_met` (both start paths) | `main@87639c0` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/process/runs.rs` (`process_runs.start`) · `crates/actions/src/board/projects.rs` (`projects.execute`) | `main@87639c0` |
| Code | `crates/store/src/document.rs` (documents by project and category) | `main@87639c0` |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/inception_gate.rs` | to create |
| Issue | #122 (the per-project inception standard), #221 (the output categories), #81 (T9's design gate) | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@87639c0`, measured 2026-11-17.
- The gate's inputs already exist as data: `project.meta.expected_outputs` (the class) and
  `document` rows with `project_id`, `unit` and `meta.category` (the artefacts).

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the gate on both start paths

A project whose declared expected outputs include the inception pair refuses a build run until both
are **published** (`published_at IS NOT NULL`) with the project's unit key. The refusal is
`409 inception_missing`, names the project and the absent categories, and writes no run.

- **P1.1** Given a delivery project whose inception pair exists only as drafts, when
  `process_runs.start` is called for one of its cards, then it is refused `409 inception_missing`
  and no run row exists; when both documents are published, the identical start proceeds.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inception_gate.rs::a_draft_inception_pair_refuses_the_build`
- **P1.2** Given a project whose expected outputs do not include the pair (P0, the platform and
  every V1-built project), when a run starts, then the gate is a no-op and the existing behaviour
  is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inception_gate.rs::a_project_without_the_pair_is_unchanged`
- **P1.3** Given `projects.execute` on a project with the pair absent, when it is called, then it is
  refused with the same reason and writes no task — the two start paths cannot diverge.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inception_gate.rs::both_start_paths_share_the_inception_gate`

### P2 — the gate reads data, not a name list

The requirement is derived from the project's own `meta.expected_outputs`; a project with no
declared outputs is unchanged. No new table, no per-project allowance list.

- **P2.1** Given a project whose `expected_outputs` gains the pair, when the next run starts, then
  the gate applies without a code change.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inception_gate.rs::the_expected_outputs_are_the_switch`

### P3 — the refusal is visible

The console's project workspace already renders absent / present-private / published per output
row; the run-start refusal carries the same reason and the absent categories, so the Build screen
explains itself.

- **P3.1** Given the refusal, when the console reads the project's outputs, then the two absent
  categories are the rows the message names.
  Verify: the deployment-gated console smoke (design study: `node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs`)

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #221 | the output standard and the seed's expected outputs carry the inception categories; without them the gate has nothing to read | open (PR #262) |
| related | #122 | A7's per-project inception standard names what an analysis and an architecture must contain | open |
| related | #81 | T9's design gate is the architecture-side gate; this unit is the build-start gate on the published pair | open |
| related | #183 | the output standard's completeness rule is the same data | closed |

Blocker: none — the data path (`meta.expected_outputs`) exists today; the categories land with #221.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline and plan named.
- [x] Every part has a `Verify:` target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited.
- [x] The category spelling is one string across the standard, the seed and the gate (see open
      question 1): `inception-analysis` + `architecture-design` (the seed class; #221 lands them in
      the standard). Decided 2026-11-17.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; the evidence table has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate`).
- [ ] Both start paths call the same gate; a test proves they cannot diverge.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` merged; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Authoring the projects' inception documents (a content programme per project; #122 sets the
  standard).
- Changing `meta.depends_on` or the programme order.
- T9's phase/contract machinery.

## Deployment prerequisite

No for construction — the gate is proved against the compose/nextest Postgres. The buildout's own
projects are exempt until their pair is published, which is the gate working, not a deployment
step.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The category spelling is not yet one string: P0's published documents use `architecture-analysis`, the seed's T-project class uses `inception-analysis` + `architecture-design`. Which is canonical? | programme owner | the seed's class (`inception-analysis`, `architecture-design`) is canonical; P0's legacy document is re-categorised at its next revision, never silently matched by a second name |
| 2 | Immediate refusal, or a one-tranche warning window before refusing? | programme owner | refuse immediately once the class declares the pair; a warning window is a second mode to test and a way for the gate to never fire |
| 3 | Does "with the project's unit key" (P1) mean `document.unit = project.key`, or project scope? | architect | project scope: the row is bound by `document.project_id`; a card-attached document has none, so it cannot satisfy a project gate. Requiring `unit` would refuse the console-composed P0 outputs, which carry the category but not the key. Recorded at delivery 2026-11-17. |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `inception_gate.rs::a_draft_inception_pair_refuses_the_build` | pass | `8e6ce25febfa201e2d21585413c9898d03236809986ed946b06a44e995149e3653a21f41a` |
| P1.2 | `inception_gate.rs::a_project_without_the_pair_is_unchanged` | pass | `8e6ce25febfa201e2d21585413c9898d03236809986ed946b06a44e995149e3653a21f41a` |
| P1.3 | `inception_gate.rs::both_start_paths_share_the_inception_gate` | pass | `8e6ce25febfa201e2d21585413c9898d03236809986ed946b06a44e995149e3653a21f41a` |
| P2.1 | `inception_gate.rs::the_expected_outputs_are_the_switch` | pass | `8e6ce25febfa201e2d21585413c9898d03236809986ed946b06a44e995149e3653a21f41a` |
| P3.1 | console smoke (design study) · live rendering | deployment-gated (#18): the design-study smoke passes (248 checks); the live refusal→workspace rendering is proven at deployment | 8e6ce25febfa201e2d21585413c9898d03236809 |

## Goal

Every model-call request the conveyor posts to the inference-router carries `X-Actor-Id` and the tenant-level `X-Project-Id`, so the router's cost events are attributed and the two billing coverage floors for `service_key=inference-router` can clear.

## Plan / audit source

Production alert follow-up (round 8 of the retired-services cleanup; private plan `~/.claude/plans/review-which-apps-can-purring-crane.md`). Router-side half landed in #235; this is the caller-side half.

## Claim

|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/258-attribution-headers` |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs:invoke_external` — the outbound builder sets only `X-Correlation-Id` and `X-Tenant-Id` | main@e3d7c4eb2bc1b0b4ee2a1b7ba561bf119d75a002 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs:chat_spec` — `captures_usage: true` marks the model calls (inference, audio, imagegen) | main@e3d7c4e |
| Code | `crates/domain/src/ids.rs:TenantId::as_uuid` — the tenant uuid the derivation needs | main@e3d7c4e |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/inference_capture.rs::a_real_external_call_records_the_router_usage_field_for_field` | main@e3d7c4e |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/coding_jobs.rs` (asserts `TENANT_HEADER` on a non-usage external call) | main@e3d7c4e |
| Issue | #235 — the router now reads both headers and stamps its own `SERVICE_ACTOR_ID` when `X-Actor-Id` is absent | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@e3d7c4eb2bc1b0b4ee2a1b7ba561bf119d75a002`, measured 2026-11-17.
- Live evidence measured 2026-11-17 (aggregate only): the last 24 h of `billing_cost_events` for `service_key=inference-router` holds 27 events, **2** with `project_id`, **3** with `actor_id`; 25 of the 27 come from the conveyor tenant. The 2 attributed events are another caller's test traffic.
- The billing owner ruling of 2026-10-07 defines the value a project-less app must send: `X-Project-Id = tenant_level_project_id(tenant)`, the tenant uuid's 32 lowercase hex characters reversed and re-formatted `8-4-4-4-12`. It is deliberately not the tenant id, so `billing_project_id_equals_tenant` does not fire, and billing keeps it without an fr ownership lookup.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 outbound identity headers | ABSENT | `grep -n 'X-Actor-Id\|X-Project-Id' crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` → no match; the builder sets `X-Correlation-Id` and `TENANT_HEADER` only |
| P2 tenant-level project derivation | ABSENT | no `tenant_level_project_id` in the workspace |
| P3 model-call scoping | PARTIAL | `captures_usage: true` exists on the inference, audio and imagegen specs; nothing reads it for headers |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — outbound identity headers on model calls

Requirement: an external action that captures usage and is tenant-scoped must send the acting principal and the tenant-level project.

- **P1.1** Given an invocation of `completions.create` by principal U in tenant T, when the engine posts to the router, then the request carries `X-Actor-Id: U` and `X-Project-Id: tenant_level_project_id(T)`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inference_capture.rs` (to extend) — the stub asserts both headers against the seeded user and tenant.
- **P1.2** Given an external action that does not capture usage (for example the coding actions), when it posts, then neither header is sent.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coding_jobs.rs` (to extend).

### P2 — the tenant-level project id derivation

Requirement: port the billing ruling exactly; the transform must agree byte for byte with the Python implementation because it is a cross-service contract.

- **P2.1** Given tenant `0195f48b-d000-7000-8000-000000000100`, then the derived project id is `00100000-0000-0008-0007-000db84f5910`.
  Verify: unit test at `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` (to create).
- **P2.2** The transform is an involution — applying it twice returns the input.
  Verify: the same unit test.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #235 | the router-side half; already merged, so the headers are read and recorded | merged |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the measured evidence recorded.
- [x] Every code/test reference resolves at the baseline.
- [x] Every part has at least one scenario with a `Verify:` target.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no blocker.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from the open PRs (touches `invoke.rs` + two test files).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; the PR body carries one evidence row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head: `rbuild` fmt + clippy `-D warnings` + the actions crate tests.
- [ ] Tests added; none skipped.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` merged; issue closed; branch deleted.
- [ ] Live verification recorded after the image rollout: the first post-deploy `inference-router` cost event carries both fields.

## Out of scope

- Per-run conveyor project ids: conveyor projects are not fr projects, so billing's owner map would classify them `unknown_project` — worse than the honest tenant-level value. Mapping conveyor projects into billing is a separate product decision.
- Changing inference-router's contract: the Rust port mirrors the Python reference, so an absent header stays absent at the router.
- Any change to the audio/imagegen services beyond the shared header convention.

## Deployment prerequisite

Yes — the conveyor image ships through Flux image automation (`$imagepolicy: flux-system:conveyor`); the live scenario waits for the rollout, not on another issue.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|

## Goal

The published issue registry refreshes on every merge to `main`, so the Contribute page's ready list
cannot lag by more than one image build. The daily cron alone is not reliable enough to promise that.

## Current state (measured)

`main@e3d7c4e`, measured 2026-11-17.

- `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:24-28` triggers only on `schedule: "23 4 * * *"` and
  `workflow_dispatch`.
- The 04:23Z trigger on 2026-11-17 produced **no run**: `gh run list --workflow issue-registry.yml`
  at 07:21Z listed five runs, all `workflow_dispatch`, newest 01:31Z.
- The repository's only other cron — `board`, hourly since 2026-11-15T19:35Z — produced **5 runs in
  ~35 h** (`gh api 'repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs?event=schedule&per_page=100'`). GitHub's
  `schedule` event is documented best-effort and drops most triggers here.
- The no-change path already exists and is proven: dispatch run 43996217807 exited with "no branch,
  no PR" and left no branch. A push-triggered run is therefore self-terminating.
- The job has no event-specific branching (`grep -n 'event_name\|inputs\.'` finds nothing), holds
  `contents/pull-requests/actions: write`, and the repo has `can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true`.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Workflow | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:24-28` — the triggers | main@e3d7c4e (blob `3a10a12`) |
| Workflow | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml:81` — the no-change exit | main@e3d7c4e (blob `3a10a12`) |
| Script | `scripts/fetch-issues.sh:6-7` — "runs it on a daily schedule" | main@e3d7c4e (blob `81ec16e`) |
| Doc | `docs/design/README.md:11-13` — same claim in prose | main@e3d7c4e (blob `410e885`) |
| CI | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml:227` — `design-pack` runs `build-docs.py --check` | main@e3d7c4e |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the push trigger

Add `push: branches: [main]` to `on:` and record in the header why: the measured scheduler drop and
that a merge is the one trigger that always fires.

- **P1.1** Given a merge to `main`, when the merge lands, then a `push`-event run of `issue-registry`
  exists for that merge sha within 120 s.
  Verify: `gh run list --workflow issue-registry.yml --limit 3 --json event,headSha,conclusion` names `push` and the merge sha.
- **P1.2** Given a run with no registry change, when it completes, then it exits 0, creates no branch
  and opens no pull request.
  Verify: the run's summary says "no branch, no PR"; `git ls-remote --heads origin automation/issue-registry` is empty.
- **P1.3** Given the workflow file, when its triggers are read, then `push` (branches `[main]`),
  `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` are all present.
  Verify: `sed -n '/^on:/,/^permissions:/p' .github/workflows/issue-registry.yml`

### P2 — the two prose statements stay true

`scripts/fetch-issues.sh` and `docs/design/README.md` both say the refresh runs "daily". Update both,
and regenerate the published HTML the docs generator owns.

- **P2.1** Given the edited prose, when the docs check runs, then the committed HTML matches its
  source and every relative link resolves.
  Verify: `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check`
- **P2.2** Given the edited prose, when both files are searched, then each names both triggers.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'every push to main' -- scripts/fetch-issues.sh docs/design/README.md` returns both paths.
- **P2.3** Given the whole patch, when git checks it, then there is no whitespace error.

## Goal

A generated registry-refresh PR is mergeable without manual intervention: the workflow approves the parked `pull_request` run that the bot PR creates, so the required contexts are associated with the pull request.

## Plan / audit source

- Measured on the first fixpoint generated PR: #247 at head `be1a502`. The PR (author `app/github-actions`) created the `pull_request` run **43988013125** as `action_required`. The workflow's `gh workflow run ci-public.yml --ref automation/issue-registry` run **43988012297** completed **success** and its check runs exist on `be1a502` (`checks`, `image`, `service-image`, `no-private-refs`, `secret-scan`, `lint`, `design-pack` — all success), **but the PR's `statusCheckRollup` lists only the CodeQL checks**, so the PR is `BLOCKED`: a workflow_dispatch run's checks are not associated with the pull request.
- Approving the parked run (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/43988013125/approve`) started it, and a `pull_request`-event run's contexts do associate with the PR.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` — the refresh workflow, incl. the `gh workflow run ci-public.yml` dispatch | main@ee4c1f1 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` — `on: pull_request` + `workflow_dispatch` | main@ee4c1f1 |
| Run | 43988013125 — the parked pull_request run | completed |
| Run | 43988012297 — the dispatch whose checks do not associate | completed |
| PR | #247 — the generated PR the measurement came from | merged |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@ee4c1f1`, measured 2026-11-17.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — the generated PR is mergeable | ABSENT | the dispatch run's checks are on the commit but absent from the PR's `statusCheckRollup`; `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — approve the parked run, keep the dispatch as fallback

Requirement: after creating or updating the PR, the workflow waits briefly for the `pull_request` run on the new head; if its conclusion is `action_required`, it POSTs the approve endpoint with the job token (`actions: write`). If the approval succeeds, it skips the `ci-public` dispatch (the pull_request run carries the associated contexts); if no parked run appears or the approval is refused, it falls back to the current dispatch and says so in the step summary (a maintainer approves manually).

- **P1.1** Given a registry change, when the refresh runs, then the generated PR's `statusCheckRollup` contains `checks`, `image`, `service-image`, `no-private-refs`, `secret-scan` and `lint` from a `pull_request`-event run, and the PR becomes mergeable when they pass.
  Verify: the generated PR's `mergeStateStatus` becomes `CLEAN`/`UNSTABLE` with those contexts in the rollup; `gh api repos/…/commits/<head>/check-runs` and the PR rollup agree.
- **P1.2** Given the approval is refused (self-approval not permitted), when the refresh runs, then it dispatches CI as before and the step summary names the manual approval step.
  Verify: the run summary; the PR shows the parked run for a maintainer to approve.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #237 / #248 / #251 — the workflow this corrects | closed / merged |

No blocker.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (main@ee4c1f1); the two runs and the rollup measurement recorded.
- [x] References resolve.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] One-PR scope.

## Definition of done

- [ ] The scenario passes; evidence filled at the PR head and after a dispatch.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` merged; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- No repository secret and no GitHub App token (decision 0003 stays).
- No change to the required checks or the ruleset.
- No auto-merge.

## Deployment prerequisite

No.

## Goal

The registry refresh runs to completion on a stock GitHub runner: it regenerates the derived data and validates the docs without the pandoc-dependent docs generator.

## Plan / audit source

- Measured failure of the fixed workflow: run **43984954645** at `8c576c9` (the first run after #249 merged) ended `failure` at `build-docs: pandoc is not installed (needed to regenerate)` → exit 1, before the branch push.
- The docs are generated from Markdown sources, which the registry refresh does not touch; the design-pack gate is `build-docs.py --check` and the CI's `design-pack` job runs it on the same stock runner **without pandoc** — so the generator call is the defect, not the check.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

| Code | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` — the `build-docs.py` generator call | main@8c576c9 |
| Code | `docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py` — `--check` needs no pandoc; regeneration does | main@8c576c9 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `design-pack` — runs `build-docs.py --check` with no pandoc install | main@8c576c9 |
| Run | 43984954645 — the measured failure | completed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@8c576c9`, measured 2026-11-17.
- Failure evidence: run 43984954645, step "Regenerate, then open or update the one generated PR".

## Current state (measured)

| P1 — the refresh runs on a stock runner | PARTIAL | fetch, seed, coverage and v2 coverage all succeeded in the run; `build-docs.py` (generator) aborted with "pandoc is not installed" before the push |

## Goal

The automated registry refresh regenerates the derived design-pack data to a fixpoint, so the generated PR's `design-pack` check is green instead of red.

## Plan / audit source

- Measured failure on the first generated PR: #247 (`automation/issue-registry`, head `9512794`); the dispatched `ci` run **43982163110**, job `design-pack` (`133701092756`) failed at `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` → `coverage: docs/design/data/coverage.json is STALE` and `coverage.js is STALE`.
- The workflow merged in #238 runs only `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` and commits only `docs/design/data/issues.json`.
- The project memory `conveyor-design-pack-data-fixpoint` records the measured regeneration order (a peer session spent four CI runs on it).

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` — the refresh workflow | main@3afaf53 |
| Code | `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` — pulls live `gh issue list`, writes `seed/programme.json` | main@3afaf53 |
| Code | `scripts/build-coverage.py` — writes `docs/design/data/coverage.json`/`coverage.js`; `--check` refused the stale pair | main@3afaf53 |
| Code | `scripts/build-v2-coverage.py` — writes the V2 coverage pair | main@3afaf53 |
| Code | `docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py` — writes the generated docs index/pages | main@3afaf53 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `design-pack` — the gate that failed | main@3afaf53 |
| PR | #247 — the generated PR that exposed the gap | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@3afaf53`, measured 2026-11-17.
- Failure evidence: job `133701092756` log (design-pack, exit 1, coverage stale).

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — derived regeneration | ABSENT | the workflow commits only `issues.json`; the generated PR's `design-pack` failed on stale `coverage.json`/`coverage.js` |
| P2 — change detection | PARTIAL | `cmp -s` on `issues.json` alone; a registry change is detected, but derived-file drift would not be |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — regenerate the derived data to a fixpoint

Requirement: after `scripts/fetch-issues.sh`, run the measured order — `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` → `scripts/build-coverage.py` (repeat until both are stable, 2–3 passes) → `scripts/build-v2-coverage.py` → `docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py` — and commit every changed generated file, not just the registry.

- **P1.1** Given a registry change, when the refresh runs, then the generated branch carries the registry and every regenerated derived file, and the `design-pack` data checks are green on that head.
  Verify: dispatch `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml`; the generated PR's `design-pack` job passes; `git show <branch>:docs/design/data/coverage.json | python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` (in a checkout of the branch) → 0.
- **P1.2** Given no registry or derived change, when the refresh runs, then no branch is pushed and no PR is created.
  Verify: a second dispatch leaves the branch head and PR unchanged (the step summary says no change).

### P2 — detect the full generated change set

Requirement: decide "changed" from the whole regenerated set (e.g. `git status --porcelain` after all generators), not from `issues.json` alone, so a derived-only change is still published.

- **P2.1** Given only a derived file changed (no registry change), when the refresh runs, then the branch is pushed with that file.
  Verify: the workflow's change check names every generated path.

## Dependencies

## Goal

The output standard carries a template — required sections and a starter skeleton — for every
category; publishing an incomplete text output is refused with the missing section names; an admin
can return a requested draft with a note; and the console shows the completeness and a Markdown
preview before publishing.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/design/README.md` § Outputs / § Projects — the console contract this extends.
- `seed/output-standard.json` — the one vocabulary and the per-class sets.
- SPEC_V2 §3 **P3** (no completion without evidence) and **P4** (the executor never approves its
  own work) — the two invariants the blocked publish and the coach triage serve.
- Issue #221 — the 17 rigour categories the templates must cover.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `seed/output-standard.json` (the standard, its classes and the console copy) | `main@4ac0ede` |
| Code | `crates/domain/src/output_standard.rs` (`canonical_category`, `categories`) | `main@cc88052` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/documents/revisions.rs:20-100` (`documents.publish`) and `:110-180` (`documents.request_publish`) | `main@cc88052` |
| Code | `crates/store/src/document.rs:720-770` (`set_publishable_tx` clears the request flag) | `main@cc88052` |
| Code | `crates/pack/src/outputs.rs:238` (`render_markdown`, the public page renderer) | `main@cc88052` |
| Code | `docs/design/v2.js:906-950` (review requests), `:1760-1810` (compose), `:1823-1877` (edit), `:2149-2228` (the hard-coded skeletons) | `main@cc88052` |
| Code | `docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs`, `check-v2.cjs`, `check-coverage.cjs` | `main@cc88052` |
| Test | `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs` (the category refusal), `crates/actions/tests/` (the new DB tests) | `main@cc88052` |
| Issue | #221 (the rigour categories) | open |
| Issue | #183 (the standard), #231 (the console), #156 (the document store) | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@cc88052`, measured 2026-11-16.
- Blobs: `docs/design/v2.js` `a7f9cd6e`, `docs/design/README.md` `528bcfe9`,
  `seed/output-standard.json` `36a596de`, `crates/actions/src/documents/revisions.rs` `6765dbdb`,
  `crates/pack/src/outputs.rs` `facda7ec`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Templates in the standard | ABSENT | `seed/output-standard.json` has `version`, `categories`, `aliases`, `classes` and no `templates` key. The console's only starter text is a hard-coded map of three real skeletons plus a generic fallback (`v2.js:2149-2228`) |
| Server-side publish block | ABSENT | `documents.publish` loads the row and calls `set_publishable_tx`; it never reads the body or the category (`crates/actions/src/documents/revisions.rs:20-100`) |
| Return with a note | ABSENT | No `documents.return` in the action registry. The review panel's only decision is Publish (`v2.js:906-950`); `documents.request_publish` sets the flag and nothing clears it except publish/unpublish |
| Markdown preview | ABSENT | The editor is a bare `<textarea>` (`v2.js:1760-1810`); the read/history views show raw text. The public page renders Markdown with `pulldown-cmark` at publish time (`crates/pack/src/outputs.rs:238`) |
| Kata record from a review | ABSENT | No durable path from a review decision to a kata record; T4/T5 are proposed and A5 is unavailable, so this unit records the human coach's kata as a `decision` document, not an agent run |
| Templates for #221's 17 categories | ABSENT | #221 adds the MSP and architecture categories; none has a template |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — templates are data

`seed/output-standard.json` gains `templates`: one entry per category with `required` headings,
optional headings and a `skeleton` whose `##` headings contain every required one. The generator
copies them to `docs/design/data/output-standard.js`; the domain exposes the template; the check
fails on a category without one, an empty required list, a duplicate heading, a missing heading in
the skeleton, or a URL in a skeleton.

- Given every category in the standard, when the gate runs, then each category has a template whose
  required headings are non-empty, unique and present in its skeleton, and the console copy equals
  the standard.
  `Verify:` `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py --self-test && python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py`
- Given a category from #221, when the standard is generated, then its template exists and the
  console copy carries it.
  `Verify:` `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py --check && jq -r '.templates | keys | length' docs/design/data/output-standard.js`

### P2 — the blocked publish

`documents.publish` with `publish=true` refuses an unpublished text output whose body lacks a
required heading, with `409 output_incomplete` naming every missing heading. A complete output
publishes; unpublish is never checked; an already-published row is never re-checked, so the
existing published outputs are not touched. `documents.request_publish` stays unblocked: the
author's request must reach the coach.

- Given a draft missing one required heading, when the admin publishes it, then `409
  output_incomplete` names that heading and `publishable` stays false.
  `Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::an_incomplete_output_cannot_be_published` (to create)
- Given a complete draft, when the admin publishes it, then it is public; given a published row,
  when it is unpublished, then the unpublish succeeds whatever its headings.
  `Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_complete_output_publishes_and_unpublish_never_blocks` (to create)

### P3 — the rework order

`documents.return` is a new admin action (`can_publish`, If-Match): input `{id, note}`. The server
computes the missing sections; the store clears `publish_requested_at`, writes
`meta.rework = {note, missing, by, at, of_version}` in one UPDATE, and emits a `document.returned`
event. A non-admin is `403`; no request is `409 not_requested`; a published row is `409
published_locked`; stale is `412`. No migration.

- Given a requested draft, when an admin returns it with a note, then the request flag is null, the
  note and missing sections are on the row, and one `document.returned` event exists.
  `Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_return_clears_the_request_and_records_the_note` (to create)
- Given a requester who is not an admin, when they return the draft, then `403` and no row change.
  `Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_non_admin_cannot_return_a_draft` (to create)

### P4 — the preview

`documents.preview` is a new read action (`documents:read`, idempotent): input `{id}`, output
`{html, missing, category}`. The Markdown renderer moves to `crates/render`; `crates/pack` delegates
so the preview and the public page use one implementation. The action is id-only and tenant-scoped
(no arbitrary-body render oracle).

- Given a saved draft whose body contains `<script>`, `onerror` and a `javascript:` link, when it is
  previewed, then the HTML contains none of the three as executable output and the missing sections
  are returned.
  `Verify:` `crates/actions/tests/authoring_standard.rs::a_preview_neutralises_author_markup` (to create)

### P5 — the console

The compose/edit dialog seeds the standard's skeleton, shows a per-heading completeness panel, and
offers Preview. The review panel gains Publish / Return / Open a kata. A blocked publish renders the
missing list and the triage. Return sends `documents.return`; Open a kata composes a `decision`
document on the selected kata project (default S18; a scratch project for tests) with meta
`{kata:true, system_issue:true, source_document_id, source_project_id, coach_note}`, publishes it,
then returns the source with a note linking the kata. Signed out makes zero `/api/` requests.

- Given a signed-in admin on a requested incomplete draft, when they publish, then the missing list
  and the Return/Open a kata controls render and the wire payloads are the actions above.
  `Verify:` `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs`
- Given the public pack signed out, when every published page loads, then no `/api/` request and no
  GitHub call is made and the output pages keep their Feedback/Discuss links.
  `Verify:` `node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | #221 | Merged 2026-11-17 as `4ac0ede`; the templates cover its 17 categories | closed |
| related | #183 | The one output standard and the queue this unit extends | closed |
| related | #231 | The console workspace and review requests | closed |
| related | #156 | The document store, provenance and the publish gate | closed |

Blocker cleared: #221 merged as `4ac0ede` on 2026-11-17; this branch starts from that main.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and every reference resolves at `main@cc88052`.
- [x] Every part has at least one BDD scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] Dependencies typed; `Blocker:` present because the status is blocked.
- [x] One-PR scope: one standard change, one document action set, one renderer move, one console
      change, one check family.
- [x] No private host, address, credential or repository in this body.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; the evidence table has one row per scenario.
- [ ] `rbuild --gate` and the design-pack checks are green at the exact head (or the PR's Linux CI
      is the authoritative Rust gate when a local service is unavailable).
- [ ] The action dump and generated design data are current; the served-spec pin is updated.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` merged; branch deleted; issue closed.

## Out of scope

- The agentic coach (T4) and kata (T5), and A5/model credentials. This unit records the human
  coach's decision; it does not run an agent.
- Members/Invites, document full-text search, a project-closure gate on outputs, and any change to
  the existing 15 categories' semantics beyond adding templates.
- The programme content itself (the documents the standard governs).

## Deployment prerequisite

Image roll only. The templates are compiled from the standard; no `migrate --seed` is needed for
them (the expected-output sets do not change). Regenerate `docs/design/data/actions.json` and the
design data in the same commit as the action change.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Where does the rework note live? | architecture | `meta.rework` + a `document.returned` event; no migration |
| 2 | Which project receives a kata record? | programme | S18, selected in the triage dialog; a scratch project for the live proof |
| 3 | Where does the Markdown renderer live? | architecture | `crates/render` (actions already depends on it); `crates/pack` delegates |
| 4 | Is the block hard for every text output? | governance | Yes, on the false→true publish only; unpublish and already-published rows are never checked |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `check-output-standard --self-test` + `--check` | 9/9 refusals; 32 templates; console copy byte-equal | `73f78a4` |
| P2.1 | `authoring_standard.rs::an_incomplete_output_cannot_be_published` | pass — 409 names Boundary/Outcomes/Who it serves; stays private | `73f78a4` |
| P2.2 | `authoring_standard.rs::a_complete_output_publishes_and_unpublish_never_blocks` | pass — published; a published row is not re-checked; unpublish free | `73f78a4` |
| P2.3 | `authoring_standard.rs::an_output_composed_straight_to_public_is_checked` | pass — the compose path is gated too | `73f78a4` |
| P3.1 | `authoring_standard.rs::a_return_clears_the_request_and_records_the_note` | pass — request null, meta.rework, version unchanged, 1 event | `73f78a4` |
| P3.2 | `authoring_standard.rs::a_non_admin_cannot_return_a_draft` | pass — 403, request stays open | `73f78a4` |
| P3.3 | `authoring_standard.rs::a_published_draft_cannot_be_returned` | pass — 409 published_locked | `73f78a4` |
| P4 | `authoring_standard.rs::a_preview_neutralises_author_markup` | pass — no script/img/executable scheme; missing returned | `73f78a4` |
| P5.1 | `check-console.cjs` | pass — completeness, preview, blocked publish + Return/kata, returned state, deleted hidden | `73f78a4` |
| P5.2 | `check-v2.cjs` | pass — signed out zero API requests; public pages unchanged | `73f78a4` |

## Goal

`@nonagenticai/maintainers` is the owner of record in `.github/CODEOWNERS` and in CONTRIBUTING, now that the team exists, so a pull request that touches a sensitive path requests the team's review and no document describes a fallback that is no longer the rule.

## Plan / audit source

- Owner instruction, 2026-11-16: create the `@nonagenticai/maintainers` team; CONTRIBUTING's "until the team exists" wording must stop being true.
- Issue #93 (closed) — the owner decision that sensitive paths are reviewed by a code owner; the arming of `require_code_owner_review` was recorded there as one admin step, deliberately deferred until the team existed.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `.github/CODEOWNERS` — every row targets `@georgiedekker`, with the "once the team exists" note | main@cc88052 |
| Doc | `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "For maintainers: accepting a contribution" and § "Review and merge" — both say "until the team exists" | main@cc88052 |
| Data | org teams: `maintainers` exists, `georgiedekker` is a maintainer, the team has `push` on `nonagenticai/conveyor` | measured 2026-11-16 with an admin token |
| Data | the `main` ruleset: `require_code_owner_review: false`, 0 approvals | measured 2026-11-16 |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@cc88052`, measured 2026-11-16.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — team | EXISTS | `GET /orgs/nonagenticai/teams` → `maintainers`; membership `georgiedekker` role `maintainer`; `GET /orgs/nonagenticai/teams/maintainers/repos/nonagenticai/conveyor` → `push: true` |
| P2 — CODEOWNERS | STALE | every row targets `@georgiedekker`; header says the target becomes the team "once that team exists" |
| P3 — CONTRIBUTING | STALE | "Until the `@nonagenticai/maintainers` team exists, the repository owner is the maintainer of record"; "once the team exists" in § "Review and merge" |
| P4 — ruleset arming | DEFERRED (recorded) | `require_code_owner_review: false`; the file's `*` row makes arming a blanket gate, while the owner decision is sensitive paths only |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — CODEOWNERS names the team

Requirement: every row targets `@nonagenticai/maintainers`; the header records that the team exists, that GitHub requests the team's review on a matching pull request, and that arming `require_code_owner_review` while `*` is owned would make the gate blanket — the owner decision is sensitive paths only, so `*` must be removed before arming.

- **P1.1** Given the file, when GitHub validates the branch, then there are no code-owner errors and no row names a personal handle.
  Verify: `gh api "repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/codeowners/errors?ref=issue/<n>-maintainers-team"` → `errors: []`; `grep -c '@nonagenticai/maintainers' .github/CODEOWNERS` → 6 (five rows + the header); `grep -c '@georgiedekker' .github/CODEOWNERS` → 0.

### P2 — the guide stops describing the fallback

Requirement: CONTRIBUTING states the team is the maintainer of record and that sensitive-path pull requests request the team's review; no sentence conditions it on the team's future existence.

- **P2.1** Given the guide, when searched, then no "until the `@nonagenticai/maintainers` team exists" or "once the `@nonagenticai/maintainers` team exists" remains, and every relative link still resolves.
  Verify: `grep -n "team exists" CONTRIBUTING.md` → empty; the relative-link scan; `git diff --check`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #93 | records the sensitive-path decision and the deferred arming | closed |

No blocker.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (main@cc88052); the team and ruleset measured.

- [x] One-PR scope.

## Definition of done

## Out of scope

No.

## Goal

The browser tests that share the machine-wide CDP launch lock run one at a time under nextest, and the five that drive a real browser have headroom above the measured launch time, so neither a queued test nor a slow launch spends its whole scenario ceiling and fails the suite.

## Plan / audit source

- **Measured failure, main run 43947147234** (`318fa4d`, 2026-11-16): `checks` failed on four `conveyor-media browser::gherkin` tests at ~20.0 s each (every step hit "the scenario exceeded its 20000 ms per-test ceiling"). The same tree passed `checks` on the PR run 43941223985, and the main rerun (attempt 2) passed — a shared-resource queue, not a code difference.
- Precedent: `.config/nextest.toml` `serial-redis-loss` — a test group with `max-threads = 1` for a binary whose tests share one resource.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/media/src/browser/cdp.rs:49,60-108` — `Session` holds `LaunchLock` for its life; `acquire()` waits up to 60 s for the machine-wide file lock | main@3d80131 |
| Code | `apps/media/src/browser/gherkin.rs:1643,1773,1814,1844,1886` — the five tests that pass `timeout_per_test_ms: 20000` | main@3d80131 |
| Code | `.config/nextest.toml` — the `serial-redis-loss` test group and its `overrides` entry | main@3d80131 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `checks` — `cargo nextest` on a 4-vCPU GitHub-hosted runner | main@3d80131 |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@3d80131`, measured 2026-11-16.
- Failure evidence: run 43947147234 job `checks` (4 failures), PR run 43941223985 (green), run 43947147234 attempt 2 (green).

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — browser-test scheduling | ABSENT | nextest runs each test in its own process concurrently; `cdp.rs:60` serialises only the *browser session*, so 4–6 concurrent tests queue on the lock inside their 20 s ceilings. `.config/nextest.toml` has one group (`serial-redis-loss`), none for `conveyor-media`. |
| P2 — per-test headroom | ABSENT | on m1, unloaded and with `--test-threads 8`, `a_click_step_changes_the_page_state` took **7.908 s** and `a_two_scenario_feature_runs_against_a_local_page` **4.805 s** (10 gherkin tests, wall 15.325 s = the sum of durations — serialised by P1's group). A 4-vCPU CI runner running 2 324 tests is far slower; the failing main run's four tests all died at 20.0 s, including the lock holder. `timeout_per_test_ms: 20000` at `gherkin.rs:1643,1773,1814,1844,1886`. |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — serialise the browser tests in the media binary

Requirement: add a `serial-browser-cdp` test group (`max-threads = 1`) and an override `filter = 'package(conveyor-media) & test(/browser/)'`, with the measured evidence in the config comment.

- **P1.1** Given the config, when the gherkin tests run with a high `--test-threads`, then the wall time equals the sum of the test durations (serialised), not their maximum.
  Verify: `rbuild -- nextest run -p conveyor-media -E 'test(/browser::gherkin/)' --test-threads 8` → `Summary [15.325s]` equals the sum of the 10 PASS durations (15.32 s). nextest 0.9.150's `--message-format json` carries no group field — measured, so the timing is the proof.
- **P1.2** Given the group, when the tests run, then every browser test passes and no test waits on the launch lock.
  Verify: the same run → 10 passed, 0 failed.

### P2 — headroom for the five real-browser tests

Requirement: the five tests that launch Chromium pass `timeout_per_test_ms: 60000` instead of `20000`. The capability's range is 1 s–600 s and the production default is 30 s, so 60 s is a test-robustness choice, not a contract change.

- **P2.1** Given the five tests, when their params are inspected and the tests run, then each uses `60000` and all pass.
  Verify: `grep -c '"timeout_per_test_ms": 60000' apps/media/src/browser/gherkin.rs` → 5; the P1 run → pass.

The CI proof is the PR's `checks` job: the same gherkin tests pass under the group.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #237 | the previous main-run flake was reported in the same session; independent | open |

No blocker.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (main@3d80131); the failure and the green reruns recorded with run ids.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] One-PR scope.
- [x] No scope correction applies.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes; evidence rows filled at the PR head.
- [ ] The PR's `checks` job is green at the head (the four gherkin tests ran).
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` merged; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- No nextest retries (a retry would hide the queue rather than remove it).
- No change to `LaunchLock` or to the production timeout semantics (the 30 s default stays).
- No other tests' ceilings and no other crate's tests.

## Deployment prerequisite

No.
