## Goal

The public issue registry (`docs/design/data/issues.json`) refreshes itself on a schedule and opens one reviewable PR when it changes, so the Contribute page never depends on a session remembering to run `scripts/fetch-issues.sh`.

## Plan / audit source

- Follow-up of #219 / PR #220 (the contribution surface): the Contribute page's ready list is the committed registry, and it goes stale the moment an issue changes.
- Precedent: `.github/workflows/board.yml` — the repo's scheduled, least-privilege workflow.
- Constraint: `docs/decisions/0003-public-ci.md` — the public CI references no repository secret; the automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN` is the only credential.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` — the registry generator (redacted, no bodies/authors) | main@0e2e351 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/board.yml` — scheduled workflow, job-scoped permissions, dry-run input | main@0e2e351 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` — `classify` (docs-only), `design-pack`, required contexts | main@0e2e351 |
| Code | `crates/api/src/design.rs:230` — the API reads `design/data/issues.json` from the image | main@0e2e351 |
| Doc | `docs/design/README.md` — the pack and its two surfaces | main@0e2e351 |
| Doc | `docs/decisions/0003-public-ci.md` — GitHub-hosted, zero-secret CI | main@0e2e351 |
| Issue | #219 / PR #220 — the contribution surface that surfaced the lag | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@0e2e351`, measured 2026-11-16.
- Registry blob: `git rev-parse origin/main:docs/design/data/issues.json` → `34985dd6d0b0a77d8b725f45a34f07180d34c2e`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — automation | ABSENT | `git grep -l fetch-issues origin/main -- .github/workflows` → no match. The registry has only ever been refreshed inside sessions (#209, #234 ran the generator by hand). |
| Actions PR permission | OFF | `GET /repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/permissions/workflow` → `{"can_approve_pull_request_reviews":false,"default_workflow_permissions":"read"}` — a workflow cannot create a PR with `GITHUB_TOKEN` until this is enabled. |
| Registry today | CURRENT (incidentally) | 146 rows = 146 GitHub issues at 2026-11-16T21:5xZ, max #235; #234 regenerated it. Nothing keeps it current on the next issue change. |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the scheduled refresh workflow

Requirement: `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` runs `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` on a daily schedule and on `workflow_dispatch`; when the file changes it force-updates the single branch `automation/issue-registry` from `main` and opens or updates one PR; when it does not change it exits without creating a branch or PR. The PR is generated data only, carries no `Closes`, and is merged by a maintainer; it never auto-merges.

- **P1.1** Given the registry matches GitHub, when the workflow runs, then no branch is pushed and no PR is created.
  Verify: dispatch run's log says no change; `gh pr list --head automation/issue-registry --state open` unchanged.
- **P1.2** Given the registry changed, when the workflow runs, then `automation/issue-registry` is force-updated from `main` and exactly one PR exists for it, with the added/removed/closed numbers in its body.
  Verify: `gh pr list --head automation/issue-registry --state open --json number,title,body`; a second dispatch with no further upstream change leaves the PR count at one and creates no new commit.
- **P1.3** Given the generated PR, when the checks run, then every required context reports. A `GITHUB_TOKEN`-created PR triggers no `pull_request` workflow (GitHub's recursion guard), so the workflow dispatches `ci-public.yml` on `automation/issue-registry`; `workflow_dispatch` is exempt and attaches the contexts to the same head commit. `image` builds without pushing (the push is main-only) and `service-image` is skipped, as on a docs-only PR.
  Verify: `gh pr checks <n> --json name,state,workflow` shows `checks`, `image`, `no-private-refs`, `secret-scan`, `service-image` and `lint` against the head SHA.

Local gate before the PR: `actionlint -color`; `uvx zizmor==1.32.0 --persona=auditor --min-severity=medium --format=plain .`; `git diff --check`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #219 | the contribution surface this keeps fresh | closed |

No blocker.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (main@0e2e351) and the registry blob recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] One-PR scope.
- [x] No scope correction applies.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes; evidence rows filled at the PR head and after the first dispatch.
- [ ] `actionlint` and `zizmor` (auditor, medium+) green at the head.
- [ ] The repository setting `can_approve_pull_request_reviews` is enabled (the zero-secret path) and recorded in the PR.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` merged; the first dispatched PR demonstrated and merged; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- No auto-merge of the generated PR (a maintainer merges; the page's ribbon already says it is a snapshot).
- No repository secret and no change to decision 0003.
- No change to what the registry contains or to `fetch-issues.sh`'s redaction.
- No build-time fetch in the Dockerfile (the registry stays a commit-time artefact).
- No cluster/gitops change.

## Deployment prerequisite

No. The first generated PR is the evidence.

Two production alerts fire because the Rust ports dropped telemetry the Python references emitted. Neither is cluster state; both are code gaps.

## 1. `BillingActorCoverageBelowFloor` / `BillingAttributionCoverageBelowFloor` (service_key=inference-router)

Measured in `billing_cost_events`, last 24 h: 26 inference-router events, **4** carry `actor_id`, **2** carry `project_id` (floor is 50%).

- `apps/inference-router/src/metering.rs` has `actor_id` on `CostEvent`, but nothing ever sets it: `grep actor_id apps/inference-router/src` matches only `metering.rs`.
- `SERVICE_ACTOR_ID` is set on the Deployment and read by nothing in the crate.
- The Python reference stamps it in `src/security.py:service_actor_fallback` (header `X-Actor-Id`, else the introspected service principal, ruling 2026-10-25).

**Fix:** add `actor_id` to `CallContext` (`apps/inference-router/src/router/completions.rs:177/320/666`), populate it from `X-Actor-Id` else the configured `SERVICE_ACTOR_ID`, and set it on every cost event (streaming and non-streaming).

## 2. `LicenseExpiryMetricAbsent`

`apps/licenses` serves `/metrics` (`src/router/observability.rs`, `metrics_exporter_prometheus`) but emits no licence-expiry family, so `absent(nonagentic_license_token_expiry_timestamp_seconds)` has been true since the Python Deployment was parked. The rule's early-warning bands (60/30/7 days) are the only signal for manual token reissue; the earliest live token expires 2027-02-17.

**Fix:** emit `nonagentic_license_token_expiry_timestamp_seconds{token_id,token_type,app,tenant,lifetime_class}` from the `licence_tokens` rows, mirroring the Python collector's labels and the `short|lt7d|lt30d|lt60d` lifetime bucketing the rule depends on. `/metrics` stays outside auth.

## Done when

- A router request carrying `X-Actor-Id` books a cost event with that `actor_id`; one without it books the service fallback; neither leaves it empty when `SERVICE_ACTOR_ID` is set.
- A scrape of `apps/licenses` `/metrics` shows the expiry family with the rule's labels; a NULL-`expires_at` token is not emitted.
- Unit tests pin both behaviours; workspace fmt/clippy(-D warnings)/test green.
issues.title: Rust telemetry parity: cost-event attribution + licence-expiry metrics

## Goal

`apps/research`'s media binary resolves the caller's tenant from a bare `X-Tenant-Id` header with no authentication. The reference it replaces required a valid credential — a `Bearer` service token, or a licence token sent as `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <token>` — and this port dropped that requirement. Until the gate is restored, any pod in the cluster that can reach port 8809 can read and write any tenant's media rows, so the reference Deployment cannot be retired.

## Plan / audit source

- Measured 2026-11-16 during the #205 shadow window, first live request against `research-media.media-discovery:8809`.
- `apps/research/src/media/tenant.rs` — its own module docs say the port "has no default"; what it does not say is that it also has no authentication.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-16)

| Call | Reference (`media-discovery:8809`) | Port (`research-media:8809`) |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/items/<id>`, no headers | `401 AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` | `401 HTTP_401` |
| same, `X-Tenant-Id: <uuid>` | `401` — "a bare X-Tenant-Id requires a valid service token in Authorization: Bearer <token>" | **`200` + the full row** |

The port's `Tenant::from_request_parts` parses the header and returns `Tenant(uuid)` with no verification of any kind. The reference's equivalent dependency calls `LICENSE_INTROSPECT_URL` (`http://licenses.licenses.svc.cluster.local:8544/license/introspect`) and refuses a header-only request.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the reference's tenant gate, restored

- **P1.1** Given a request with no credential, when any `/api/*` operation is served, then it answers 401 and no row is read. **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::no_credential_is_refused`
- **P1.2** Given a `Bearer` service token, when `GET /api/items/{id}` is served, then it answers the row for the token's tenant and refuses a row belonging to another tenant. **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::a_service_token_scopes_the_tenant`
- **P1.3** Given a licence token presented as `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <token>`, when an operation is served, then the tenant is the one the licence names, and an expired or unknown licence is refused with the reference's 401 shape. **Verify:** `apps/research/tests/tenant.rs::a_licence_token_names_the_tenant`

### P2 — the deployment keeps working

- **P2.1** Given the restored gate, when the shadow binary is probed with each of the three credential shapes, then the answers match the reference's status and body shape for all three. **Verify:** the shadow table in `docs/evidence/2026-11-16-research-cutover.md`, `unexplained == 0`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Source | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocks | #205 (P4 — retire `media-discovery`) | the cut-over cannot remove an authenticated service in favour of an unauthenticated one | open |

## Definition of ready

The three credential shapes are named with the reference's exact refusals; every part carries a `Verify:`; the one dependency is open and marked; scope is `apps/research` plus its tests only.

## Definition of done

All three scenarios pass at the merged head; the reference and the port agree on all three credential shapes; #205 records the restored gate in its evidence doc before the media Deployment is retired.

## Out of scope

- The scraper binary (stateless, no tenant-owned rows).
- General broker authn (`crates/auth`) — this is the standalone service's own gate.
- Any change to the licence service.

## Evidence at completion

## Goal

An external contributor can start with a five-minute step, land a small fix without a unit brief, be credited for merged work, and the maintainer has one written path to triage and accept it.

## Plan / audit source

- Owner assignment, 2026-11-16: make contribution compelling and easy for external contributors, credit their work, and let the maintainer accept it directly.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the contribution contract this unit extends.
- `README.md` — the public entry point.

- Issue #93 (closed) — delivered external intake, the fork claim, DCO and the public CI gate; this unit adds the paths, the credit and the maintainer acceptance that #93 left open.

## Claim

| Branch | `issue/219-contributor-experience` |

| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Doc | `CONTRIBUTING.md` | main@a8149d6 |
| Doc | `README.md` | main@a8149d6 |
| Code | `.github/pull_request_template.md` | main@a8149d6 |

| Issue | #93 — external intake, fork claim, DCO, public CI | closed |
| Issue | #42 — the public collaboration surface | closed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@a8149d6b70dd91018e75351a4399e15f28725fd7`, measured 2026-11-16.
- Doc blobs: `CONTRIBUTING.md@cfe7b8b` · `README.md@776be9f` · `.github/pull_request_template.md@bf9d93d` · `docs/design/v2.js@2eb1a52`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — newcomer paths and the small-fix path | ABSENT | `rg -n 'Ways to contribute\|go straight to a pull request' CONTRIBUTING.md` → no match; `README.md` "Contributing" links the organisation-wide `.github` CONTRIBUTING, not this repository's |
| P2 — credit for merged work | ABSENT | `test -f CONTRIBUTORS.md` → missing; `rg -ni 'credit\|contributors' CONTRIBUTING.md README.md` → no match; the v0.1.0 release notes name no contributor |
| P3 — maintainer acceptance path | PARTIAL | `CONTRIBUTING.md` § "Review and merge" states a maintainer reviews and merges; it names no triage, DCO, merge method or credit step. `.github/pull_request_template.md` is unit-only (scenario evidence, WIP cap) |
| P4 — public Contribute page truth and recognition | PARTIAL | `docs/design/v2.js:3949` labels the count "Ready to claim" with "no branch, no PR, no claim comment"; the page has no first-step paths and no credit link |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — newcomer paths and the small-fix path

Requirement: a first-time visitor sees what they can do in 5 / 15–30 / 30+ minutes, and a change that does not alter behaviour can open a pull request without a unit issue.

- **P1.1** Given a newcomer reading `CONTRIBUTING.md`, when they reach the top, then they see a time-boxed first-step table (design feedback, proposal review, docs/code) and a plain statement that a typo, a broken link or a docs clarification can go straight to a pull request, while anything that changes behaviour starts from a maintainer-triaged unit.
  Verify: `rg -n 'Ways to contribute|go straight to a pull request|does not alter behaviour' CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **P1.2** Given the README, when a reader follows the Contributing section, then it links this repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md` (not the organisation-wide file), names the small-fix path and links the credit file.
  Verify: `rg -n 'CONTRIBUTING.md|small fix|CONTRIBUTORS.md' README.md`; `! rg -n 'nonagenticai/\.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING' README.md`.

### P2 — credit for merged work

Requirement: every merged contribution can be credited publicly, and the policy is written before the first contribution lands.

- **P2.1** Given a merged contribution, when the maintainer closes it, then `CONTRIBUTORS.md` holds one row (name, handle, what landed, PR link), and `CONTRIBUTING.md` states where credit appears — the file, the release notes and the merge comment — with an opt-out.
  Verify: `test -f CONTRIBUTORS.md && rg -ni 'credit|opt out' CONTRIBUTORS.md CONTRIBUTING.md`; `rg -n 'release notes' CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### P3 — the maintainer's acceptance path

Requirement: the maintainer can triage a report, accept a small fix, and accept unit work without re-deriving the rules, including the DCO and sensitive-path checks and the credit step.

- **P3.1** Given an external pull request, when the maintainer accepts it, then `CONTRIBUTING.md` has a "For maintainers" section naming: triage (small fix vs unit, `good first issue`), review (diff, sensitive paths, the DCO sign-off is the author's), checks (a docs-only PR skips the heavy jobs), merge (`gh pr merge <n> --rebase --delete-branch`), and the credit action.
  Verify: `rg -n 'For maintainers|good first issue|gh pr merge|Signed-off-by|sensitive path' CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **P3.2** Given a small-fix pull request, when its author reads the PR template, then it offers a small-fix track that does not require a unit issue, keeps the unit evidence section, and asks for the credit name.
  Verify: `rg -n 'Small fix|Closes #|Credit' .github/pull_request_template.md`.

## Goal

A tenant's `media.generate_image` call, made against the deployed conveyor, renders on the estate's
image host and returns a stored artefact instead of `503 action-service-unconfigured`.

## Plan / audit source

Follow-up to #174 (`media.generate_image` + `Effect::Spend` + the engine-owned artefact write, PR
#204). That issue shipped the action; the deployment was never given the destination, so the action
is permanently unconfigured in production. No slice plan covers a deployment binding — the source is
the action's own declaration and the deployment manifests.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/imagegen.rs:13` — "`CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_GEN_URL`, no default — unset is a visible `unconfigured` refusal" | main@3d698fb |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/imagegen.rs:34-36` — `SERVICE = "image_gen"`, the env key's underscore spelling | main@3d698fb |
| Code | `crates/actions/tests/generate_image.rs:109` — the test that proves the URL is read from the environment | main@3d698fb |
| Manifest | `clusters/strato/services/conveyor/deployment.yaml` — the externals block in both containers; `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_GEN_URL` is absent | to update |
| Manifest | `clusters/strato/services/conveyor/networkpolicy.yaml` — egress admits the pod and service CIDRs, MinIO, the Postgres primary and public 80/443 (excluding the tailnet block); the image host is in that excluded block | to update |
| Issue | #174 — the action this binds | closed, PR #204 |

## Baseline

Code `main@3d698fb`, measured 2026-11-16. The deployed conveyor reports
`CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_{INFERENCE,CODING,LAYA}_URL` and nothing for image generation.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 the destination env | ABSENT | grep of `deployment.yaml` for `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_GEN_URL` returns 0 hits in both containers |
| P2 egress to the image host | ABSENT | `networkpolicy.yaml` admits `0.0.0.0/0` **except** the tailnet block, where the image host lives; the MinIO rule shows the shape a host rule takes in this file |
| P3 the action's expectation | DONE | `imagegen.rs:13` refuses visibly when the key is unset — which is exactly what production does today |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the destination is configured in both containers

Requirement: `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_GEN_URL` names the image host's base URL in the **serve** and
the **worker** container. Both, because an action is invoked over HTTP in serve and as a job step in
the worker, and the engine reads the key per process.

- **P1.1** Given the deployed conveyor, when an admin reads the deployment's env, then the key is
  present in both containers with the image host's base URL.
  Verify: `kubectl -n conveyor get deploy conveyor -o jsonpath=...` and the same for
  `conveyor-worker`, recorded in the PR body.

### P2 — the pod may reach the host

Requirement: an egress rule admits TCP 9204 to the image host's address only, in the same shape as
the existing MinIO rule. Without it the URL alone buys a timeout, not a render.

- **P2.1** Given the deployed pod, when it calls the image host's health route, then the call
  succeeds from inside the conveyor namespace.
  Verify: a recorded in-cluster probe (the same call the render uses).

### P3 — a real render through the deployed engine

Requirement: one `media.generate_image` invocation through the deployed conveyor stores an object
and creates a document, with no `unconfigured` refusal.

- **P3.1** Given a tenant and a prompt, when `media.generate_image` is invoked, then the response
  carries an artefact reference and the object exists in the store.
  Verify: the invocation's document id, byte size and elapsed time recorded in the PR body — never
  the image bytes.

## Dependencies

| Kind | Issue | State |
|---|---|---|
| related | #174 — the action being bound | closed (PR #204) |
| related | #160 — the tenant-registered destination direction; this issue binds the platform URL the way `coding` is bound | open |

## Definition of ready

- The env key is fixed by the action's code (`CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_IMAGE_GEN_URL`), not chosen here.
- The host, port and DNS name are unchanged since the FLUX→MOSS cutover.
- No open blocker.

## Definition of done

- P1–P3 accepted; the manifests are merged and Flux has reconciled them.
- The live render evidence is in the PR body and on this issue.
- Exactly one PR in the private deployment repository, `Closes` not applicable (it is not this repo);
  this issue is closed with the evidence.

## Out of scope

- Moving the destination to tenant configuration (#160).
- The same binding for speech and transcription (#173) — separate hosts, separate rules.
- Changing the action's input schema or its effect.

## Deployment prerequisite

This issue **is** the deployment change; it lands in the private deployment repository, not in this
one. The action and its client already ship here.

## Open questions

- None. The render budget (`MLXCEL_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_SECS=1800`) is already recorded in the manifests by
  the cutover lane.

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Command / route | Result | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | | | |
| P2.1 | | | |
| P3.1 | | | |

## Goal

The dead media estate is removed from the cluster: every zero-replica legacy Deployment and its
Service in the `w2v` namespace is deleted, and the VirtualService/DNS entries that still route
`studio.nonagentic.ai` and `w2v.redacted` at backends that have not existed for weeks are removed.
No data is deleted; every manifest stays in git history and is one revert away.

## Plan / audit source

- ADR 0006 §1–2 (the group is absorbed; the eighteen stage directories are a vocabulary, not services)
- `docs/plans/04-TOOL-ESTATE-INVENTORY.md` §1, §6 (the orchestrator and the SPA are out of scope; their
  runtime is retired at cutover)

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

Measured 2026-11-16: all 17 Deployments report `0/0`; the Services and two VirtualServices still
exist and still route `studio.nonagentic.ai` / `w2v.redacted` to those dead backends; 17 Services
remain addressable in-cluster.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the delete set is named and justified

- **P1.1** Given the namespace, when the delete list is written, then every Deployment in it has `readyReplicas` absent or 0 and no pod. **Verify:** `kubectl -n w2v get deploy,pods` recorded in the evidence document, plus the list of names deleted.
- **P1.2** Given a Deployment not on the list, when the PR is reviewed, then the reason it stays is stated (a live consumer or a live process). **Verify:** the PR body names each survivor.

### P2 — the removal

- **P2.1** Given the PR, when it merges and Flux reconciles, then `kubectl -n w2v get deploy` returns no resources (or only the survivors P1.2 named) and no pod exists. **Verify:** the recorded `kubectl` output.
- **P2.2** Given the routing, when the hostnames are resolved, then `studio.nonagentic.ai` answers from a deliberate target (a redirect or a 404), never a hung connection to a dead backend. **Verify:** `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://studio.nonagentic.ai` and one in-cluster `getent hosts w2v.redacted` recorded.
- **P2.3** Given the namespace's Redis, when it is deleted, then no other namespace's Deployment names it. **Verify:** an env scan over every Deployment recorded in the evidence.

### P3 — evidence

- **P3.1** Given the unit, when it closes, then `docs/evidence/2026-11-16-w2v-retirement.md` carries one row per scenario with command and output. **Verify:** the document and `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` green on it.

Blocker: #299 — the Rust port trusts a bare `X-Tenant-Id` (same class as #226); the
service cannot run live until its gate is restored. The image, the Deployment swap and the
Python retirement land now at replicas 0 (the reference's parked state); P2.2/P2.3 unblock
with #299.

## Goal

`apps/scientific` — absorbed in #105, merged and never deployed — is the live `scientific-processor`
service: a published image, the existing Deployment running it with its existing ConfigMap and
Secret, the Python image gone, and the reference repository archived after its High set is clear.

## Plan / audit source

- ADR 0006 §1 (`apps/scientific` is absorbed, not deployed), §3 (sequence)
- ADR 0007 §1 (destination table), §Consequences (deployment is a later unit)
- Precedent: #205 (research deploy and cutover), #71/#95 (per-app deploy-and-cutover)

**Split reason:** the publish row is a change in this repository with a code gate; the deployment
lives in the private deployment repository with a different acceptance gate. Two units, two PRs.

## Claim

| Field | Value |

| Branch | `issue/212-scientific-deploy` |
| HEAD | `dc3f9d9` |

| Contract | `apps/scientific/contract/` — captured document, drop table, lock | main |
| Publish | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` `publish-service-images` matrix | main |
| Deploy | `clusters/strato/services/scientific-processor/` | deployment-repository main |
| Evidence | `docs/evidence/2026-11-16-scientific-cutover.md` | to create |

## Current state

| P2 — deployed | ABSENT | the Deployment runs the Python image at `replicas: 0` |
| P3 — legacy retired and archived | ABSENT | the reference deployment exists; its repository is unarchived |
| P4 — evidence | ABSENT | no document |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the publish row

- **P1.1** Given `apps/scientific` is on `main`, when the workflow is read, then a matrix row names `package: conveyor-scientific`, `bin: conveyor-scientific` and `image: conveyor-scientific` (never `scientific-processor`, which Flux auto-deploys). **Verify:** `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` names the row; the main push after merge publishes the image.
- **P1.2** Given the published image, when it is smoke-tested, then `--check-lock` passes inside the image. **Verify:** the publish job's smoke step and `docker run --rm <image> --check-lock`.

### P2 — the deployment

- **P2.1** Given the digest P1 published, when the Deployment is read, then it pins that digest by index digest and still references the existing `scientific-processor-secrets` Secret. **Verify:** `kubectl -n scientific-processor get deploy scientific-processor -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` and the secret refs.
- **P2.2** Given the deployed pod, when its readiness probe fires, then `/health` answers 200 and no restart occurs. **Verify:** `kubectl -n scientific-processor get pods` (0 restarts) and one recorded `/health` response.
- **P2.3** Given the deployed service, when one `/api/stats` request runs, then it answers with the captured contract's shape. **Verify:** the recorded request/response in the evidence document.

### P3 — retire and archive

**Definition of Ready**

The published design pack names the cluster's machines in running text: `hp1`, `hp2`, `mf1`,
`worker1`, `worker3`, `mini<N>`. Examples:

- `SPEC` — "The grading node is `hp1` … `hp1` is not hp2 (CI capacity) and not mf1 (MinIO + the PG standby)."
- `plans/00-INDEX` — "Benchmark sandbox Jobs run on `hp1` … not hp2 (CI capacity), not mf1."

`no-private-refs` does not catch these and should not: it matches a machine name only in a host
position (next to a login command, or with a `.local`/`.redacted`/`.[tailnet]` suffix), because a rule
that fired on every bare name would cry wolf across the whole estate. #186 removed the host-position
occurrences; this is the remaining prose class.

**Acceptance**

- No bare estate node name in `docs/**/*.md`, and the pack regenerated from those sources.
- The documents still say what they mean: "the grading node", "the CI node", "the MinIO and standby
  host" — the identity of a machine is not information a public reader can act on, but its role is.

**Definition of Done**

- One commit on `issue/<n>-node-names`, one PR, `Closes #<n>`.
- `build-docs.py --check` clean, so the generated pack matches its sources.

Follow-up to #184 / #186, which deliberately stopped at the host-position matches.

| P1 the deadlock | CONFIRMED | Cord pulled 00:11:43; `licence.sync` is not in `ANDON_ALLOWED_KINDS`, so `app_licence.checked_at` stayed at 00:10:19 while the worker kept serving; at 03:46 the console refused with `the conveyor entitlement was last confirmed 12998s ago, which is older than 3600s`. `POST /api/actions/andon.release/invocations` requires the same fresh entitlement, so the sanctioned release could not run. The cord was released by a direct `andon_state` update at 03:58:47, after which the sync resumed and refreshed by 04:00. |
| P2 the console under a pulled cord | CONFIRMED | The whole SPA refuses to start while the entitlement is stale, including the screens an operator would use to diagnose the cord. |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the release path must not depend on what the cord blocks

- **P1.1** Given a pulled cord and an `app_licence` older than `STALE_AFTER`, when a permitted principal invokes `andon.release`, then the action succeeds and the worker resumes claiming every kind on its next tick.
  Verify: an integration test that pulls the cord, ages `app_licence.checked_at` past `STALE_AFTER`, and invokes `andon.release` → 200 (to create in `crates/actions/tests/`).
- **P1.2** Given the same state, when the worker ticks, then `licence.sync` (which starts no work; it refreshes an entitlement) is claimable while the cord is pulled.
  Verify: the claim filter includes `licence.sync` under an engaged cord, tested at `crates/store/tests/jobs.rs` (claim-with kinds).

**Definition of Ready**

`apps/research/tests/media_parity.rs:192` replayed `score_report` for the media golden and failed:

```
avg_score: 0.7333      (produced)
avg_score: 0.7332      (captured)
```

**Cause.** `apps/research/contract/media/tolerances.toml` declares `quality_score` and `freshness`
volatile, so both are normalised to `<volatile>` on each side before comparison. `avg_score` is
**not** declared volatile, and `apps/research/src/media/scoring.rs:188` documents it as
`(0.7646 + 0.7021) / 2 — the captured score_report.avg_score`. The fixture therefore normalises
the two inputs it admits can move, then pins their mean to four decimals — and `freshness` is
wall-clock dependent, so the mean lands on the wrong side of a rounding boundary when the run
happens at a particular time.

This is why `main` passed the same suite minutes after the PR failed it: same code, different run
time. It is a time-dependent capture, not a code difference.

**Acceptance**

- The parity replay is deterministic: repeated runs of the same commit agree, whatever the clock.
- The captured `score_report` still proves what it is for — that the score components and the
  total item count match.

**Definition of Done**

- Either `avg_score` joins the volatile list, or the capture's freshness is pinned so the mean is
  stable; whichever the owner prefers, with the choice recorded here.
- The Rust suite is green twice in a row on the same commit, run through the estate build guard.

Found while scrubbing estate machine names from the tree (#184); unrelated to that change — this
issue exists so the next PR does not have to argue with it again.

Requirement: a host row (addressable host, role, allowed unit names) and an `apps/host-agent` binary answering `status`, `logs` and `restart` over that unit list and nothing else; the key that reaches it is forced-command, so no arbitrary command can be asked for.

- **P1.1** Given a verb outside the set, when the agent receives it, then it refuses and logs the refusal.
  Verify: `apps/host-agent/tests/verbs.rs::an_unknown_verb_is_refused`
- **P1.2** Given a unit name outside the host's row, when `restart` runs, then it refuses.
  Verify: same file → `::an_unknown_unit_is_refused`
- **P1.3** Given the forced-command key, when a shell is requested, then the agent runs no command and exits non-zero.
  Verify: same file → `::the_key_cannot_run_a_command`

### P2 — the host actions

Requirement: `ops.host_status` and `ops.host_logs` are reads; `ops.host_restart_unit` is `Effect::Destructive` and reuses #171's approval gate.

- **P2.1** Given an unregistered host, when `ops.host_status` runs, then it refuses with a typed error.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops_host.rs::an_unregistered_host_refuses`
- **P2.2** Given an approved restart, when `ops.host_restart_unit` runs, then the unit's state is read back in `checks[]`.
  Verify: same file → `::the_restart_reads_back`

## Dependencies

| blocked-by | #171 | open |
| related | #170 | open |

## Definition of ready

      ⚠️ Corrected 2026-11-16: an earlier note on this issue named "SPEC_V2 §10.4.1"; **no such subsection exists** (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.4 has no `10.4.x`). The host-control mechanism is plan 04 §4; the spec fixes only the effect class and the broker rules.
- [x] Every part carries a `Verify:` naming the test that will exist (`apps/host-agent/tests/verbs.rs`, `crates/actions/tests/ops_host.rs`).
- [x] Dependencies are typed: `blocked-by #171` — the approval binding `ops.host_restart_unit` reuses — is open and is the only construction blocker; `related #170` is delivered by PR (the client pattern is in `crates/ops`).
- [x] One-PR scope: `apps/host-agent` (binary), one registry migration, the three `ops.host_*` actions and their tests. Agent installation on a host is the separate "Deployment prerequisite" step and is not a second PR.
- [x] The credential boundary is fixed by plan 04 §4: the **agent** holds the host credential; the conveyor holds none. The agent answers a fixed verb set over a forced-command key; no arbitrary command surface exists.
- [x] The two OS mechanisms are named: `launchctl` (mini1/mini2, macOS) and `systemctl` (pgx/[host], Linux) behind one small trait; a host row names which applies.
- [x] The live proof target is decided: a throwaway probe unit created for this unit (`com.nonagentic.conveyor-probe` on mini2, launchd), so the approved restart exercises the destructive path **without touching a production unit**; read-only `status`/`logs` additionally exercise one real unit.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/167-sse-delivery-measurement` |
| HEAD | `a120787` + the fix |
| Session | m4.local · claude-code · `#167` |
| Updated | 2026-11-15 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## What happens

`crates/api/tests/sse_board.rs::a_second_client_on_the_board_sees_card_moved_live_and_on_replay`
fails the full-suite local gate on a loaded developer box, and passes alone and on CI.

Measured on m4.local, 2026-11-15, three consecutive `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` runs at three
different heads:

| run | delivered | gate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (#118's session, recorded) | 258 ms | red |
| 2 | 305 ms | red |
| 3 | 312 ms | red |
| 4 | 373 ms | red |

The same test passes on its own (`cargo-guard test -p conveyor-api --test sse_board` → 1 passed,
4.7 s), and `main@53d7bac`'s CI `checks` job is green — so the 200 ms property holds on the
4-core runner and misses on this box while 2 211 tests run in parallel.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than re-running

1. **Every lane pays it.** The local gate is the precondition for opening a PR; a red gate for an
   unrelated reason is how a lane learns to re-run until green.
2. **The measurement conflates two things.** The clock starts before `move_card` (an HTTP request
   that claims a card, writes it and publishes the event) and stops when the frame arrives. Under
   load the mover's own write dominates. Property (e) is about **delivery** latency; the test
   needs the publish instant (the event row's own timestamp, or a header the move returns) and to
   measure from there.

## Shape of the fix

- Measure delivery from the published event's own timestamp, not from before the mover's request.
- Keep 200 ms as the bound on that measurement.
- If the bus exposes no publish instant today, that is the missing piece and it belongs on the
  event row, not on a wider test budget.

## Acceptance

Given the full suite on a loaded box, when the gate runs, then the property is measured from the
publish instant and holds — and the assertion's message names the two instants it used.
Verify: `cargo nextest run -p conveyor-api --test sse_board` repeated 20 times under
`--test-threads` saturation stays green.

## Goal

(`.pptx`) and the same model renders to PDF and PNG, so no Python service and no LibreOffice stand
between a project's cards and its deck.

## Plan / audit source

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

| Code | `crates/actions/src/media.rs` — the toolkit pattern this family follows | main@53d7bac |
| Capture | `apps/media/contract/slide_service/{cases.txt,seed.sql}` — the started-and-stopped capture | main@53d7bac |
| App | `crates/deck` | to create |
| Test | `crates/deck/tests/pptx.rs::a_package_opens_as_a_zip_and_carries_the_four_layouts` | to create |
| Test | `crates/deck/tests/render.rs::one_deck_renders_to_pdf_and_png_with_the_same_text` | to create |
| Issue | #83 | open (binds published toolkits) |
| Issue | #158 | merged (the media unit this follows) |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@53d7bac850b6edc91373d7090446ba7c4bb15802` · measured 2026-11-15
- Docs: ADR 0007 blob `c66f941b` · ADR 0006 blob `18afa65b` · `03-DELIVERY.md` blob `77444c83`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 deck model + OOXML writer | ABSENT | `git ls-tree main crates/` → no `deck`; `git ls-tree main crates/render` → model→SVG/PNG/PDF/XMI only |
| P2 PDF/PNG from the same model | ABSENT | `crates/render/src/lib.rs` exposes `ModelSnapshot` rendering; no deck model exists to render |
| P3 the deck toolkit | ABSENT | `crates/actions/src/` has no deck family; registry is 332 actions, none a deck |
| P4 the reference capture | PARTIAL | `apps/media/contract/slide_service/cases.txt` (26 lines) and `seed.sql` only — no lock, no goldens, no drop table |

The capture was started and stopped because ADR 0007 §7 moved decks out of `apps/media`; completing it
is part of this issue so the drop table is evidenced rather than assumed.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the deck model and the OOXML writer

Requirement: one deck model (slides, each one of the four fixed layouts) is written as a `.pptx`
package that PowerPoint and LibreOffice open, with no Python and no LibreOffice in the pipeline
(ADR 0007 §7).

- **P1.1** Given a deck of one slide per layout, when the package is written, then it is a valid ZIP
  whose part tree contains `[Content_Types].xml`, `ppt/presentation.xml`, one `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`
  per slide and a notes part for the notes layout.
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/pptx.rs::a_package_opens_as_a_zip_and_carries_the_four_layouts`
- **P1.2** Given a deck that names any layout outside the fixed four, when it is written, then the
  request is refused by name listing the supported layouts — never silently downgraded.
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/pptx.rs::a_layout_outside_the_fixed_four_is_refused_by_name`
- **P1.3** Given the same deck model twice, when each is written in a separate process, then the two
  packages are **byte-identical** (no timestamp, no random id, no hash-map order).
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/pptx.rs::two_processes_write_identical_packages`

### P2 — PDF and PNG through `crates/render`

Requirement: the same deck model renders to PDF and to PNG through the existing pure renderer, so the
deck and the document cannot disagree about the text (ADR 0007 §7).

- **P2.1** Given the same deck, when it is rendered to PDF and to PNG, then both carry the same slide
  text and the same page count.
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/render.rs::one_deck_renders_to_pdf_and_png_with_the_same_text`
- **P2.2** Given a deck with an image layout, when the image file is absent, then the render fails
  typed naming the slide and the field — never a blank frame.
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/render.rs::a_missing_image_names_its_slide_and_field`
- **P2.3** Given the same deck twice, when rendered in two processes, then each format's bytes are
  identical (the renderer's own determinism contract, carried to the deck model).
  Verify: `crates/deck/tests/render.rs::rendering_is_byte_identical_across_processes`

### P3 — the deck toolkit

Requirement: a project reaches a deck through the broker, not through a library call: one action with
its effect class, its idempotency and a closed schema, beside the other families (SPEC_V2 §11.3).

- **P3.1** Given the registry, when it is listed, then `decks.render` exists with effect `write`, an
  idempotency declaration and a closed input schema naming the deck model's fields.
  Verify: `crates/actions/src/deck.rs` + `crates/actions/tests/registry.rs::the_registry_is_exactly_the_declared_set`
- **P3.2** Given a deck request, when the action runs, then the artefact lands through conveyor's
  document/artefact route with its content hash and tenant prefix — no store credential is read by
  the crate.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/parity_http_mcp.rs` sample for `decks.render`
- **P3.3** Given a caller whose binding ceiling is below `write`, when it invokes `decks.render`, then
  it is refused by the ceiling before the deck is built.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/tool_effect.rs::effect_ceiling_is_never_raised` (existing harness, new case)

### P4 — the reference capture and its drop table

Requirement: what `slide_service` served is captured from its running image and every operation is
either reproduced by this model or dropped with a reason (the #105/#139 precedent).

- **P4.1** Given the reference image, when the capture runs, then `openapi.lock.json`,
  `operations.txt`, `capabilities.txt`, `manifest.json` (digest) and goldens for the admission
  branches exist under `apps/media/contract/slide_service/`.
  Verify: `ls apps/media/contract/slide_service/` → the five files, and each golden case in `cases.txt`
- **P4.2** Given the captured operations, when the drop table is read, then every operation is
  "reproduced by `crates/deck`" or dropped with a reason, and the LibreOffice-only rendering paths
  are named as the accepted fidelity deviation.
  Verify: the drop table in `apps/media/contract/slide_service/README.md` has no unaccounted row

| Kind | Issue | Source | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #158 | the media unit that captured `slide_service` partially; ADR 0007 §7 moved decks out of it | merged |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #83 | binds the toolkits this issue publishes and deploys them | open |
| related | #144 | `runner/v1`; a deck is built in-process, so no executor image is needed | merged |

No `blocked-by`: the work can start now. The toolkit is published before #83 binds it, exactly as
#139's toolkit was.

## Definition of ready

- Every path in References resolves at its stated ref (or is marked `to create`).
- Every part carries a scenario with a `Verify:` line.
- No `blocked-by` issue is open.

## Definition of done

- Every part's scenarios green.
- The local gate is green before the PR: fmt, clippy with warnings denied, the workspace suite, and
  the design-pack gates.
- One non-draft PR, `Closes #<this issue>`, merged.

## Out of scope

- LibreOffice layout fidelity. ADR 0007 §7 accepts the deviation: the v1 template set is fixed so
  "PPTX support" cannot become unlimited work, and a deck LibreOffice would lay out differently is
  in scope only when a v2 template set is agreed.
- Arbitrary template editing, theme CRUD, animated transitions, speaker notes beyond the notes layout,
  and slide-level scripting — the reference's catalogue surfaces are dropped in P4 with reasons.
- The retired w2v orchestrator's deck stages; the conveyor's own project/card model drives a deck.

## Deployment prerequisite

None at merge time: `crates/deck` is a library and `decks.render` runs in `apps/server`. The toolkit
is bound and deployed by #83.

1. Does the PDF/PNG path need a new public entry in `crates/render` (`svg → png|pdf`), or can the deck
   model reuse `ModelSnapshot`? Measured: `crates/render` renders one model; a small generic
   SVG-to-bytes entry is the likely shape, and it must not become a second renderer.
2. Are the four layouts (title, bullets, image, notes) the complete v1 set, or does the reference's

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/inference_tenant_endpoint.rs` (to create) — two tenants, two stub destinations, each run reaches its own.
- **P1.2** Given a tenant with no registered destination, when an agent step runs, then the platform default applies if configured, else the action refuses `unconfigured` exactly as today.
  Verify: same file, `::a_tenant_without_a_destination_gets_the_platform_default_or_a_visible_refusal`.

### P2 — a tenant-admin registers it in the console

- **P2.1** Given a tenant-admin, when they register a destination and a credential, then it is usable without a pod restart, the credential is sealed (never readable back), and the registration is audited.
  Verify: `path::test` (to create) plus a live console click-through recorded here.
- **P2.2** Given a non-admin caller, when they attempt the registration, then it is refused and nothing is written.

## Goal

Give every programme output durable provenance — author, append-only revision, attachments, and an
admin-only publish gate — so invited tenant members can do the work and an admin decides what the
public sees.

## Plan sources

- `docs/plans/slices/S09-documents-integrations.md` — the document aggregate this extends.
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` — the issue and PR contract.
- Session plan (owner-approved 2026-11-15, rev 3): the work-store lane, slices A–E.

## References

| Ref | What it resolves to | State |
|---|---|---|
| `migrations/0013_documents.sql` | `document` table and `kind` CHECK | exists |
| `migrations/0039_document_outputs.sql` | `body`, `publishable`, `card_id` | exists |
| `migrations/0002_domain.sql:341` | generic `revision` table, unique `(tenant, entity_type, entity_id, seq)` | exists |
| `crates/actions/src/documents/actions.rs` | create/compose/get/list/download/update/delete | exists |
| `crates/store/src/document.rs` | document store reads/writes | exists |
| `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs:207` | `HandlerCtx.role` and `actor_id` | exists |
| `crates/store/src/governance.rs:539` | `write_snapshot_revision` — the one revision writer | exists |
| `crates/api/src/design.rs` | public design routes | exists |
| `crates/pack/src/outputs.rs` | `outputs.js` metadata | exists |
| `docs/design/v2.js`, `docs/design/console.js` | the console | exists |
| `docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` | console controls cross the wire | exists |
| `crates/api/tests/documents_roundtrip.rs` | document action tests | exists |
| `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs` | public design route tests | exists |
| `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs` | provenance/revision/publish tests | to create |
| `crates/store/tests/document_revision.rs` | revision store tests | to create |

## Baseline

`main@abe6f8d681eee9359753c9f734eb0734414e26bf`, measured 2026-11-15. Doc blobs:
`03-DELIVERY.md` `8a69200639243f74faae93cbf8f4c4e349a28cb5`,
`0039_document_outputs.sql` `78107ff2efd09d96a1227baf2f17157b2b8fc27f`,
`documents/actions.rs` `6adc98ede0286bae4bf6a8e0706de88f5f3e41f4`,
`store/document.rs` `75e61db66de4fcce530ffd62f757025c2b7b0127`,
`docs/design/README.md` `abdf6d5b23ce52c2bf2b60371d9557bc8e0e0af5`.

## Current state

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 authorship | ABSENT | no `created_by`/`updated_by` in `0013`/`0039`; `DocumentOut` has no author |
| P2 revisions | ABSENT | no document arm of `write_snapshot_revision`; `revision` has zero document rows by design |
| P3 publish gate | PARTIAL | `publishable` exists; any `documents:write` holder flips it in `documents.update` |
| P4 attachments | ABSENT | `documents.create` stores objects; no parent link, no `attachment` kind, pack reads `body IS NOT NULL` only |
| P5 console | PARTIAL | compose/edit/read/delete/publish wired; no author, history, attachments, queue; register caps at 200 |
| P6 tests/docs | PARTIAL | document tests exist; none cover provenance, revisions, attachments or the gate |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — authorship on every row

Given a member composes a document, when it is read back, then `created_by`/`updated_by` name that
member and `DocumentOut` carries the display names; a legacy row renders author null ("unrecorded"),
never an invented name.

Verify: `rbuild -- nextest -p conveyor-api --test document_workflow` (to create).

### P2 — append-only revisions

Given a document at v1, when a writer saves v2, then `documents.revision_list` returns seq 1 with
the v1 content and its author; `documents.revision_restore {seq: 1}` creates v3 with the v1 content
and `publishable=false`; the first mutation of a legacy row writes its pre-image first.

Verify: `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::a_member_drafts_and_requests_an_admin_publishes_and_history_restores` and `::the_first_edit_of_a_legacy_row_writes_its_pre_image`.

### P3 — admin-only publish + request queue

Given a `member`, when they call `documents.publish`, then 403 `publish_forbidden`; given an `admin`
or `kata_executor`, then `publishable=true` and `published_at/by` set. Given a member, when they
update a published row's title/body, then 409 `published_locked`; a stale `If-Match` is the repo's 412, not a 409. `documents.request_publish` sets a
queue flag an admin can filter; the operator CLI (kata) keeps importing published content.

Verify: `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::publish_gate`.

### P4 — attachments, safely published

Given a published text output, when a writer attaches a PNG with a `parent_document_id`, then the
child row is `kind='attachment'` and `GET /design/docs/attachment-<id>` serves it `inline` with `nosniff` and
a sandbox CSP; an SVG is served `attachment`, never inline; an attachment whose parent is unpublished
is a 404 `no-store`; ETag is the content hash and honours `If-None-Match`.

Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs::published_attachments_are_served_safely_and_leave_with_the_parent`
and `crates/api/tests/document_workflow.rs::an_attachment_is_a_child_document_with_its_parents_scope`.

### P5 — the console work panel

Given a signed-in member on a project, when the work panel renders, then each output shows author,
category, unit and state, with History and Attach controls; Request publish is visible to writers,
Publish/Unpublish only to admins; the register filters by project/unit/category/state/author and
pages past 200 via `next_cursor`; signed out, the page makes zero API requests.

Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` (extended cases).

### P6 — docs and gates

Given the design pack, when `build-docs --check`, `check-docs` and `no-private-refs` run, then green;
`docs/design/README.md` states the roles, the publish gate and attachments.

Verify: `python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check && node docs/design/scripts/check-docs.cjs
&& bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh`.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Source | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| acceptance-blocked-by | #149 | shared `docs/design/v2.js` (its PR #150 is open); console slice rebases on it | open |
| related | #151 | export mirror should carry category/unit after this lands | open |
| related | #97 | the signed-in live proof needs the owner's Keycloak session | open |
| related | #128 | the live public window this extends | closed |

No `blocked-by`: the backend slices are file-disjoint from #149; construction starts now.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline sha and doc blob shas named.
- [x] Every reference resolves at `origin/main`.
- [x] Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no open `blocked-by`.
- [x] One PR, one branch; overlaps with #149 sequenced through `acceptance-blocked-by`.
- [x] No private repository or host named.

## Definition of done

- All six parts pass at the PR head with evidence rows.

## Goal

No open issue can carry `status:ready` while a branch or an open PR proves the work is live, because an hourly server-side check restores the label instead of a session remembering to.

## Plan / audit source

- **P1.3** Given `status:blocked` whose plain `Blocker: #N` line names a closed or missing issue, or `status:claimed` with no branch, no PR and no update in 48 h, when `board.py` runs, then it reports it in its summary and changes nothing.

## Goal

The analysis stage service of the media estate exists in this workspace as the library
`crates/analysis` — the `analyse.*` rubric/scoring families with no HTTP transport, no database and
no job rows of its own — and one operation (`analyse.site`) is invocable through the action
registry.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/decisions/0007-tool-estate-conveyor-and-coding.md` §Decision 1 (the `crates/analysis` row),
  §5 (library, not a service), §8 (providers), §Consequences (the sequence after #144)
- `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §Decision and §3 (the absorption sequence)
- `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" (the five-step contract this follows)
- `docs/plans/04-TOOL-ESTATE-INVENTORY.md` §1/§5 (the group's measured state and the destination
  list)
- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.4 and §10.4.1 (`analyse.*` and its boundary against `metrics.*`), §11.2
  (the live row), §11.3 (the broker), §11.4 (effect classes)

## Claim

The capture source (P1) is the deployed analysis service, whose repository is private and is
therefore not linked from this public issue. Its identity is recorded in the capture document by
revision sha, image digest and capture date — a private source may inform an issue but must not be
named by repository path here.

## Baseline

- Code: `main@4f7aa4adf55ce4731bc5fa64343000bd8571bf69` · measured 2026-11-15
- Docs: ADR 0007 blob `c66f941b7d3050cfed28eb369f3ec48320b06326` · inventory blob

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 capture + drop table | **landed** on `issue/154-analysis` @ `47b0a39` | `docs/evidence/analysis-capture-2026-11-15.md` + the served document beside it; 92 operations, measured — not 46. The `capture` tests in `tests/parity.rs` fail on an unaccounted operation |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the capture and the drop table

`0007` §Decision 1 · `0004` §"How a service joins" step 1

Requirement: every absorbed operation has a recorded request/response pair pinned to the captured
revision and image digest, and every operation that is not ported is a row with a reason.

- **P1.1** Given the capture, when it is inspected, then it names the source revision, the image
  digest, the capture date and a request/response pair per operation.
  Verify: `ls docs/evidence/analysis-*.md` → one capture document, every row carrying all four
  (`to create`)
- **P1.2** Given the capture, when an operation is not ported, then its row carries one of the
  reasons `dropped: transport`, `dropped: no consumer`, `dropped: deferred` — never an empty cell.
  Verify: the capture's drop table has no row without a reason (`to create`)

### P2 — the crate and the rubric kernel

`0007` §5 · `0006` §2

Requirement: `crates/analysis` is a pure library — no `reqwest`, no `sqlx`, no job row — carrying
the one scoring kernel that the SEO, CRO and marketing scorecards each re-implemented in the
source.

- **P2.1** Given a finding set for one category, when it is scored, then the score is
  `floor + (100 − floor)·e^(−penalty/k)`, rounded half-to-even to one decimal, floored at
  `score_floor`, with severity weights 30/15/7/3/0 and `k = 25`.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis rubric` (`to create`)
- **P2.2** Given two findings that are the same underlying issue under different `check_id`s, when
  findings are deduplicated, then one survives and the cross-scanner equivalence map is what
  decided it.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis rubric -- dedupe` (`to create`)
- **P2.3** Given the crate's manifest, when its dependency tree is inspected, then no transport or
  database crate is present.
  Verify: `cargo tree -p conveyor-analysis --depth 1` names no `reqwest`, `hyper` or `sqlx`

### P3 — `analyse.site`, the deterministic base scan

`SPEC_V2` §10.4 · `0007` §Decision 1

Requirement: the nineteen base checks of the source scanner run over a supplied document (URL +
HTML), producing findings whose `check_id`s and severities are those of the source.

- **P3.1** Given a page missing a title and a meta description, when it is analysed, then both
  findings are returned with their source `check_id`s and severities.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test site` (`to create`)
- **P3.2** Given the same document twice, when it is analysed twice, then the two reports are
  byte-identical — the scan is a pure function of its input.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test site -- determinism` (`to create`)
- **P3.3** Given a document, when the crate analyses it, then the crate performs no network call
  and reads no database.
  Verify: `cargo tree -p conveyor-analysis --depth 1` plus review of `src/site/`

### P4 — `analyse.site`, the audit groups

`SPEC_V2` §10.4 · `0007` §Decision 1

Requirement: the seven deterministic audit groups of the source's full scan (readability, keyword,
snippet, E-E-A-T, schema coverage, internal linking, geo) run in the same pure pass.

- **P4.1** Given a page with structured data absent, when the full scan runs, then the schema
  group contributes its finding and the group score reflects it.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test site -- audit` (`to create`)
- **P4.2** Given a group with no findings, when the scorecard is computed, then that group scores
  100.0 and still appears in the breakdown.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test site -- empty_group` (`to create`)

### P5 — `analyse.app` and `analyse.brand`

`SPEC_V2` §10.4 (`analyse.app`, `analyse.brand`) · `0007` §Decision 1

Requirement: the critique scanners' scoring and the brand extraction/comparison run over evidence
captured by the media executors rather than over a page the library fetches.

- **P5.1** Given a captured page-evidence bundle, when `analyse.app` runs, then a11y, performance,
  security and UX findings are returned with the source's category weights.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test app` (`to create`, live scenario waits on #139)
- **P5.2** Given two brand snapshots, when they are compared, then the comparison names the
  changed attributes and their direction.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test brand` (`to create`)

### P6 — the remaining families and the generation providers

`SPEC_V2` §10.4 (`analyse.content`, `analyse.report`) · `0007` §8

Requirement: the remaining two families exist as library entry points, and the seven generation
providers are request/response mappings carrying the `(job_id, attempt)` idempotency key, with no
transport in this crate.

- **P6.1** Given a content document and a rubric, when `analyse.content` runs, then the findings are
  those of the captured contract.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test content` (`to create`)
- **P6.2** Given a provider submission for a retried attempt, when the request is built, then it
  carries the same `(job_id, attempt)` key as the first attempt.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test providers` (`to create`)

### P7 — the parity gate

`0004` §"How a service joins" step 5

Requirement: a test reads the capture and fails when any captured operation is neither ported nor
explicitly dropped, so the port cannot quietly shrink.

- **P7.1** Given the capture, when the parity test runs, then every operation id resolves to a
  Rust entry point or to a drop row with a reason, and an unaccounted row fails the test.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-analysis --test parity` (`to create`)

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #144 | `0007` §Consequences: the runner substrate is the enabler for the media images this crate's `analyse.app` consumes | merged (`4f7aa4a`) |
| related | #139 | `0007` §Consequences places the media images before this crate; `analyse.app` reads their evidence | open, claimed |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #139 | P5's live scenario needs a captured evidence bundle from a media executor; P2–P4 and P6–P7 do not | open |
| related | #83 | T14 binds the published toolkits; this crate publishes operations, not bindings | open |

No `blocked-by` edge: the crate is file-disjoint (`crates/analysis/**`, and `crates/actions` for
P2's one action) from every in-flight unit, so construction starts now.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named and the decision/plan/spec blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every reference resolves at `main@4f7aa4a`; #83, #139, #144 resolve.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; no `Blocker:` line, so not `status:blocked`.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from other ready issues.
- [x] Scope corrections applied: deployment, cutover, public flip and archive are out (the cutover
  unit), and the seven model servers stay external per `0007` §1.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the workspace suite, the design
  packs, `no-private-refs`).
- [ ] Tests added per part; none skipped; the ported cases come from the source's own suite.
- [ ] Docs updated: the inventory row for this group names the state, and the capture document
  exists under `docs/evidence/`.
- [ ] `--check-lock` regenerated if the action in P2 changes the served spec.
- [ ] Live verification recorded where a part is deployment-gated.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Deployment, cutover, the public flip and archiving the absorbed service — the cutover unit.
- The orchestrator: out of scope by ADR 0006 §Decision; conveyor's own project engine replaces it.
- The script-writing and content-generation services of the same estate: they are `produce.*`
  thin operations, not `analyse.*`, and no part of this issue ports them.
- `app_inspector`: deferred outright by `0007` §6 — not ported, not bound, not measured.
- The seven model servers: they stay external HTTP hosts bound as toolkits (`0007` §1).
- Any LLM-dependent enrichment (`content-gap`, the recommendation writer, the report critic, the
  narrative): recorded as a drop reason in P1, not silently omitted, and out of this unit's code.

## Deployment prerequisite

No. This unit is a library plus one action; nothing here deploys. The media evidence P5 needs is
deployment-gated by #139 and its own deploy unit.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which captured operations have a measured consumer? | capture (P1) | **Answered** at `47b0a39`: 92 operations, 16 with a measured consumer (14 in code, 2 by product contract). An operation with no measurable consumer is `dropped: no consumer`, recorded, not guessed |
| 2 | Does `analyse.site` belong in the action registry now, or wait for the T13/T14 broker? | owner | In the registry now — a library with no caller is dead code, and the broker later binds a toolkit to the same operation |
| 3 | Which version of the deterministic scan is the parity target when the source has both `scan` and `scan_audit`? | owner | Both: `scan` is P3, `scan_audit`'s additions are P4 |
| 4 | P3/P4 were ported from a checkout that is not `origin/main`; `geo` and `schema_coverage` have since moved. Re-port them, or pin the older revision as the parity target? | owner | Recorded, not silently re-ported — see the P1 evidence comment |

## Deviations recorded (not silent)

| # | Source behaviour | Here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | every finding carries a `finding_id` (`uuid7`) | no id in the library | a time-based id makes two runs of the same input differ, and P3.2's determinism is the contract; identity belongs to the row that persists a finding |
| 2 | `title.string` (a single text child) decides the title length checks | descendant text | a title that wraps its text in a child element would otherwise be skipped silently |
| 3 | `urlparse(...).netloc` compares hosts, including userinfo | host + explicit port | userinfo in a page URL is not a host difference |
| 4 | `seo_audit` fetches the page, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` itself | the caller supplies the bytes | fetching is `apps/research`'s contract and `apps/media`'s browser; a library that crawls is a second crawler |
| 5 | the scan mints findings through a dict factory with mutable defaults | typed `Finding` with explicit constructor | a field a check forgets is a compile error, not a missing key |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|

## Goal
The database's published programme outputs render deterministically to a public `programme/` Markdown tree with a manifest, so a contributor can read and propose a design change in git.

## Plan / audit source
`~/.claude/plans/coneyor-repo-is-public-zazzy-snowflake.md` § Unit 3 (owner-approved 2026-11-15: one-way export; no automated inbound sync).

## Current state (measured 2026-11-15)
| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Public live routes | DONE | `crates/pack/src/live.rs`, `/design/data/snapshot.js`, `/design/docs/outputs.js` |
| Published documents | DONE | 56 published rows in the `nonagentic` tenant |
| DB→`programme/` export | ABSENT | no `crates/pack/src/export.rs`, no `conveyor programme export` |
| Export gate | ABSENT | no `scripts/check-programme-export.py` |

## Parts and acceptance
**P1 — renderer.** `crates/pack/src/export.rs` renders `programme/README.md`, `programme/<project>/<category>/<slug>-<id8>.md` (frontmatter: document_id, version, title, project, unit, category, published_at) and `programme/manifest.json` (path, id, version, sha256). Deterministic: sorted paths, `generated_at` = max `updated_at`; only `publishable AND active AND body` rows; reuse `redact_text`.
Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-pack --locked` (render determinism + empty-body cases).

**P2 — CLI.** `conveyor programme export --tenant <slug> --out <dir|->` and `--check <dir>`; `-` prints one JSON document. No new auth surface; it reads the same DB URL as `snapshot`.
Verify: `conveyor --help` lists `programme`; `--check` on a stale tree exits non-zero.

## Goal

Conveyor can dispatch one unit of heavy work to a stateless, credential-free Kubernetes Job and take back a verified result, so no media or analysis capability ever needs its own queue, database or service API.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/decisions/0007-tool-estate-conveyor-and-coding.md` §Decision 3–4 (to create — lands with #143)
- ADR 0006 §Decision `apps/media` row (superseded on destination by 0007)
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` §"Issue content contract"; `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.3–§11.4 (broker, effect classes)
- Precedent in code: `apps/server/src/sandbox.rs` (benchmark Jobs)

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/144-runner-substrate` |
| HEAD | `056bf2cd8c2f895b3e152d7fc8814d6fb9b9dd40` |

| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0007-tool-estate-conveyor-and-coding.md` §Decision 3–4 | to create (lands with #143) |
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §Decision | main@085b11d |
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.2, §11.4 | main@085b11d |
| Code | `apps/server/src/sandbox.rs` — the batch/v1 create/get/delete shape, ConfigMap payload, no SA token | main@085b11d |
| Code | `crates/store/src/jobs.rs:claim_with` — leased claims with a kind filter | main@085b11d |
| Code | `apps/server/src/worker.rs` — poll loop, lease renewal, andon gate | main@085b11d |
| Code | `crates/api/src/documents.rs` — the byte-route + tenant/hash pattern to reuse | main@085b11d |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/objects.rs` — "no presigned URLs, ever" | main@085b11d |
| Code | `crates/domain/src/executor.rs` — the T0 run-executor seam this must NOT be confused with | main@085b11d |
| Test | `crates/runner/tests/job_spec.rs::job_has_no_service_account_token` | to create |
| Test | `crates/runner/tests/token.rs::token_is_refused_after_the_job_finishes` | to create |
| Test | `crates/api/tests/job_routes.rs::foreign_tenant_job_is_refused` | to create |
| Test | `apps/server/tests/runner_dispatch.rs::infrastructure_failure_retries_once` | to create |
| Issue | #139 | open (destination superseded) |
| Issue | #76, #83 | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@085b11d069ce5246e42bac780d60c6817f1ce014` · measured 2026-11-15
- Docs: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` blob `cc4a6a6d2e9d8b3f931670b34c65dd66d2f56198` · `03-DELIVERY.md` blob `3b0537d4ea783f14757043ac16791090ec84e0fd0` · ADR 0006 blob `3a5df580b27a9a3dde4d433b5475703f87955d7b`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 runner/v1 contract types and generated schemas | ABSENT | `crates/domain/src/runner.rs` absent; `crates/domain/src/executor.rs` is the T0 seam, a different concept |
| P2 generalised Job dispatch | PARTIAL | `apps/server/src/sandbox.rs:374` builds a `batch/v1` Job for benchmarks only; no configurable image map, no Secret, no attempt rows |
| P3 job-token byte routes | ABSENT | `crates/api/src/documents.rs` serves documents only; no `/api/jobs/*` routes |
| P4 attempt/runner rows | PARTIAL | `crates/store/src/jobs.rs` has leased jobs; no runner attempt or artefact rows; next migration is `0041` |
| P5 dispatch/poll/reap worker kinds | ABSENT | `apps/server/src/worker.rs` knows benchmark poll kinds, not a runner |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the runner/v1 contract, generated not hand-written
ADR 0007 §Decision 4

Requirement: one versioned instruction and result type in `crates/domain/src/runner.rs`, serialised to JSON Schema checked into `docs/contracts/runner/v1/`, with a golden round-trip test.

- **P1.1** Given the domain types, when the schema test runs, then the checked-in `instruction.schema.json` and `result.schema.json` match the generated bytes exactly.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-domain --test runner_contract` and `git diff --exit-code docs/contracts/runner/v1` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given an instruction JSON with an undeclared extra field, when parsed, then it is refused (`deny_unknown_fields`), and a full instruction round-trips byte-identically.
  Verify: `crates/domain/tests/runner_contract.rs::instruction_round_trips_and_refuses_unknown_fields` (to create)

### P2 — the generalised Job dispatcher
ADR 0007 §Decision 3; `apps/server/src/sandbox.rs`

Requirement: `crates/runner` builds a `batch/v1` Job from an instruction, with the payload in a ConfigMap, the job token in a Secret, resource limits, `activeDeadlineSeconds`, an image from a capability→image config, and create/get/delete against the API server with no `kube` crate; `sandbox.rs` delegates to it and the benchmark behaviour is unchanged.

- **P2.1** Given a dispatch, when the Job spec is built, then the pod has no service-account token, carries the instruction ConfigMap and the token Secret, and sets CPU/memory/ephemeral caps and the deadline.
  Verify: `crates/runner/tests/job_spec.rs::job_has_no_service_account_token` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given the refactor, when the benchmark suite runs, then the sandbox path still creates, polls and deletes its Jobs with the same contract.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test benchmark_jobs` (exists)

### P3 — job-token-fenced bytes and results
ADR 0007 §Decision 4; `crates/actions/src/integrations/objects.rs`

Requirement: conveyor mints a short-lived HMAC job token and serves `/api/jobs/{id}/inputs/{name}` (GET), `/outputs/{name}` (POST), `/result` (POST), `/progress` (PUT), fenced by the token **and** the job row (running, live lease, matching attempt and tenant); no presigned URL exists and no store credential leaves conveyor.

- **P3.1** Given a finished job, when its token is reused, then every job route answers 403; a token for tenant A on a tenant B job is refused; an expired token is refused.
  Verify: `crates/runner/tests/token.rs::token_is_refused_after_the_job_finishes` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given an uploaded output, when conveyor stores it, then the key is tenant-prefixed and the recomputed sha256 matches the manifest, and a key outside the instruction's declared outputs is refused.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/job_routes.rs::foreign_tenant_job_is_refused` and `::undeclared_output_key_is_refused` (to create)

### P4 — attempt and artefact rows
migration `0041`

Requirement: `runner_run(job_id, attempt, image_digest, namespace, job_name, status, started_at, finished_at)` plus runner artefacts, so a stale attempt's result cannot finish a newer one.

- **P4.1** Given attempt 1 superseded by attempt 2, when attempt 1's result arrives, then it is rejected and the job row is untouched.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/runner.rs::stale_attempt_result_is_rejected` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a migration applied to a fresh database, when the workspace migrates, then `0041` applies cleanly and the job table is unchanged.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store migrations` (exists)

### P5 — dispatch, poll and reap
`apps/server/src/worker.rs`

Requirement: `runner.dispatch` creates the Job and records the attempt; `runner.poll` reads progress/result and finishes the job; `runner.reap` deletes Jobs past their deadline; an infrastructure failure retries once with a new attempt, a `failed` result with a non-retryable code is permanent, and cancellation deletes the Job and revokes the token.

- **P5.1** Given a stubbed API server, when a dispatch job runs, then a Job is created and the row records the attempt, and the poll kind finishes it only after a valid result.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/runner_dispatch.rs::dispatch_then_poll_finishes_the_job` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given a pod that dies before posting a result, when the poll sees the failed condition, then the job goes to `pending` for exactly one retry, then dead-letters.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/runner_dispatch.rs::infrastructure_failure_retries_once` (to create)

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #139 | the media group this substrate serves; its destination moved to ADR 0007 | open |
| related | #76 | T13 tool platform: the broker catalogue over the same destinations; no ordering | blocked |
| related | #83 | T14 estate toolkits; consumes the runner later | blocked |
| blocks | #139 | the media executor images are this substrate's first consumer (ADR 0007 §Consequences) | blocked |

## Definition of ready

- Baseline and doc blob shas named; every cited path resolves at `main@085b11d` or is marked to create.
- Every part has a scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- No `blocked-by`; no `Blocker:` line; the state label is `status:ready`.
- No private repo slug, host or address in this body.

## Definition of done

- P1–P5 scenarios green at the PR head, each with an evidence row.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` green at the exact head.
- Migration `0041` applies on a fresh database; `Cargo.lock` committed for the schema dependency.
- `scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` green; `check-coverage` unchanged.
- One PR `Closes #N` merged; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- Creating the `media` or `analysis` repositories, their images, or any capability implementation.
- Creating the runner namespace, its RBAC, NetworkPolicy or egress controls (deployment session).
- The deck/PPTX crate, the media project type, seed data and frontend screens.
- Any change to the benchmark sandbox's observable behaviour.

## Deployment prerequisite

None to land the code. Before a live dispatch: a namespace, an RBAC rule allowing this service account to create/get/delete Jobs, the image map, and `CONVEYOR_JOB_TOKEN_KEY` (32 bytes, fail-closed when unset) — all supplied by the deployment unit, not this one.

## Open questions

1. Should the job token be HMAC over claims with a dedicated `CONVEYOR_JOB_TOKEN_KEY`, or reuse a Keycloak-issued service token? Dedicated HMAC is proposed because the token must be revocable per job and must not require an external issuer.

## Evidence at completion

| Part | Evidence | Date |
|---|---|---|
