<!-- issue-contract: v2 -->

## Goal

The Rust `inference-router` reproduces the reference's blank/vacuous completion handling — classification, one retry, recovery/refusal, and the attempt metric's `empty`/`empty_result` outcomes — so the #71 cutover neither changes user-visible behaviour nor disarms `InferenceRouterDeepseekEmptyCompletionsHigh`.

## Plan / audit source

Found during conveyor#137 P2 (2026-11-15). A source sweep of `apps/inference-router/src` for `blank`, `empty_result`, `vacuous` and `retry` finds no completion classification. The reference classifies every 2xx completion as blank, `empty_result` or `ok`, retries a blank once, and refuses a second blank with 502 `upstream_empty_completion`; `empty_result` is observe-only. Its attempt counter carries `outcome=empty|empty_result|ok` and the DeepSeek alert is keyed on that label.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/inference-router/src/routing.rs` — attempt snapshot, no empty classification | `origin/main@ad89f74` |
| Code | `apps/inference-router/src/provider/mod.rs` — the upstream response | `origin/main@ad89f74` |
| Issue | #137 — the metric families that need these outcome values | open |
| Issue | #71 — the cutover this blocks | open |

## Baseline

- Rust code: `main@ad89f74`, measured 2026-11-15.
- Reference behaviour: blank = every choice has no text and no tool calls; `empty_result` = schema-valid but vacuous; blank is retried once; a second blank is a 502 `upstream_empty_completion`; `empty_result` never retries and never refuses.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| classification | ABSENT | no `blank`/`empty_result`/`vacuous` in `apps/inference-router/src` |
| one-retry | ABSENT | no retry on a successful response |
| refusal | ABSENT | no `upstream_empty_completion` |
| metric outcomes | ABSENT | #137 P2 cannot emit `empty`/`empty_result` from the current attempt |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — classification

- **P1.1** Given a 2xx completion, when every choice has no text and no tool calls, then it is classified blank; when it is schema-valid but vacuous, `empty_result`; otherwise `ok`. Verify: unit tests for all three.

### P2 — one retry and the refusal

- **P2.1** Given a blank first attempt, when it is retried, then the second attempt is booked, and a second blank is refused with 502 `upstream_empty_completion`; an `empty_result` never retries and never refuses. Verify: recorded tests for both paths.

### P3 — metric outcomes

- **P3.1** Given a served or failed attempt, when #137 P2 emits `inference_router_provider_attempts_total`, then its `outcome` is `ok|empty|empty_result|invalid|error` per the reference. Verify: a scrape after a seeded blank and a seeded `empty_result`.

### P4 — parity proof

- **P4.1** Given the reference's golden cases plus one blank and one `empty_result`, when replayed, then the response and the attempt outcomes match. Verify: the existing contract harness/goldens extended with the two cases.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocks | #71 | the cutover must not change blank-completion behaviour or silence the alert | open |
| related | #137 | the metric families and their outcome labels | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named.
- [x] Every part has a BDD scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited.

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 1

Requirement: the group ships as few deployables as the runtime shapes allow — a browser image, an
ffmpeg image, and the thin operations hosted in the main server — with the toolkits kept separate

## Goal

The Rust `inference-router` reports the Prometheus families the estate's alert rules read, on a dedicated metrics listener, so the conveyor#71 cutover does not silence the router's token, cost and provider alerting.

## Plan / audit source

- conveyor#71 P2–P4 — the cutover this issue blocks. Found during #71 P2 (2026-11-15): the Rust binary serves **no** `/metrics`; cutting over would also empty the rules' inputs.
- The reference service's `src/observability/metrics.py` (2,339 lines, ~30 families) — the names and labels are fixed by it and by the rules below.
- The alert rules in the private deployment repository: 15 `inference_router_*` families are referenced, and `InferenceRouterMetricsAbsent` fires on the absence of `inference_router_requests_received_total` (warning, 10m).

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `apps/inference-router/src` — no metrics module today | main@ad89f74 (measured 2026-11-15) |
| Code | `apps/licenses/src/router/observability.rs` — the estate's Rust `/metrics` shape (`metrics-exporter-prometheus`) | main |
| Code (old) | the reference service's `src/observability/metrics.py` | the image pinned by `apps/inference-router/contract/manifest.json` |
| Rule | `InferenceRouterMetricsAbsent` — `absent(inference_router_requests_received_total)`, warning, 10m | private deployment repository |
| Deployment | the private deployment repository: `candidate-deployment.yaml` carries `alerting.nonagentic.ai/coverage: "none"` as the explicit placeholder | merged 2026-11-15 |
| Issue | conveyor#71 — the cutover this blocks | open |

## Baseline

- Rust code: `main@ad89f74`, measured 2026-11-15. A source sweep of `apps/inference-router` finds no metric emission (only comments and the OpenAPI description).
- Live Python service: 2 scrape targets `up=1` at `:9150` (measured 2026-11-15); the Service carries `prometheus.io/port: "9150"`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — metrics listener | ABSENT | no `/metrics` route and no metrics dependency; the image's only listener is `:8150` (`BIND_ADDR`) |
| P2 — alert-keyed families | ABSENT | 15 families referenced by rules: `provider_attempts_total`, `tokens_total`, `requests_received_total`, `cost_usd_unlicensed_total`, `provider_attempt_seconds_total`, `cost_events_unlicensed_total`, `cost_events_malformed_tenant_total`, `provider_errors_total`, `cost_tokens_unlicensed_total`, `cost_events_unattributed_total`, `effective_tenant_total`, `project_id_header_total`, `license_introspection_total`, `license_introspection_by_caller_total`, `inference_call_write_failed_total` |
| P3 — family-set gate | ABSENT | no test pins the exported set |
| P4 — scrape restored after cutover | BLOCKED | the candidate is explicitly opted out of alert coverage (`coverage: none`) |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — a dedicated metrics listener

- **P1.1** Given the service runs, when `GET /metrics` is scraped on the metrics port, then it answers 200 in the Prometheus text format, and the API port `:8150` has no `/metrics` route.
  Verify: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<pod>:<metrics>/metrics` → 200; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://<pod>:8150/metrics` → 404.
  ⛔ The metrics port must be separate: `:8150` is the unauthenticated inference API, and the estate deliberately moved `/metrics` off it (see the metrics PeerAuthentication in the private deployment repository).

- **P1.2** Given `metrics-exporter-prometheus` is installed once per process, when tests build several routers, then the recorder install does not panic.
  Verify: the crate's test suite (the `licenses` crate's `observability.rs` is the pattern).

### P2 — the alert-keyed families

- **P2.1** Given the rules' expressions, when the service answers `/metrics`, then every one of the 15 families above is present with the label sets the rules read.
  Verify: a test that parses the rendered exposition and asserts the family names, plus one recorded scrape compared against the Python service's exposition for the same synthetic call.
- **P2.2** Given a completion, when it is served, then `provider_attempts_total`, `tokens_total` and `requests_received_total` move by the same amounts as the reference for the same request.
  Verify: a parity test seeded from `apps/inference-router/contract/golden/`; the reference's own metrics test is the tolerance source.

### P3 — the family-set gate

- **P3.1** Given the codebase, when the test suite runs, then a test asserts the exported family set contains the 15 above and fails if one disappears.
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-inference-router metrics_families`.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — one library, one published-set read

Requirement: the snapshot/output renderers move to a library crate that both the CLI and the API
can call; one read-only transaction produces the whole public view byte-identically.

- **P1.1** Given a tenant with published outputs, when `site_view` builds the site, then it opens
  one scoped read-only transaction, reads only `publishable AND status='active'` rows with a body,
  and `generated_at` is the max row `updated_at` (constant on an empty tenant), never `now`.
  Verify: `crates/pack/tests/live.rs::one_tx_and_max_updated_at` (to create at `crates/pack`).
- **P1.2** Given the same tenant and database, when `conveyor snapshot --out D` writes files, then
  they are byte-identical to the live view's `snapshot.js`/pages.
  Verify: `apps/server/tests/snapshot_deterministic.rs::cli_and_live_bytes_match` (extend).

### P2 — live unauthenticated routes

Requirement: `GET|HEAD /design/data/snapshot.js`, `/design/docs/outputs.js` and

  placeholder.

Requirement: every public byte passes the snapshot redaction and the existing XSS hardening.

  then the rendered JS/HTML carries the redacted form. Given `<script>`, `onerror=` and a
  `javascript:` link in the body, then the page has no executable markup or unsafe URL.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/design_live.rs::redaction_and_xss_inert`.

## Goal

A publish is visible on `nonagentic.ai/design` immediately: the design pack's HTML (dynamic, never cached) references its JS/CSS/data with a per-publish version, so Cloudflare's 4 h static-asset cache cannot serve the previous pack's scripts.

## Current state (measured 2026-11-15)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| HTML is dynamic | `curl -I https://nonagentic.ai/design/studio.html` → `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` |
| Assets are cached 4 h | `v2.js` → `cache-control: max-age=14400`, `cf-cache-status: HIT`, `age: 5984` |
| The cache can defeat a publish | after the a7e805e publish, the plain URL served the previous 240 KB `v2.js` (no Validation page) while `?cb=` served the current 246 KB file; a browser check confirmed the old nav |
| No purge credential exists locally | recorded in the design-site publication memory |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — version the pack's asset URLs at publish
`docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh` (or the homepage build, if that proves the smaller change) appends `?v=<merge sha>` to local `.js`/`.css`/data references in the mirrored `design/*.html` when it mirrors the pack. The HTML stays dynamic, so every publish yields fresh asset URLs.
- **P1.1** Given a publish, when the mirrored HTML is read, then every local script/style/data `src`/`href` carries the publish version exactly once (no double `?`, no external URLs or `data:` touched).
  Verify: a new `check-assets.cjs` fixture or a `--check` mode over a sample pack.

### P2 — proven on the live site
- **P2.1** Given two consecutive publishes, when the second lands, then a plain-URL browser load renders the second pack without a purge and without waiting for the TTL.
  Verify: browser check of the changed page immediately after the deploy.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why | State |

| related | #123 | measured-truth publish, where this was measured | closed |
| related | #133 (homepage) | the publish path it changes | merged |

## Out of scope

- Purging the Cloudflare cache by API (no credential); changing Cloudflare cache rules.
- The homepage's site-wide build pipeline beyond the design pack.

## Definition of done

- Every scenario passes at the PR head; one PR merged; one publish proves P2.1 live.

`architecture-analysis`, `reuse-map` and `brief-template`. A1–A5 are delivered; this lane delivers
A7 and re-verifies A6. The close is the owner's acceptance act.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### A1 — Current-state analysis

What exists today, measured: the V1 slices and their code, the T0 organisation spine, the seeded
catalogues/processes, the deployed estate. It cites `path:symbol` inside the repo.

`Verify:` the document exists on P0 with `meta.category=analysis` and is published.

### A2 — Reuse inventory inside the conveyor repo

For each capability the delivery projects need: the existing tables, actions, modules and tests
that can be reused, and what must be built. It starts from `coverage.json`'s measured rows.

`Verify:` every delivery project brief names at least one reuse source; the map resolves
`path:symbol` at the baseline (spot-checked by the P1 gate's references).

### A3 — Reuse inventory outside the conveyor repo

The estate's absorbed services and modules and the upstream crates: the reuse candidate, the
boundary, the licence/contract constraint. It names capabilities, not private hosts or URLs; a
version-specific detail cites the crate/version.

`Verify:` the document is published; `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` still passes on the repo.

### A4 — Options, risks and the dependency map

Build vs reuse vs buy per capability, the risks, and the project dependency map that the programme
plan's tranches follow.

`Verify:` the programme plan's tranche edges match the map; `check-coverage` reports 0 cycles.

### A5 — The per-project inception standard

The template every delivery project applies: **analysis** (reuse inside/outside/upstream,
build-vs-reuse, risks) and **architecture** (aggregates, tables, actions, modules, integrations,
decision record, acceptance). The architecture half is produced to the artefact standard
(SPEC_V2 §8.1): its phase and plateau set — the PSA artefacts at inception, the HLD and SD sets as
it matures — each artefact carrying the common metadata, its entries and its derivation/
realization/reuse links, under the live `architecture_contract` that governs the project. Both are
documents with `meta.category`; a project without both published is an inception gap.

`Verify:` deployment-gated: for a sampled delivery project, the console's inception checklist shows
the pair's state; its build units are not claimable while one is missing, and its brief names the
ADM phase/plateau and the governing contract.

### A6 — The architecture/analysis pack

The pack that the blueprint references: current-state, target, options, risks, decisions, and the
architecture artefacts the blueprint rests on — typed catalogs, matrices and diagrams with the
standard's common metadata and their links. It is the reference the per-project architectures must
fit; a deviation is a decision record.

`Verify:` the pack is published on P0 and linked from the blueprint; a sampled artefact carries
its owner, reviewer, review date, version, phase, plateau and at least one link.

catalogue; the Architecture Board charter, membership and decision limits; the governance, contract

with its development milestones. It is the programme's default `adm_profile`; the T9 implementation

## Goal

Media discovery is a Rust service in `apps/research` that serves its 23 operations — search,
collections, items, scoring, transcripts and download jobs — against its **own** Postgres schema,
proven against a contract captured from the running service.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" — the absorption procedure.
- `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §1/§3 — `apps/research` absorbs the scraper and
  media discovery; this issue is the media-discovery half.

**Split (documented exception):** #117 (the scraper half) is independent of this unit: it claims no
database and no background jobs, while this one owns a Postgres schema and a download-job runtime.
Merging them would make the scraper's green gate hostage to the database unit.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" | main@b72ca5d (blob ac9a7e3) |
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §1/§3 | `issue/117-webscraper@4529d39` (main with #105/#116/#117) |
| Code (old) | `nonagenticai/media-discovery` — `src/app.py`, `src/routers/`, `src/services/{collection,search,embedding}.py`, `src/adapters/{youtube,podcast}.py`, `alembic/versions/` (3 revisions) | `main` (measured 2026-11-14) |
| Code | `apps/research/contract/` — the capture pattern this unit repeats | `issue/117-webscraper@4529d39` |
| Code | `crates/store/src/` — migrations and RLS conventions | main@b72ca5d |
| Code | `apps/scientific/src/clients/inference.rs` — the embedding-call client shape | main with #105 |
| Code | `apps/research/src/media/**` | to create |
| Test | `apps/research/tests/media_contract.rs::served_openapi_equals_the_lock` | to create |
| Test | `apps/research/tests/parity.rs::golden_replay_matches_the_capture` | to create |
| Issue | #117 — the scraper half; lands the capture/lock shape this unit reuses | open |
| Issue | #83 — T14, which owns image publication and the probe | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@b72ca5d` + #105/#116/#117 as they land, measured 2026-11-14.
- Live service: `media-discovery` namespace, `1/1`, 188 d, port 8809, with a `migrate` init
  container (its own Postgres) and `MEDIA_DISCOVERY_*` env naming the webscraper, the
  modality-gateway (embeddings) and MinIO.
- Captured this session: `GET /openapi.json` → 20 paths / 23 operations / 19 schemas,
  `Media Discovery API`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 captured contract | ABSENT | no `apps/research/src/media/**` on main; the old repository commits no OpenAPI snapshot |
| P2 Rust service | ABSENT | same app directory as #117, a separate module tree |
| P3 schema | ABSENT | 3 alembic revisions to mirror as sqlx migrations; one service = one database = one role |
| P4 parity | ABSENT | no lock, no goldens, no tolerance list |
| P5 deploy | NOT THIS UNIT | the live Deployment is untouched; #83 owns image publication and the probe |
| Upstreams | LIVE | webscraper, modality-gateway (embeddings), MinIO, licences — every call in the contract is upstream-dependent, so stub-upstream contract tests are the shape (as `apps/scientific` did) |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — capture the contract

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 1

- **P1.1** Given the live service, when `contract/capture.sh --live <url>` runs, then
  `apps/research/contract/media-discovery/openapi.lock.json` and `manifest.json` are written.
  Verify: `apps/research/contract/capture.sh --live http://127.0.0.1:PORT`; `jq -e '.openapi' apps/research/contract/media-discovery/openapi.lock.json`
- **P1.2** Given the golden set, when read, then every payload is synthetic.
  Verify: `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh`

### P2 — the schema

Requirement: the three alembic revisions become sqlx migrations with the same tables, constraints,
indexes and tenant/RLS model; the service refuses to boot against a schema it does not own.

- **P2.1** Given a fresh database, when the service migrates, then the table set, the forced RLS
  policies and the unique constraints match the captured schema inventory.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test media_contract::migrations_create_the_captured_schema`
- **P2.2** Given an unprivileged role, when it reads another tenant's row, then it sees nothing.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test media_contract::a_second_tenant_sees_nothing`

### P3 — the operations

- **P3.1** Given the crate, when `--check-lock` runs, then the served document equals the capture.
  Verify: `cargo run -p conveyor-research --features media -- --check-lock` (exit 0)
- **P3.2** Given a scoring request, when the embedder is unreachable, then the answer is the captured
  degraded shape, never a 500.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::an_unreachable_embedder_is_degraded`
- **P3.3** Given a download job, when it is submitted, then its state transitions match the captured
  job contract.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::a_download_job_moves_through_the_captured_states`

### P4 — parity

- **P4.1** Given the goldens, when `parity` runs, then every captured operation reproduces its
  captured status and shape, with an explicit tolerance list for the heuristic fields (search
  ordering and score values).
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity`

### P5 — not a deploy

- **P5.1** Given the unit lands, when the cluster is read, then `media-discovery` is the same
  Deployment with the same image digest and replica count.
  Verify: `kubectl -n media-discovery get deploy media-discovery -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` → unchanged

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | #117 | lands the capture/lock shape in the same app | open |
| related | #83 | image publication and the probe | open |

`Blocker: #117`.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named; live service measured; captured OpenAPI counted.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref; #117 and #83 resolve.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies typed; `status:blocked` while `blocked-by` #117 is open.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from #117's files (`apps/research/src/media/**`,
      `apps/research/tests/media_contract.rs`, `migrations/media/`).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head.
- [ ] Tests added per part; none skipped.
- [ ] `--check-lock` green; migrations idempotent; no private references in the tree.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- The corpus the old service indexes and any data it holds — this unit ships code and schema, not
  content.
- Cutover of the live Deployment and its probe (#83).
- The scraper half (#117).

## Deployment prerequisite

No for this unit; the image and probe are #83's.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Does the embeddings call stay on `modality-gateway`, or move to the workspace's inference client? | implementer, by capture | whatever the captured contract names; changing upstream is not this unit |
| 2 | Search ordering parity: exact or a declared rank tolerance? | implementer, by measurement | declared tolerance on order, exact on the result set |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|

## Goal

The web-scraper service is a Rust `conveyor-research` crate in `apps/research` serving its six
operations for the static-HTTP path, with every browser-only capability refused **by name** instead
of silently ignored, proven against a contract captured from the running service.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" — the absorption procedure.
- `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §1/§3 — `apps/research` absorbs the scraper and
  media-discovery; this issue is the scraper half.
- `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §3 — the sequence this unit follows.

**Split (the documented exception, ≤5):** ADR 0006 groups both services in one app because both are
outbound fetchers. They are delivered as two issues because they have different acceptance and
different deployment gates: this one claims **no database** and no background jobs, while
media-discovery owns a Postgres schema and a download-job runtime. Merging them into one branch
would make the scraper's green gate hostage to the database unit.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | — |
| HEAD | — |
| Session | — |
| Updated | — |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" | main@b72ca5d (blob ac9a7e3) |
| Decision | `docs/decisions/0006-tool-absorption-grouping.md` §1/§3 | `issue/105-scientific@984305c` (main with #105) |
| Code (old) | `nonagenticai/webscraper_service` — `src/routers/scrape.py`, `src/schemas/scrape.py`, `src/services/{base_scraper,httpx_scraper,curl_cffi_scraper,content_extraction,link_scoring,image_utils,cache}.py`, `pyproject.toml` | `main` (measured 2026-11-14) |
| Code | `apps/scientific/contract/{capture.sh,capture-goldens.sh,README.md}` — the capture pattern this unit repeats | `issue/105-scientific@984305c` |
| Code | `apps/lean4-prover/{src/contract.rs,contract/}` — the lock check this unit repeats | `issue/116-lean4@6f5df94` |
| Code | `crates/auth/src/service.rs` — `X-Tenant-Id` / bearer patterns | main@b72ca5d |
| Code | `apps/research/**` | to create |
| Test | `apps/research/tests/contract.rs::served_openapi_equals_the_lock` | to create |
| Test | `apps/research/tests/parity.rs::golden_replay_matches_the_capture` | to create |
| Issue | #116 — the lean4 unit that lands the capture/lock shape used here | open |
| Issue | #83 — T14, which owns image publication and the probe | open |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@b72ca5d` + #105/#116 as they land, measured 2026-11-14.
- Live service: `webscraper` namespace, `1/1`, 188 d, port 9119.
- Captured this session: `GET /openapi.json` → 6 paths / 6 operations / 17 schemas, served by
  `WebScraper Service` 1.0.0.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 captured contract | ABSENT | no `apps/research/**` on main; the old repository commits no OpenAPI snapshot |
| P2 Rust crate | ABSENT | `git ls-tree -d origin/main apps/` → `inference-router, lean4-prover, scientific, server, web` |
| P3 parity | ABSENT | no lock, no goldens, no tolerance list |
| P4 deploy | NOT THIS UNIT | the live Deployment is untouched; #83 owns image publication and the probe |
| Runtime shape | **BROWSER + ANTI-BOT** | `pyproject.toml` depends on `trafilatura`, `scrapy`+`protego`, `playwright`+`playwright-stealth`, `curl-cffi` (Chrome TLS/JA3 impersonation). ADR 0006 called this group "thin fetch"; the measured contract says otherwise |
| Default call shape | STATIC | `javascript_enabled` defaults `false`; `scraper_type` defaults `auto`, which starts at httpx and escalates |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — capture the contract

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 1
Requirement: the OpenAPI document and a synthetic golden set, captured by committed scripts, with
the reference implementation run locally against fixture pages (a public repository is never a
fixture target, and the service in the cluster cannot reach a fixture).

- **P1.1** Given the reference service, when `contract/capture.sh --live <url>` runs, then
  `apps/research/contract/webscraper/openapi.lock.json` and `manifest.json` are written with the
  source commit and the operation count.
  Verify: `apps/research/contract/capture.sh --live http://127.0.0.1:PORT`; `jq -e '.openapi' apps/research/contract/webscraper/openapi.lock.json`
- **P1.2** Given the fixtures under `contract/fixtures/`, when `capture-goldens.sh` runs, then one
  request/response pair per case exists and every payload is synthetic.
  Verify: `apps/research/contract/capture-goldens.sh --live http://127.0.0.1:PORT`; `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh`

### P2 — the crate

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 2
Requirement: `apps/research` serves the six operations for the static path, and answers a named
refusal for every capability that needs a browser, an anti-bot TLS stack, or a JS engine.

- **P2.1** Given the crate, when `--check-lock` runs, then the served document equals the capture.
  Verify: `cargo run -p conveyor-research -- --check-lock` (exit 0)
- **P2.2** Given a static fixture page, when `POST /api/scrape/url` runs, then `markdown_content`,
  `text_content`, `title`, `links` and `images` are produced from the page.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::a_static_page_yields_its_text`
- **P2.3** Given `scraper_type` naming `playwright`, `scrapy` or `curl_cffi`, or any of
  `stealth`, `virtual_scroll`, `screenshot`, `wait_for_selector`, when the request arrives, then the
  answer is the captured validation error naming the field — never a silent downgrade.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::a_browser_only_capability_is_refused_by_name`
- **P2.4** Given the bulk route, when it runs, then it reuses the same extractor and cache as the
  single-URL route.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::bulk_reuses_the_single_url_path`

### P3 — parity

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 3
Requirement: the lock, the golden replay, and an explicit tolerance list — with the extraction
deviation named and bounded, never asserted away.

- **P3.1** Given the goldens, when `parity` runs, then every captured operation reproduces its
  status, and each text field matches exactly or inside the declared similarity bound.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity`
- **P3.2** Given a field whose tolerance is undeclared, when compared, then the run fails.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-research --test parity::undeclared_difference_fails`
- **P3.3** Given the extraction module, when read, then the contract states which of the reference's
  two extraction passes it implements and why the other one is not portable.
  Verify: `apps/research/contract/README.md` §"Extraction"

### P4 — not a deploy

- **P4.1** Given the unit lands, when the cluster is read, then `webscraper` is the same Deployment
  with the same image digest and replica count.
  Verify: `kubectl -n webscraper get deploy webscraper -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` → unchanged

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | #116 | lands the capture/lock/parity shape this unit repeats | open |
| related | #118 | the media-discovery half of `apps/research`; independent acceptance | open |
| related | #83 | image publication and the probe | open |

`Blocker: #116` — the branch is cut from the tree that carries the lock pattern.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named; live service measured; captured OpenAPI counted.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref; #116, #118, #83 resolve.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies typed; `status:blocked` while `blocked-by` #116 is open.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from every open issue: `apps/research/**`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`fmt --all --check`, `clippy --all-targets --locked --
      -D warnings`, `nextest run --locked`).
- [ ] Tests added per part; none skipped.
- [ ] `--check-lock` green; no private references in the tree.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- The Playwright, scrapy and curl-cffi backends, `stealth`, `virtual_scroll`, `screenshot`,
  `wait_for_selector` and `storage_state`. No Rust equivalent exists in this workspace; they are
  refused by name (P2.3) and named in the contract README, which is the same treatment
  `z3`/`sympy` got in `apps/scientific` (ADR 0006 §4).
- `trafilatura`'s article extractor — the deviation is bounded by P3.1/P3.3, not by a claim of
  equivalence.
- The Deployment, its image and its probe (#83), and media-discovery (#118).

## Deployment prerequisite

No. Code and a captured contract only.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Is a static-only scraper useful to its one consumer (media-discovery, which also runs a browser)? | owner | ship the static path and measure; the browser path stays refused until a Rust CDP runtime is funded |
| 2 | Fixture corpus size for the similarity bound | implementer | 12 synthetic pages: article, table/directory, consent banner, SPA shell, login wall |

|---|---|---|---|

operations the live deployment serves, proven against a contract captured from that deployment — the
crate moves into this workspace while the deployable, its 10.6 GB toolchain image and its node pin

## Parts and acceptance criteria

behaviour intact — licence middleware, admission/shedding, the Lean runner, metrics — and serves the
seven captured operations plus a document that `--check-lock` compares.

  the captured unauthenticated status and body, and the health/metrics routes stay public.

- **P2.3** Given a saturated prover, when a proof is requested, then the answer is the captured
  `503` + `Retry-After` shed, never a `500`.

  conflicting pin: versions come from the workspace, and the crate builds under `-D warnings`.

### P3 — parity

`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"How a service joins" step 3
Requirement: the OpenAPI lock, the golden replay, and an explicit list of what cannot be replayed —
with the reason.

- **P3.1** Given the captured goldens, when `parity` runs, then every recorded operation reproduces
  its captured status and body.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-lean4-prover --test parity`
- **P3.2** Given an operation whose answer depends on the Lean toolchain, when the harness runs
  without it, then the test declares it in `DECLARED_UNCAPTURABLE` with the reason instead of
  asserting a fabricated result — and a stale declaration fails the run.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-lean4-prover --test parity::every_route_is_replayed_or_declared`

### P4 — not a deploy

Requirement: this unit changes no cluster object. The image, its registry path, the hp2 pin and the
toleration stay as they are; publishing a per-service image and the probe belong to #83.

- **P4.1** Given the unit lands, when the cluster is read, then `lean4-prover` is the same Deployment
  with the same image digest and the same replica count as the baseline above.
  Verify: `kubectl -n lean4-prover get deploy lean4-prover -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` → unchanged

## Dependencies

## Goal
Every third-party action conveyor's CI runs is pinned to a commit SHA, and `.github/workflows/` is gated on every PR by actionlint plus zizmor (medium and above), so an unpinned or structurally unsafe workflow change cannot merge.

## Plan / audit source
Post-rollout hardening of the public CI: cf. #35 (the self-contained public CI this hardens) and the merged precedent in `nonagenticai/ci-workflows` PR #8 (SHA pins + a required `lint` gate). This unit is conveyor-local; the archetype itself is #17.

## Claim
| Field | Value |

| Branch | `issue/102-ci-supply-chain` |
| HEAD | `bc65339` |
| Session | `coding-rollout-remaining-work` |
| Updated | 2026-11-14 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References
| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` | main@df986d7 |
| Issue | #35 (closed — the public CI) | closed |
| Issue | #17 (open — archetype rebuild, other session) | open |
| Repo | `nonagenticai/ci-workflows` `.github/workflows/selftest.yml:21-49` (public) | main |

## Baseline
- Code: `main@df986d7bc35e035ae873befdbebd29e25fbc6955` · measured 2026-11-14
- Docs: n/a — this unit has no plan/audit blob

## Current state (measured)
| Part | State | Evidence |

| P1 SHA pins | PARTIAL | `grep -n 'uses: actions/' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml` → 5 × `actions/checkout@v7`, 1 × `actions/cache@v6` — mutable tags |
| P2 persist-credentials | ABSENT | `grep -c persist-credentials` → 0 |
| P3 lint gate | ABSENT | no `actionlint`/`zizmor` step in any workflow |
| P4 required check | ABSENT | ruleset 27178695 requires `checks, image, no-private-refs, secret-scan, service-image` only |
| P5 zizmor baseline | ABSENT | never measured on this file before this unit |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — third-party actions pinned by SHA
`ci-public.yml` (all `uses:` lines). Requirement: every third-party `uses:` names a 40-hex commit with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, which is the shape Dependabot maintains.

- **P1.1** Given `main@df986d7`, when the workflow is scanned, then no `uses:` names a mutable tag.
  Verify: `! grep -nE 'uses: [^ ]+@v[0-9]' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml`
- **P1.2** Given the pins, when the file is read, then every pin carries its version comment.
  Verify: `test "$(grep -c 'uses: [^ ]*@[0-9a-f]\{40\} # v' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml)" -eq 7`

### P2 — checkouts do not persist credentials
Requirement: every checkout passes `persist-credentials: false` (zizmor `artipacked`).

- **P2.1** Given the workflow, when it runs, then no job leaves the token in the workspace `.git/config`.
  Verify: `test "$(grep -c 'uses: actions/checkout@' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml)" = "$(grep -c 'persist-credentials: false' .github/workflows/ci-public.yml)"`

### P3 — static gate job
Requirement: a `lint` job runs actionlint (1.7.12, sha256-pinned tarball) and zizmor (1.32.0, auditor persona, medium+) on every PR.

- **P3.1** Given the workflow tree, when both tools run, then neither reports a finding at its gate.
  Verify: `actionlint .github/workflows/` → exit 0; `uvx zizmor==1.32.0 --persona=auditor --min-severity=medium --format=plain .github/workflows/` → `No findings to report`
- **P3.2** Given a PR, when `ci` runs, then the `lint` job is present and green.
  Verify: `gh pr checks <PR>` shows `lint` pass

### P4 — `lint` is required on main
Requirement: ruleset 27178695 requires `lint`, so a PR that fails it cannot merge. The job lands first (a required check that does not exist blocks every PR).

- **P4.1** Given the ruleset after merge, when a PR is evaluated, then `lint` is a required status check.
  Verify: `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/rules/branches/main --jq '[.[]|select(.type=="required_status_checks")][0].parameters.required_status_checks[].context'` contains `lint`

### P5 — no regression
Requirement: the publish path is untouched; main stays green and the deployed workload does not roll.

- **P5.1** Given the merged head, when main runs, then every job is green.
  Verify: `gh run list --branch main --workflow ci-public.yml --limit 1 --json conclusion --jq '.[0].conclusion'` → `success`
- **P5.2** Given the merge, when the cluster is read, then conveyor and conveyor-worker are still healthy (the image did not change).
  Verify: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/[host] admin@[tailnet] "sudo KUBECONFIG=/etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml kubectl -n conveyor get deploy"` → 2/2 and 1/1

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #35 | the public CI this hardens | closed |
| related | #17 | the archetype/ARC rebuild is a different subject, owned by its own session | open |

No `blocked-by`.

## Definition of ready
- [x] Baseline named (`main@df986d7`, measured 2026-11-14); no plan/audit blob applies.
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no blocker, so no `Blocker:` line.
- [x] One-PR scope, file-disjoint: only `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml`, plus the ruleset API after merge.
- [x] Scope corrections: n/a for this unit.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Gate green at the exact head: the PR's own `ci` run. No Rust source changes, so `rbuild --gate` is not applicable.
- [ ] No tests added or changed (workflow-only).
- [ ] Ruleset updated after merge and read back.
- [ ] Live verification: fresh main run and the two Deployments.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope
- The image publish path (`docker build` + `docker push`) — no buildx or provenance change; that path is what deploys.
- Archetype/ARC changes (#17).
- The Dependabot queue.
- Any Rust source change.

## Deployment prerequisite
No — CI-only; the deployed image is untouched.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add provenance attestations to the published image? | George | Not now — the publish path is the deploy path and the change buys nothing this estate consumes |

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|

## Goal

An external contributor can report a bug, have it triaged into a unit, claim it in their fork, open a PR and see it merge — with no write access, no private infrastructure and no Claude session; and the public CI enforces the rules CONTRIBUTING states (DCO, sensitive-path review) instead of only documenting them.

## Plan / audit source

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the human path this unit makes true end to end.
- `docs/decisions/0003-public-ci.md` — the public workflow is inline and self-contained; the private archetype is not reusable.
- `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` § "Licensing and contributions" — Apache-2.0, DCO, no CLA, maintainer review.
- `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Claim — four checks, then push" and § "CI budget and WIP cap" — the maintainer-shaped claim path.
- Owner decisions, 2026-11-14: merge gate gains **CODEOWNERS review on sensitive paths only**, not a blanket approval; `strata_ingest`/`strata_rag` stay external.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/93-public-collaboration` |
| HEAD | `bf76b4e` |
| Session | `mini3/claude (claim nonce 61F5C4C8-FF4C-432B-9508-C61F6F6D481D)` |
| Updated | `2026-11-15` |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Doc | `CONTRIBUTING.md:7-22,49-53` — issue-first, fork, DCO, review | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Doc | `README.md:28-33` — the contributing pointer | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Doc | `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "Claim — four checks, then push" (§ starts `## Claim`) | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Code | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.md` — the maintainer-shaped unit form | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Code | `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feedback.yml` — the only non-unit form | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Code | `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml:21-26,36-65,72,91,195,248` — `on:`, secret scan, jobs | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Code | `scripts/ci/gate.sh:71-75` — gitleaks, while CI uses betterleaks | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Code | `.github/CODEOWNERS:2-3` — one personal handle; the team note | main@1bf5a8d9 |
| Data | the `main` ruleset — 5 required checks, 0 approvals, `require_code_owner_review: false` | measured 2026-11-14 |
| Issue | #17 — the private CI/ARC archetype; do not fork a second CI effort | open, claimed |
| Issue | #42 — the CODEOWNERS team note | closed |
| Issue | #45 — the active absorption lane; independent of this unit | open, claimed |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@1bf5a8d9`, measured 2026-11-14.
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` is the only public workflow; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is #17's and is out of scope.
- Ruleset: `main` active; required contexts `checks`, `image`, `no-private-refs`, `secret-scan`, `service-image`; `required_approving_review_count: 0`; `require_code_owner_review: false`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 — external intake | ABSENT | only `unit.md` (maintainer-shaped: plan/audit shas) and `feedback.yml`; no bug/feature form and no template chooser |
| P2 — fork claim path | PARTIAL | `CONTRIBUTING.md:17` says fork, but `03-DELIVERY.md` § Claim pushes `issue/N-*` to `origin` and flips labels — impossible without write access |
| P3 — DCO enforcement | ABSENT | `CONTRIBUTING.md:18` requires `git commit -s`; no CI check exists (`ci-public.yml` has no DCO job) |
| P4 — public CI docs gate + scanner parity | ABSENT | every docs-only PR runs the 120-minute `checks` job and both image builds (no changed-files classifier); `gate.sh:71-75` scans with gitleaks, CI scans with betterleaks |
| P5 — sensitive-path review | PARTIAL | `.github/CODEOWNERS` is one personal handle; the ruleset requires 0 approvals and no code-owner review |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — external intake

- **P1.1** Given a non-maintainer with a bug or a feature idea, when they open the new-issue chooser, then `Bug report` and `Feature request` forms are offered alongside `Unit of work` and `Design feedback`, and each carries a required privacy checkbox (no credential, personal data or private infrastructure detail).
  Verify: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` + `bug.yml` + `feature.yml` exist; a maintainer renders each form once and records the links; `git diff --check` clean.
- **P1.2** Given an accepted report, when a maintainer triages it, then `CONTRIBUTING.md` states the rule: the report is converted into a `unit` issue (the full contract) and linked, never rewritten in place.
  Verify: the written rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; one worked example linked in the PR.

### P2 — fork claim path

- **P2.1** Given a contributor with no write access, when they comment they will take issue #N and a maintainer applies `status:claimed`, then the branch lives in their fork, the PR head is `<owner>:issue/N-*`, and every claim check is performable without pushing to `origin`.
  Verify: `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `03-DELIVERY.md` § Claim carry the path; one scratch-fork PR is walked end to end and linked.
- **P2.2** Given the ≤2 open `issue/*` PR cap, when an outside PR is open, then the cap counts maintainer PRs in this repository, not fork PRs.
  Verify: the documented predicate excludes fork heads (`gh pr list --json headRefName,headRepositoryOwner`); the count on the day is recorded.

### P3 — DCO enforcement

- **P3.1** Given a PR whose every commit carries `Signed-off-by:`, when CI runs, then the DCO check passes; given one unsigned commit, it fails and names the commit.
  Verify: a `dco` job in `ci-public.yml`; one deliberately unsigned scratch branch (red run recorded) and a signed head (green run recorded).
- **P3.2** Given `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the PR template, when read, then they name DCO 1.1, `git commit -s`, and the check.
  Verify: the text; the check name matches the workflow job.

### P4 — public CI docs gate and scanner parity

- **P4.1** Given a docs-only PR (every changed path under `docs/**`, `.claude/**` or a `*.md`), when CI runs, then `checks`, `image` and `service-image` are **created and skipped** and the PR stays mergeable; a single code path puts the full suite back.
  Verify: a changed-files classifier inside the jobs (never `paths-ignore`, which would leave required contexts missing); one real docs PR and one code PR with their runs recorded.
- **P4.2** Given `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh`, when the secret scan runs, then it uses `betterleaks` with `.betterleaks.toml` and `.betterleaksignore` — the same scanner and ignores as CI — or the script states that it is an approximation and names the difference.
  Verify: `grep -n 'betterleaks\|gitleaks' scripts/ci/gate.sh .github/workflows/ci-public.yml`; a planted secret in a temp file fails the local gate with the same scanner.

### P5 — code-owner review on sensitive paths

- **P5.1** Given `@nonagenticai/maintainers` exists, when a PR touches `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `SECURITY.md` or `scripts/ci/**`, then a code-owner approval is required; every other path keeps required checks only.
  Verify: `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/rulesets/<id>` → `require_code_owner_review: true`; `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/branches/main/protection`; the team exists (org-admin token). ⚠️ Until the team exists the rule must stay unarmed — a personal handle would block every CI PR.
- **P5.2** Given the team does not exist, when the ruleset still requires 0 approvals, then the limitation is recorded on this issue, not silently skipped.
  Verify: `gh api orgs/nonagenticai/teams` under an admin token; the measurement (including the 403 with the shared token) is in the PR.

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| related | #17 | the private CI archetype; this unit touches `ci-public.yml` only and must not fork a second CI effort | open, claimed |
| related | #42 | the CODEOWNERS team note this unit completes | closed |
| related | #45 | the active absorption lane; this unit is independent (docs, templates and the public workflow) | open, claimed |

No blocker: every referenced file resolves at `main@1bf5a8d9`; the team existence is a prerequisite for P5.1's enforcement, not for the rest.

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named; the ruleset state measured.
- [x] Every path reference resolves at its ref.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; `Blocker:` absent because nothing blocks construction.
- [x] One-PR scope (docs, templates and `ci-public.yml`); the ruleset change is one admin action after merge.
- [x] Scope corrections applied: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (#17) untouched; no CLA; no team creation in code; no private archetype change.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Public gate at the exact head: the docs checks (`git diff --check`, every relative Markdown link) plus `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh`.
- [ ] The ruleset state after the merge is recorded (armed or explicitly deferred with the team's absence).
- [ ] One PR `Closes #<n>` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the private archetype — #17's.
- Creating `@nonagenticai/maintainers` (org admin; the rule is armed after it exists).
- A CLA; Apache-2.0 §5 and DCO stand.
- The `.claude/skills/*` internals; `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the human path and must not depend on a Claude session.
- The absorption lanes (#45, #46).

## Deployment prerequisite

No.

## Open questions

| 1 | Which credential can edit the `main` ruleset and list org teams? | this unit | the shared GitHub App token cannot (`403 Resource not accessible by integration`); use an owner token for the one admin action and record it |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — A tenant brief plus documents become a reviewed, published catalogue
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.7 "Input → produces", dependency-order rule, "Instruments" · §10.4 `authoring.intake|draft|review|publish`, `authoring.assets` · §10.5 Authoring destination · §15.1 D55 — Requirement: chat input and documents draft organisation, department, job, procedure and policy assets into a draft catalogue with their source recorded; authoring refuses a draft whose referenced asset is unpublished; a person's review is what publishes each asset, and the catalogue reports the published set.

- **P1.1** Given a short tenant brief as chat input, when the authoring intake runs, then organisation, department and job drafts exist in the draft catalogue and none is published.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/authoring.rs::a_chat_brief_drafts_the_org_and_job_catalogue` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given the same tenant supplies documents alongside the brief, when intake runs, then each document is recorded as a source and its procedure and policy drafts link to it.
  Verify: `authoring.rs::documents_yield_linked_procedure_and_policy_drafts` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a draft whose referenced asset is unpublished, when the authoring job validates it, then the draft is refused naming the unpublished dependency, in the order industry → department → job → procedure → policy.
  Verify: `authoring.rs::a_draft_that_references_an_unpublished_asset_is_refused` (to create)
- **P1.4** Given the drafts in review, when a person approves each asset, then departments, jobs, procedures and policies report `published` with the approving decision recorded against each release.
  Verify: `authoring.rs::a_reviewed_catalogue_publishes_with_its_decisions` (to create)
- **P1.5** Given a tenant with a reviewed catalogue, when the Authoring destination opens, then the intake queue, draft catalogue and per-asset dependency status render live rows, not fixtures.
  Verify: `apps/web/e2e/authoring.spec.ts::the_authoring_destination_shows_the_live_catalogue` (to create)

### P2 — No asset can publish itself or widen a tool grant
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.7 first rule · §5.4 approvals default to human · §10.4 `approvals.*` · §15.1 D55 · §15.2 #14 — Requirement: every authored asset reaches `published` only through a recorded approval whose decision satisfies the tenant's configured policy (default human), the job that drafted an asset can never satisfy its gate, and intake output can never create a tool grant or widen an effect ceiling.

- **P2.1** Given a draft asset authored by a job, when that same job attempts its publish, then the attempt is refused and the asset stays in review.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/asset_review.rs::the_authoring_job_cannot_publish_its_own_asset` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a tenant on the default approval policy, when a `rule` or `agent` decision is the only decision on an asset gate, then the publish is refused until a human decides.
  Verify: `asset_review.rs::a_non_human_decision_cannot_complete_an_asset_gate` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a chat message or document asking for a new tool grant or a wider effect ceiling, when the draft is validated, then the request is refused and the tenant's ceiling and tool bindings are unchanged.
  Verify: `asset_review.rs::an_asset_never_widens_a_tool_grant` (to create)

> **Re-baselined 2026-11-22 at `origin/main@490ad555`.** T13 (#76) and T14 (#83) merged: the four
> tool tables (migration 0055), `tools.call`, `toolkits.publish`, `tools.probe` and `tools.usage`
> exist. The tool-surface units #556 (bound-tool projection), #557 (bindings/catalogue/publish
> contract), #558 (provenance), #561 (research/Lean) and #560 (scientific draft) are the practical
> prerequisites. The scope below is unchanged; the stale state rows, dependency states and the
> gate line are corrected.

## Goal

A tenant can generate a tool from an OpenAPI document and have a job call it, publish it behind an approval that defaults to a human and is the tenant's to configure, bind a remote MCP server so only the narrowed subset is callable and audited, and no authoring, binding or promotion path can reach past its effect ceiling.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.5 (BYO tools, D42) · §11.6 (tools that generate tools, D43) · §11.4 (effect classes) · §11.8 (data model) · §12 row **T15** (at claim `origin/main@00094194:8994c95b`)

| Code | `crates/actions/src/ingest.rs:193`:discover, `:415`:apply — OpenAPI → `action_registry` external actions; the nearest analogue, not a toolkit | origin/main@00094194 (re-verified at claim) |

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 spec → published tool, called by a job | PARTIAL | the four tool tables (`migrations/0055`), `tools.call` (#76), `toolkits.publish` (#83) and `tools.probe` exist; `tool_authoring.*`, the OpenAPI draft import and the `tool_draft` governed-asset kind are absent; the call half is #556 |
| P2 publication approval defaults to human, tenant-configurable | ABSENT | `approval_policy` now exists (#282, migration 50), but `toolkits.publish` is a `tools:write` action with no approval; no publication gate names a policy row |
| P3 BYO MCP server bound, narrowed, audited | ABSENT | `/mcp` remains an `rmcp` `RoleServer`; the build enables no MCP client transport, so the conveyor has never been an MCP client |
| P4 a tenant cannot exceed its effect ceiling | PARTIAL | `tool_binding.effect_ceiling` and the broker's rank check exist (`migrations/0055`, `crates/actions/src/broker.rs`); no authoring or promotion path reads a ceiling, so publishing is not yet bounded |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — A tool generated from a spec is published and called by a job
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.6 paths 1–2 · §11.5 item 1 · §11.8 · §12 T15
Requirement: an OpenAPI document is imported as draft operations under `governed_asset(kind='tool_draft')`, validated and published as an immutable toolkit version through the `tool_authoring.*` / `toolkits.*` families, and a bound job then calls it by that pin. The import/publish half is this unit's; the call half is #556's.
- **P1.1** Given an OpenAPI 3.1 document for an operation with no tool, when it is imported and published, then one immutable toolkit version exists and a bound job's call reaches the registered destination alias at that pin.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_authoring.rs::a_tool_generated_from_a_spec_is_published_and_called` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given a service scaffolded from `template-rust-service` and deployed, when its OpenAPI is registered, then the tool is that service's own operation — one toolkit, no wrapper around it.
  Verify: `tool_authoring.rs::a_scaffolded_service_registers_its_own_openapi` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a draft with wildcard egress, a free-form input schema, a write effect without an idempotency declaration, or no declared effect class, when publication is requested, then the first three are refused with no version written and the fourth publishes as `read`.
  Verify: `tool_authoring.rs::publication_refuses_an_unbounded_draft_and_defaults_the_class_to_read` (to create)

### P2 — Publication approval defaults to a human and is tenant-configurable
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.5 item 1 · §11.6 · D43 · §5.4 · §10.3 `approval_policy` · §12 T15
Requirement: every tool or toolkit publication is a gate naming an `approval_policy` row whose default is a human approver with one required decision, and a tenant may change approver kind, count and expiry except where a destructive tool demands a named approver.
- **P2.1** Given a tenant with no publication policy override, when a validated toolkit is published, then it waits for a human decision and the approval records a human `decided_by_kind`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_authoring.rs::publication_waits_for_a_human_by_default` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a tenant whose publication policy names a different approver kind or required decisions, when the same toolkit is published, then that policy is applied and its version is recorded on the approval — no code change.
  Verify: `tool_authoring.rs::a_tenant_policy_changes_the_publication_gate_without_a_code_change` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a destructive tool and a policy that names no approver, when publication is requested, then it is refused and no toolkit version is written.
  Verify: `tool_authoring.rs::a_destructive_tool_needs_a_named_approver` (to create)

### P3 — A BYO MCP server is bound, narrowed and audited
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.5 item 2 · §11.3 steps 5–7 · D42 · §12 T15
Requirement: a tenant registers a streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint whose tools the conveyor discovers and binds by credential alias, exposes only the bound subset to that tenant's jobs (binding-scoped discovery), and records each call as one `tool_call` row and one `tool.called` event.
- **P3.1** Given a registered BYO MCP server whose discovery returns more tools than the binding selects, when the job calls a bound tool and then an unbound one, then the bound call lands one `tool_call` row naming that binding and the unbound tool is absent from the job's tool set and refused.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/byo_tools.rs::only_the_bound_subset_is_callable_and_each_call_is_audited` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a caller-supplied URL at call time, when `tools.call` runs, then it is refused and the destination alias registered and reviewed at publication is the only route; another tenant cannot see or call the toolkit.
  Verify: `byo_tools.rs::a_call_time_url_is_refused_and_a_byo_toolkit_is_tenant_scoped` (to create)

### P4 — A tenant cannot exceed its effect ceiling
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.4 · §11.6 final sentence · §11.5 final sentence · D42, D43 · §12 T15
Requirement: the authoring job publishes only within its own binding's effect ceiling, a binding narrows and never raises, and promoting a tenant toolkit to the platform catalogue is a development project with a platform review, never an admin toggle.
- **P4.1** Given an authoring job bound at `write`, when it publishes a `destructive` tool, then the publication is refused and no `tool` version is written.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_authoring.rs::the_publishing_job_cannot_widen_its_own_effect_ceiling` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a published tenant toolkit, when a tenant admin attempts to promote it into the platform catalogue, then the promotion is refused and only a development project with a platform review can.
  Verify: `tool_authoring.rs::promotion_is_not_an_admin_toggle` (to create)

issues.body:
## Goal

A tenant-supplied SOP and a BPMN process document each land as a governed source and convert into a PDDL procedure draft that only a human can publish; the derived SOP and its executable keep their provenance and knowledge-pack pairing on every re-ingest; a job bound to the procedure executes its PDDL steps; and a source nobody reviewed can never bind. An OWL/Turtle document lands as a governed source whose knowledge pack is a `strata_ingest` reference — conveyor runs no RDF store and no reasoner (owner decision 2026-11-19: the PKO tables are not built; knowledge lives in strata_rag/strata_ingest, recorded in #413 / PR #419).

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 (procedure authoring and SOP ingestion), §10.4 (`procedures` action family), §10.5 (Procedures screen), §12 row **T16**, §13 Procedures row, §14 R17, §15 D53/D55 and open question 13 — scope only, no plan prose.
- **Owner decision 2026-11-19 (this unit's re-baseline):** no `pko_release`/`pko_entity`/`pko_relation`; an RDF/OWL/Turtle document is import material for `strata_ingest`, whose knowledge pack the derived procedure names. This supersedes the claim's `0058_pko.sql` (deleted; the migration is `0060_procedure_ingestion.sql`).
- `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.md` rows `actions:authoring` (`new`), `actions:procedures` (extend), `destination:Procedures` (extend) · `seed/programme.json` project `T16` `meta.gate`, `meta.depends_on`.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | `issue/85-t16-sop-ingestion` |
| HEAD | `79b7b5ec` (main integrated; full suite reported) |
| Session | mini3, 2026-11-19 |
| Updated | 2026-11-19 |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6, §10.3, §10.4, §10.5, §12 T16, §13, §14 R17, §15 D53/D55 + #13 | origin/main@6c46d92e |
| Decision | #413 / PR #419 — no PKO tables; knowledge lives in strata | origin/main@6c46d92e |
| Evidence | `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.md` rows named above | origin/main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `migrations/0058_data_model_gaps.sql` (`procedure.action_text`, `process_step.action_text`) · `migrations/0060_procedure_ingestion.sql` (to create: source/pack provenance, PDDL state, publication approval) | branch |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/procedure/procedures.rs:235` `procedures.publish` · `crates/actions/src/process/processes.rs` `processes.publish` · `crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs` `approvals.request` · `crates/actions/src/process/step.rs` `execute_step` · `migrations/0035_process_tree.sql` (`process`/`process_step`/`run_step`) · `crates/domain/src/process.rs:500` publish-time reference check | origin/main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/documents/ingest.rs` → `strata_ingest` (`crates/actions/src/integrations/ingest.rs`) · `crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs` (`CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_INFERENCE_URL`) · `crates/actions/src/organisation.rs` `job_bindings.create` | origin/main@6c46d92e |

| Issue | #73, #76 (both closed) | closed |

## Baseline

- Code `origin/main@6c46d92e`, measured 2026-11-19 · `seed/programme.json` T16 `depends_on: ["T2","T13","P0"]` · #73 and #76 closed; P0 closed · next migration on main is 0060.

## Current state (measured at `origin/main@6c46d92e`)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 SOP/BPMN ingested end to end; OWL → strata pack | ABSENT | no SOP/BPMN parser (`git grep -n -i -e bpmn -e 'draw\.io' -- crates apps` → 0); no ingest action; the `sop_source` asset kind exists (`migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql:416`) but no action writes it; `documents.ingest` already pushes a document to `strata_ingest` |
| P2 draft published behind a human gate | PARTIAL | `processes.publish` flips `draft → published` on a `processes:write` scope with no approval check; `approvals.request|decide` and `approval_decision.decided_by_kind` exist (`migrations/0002_domain.sql:239`), and the requester-cannot-decide rule is enforced in `store::approval::record_decision_tx` |
| P3 a re-ingest is versioned | ABSENT | no source provenance on `process`/`procedure`; the process version model exists (`processes.create` copy-forward, draft/published partial uniques) but nothing derives from a source |
| P4 a bound job runs the PDDL steps | ABSENT | `process_step.action_text` exists (0058) but there are no preconditions/effects, no run fact state and no check in `execute_step`; `job_binding` exists (`0040`) and a retired binding already refuses `409 job_binding_stale` (`crates/actions/src/control/runs.rs:199`) |
| P5 an unreviewed source never binds | ABSENT | no source review action; `job_bindings.create` checks existence only (`crates/actions/src/organisation.rs`) |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — A real SOP, an OWL file and a BPMN diagram are each ingested end to end
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 "SOP intake", "Conversion", "Process documents", "Design reuse" · §10.4 `procedures.ingest_sop|ingest_process|ingest_rdf` · §15 D53 — Requirement: an SOP (PDF or URL) and a BPMN/draw.io export each enter as a `governed_asset(kind='sop_source')` carrying provenance and convert into a PDDL procedure draft; an OWL/Turtle document enters the same way and is handed to `strata_ingest`, whose knowledge pack the draft names. Never as instructions, never read from an RDF store at runtime.

- **P1.1** Given a tenant-supplied PDF SOP, when intake runs, then a `sop_source` asset records the source and a draft procedure exists whose steps are PDDL actions with preconditions and effects.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/sop_ingestion.rs::a_pdf_sop_becomes_a_pddl_procedure_draft` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given an OWL/Turtle file, when it is ingested, then a `sop_source` asset records it, the bytes are pushed to `strata_ingest`, and the returned job id is recorded as the knowledge pack; no RDF store or reasoner is started and no local ontology rows are written.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::an_owl_file_becomes_a_knowledge_pack` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a BPMN 2.0 XML, when it is ingested, then activities become procedure steps and gateways become gates in the draft.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::a_bpmn_diagram_becomes_a_procedure_draft` (to create)
- **P1.4** Given a converted SOP, when the design job runs, then capability, agent and job drafts exist and none is published.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::an_sop_yields_capability_and_job_drafts` (to create)

### P2 — The procedure draft is published behind a human gate
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 "Gates" · §6.7 "Publish a procedure" · §5.4 · §15 D43 — Requirement: a procedure draft reaches `published` only through a recorded `approval` plus `approval_decision(decided_by_kind='human')`, the gate is tenant-configurable but defaults to human, and the job that drafted it can never satisfy its own gate.

- **P2.1** Given a draft procedure, when the drafting job attempts publication, then the attempt is refused and the procedure stays `draft`.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::the_drafting_job_cannot_publish_its_own_procedure` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a pending publish gate, when a human approves it, then the procedure is `published`, the approval id is recorded against the release and one publication event is emitted.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::a_human_approval_publishes_the_procedure` (to create)

### P3 — A re-ingest is versioned and never mutates a published procedure
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 "PKO storage and ingestion" (re-scoped by the 2026-11-19 owner decision: the versioned knowledge is the strata pack, not local rows) · §10.4 — Requirement: re-ingesting a source creates the next draft version of the derived SOP/executable; the published row keeps the source, converter and knowledge-pack references it was released with; no row is mutated in place.

- **P3.1** Given a published derived procedure, when its source is ingested again, then a new draft version exists and the published version still returns its original steps.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/procedure_versioning.rs::a_reingest_creates_a_new_draft_version` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a published derived procedure, when a new source version is imported, then the published row still names its original source and knowledge pack and the new draft names the new ones.
  Verify: `procedure_versioning.rs::the_published_procedure_keeps_its_source_and_pack` (to create)

### P4 — A job bound to the procedure runs the PDDL steps
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 "Two spaces" · §4.4 job binding · §10.3 (`procedure`/`process_step` extend with PDDL action text) — Requirement: a binding pins the published procedure and a run executes its PDDL actions in order — preconditions checked against typed facts, effects applied, each step recorded on `run_step` with its fact state — while a retired or unpublishable binding refuses.

- **P4.1** Given a binding pinned to a published procedure, when the run starts, then each step's precondition is checked, its effect applied and the step recorded on `run_step` in position order with its before/after state.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::a_bound_job_runs_the_pddl_steps` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a step whose precondition does not hold, when the run reaches it, then the run fails at that position and no later step executes.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::a_false_precondition_stops_the_run` (to create)

### P5 — An unreviewed source never binds
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.6 "Gates" · §5.7 rules · §14 R17 · §15 D53/D55 — Requirement: a source that has not passed its review gate cannot be referenced by a published procedure or binding, and no SOP can grant a tool, widen an effect ceiling or change an approval policy.

- **P5.1** Given a `sop_source` still in `draft` or `in_review`, when a procedure or binding references it, then the publish or bind is refused naming the unreviewed source.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::an_unreviewed_source_cannot_bind` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given a converted SOP whose draft asks for a tool or a wider effect ceiling, when the draft is validated, then the request is refused and the ceiling is unchanged.
  Verify: `sop_ingestion.rs::an_sop_cannot_grant_a_tool` (to create)

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | 4 — `seed/programme.json` (live `tranches.list`: tranche 0 closed, review `continue` by the owner 2026-11-17; tranches 1–13 planned) |

| blocks | #87 | §12 "T17 after T16 and T3" — the general authoring path reuses this intake pipeline | open |
| blocks | #88 | §12 "T12 after all" | open |


## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline re-measured at claim; every path and `#N` above re-resolves at that ref.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` target; both new test files are named.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; both blockers are closed.
- [x] One-PR scope, disjoint from #73 and #76: one migration, one intake/convert module, two test files.
- [x] Scope corrections applied (no old-system shutdown/parity, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity; no PKO tables — owner decision 2026-11-19).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate` and `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`).
- [ ] Real Postgres 18 integration tests per part; none skipped; the schema/migration-ledger checks pass.
- [ ] Docs updated; migration ledger handled (both ledgers record 0060).
- [ ] One PR `Closes #85` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

The general chat + document authoring path, the asset matrix and per-asset review depth (T17); the estate toolkit import wave including `lean4_prover` (T14); tool generation and BYO (T15); hosting an RDF store, reasoner or embeddings; the local PKO tables (owner decision 2026-11-19); the one-time import of the legacy `procedure_management` OWL/Turtle corpus (it reuses P1.2's path). No old-system freeze, dump, shutdown or rollback; no old-ledger import; no 218-item parity.

## Deployment prerequisite

No — every scenario is proved locally against real Postgres 18, with the model and the strata/submission calls served by the repo's existing stub HTTP server seam; no host or cluster is required.

## Open questions

| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | How deep does the ontology go, and is `lean4_prover` mandatory for a procedure class? | architecture | Decided by the first T16 pilots (§15 #13); the proof class ships without it |
| 2 | Where does the knowledge pack live, and who versions it? | architecture | Resolved 2026-11-19: strata_ingest owns it; conveyor records the job id as `knowledge_pack_ref` |
| 3 | The code calls the executable artefact `process`/`process_step` and the SOP `procedure` (0035) | architecture | Follow the code; no second rename (0058 already put `action_text` on both) |
| 4 | Is batch intake one job per source or one job per batch? | delivery | One job per source, so one failure cannot poison a batch |

## Goal

Every metric and every metering level recomputes from rows; the reconciliation with `billing_service` is exact or opens an incident; a C0–C5 level changes only when the measured evidence crosses its recorded threshold; and a gate that never refused is flagged.

## Plan / audit source

## Parts and acceptance criteria

Requirement: the flow, quality, cost, governance and knowledge metrics of §7.5 and the tenant, department/industry, programme, project and job metering levels with the run/step/call drill-down are derived at read time from the rows §7.5 names — no stored metric, no stored cost column, an unattributed call counted in its own bucket, and a source that does not exist yet reported unavailable rather than zero.
