### P2 — The reconciliation with `billing_service` is exact or opens an incident
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.5 (reconciliation) · §9.2 · §10.1 · T11 row
Requirement: the conveyor's metering for a tenant and period is compared with `billing_service`'s roll-up, a match is recorded as reconciled, and any difference opens an incident card carrying both figures and the delta — never an adjustment and never a silent pass; an unreachable `billing_service` is unavailable with the upstream reason, not a zero difference.

- **P2.1** Given both sides report the same total, when reconciliation runs, then it records the matched totals and opens no incident.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::an_exact_reconciliation_opens_no_incident` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given `billing_service` reports a different total, when reconciliation runs, then an incident card is opened carrying both totals and the delta.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_reconciliation_difference_opens_an_incident` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given `billing_service` is unreachable, when reconciliation runs, then the result is unavailable with the upstream reason and no difference is reported as zero.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::an_unreachable_billing_service_is_unavailable_not_zero` (to create)

### P3 — A C0–C5 level changes only when the measured evidence crosses its recorded threshold
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §15.1 D37, D50 · T11 row
Requirement: a maturity level is computed from named metrics over recorded rows against a tenant-scoped, versioned threshold configuration calibrated from that tenant's recorded run/approval rows — never a literal in code — and the level moves only when the evidence crosses the threshold in force; each computed level records the threshold version it used.

- **P3.1** Given a tenant whose next level's threshold is not met, when the level is computed again on the same evidence, then it does not move.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_level_does_not_move_below_its_threshold` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given evidence that crosses the recorded threshold, when the level is computed, then it moves and the result names the threshold version.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_level_moves_when_the_evidence_crosses` (to create)
- **P3.3** Given a tenant changes its threshold configuration with no code change, when the same evidence is recomputed, then the level follows the new version.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_threshold_change_is_configuration_not_code` (to create)
- **P3.4** Given two tenants, when one tenant reads its threshold configuration, then the other tenant's rows are invisible.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/rls_domain.rs::metric_thresholds_are_tenant_isolated` (to create in this file)

### P4 — A gate that never refused is flagged
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §15.1 D37 · §7.5 (governance metrics) · T11 row
Requirement: for every gate key over the configured window, governance metrics count approvals and refusals from `approval` and `approval_decision`, and a gate with no refusal is reported as never-refused with its counts, so a rubber stamp cannot read as health.

- **P4.1** Given a gate with recorded approvals and no rejecting decision, when governance metrics are read, then it is listed as never-refused with its approval count.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::a_gate_with_no_refusal_is_flagged` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given the same gate with one rejecting decision, when the metric is read, then it is not flagged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::one_refusal_clears_the_flag` (to create)

### P5 — the MSP programme metrics recompute from MSP rows
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 (the metrics sentence) · §7.5 · D37 · D62 · T11 row
Requirement: benefits realised versus planned, tranche gate outcomes and the benefit-at-risk count are computed at read time from `benefit_profile`, `benefit_transition`, `benefit_link` and `programme_tranche`; a benefit whose baseline is unmeasured is reported as unmeasured, never as zero; the tranche and benefit review gates go through P4's never-refused rule.

- **P5.1** Given benefit profiles with targets and transitions with post-measurements, when the programme metric is read, then realised-versus-planned equals the transition rows over the profile targets and reading it writes no row.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::benefits_realised_versus_planned_recomputes_from_rows` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given a slipped project dependency, when the programme metric is read, then the benefit-at-risk count follows the `benefit_link` edges from that project's output and names each benefit.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::the_benefit_at_risk_count_follows_the_map_edges` (to create)
- **P5.3** Given a tranche review gate and a benefit review gate with only approvals in the window, when governance metrics are read, then both are flagged never-refused with their counts, by P4's rule.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::the_tranche_and_benefit_gates_are_subject_to_the_never_refused_rule` (to create)
- **P5.4** Given a benefit profile whose baseline is null, when the programme metric is read, then that benefit is reported `unmeasured` with its id and the other figures are unaffected.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/metrics.rs::an_unmeasured_baseline_is_unmeasured_not_zero` (to create)

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | 1 — live `tranches.list` (`conveyor buildout`): tranche 0 is closed, the tranche-0 review decision is `continue`, authorised by the programme owner 2026-11-17; tranche 1's exit set is S02, T1, T11 |
| Brief | T11 project brief, published live (`/design/docs/output-01a1e008-25c1-776f-932f-c0ea29c05de8.html`); inception-analysis and architecture-design also published |
| ADM phase/plateau | Phase G — implementation governance. No live T11 architecture contract exists (measured 2026-11-19: `architecture.contracts_list {project_id: T11}` → 0 rows); the inception architecture-design is the published design record. Recorded as a measured gap, not bypassed. |
| Benefits | B1–B6 — the six live `benefits.list` rows (all `draft`, baselines unmeasured); this unit's P4/P5 are their measurement instrument, including B6 (seed/coverage/published checklist agreement) |

## Dependencies

| blocked-by | #72 | §7.5's programme and project metering levels aggregate over the plan spine's rows | closed 2026-11-17 (merged `e3d7c4e`) |
| blocked-by | #74 | Derived from this unit's gate, not from the seed: the governance and never-refused metrics read the `approval` rows the PM's gate routing produces, and D37 calibrates the C0–C5 thresholds from those run/approval rows | closed 2026-11-17 (PR #313; CI green, merge queued) |
| blocks | #88 | `seed/programme.json` T12 `meta.depends_on` lists T11; §12 "T12 after all" | open |
| related | #46 | Its title claims "metering reconciliation" for the billing-service absorption while this unit owns the conveyor-side reconciliation; no ordering, but the two must not build it twice | open |

Met: #74 — the metrics and metering this issue computes over run and approval rows cannot be built before the PM job exists; #72's plan spine is merged (`e3d7c4e`).

## Definition of ready
- [x] Baseline named and the plan/audit blob shas recorded.
- [x] Every spec/plan/code/test reference resolves at its ref; every `#N` resolves.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [x] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; `Blocker:` present iff `status:blocked` (no open `blocked-by`; `status:ready`).

- [x] Scope corrections applied (no old-system shutdown/parity, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity).

## Definition of done

- [x] Repo gate at the exact head: clippy `--all-targets -D warnings`, fmt, registry, parity, the 17 scenarios, RLS, seed/schema/programme and `--check-lock`. The full workspace suite runs in the PR's `checks` job (`rbuild --gate` resolves to archetype defaults with no services on this repo).
- [x] Tests added/updated per part; none skipped.
- [x] Docs updated; the migration ledger (58), the action dump, the served-spec lock and v2 coverage regenerated.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #84` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted — PR #404 is open (opened over the WIP cap on the owner's "unblock yourself" instruction).

## Out of scope
- Per-tool metrics, health probes, zero-call retirement and schema-drift katas (§11.9): they read `tool_call` and `tools.probe`, which T13/T14 create. Metering adds tool spend by the same derivation when that ledger lands; until then it reads unavailable.
- Any metric store, snapshot table, nightly roll-up or backfill: a metric is never persisted (§7.5, D37).
- Charging and entitlement (`licenses`/`billing_service`, §10.1) and the V2 destination panels (§10.5): this unit reads and reconciles and never invoices; the actions are the read surface, and the UI reads the same derivation later.
- Building T1's plan tables or T3's PM path — this unit consumes them.
- Freezing, dumping or shutting down any old system; old-ledger import; old-backlog parity; old-service rollback; retiring old flows.

## Deployment prerequisite
No for construction — proved by compose plus a real Postgres integration run (§12 preamble). The live half of P2 (a real `billing_service` answer) is recorded when the platform is deployed; no unit gates this issue.

## Open questions

issues.body:
## Goal
Every live estate service in `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.2 is a published toolkit with a green read-only probe and one live call recorded through the broker — `scientific_processor` included, probed and called after an explicit scale-up from zero and returned to zero — a zero-use report names every toolkit with no calls in the cycle, and a backend outage refuses new runs `409 tool_not_ready` while in-flight runs finish.

## Plan / audit source
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.2 (the estate table, measured 2026-11-11) · §11.9 (probe, unbind, zero-use) · §11.3 step 1 and §11.4 (the broker and effect rules this gate depends on) · §12 row **T14 — Estate toolkits** · `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.md` rows `actions:tools`, `destination:Tools`, both `new`.

## Claim
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | — |
| HEAD | — |
| Session | — |
| Updated | — |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References
| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.2, §11.9, §12 T14 | main@f14b7d36 |
| Spec | §11.3 step 1 (`409 tool_not_ready` before any network call), §11.4 (k8s scale is `destructive`: approval + dry-run + dual control), §3 P8/P10 | main@f14b7d36 |
| Code | `crates/api/src/actions.rs:161` — `/api/actions/{name}/invocations`, where `tools.*` arrives | main@f14b7d36 |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/integrations/external.rs:93` `HandlerRef::External` — V1's direct job-backend calls, whose operations move onto toolkit operations in #76 | main@f14b7d36 |
| Harness | `compose.yaml:140` profile `strata` + `scripts/strata/README.md` (a real `strata_rag` locally) · `scripts/prove-s3.sh` is the proof-script precedent | main@f14b7d36 |
| Schema | `tool`, `toolkit`, `tool_binding`, `tool_call` | shipped by #76 — extend only |
| Test | `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs` · `scripts/prove-estate.sh` | to create |
| Issue | #76 | CLOSED 2026-11-17 — dependency met |

## Baseline
Code `main@f14b7d36` (2026-11-19); re-measured at claim 2026-11-19 after #76 (T13) merged `migrations/0055_tool_platform.sql` and the broker. The 2026-11-13 baseline (`main@5cf3d75`) is superseded: the four tables exist, `tools.call` is served, and the §11.2 estate has been rewritten to Rust — see the re-baselined current state below.

## Current state (measured)
| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 every published toolkit has a probe and one live call | ABSENT | at `main@f14b7d36`: `git grep -n -e 'tools.probe' -e 'toolkits.publish' -- crates migrations` → 0 hits; the only production-shaped insert into `toolkit`/`tool` is `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs:191`; `tools.call` is the only `tools.*` action |
| P2 `scientific_processor` scale-up, probe, one call, scale-back | N/A — superseded, deviation recorded below | the Python `scientific_processor` deployment no longer exists; `scientific-processor/scientific-processor` runs `conveyor-scientific@sha256:54f33fa…` at 1/1 |
| P3 a zero-use report exists | ABSENT | `git grep -n -e 'zero-use' -e 'zero_use' -e 'unused_tool' -- crates migrations scripts` → 0 hits |
| P4 an outage unbinds new runs and in-flight runs finish | PARTIAL | `store::tool::resolve` already filters `b.enabled`, published toolkit and published tool (`crates/store/src/tool.rs:178-183`), but nothing disables a binding on a probe failure and the broker's `409` carries no `errors[]` naming the tool |

## Parts and acceptance criteria
### P1 — Every published toolkit has a probe and one live call
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.2 · §11.9 · §12 T14
Requirement: the import wave publishes one immutable toolkit version per live service, each with a green read-only `tools.probe` and one live call ledgered as a `tool_call`; a service that is not deployed or not configured enters only as `draft` — unbound and uncallable.

**Re-baselined estate (measured 2026-11-19).** The publishable set is exactly the registry's `HandlerRef::External` actions grouped by service: `coding` (`coding_jobs.create`/`.get`), `tts` (`produce.speech`), `asr` (`media.transcribe`), `image_gen` (`media.generate_image`) — all four configured on the deployed conveyor; `strata_rag` (`retrieval.query`) and `strata_ingest` — live but not configured on today's Deployment; `artifacts`, `billing_service` and `worker_management` publish as `draft` because their base URL is unset or their upstream (w2v) is retired. The kag-era services in the 2026-11-11 table no longer exist as separate services: `webscraper`, `media_discovery` and `scientific_processor` are `conveyor-research`, `conveyor-research-media` and `conveyor-scientific`, `evidence_review` is absorbed into `conveyor-scientific`, and their capabilities are in-process conveyor actions, not external toolkits.

- **P1.1** Given the published toolkits, when `tools.probe` runs for each, then every probe answers its registered destination alias and none is refused `tool_not_ready`.
  Verify: `scripts/prove-estate.sh probe-all` (to create) → one row per published toolkit
- **P1.2** Given a published toolkit, when one declared read-class operation is called through the broker, then the call succeeds and exactly one `tool_call` row carries it.
  Verify: `scripts/prove-estate.sh call-all` (to create) + `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::every_published_toolkit_has_one_live_call` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a `draft` service, when a job asks to bind or call it, then the catalogue shows no binding and the call is refused `409 tool_not_ready`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::a_draft_toolkit_is_unbound_and_uncallable` (to create)

### P2 — a destination that is not serving refuses new runs, and the refusal lifts
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.9 · §11.3 step 1 · §12 T14

**Deviation, recorded at claim 2026-11-19.** The original P2 exercised a scale-to-zero cycle on
`scientific_processor`. That deployment no longer exists: the service was rewritten as
`conveyor-scientific` (Rust), which runs 1/1, and no Python `scientific_processor` workload
remains in the cluster. Scaling a live service to zero to manufacture the scenario would weaken,
not strengthen, the estate. The property P2 exists to prove — a toolkit whose destination is not
serving refuses new runs `409 tool_not_ready`, and the refusal lifts when the destination returns
— is proved on a real unconfigured destination (`artifacts`, `billing_service` or
`worker_management`, each `draft` in today's estate) and by the real-destination outage drill in P4.

- **P2.1** Given a toolkit whose destination has no configured base URL, when `tools.probe` runs, then it reports that toolkit `unconfigured`, no binding exists, and any call is refused `409 tool_not_ready`.
  Verify: `scripts/prove-estate.sh probe-all` (to create) shows `unconfigured` for that toolkit + `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::an_unconfigured_toolkit_is_draft_and_uncallable` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a destination that is configured and a green probe, when the toolkit is published and bound, then one call succeeds and its `tool_call` row exists — the refusal has lifted.
  Verify: `scripts/prove-estate.sh call-all` (to create) + `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::a_probe_green_toolkit_is_callable` (to create)

### P3 — A zero-use report exists
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.9 · §3 P10 · §14 R13
Requirement: a report lists every published tool version with its call count for the programme cycle and flags the zero-use set for retirement, computed from `tool_call` rows over the programme's configured cadence — never a hand-maintained list.

- **P3.1** Given one tool called once and one never called in the cycle, when the report runs, then only the uncalled one appears in the zero-use set.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::the_zero_use_report_flags_only_uncalled_tools` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given the live estate, when the report is generated, then every published toolkit appears exactly once with a count and an owner.
  Verify: `scripts/prove-estate.sh zero-use-report` (to create)

### P4 — A backend outage unbinds new runs and in-flight runs finish
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.9 · §11.3 step 1 · §3 P8
Requirement: a probe failure disables the binding for new runs — refused `409 tool_not_ready` before any network call, with `blocking[]` naming the tool — while a run already in flight on that tool finishes and its `tool_call` rows record the outcome.

- **P4.1** Given a live binding, when its destination stops answering, then a new run is refused `409 tool_not_ready` before the call and the binding is disabled.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::an_outage_refuses_new_runs_before_the_call` (to create) + `scripts/prove-estate.sh outage` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a run in flight when the outage begins, when it reaches the tool, then it completes and its `tool_call` rows are recorded; the unbind never kills it.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/estate_toolkits.rs::an_in_flight_run_finishes_after_the_unbind` (to create)

## Programme

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tranche | 4 — `seed/programme.json` (live `tranches.list`: tranche 0 closed, review `continue` by the owner 2026-11-17; tranches 1–13 planned) |

## Dependencies

| blocked-by | #76 | `seed/programme.json` T14 `meta.depends_on: ["T13"]`; §12 "T14 after T13" — the four tables and broker shipped there; `tools.probe` did **not** (measured: only `tools.call` exists) | CLOSED 2026-11-17 — dependency met |
| blocks | #88 | §12 "T12 after all"; T14 is one of T12's dependencies | open |


## Definition of ready
- [x] Baseline named (`main@f14b7d36`, 2026-11-19); every reference resolves at that commit; #76 closed, so the dependency is met.
- [ ] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.

- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate` and `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

## Out of scope
The tool platform itself — tables, broker, effect classes, credential profiles, storage adapter — is #76's; BYO, OpenAPI import and tool authoring are T15. No call through `nonagenticai_mcp_server` (D44), and no toolkit for anything §11.2 lists as deliberately not a tool (n8n, fr, Planka, `worker-management`, `inference-router`/laya, provisioning, `artifact_service`/`storage-api`). No old-system freeze, dump, shutdown or rollback; no 348-flow retirement; no old-ledger import; no 218-item parity.

| 3 | Do `video-compiler` and the w2v orchestrator import before their Rust rewrite (D54/D58)? | architecture | Yes, as external toolkits; they re-import when rewritten |

## Goal
A programme runs on the SAFe cadence and is managed in MSP tranches: PI planning turns the WSJF-ranked backlog into WIP-bounded draft cards a person approves, a deliverable must exhibit evidence to earn demo credit, every retro ends in lessons, an end-of-tranche review with no evidence is refused, and a transition that never measured its baseline cannot report the benefit realized.

## Plan / audit source
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 · §12 row **T10** · `seed/programme.json` project `T10` (`meta.gate`, `meta.depends_on`). `docs/plans/00-INDEX.md` "Queue status 2026-11-13" states SPEC_V2 §12 carries V2 scope; no `S##` slice plan exists for a `T` unit.

## Claim

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §10.3 — `programme_cadence`, `programme_tranche`, `benefit_profile`, `benefit_link`, `benefit_transition`, `wbs_node` WSJF inputs, `lesson` | main@48fc44c |

## Baseline

- Code: `origin/main@e3d7c4e`, measured 2026-11-17; #72 (T1) is merged and #74 (T3) remains; re-measure both at claim time.
- Docs: SPEC blob `cc4a6a6d2e9d8b3f931670b34c65dd66d2f56198` · seed blob `f409d304f2e89f6a1c6eb585f379732faefd6783` (`git rev-parse origin/main:<path>`).

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 PI planning by WSJF within WIP | PARTIAL (WIP cap only) | `git grep -n 'wsjf' -- crates migrations apps tests` → no matches; `git grep -n 'programme_cadence' -- crates migrations` → no matches; `git grep -n 'wip_limit' -- migrations crates` → `migrations/0002_domain.sql:85`, `crates/actions/src/board/pull.rs:71` |

| P3 retro produces lessons | ABSENT | `git grep -ni 'retrospective\|retro' -- crates migrations apps tests` → no matches; `git grep -n 'lesson' -- crates migrations apps tests` → prose comments only, no `lesson` table |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — PI planning materialises the backlog by WSJF within WIP
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 (PI planning; "WSJF is arithmetic, not opinion"). Requirement: a `programme_cadence(kind='pi')` job drafts the next cadence's cards from the standing backlog ordered by `(business_value + time_criticality + risk_reduction) / job_size`, bounded by the active lane's WIP slots, and a person approves the plan.

- **P1.1** Given backlog rows carrying the four typed integer inputs, when the cadence materialises, then drafts are ordered by the computed score descending and no computed score is stored on the row.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test programme_cadence wsjf_is_computed_not_stored` (to create at `crates/store/tests/programme_cadence.rs`)
- **P1.2** Given an active lane with `wip_limit` N and b live cards, when materialisation runs, then at most N−b drafts are created and the remaining backlog rows are untouched.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test programme_cadence materialisation_respects_wip_slots` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a due `programme_cadence(kind='pi')`, when the worker tick runs twice, then the first run creates one draft per backlog row and the second creates none.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test cadence_jobs pi_tick_is_idempotent` (to create at `apps/server/tests/cadence_jobs.rs`)
- **P1.4** Given a backlog row with `job_size = 0`, when it is scored, then the call is a typed refusal and no draft is created.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test programme_cadence a_zero_job_size_is_refused` (to create)

### P2 — A deliverable without evidence cannot demo
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 (System demo) · §5.4 (gate evidence). Requirement: the `programme_cadence(kind='demo')` event records a credit only for a completed deliverable exhibiting at least one evidence ref (run, artefact or eval id); otherwise the demo is refused and no credit is recorded.

- **P2.1** Given a completed deliverable with an evidence ref, when the demo event records it, then a demo credit is recorded against that cadence.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test demo_gate a_delivered_item_with_evidence_earns_credit` (to create at `crates/store/tests/demo_gate.rs`)
- **P2.2** Given a completed deliverable with no evidence ref, when the demo attempts to record it, then the recording is refused with §5.4's missing-evidence code and no credit row exists.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test demo_gate evidence_less_deliverable_cannot_demo` (to create)

### P3 — Retro produces lessons
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.2 (Inspect & adapt) · §10.3 `lesson`. Requirement: a `programme_cadence(kind='retro')` event opens one retro card owned by the coach, and a retro closes only when every finding it recorded has a `lesson` proposal carrying its evidence refs.

- **P3.1** Given a cadence period whose work is complete, when its retro runs, then one retro card is opened for that programme and assigned to the coach.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test retro retro_card_is_the_coachs` (to create at `crates/store/tests/retro.rs`)
- **P3.2** Given a retro card with findings, when it is closed, then each finding has a `lesson` row in `proposed` state carrying its evidence refs and the cadence it came from.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test retro every_finding_becomes_a_lesson` (to create)
- **P3.3** Given a retro card with a finding that has no `lesson`, when close is attempted, then the close is refused.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test retro retro_cannot_close_without_lessons` (to create)

### P4 — the end-of-tranche review is a programme decision
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 · D62 · T10 row — Requirement: a `programme_tranche` carries its entry and
exit criteria, its baseline and its review date; the review is an approval by the sponsoring group
with the baselines, the benefit status against the profiles and the risk register as evidence; it
records continue, pause or stop; a re-baseline goes through change control, never through the review.

- **P4.1** Given a tranche whose review evidence is the baselines, benefit status and risk register, when the sponsoring group records the decision, then the tranche state and the next tranche's authorisation follow it.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_review_records_continue_pause_or_stop` (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a tranche review with no baselines, benefit status or risk evidence, when it is requested, then it is refused and no decision row is written.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_review_without_evidence_is_refused`
- **P4.3** Given a tranche that needs a new baseline, when the review tries to set it, then the review is refused and a change request is the only path.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_rebaseline_goes_through_change_control`
- **P4.4** Given a programme whose first tranche has no authorisation review, when a project in that programme starts, then the start is refused `409 tranche_not_authorised` and no run is created; after the sponsoring group records the review with its evidence, the identical start proceeds.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/tranche_review.rs::a_project_cannot_start_before_its_tranche_is_authorised` (to create)
- **P4.5** Given a dependency slip recorded against a project, when the slip is recorded, then the benefits put at risk are named through the `benefit_link` edges that depend on that project's output — the response and the register row carry the benefit ids, not prose.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/benefit_transition.rs::a_dependency_slip_names_the_benefits_at_risk` (to create)

### P5 — benefits realization is a procedure after delivery
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 · D62 · T10 row — Requirement: a `benefit_transition` records the baseline
measured while the old practice is observable, the readiness assessment, the transition, the
post-transition measurement and the legacy retirement; a benefit whose baseline was never measured
cannot report a realized improvement, and the programme closes only with a realization plan that
names post-closure measurement.

- **P5.1** Given a benefit whose baseline was measured and whose transition is enacted, when the post-transition measurement runs, then the delta against the baseline is attributable to the operational area and the legacy practice is retired.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/benefit_transition.rs::a_measured_baseline_enables_realization` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given a benefit with no measured baseline, when a transition attempts to report a realized benefit, then it is refused `benefit_baseline_missing` and no realization row is written.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/benefit_transition.rs::a_missing_baseline_cannot_claim_realization`
- **P5.3** Given a programme closing, when its realization plan does not name who continues measurement, then closure is refused.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/benefit_transition.rs::a_close_without_a_post_closure_owner_is_refused`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | #72 | T1 supplies `programme_cadence`, `wbs_node` with the WSJF inputs and the programme `shared_config` the cadence inherits (`seed/programme.json` T10 `depends_on` includes T1) | closed 2026-11-17 (merged `e3d7c4e`) |
| blocked-by | #74 | T3 supplies the PM job and the gate routing the materialised cards and demo credits pass through | closed 2026-11-17 (PR #313; CI green, merge queued) |
| related | #303 | the benefit profile's edit/retire lifecycle that the realization rows assume | open |
| blocks | #88 | T12 `depends_on` includes T10; its loop ends with the lesson this retro produces | open |

Met: #74 — the PM gate routing must exist before construction. #72's cadence/WBS rows and #73's decision ladder are merged.

## Definition of ready

- [ ] Baseline named; SPEC and seed blob shas recorded.
- [ ] Every spec/code/test reference resolves at `origin/main@e3d7c4e`; #74 resolves and is open.
- [ ] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [ ] Dependencies typed and cited; `Blocker:` line present.
- [ ] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from other ready issues; scope corrections applied (no old-system shutdown/parity, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate`); tests added per part, none skipped.
- [ ] Migrations and the action registry updated when touched; `--check-lock` handled.
- [ ] Every gate ships with its negative test (§5.4); each part's refusal path is reachable.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope

- T9's TOGAF phases and contracts; T11's metering and C0–C5; T8's lesson review, promotion and knowledge-source path (this slice writes `proposed` lessons only); kata execution, measurement and adoption (T5) — at most a kata candidate is opened.
- A portfolio optimiser or schedule solver, a SAFe compliance badge, any certification claim (§8.5).
- The audit's scope corrections: old-system freeze/dump/shutdown, 348-flow retirement, old-ledger import, 218-item parity, old-service rollback.

## Deployment prerequisite
No — every scenario runs locally against the compose Postgres.

## Open questions

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Which slice creates the `lesson` table — T8 owns the lifecycle, T10's retro writes proposals (§10.3 names the row, no slice claims it) | programme owner | whichever lands first creates it; T10 writes `proposed` rows only |
| 2 | §8.2's backlog-refinement job (re-score WSJF, flag stale) is named in the T10 slice row but not in the gate | programme owner | in scope as a scheduled re-score on the same typed inputs; no extra gate |

## Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `programme_cadence.rs::wsjf_is_computed_not_stored` | PASS — score ordered in the query, no `wsjf` column | `e452523f` |
| P1.2 | `programme_cadence.rs::materialisation_respects_wip_slots` | PASS — 2 drafts for wip 3 − 1 live, 3 rows untouched | `e452523f` |
| P1.3 | `cadence_jobs.rs::pi_tick_is_idempotent` | PASS — first tick drafts 2, second none, cadence `materialised` | `e452523f` |
| P1.4 | `programme_cadence.rs::a_zero_job_size_is_refused` | PASS — typed refusal + the row is unstorable | `e452523f` |

| P3.1 | `retro.rs::retro_card_is_the_coachs` | PASS — one card per cadence, `owner_kind: coach` | `e452523f` |

issues.title: T10 — SAFe cadence and MSP tranches

issues.body:
## Goal

The conveyor runs a TOGAF ADM capability, not a document library: the Preliminary phase
establishes the principles, the tailored profile, the artefact standard and repository, the
Architecture Board, governance, maturity and skills; an `architecture` project walks phases A–H as
WBS nodes with typed artefacts and contract gates; a delivery project cannot pass its design gate
without the live contract that governs it; a phase-G compliance review records exactly one level
and a waiver names its accepting owner and review date; a phase-H review produces exactly one
change request or kata candidate.

## Plan / audit source

`docs/plans/T9-architecture-capability.md` — the implementation plan behind SPEC_V2 §12 row T9.
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1 (the capability), §8.5 (the trace chain), §10.3 (the eleven tables), §10.4
(the `architecture.*` family), §10.5 (the destination), D63. No T9 plan existed before #216; this
issue is now the plan's one delivery unit.

## Claim

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Branch | — |
| HEAD | — |
| Session | — |
| Updated | — |
| Adopted-from | — |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | `docs/plans/T9-architecture-capability.md` | `main` (merged in PR #232) |
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.1, §8.5, §10.3, §10.4, §10.5, §12 T9, D63 | same |
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §8.3 (the MSP layer this sits beside) · §8.4 (PMP rows) | same |
| Gate | `seed/programme.json` T9 `meta.gate` and `meta.depends_on` | regenerated from SPEC §12 |
| Code | `migrations/0002_domain.sql:governed_asset` (kind CHECK), `:trace_link`, `catalogue_entry` | `main@48fc44c` |
| Code | `crates/domain/src/catalogue.rs:CatalogueKind` (`ProjectType`, `Phase`, `Gate`) | `main@48fc44c` |
| Code | `migrations/0035_process_tree.sql:process_map` · `crates/actions/src/process/step.rs` (gate steps) | `main@48fc44c` |
| Code | `migrations/0008_s08_portfolio.sql:register_item` (kinds `resource\|risk\|benefit`) | `main@48fc44c` |
| Code | `crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs:approvals_decide` (the gate primitive) | `main@48fc44c` |
| Test | `crates/api/tests/architecture_artifacts.rs`, `architecture_capability.rs`, `togaf_architecture_phases.rs`, `togaf_delivery_design_gate.rs`, `architecture_compliance.rs`, `togaf_h_change.rs` | to create |
| Issue | #72 (closed 2026-11-17), #74 | open |
| Issue | #216 (the spec and plan), #221 (the output categories) | closed (PR #232) / open (PR #262) |

## Baseline

- Code: `main@9d75dc3` · re-measured 2026-11-17 · measured 2026-11-16
- Plan: `docs/plans/T9-architecture-capability.md` on `main` (merged in PR #232).
- Seed: `seed/programme.json` T9 `depends_on: ["T1","T3","P0"]`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 artefact standard and repository | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'architecture_artifact\|artifact_type' -- crates migrations` → 0 |
| P2 Preliminary capability | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'adm_profile\|governance_body\|architecture_maturity' -- crates migrations` → 0 |
| P3 phases and contracts | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'architecture_contract' -- crates migrations` → 0; `governed_asset.kind` is `requirement\|principle\|adr` (`migrations/0002_domain.sql:256`) |
| P4 delivery design gate and compliance | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'design_gate\|compliance_review\|architecture_waiver' -- crates migrations` → 0 |
| P5 phase H | ABSENT | `project_register_item` allows `resource\|risk\|benefit` only (`migrations/0008_s08_portfolio.sql:112`); no kata table |
| P6 console and seed | ABSENT | the design study previews the destination (#216); no live rows |

Reused, not rebuilt: `governed_asset` (requirements, principles, ADRs and their supersession),
`trace_link` (both directions, unique edge), `catalogue_entry` (project-type × card-type and the
seeded phase catalogue), `process_step.kind='gate'`, the approval primitive and dual control,
`document` + MinIO for artefact documents, `wbs_node` (T1) and the PM's gate routing (T3).

**Preliminary content, measured 2026-11-17.** P0 publishes the five Preliminary documents — `architecture-principles` (PF-1), `adm-profile` (ADM-1), `artifact-standard` (AS-1), `maturity-assessment` (MA-1) and `skills-assessment` (SA-1) — each "proposed for P0 acceptance" (#122's A7). The `architecture_board` governance-body row, the contract and waiver rows and the typed artefact repository remain this issue's schema and actions (D2–D4).

## Parts and acceptance criteria

One part per plan deliverable; the plan carries the full scenarios. Each part's `Verify:` is the
test target this issue creates.

### P1 — the artefact standard and repository (`Plan D1`)

`artifact_type` seeded; `architecture_artifact`, `architecture_artifact_entry`,
`architecture_artifact_link`; `architecture.artifacts.*` and `architecture.repository.search`;
approve/supersede immutability; catalog entries and matrix axes queryable; diagram metadata with a
viewpoint.

- Given a catalog with ten entries, when it is queried, then the entries are rows and the
  artefact's metadata names its owner, reviewer, version and document.
  `Verify:` `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test architecture_artifacts a_catalog_is_queryable_rows`
- Given an approved artefact, when it is edited, then the edit is refused and a new version
  supersedes it; the approved body is unchanged.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/architecture_artifacts.rs::an_approved_artefact_is_immutable`
- Given a solution artefact, when a `reuse` link is recorded, then the repository search returns
  the reused enterprise artefact across plateaus.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/architecture_artifacts.rs::reuse_is_searchable_across_plateaus`

### P2 — the Preliminary capability (`Plan D2`)

The principles catalog; `adm_profile`; the seeded mandatory sets; `governance_body` (the
Architecture Board); the nine-dimension maturity assessment; the seven-category skills assessment.

- Given the profile, when a phase's mandatory set is read, then it is filtered by the phase and
  plateau and the board charter is a governance body row.
  `Verify:` `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test architecture_capability the_profile_names_the_mandatory_set`
- Given a maturity assessment, when a dimension is missing, then the assessment is refused.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/architecture_capability.rs::a_maturity_assessment_needs_every_dimension`
- Given a skills assessment, when a role's proficiency is recorded, then it names the seven
  categories and the job key.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/architecture_capability.rs::a_skills_assessment_names_its_role`

### P3 — the architecture project, phases and contracts (`Plan D3`, was P1)

The `architecture` project type; Preliminary and A–H as WBS nodes; the four contract kinds; a
phase advance refuses on a missing mandatory artefact or a non-live contract; a contract change is
a new version and re-opens the gate.

- Given every mandatory artefact approved and a live SAW, when phase A is advanced, then it closes
  and B is open.
  `Verify:` `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test togaf_architecture_phases phases_a_to_f_pass_in_order`
- Given one mandatory artefact still draft, when the phase is advanced, then it is refused naming
  that artefact and no contract row is written.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/togaf_architecture_phases.rs::a_draft_artefact_refuses_the_contract`
- Given an approved contract, when its content changes, then a new version supersedes it and the
  phase gate re-opens; the approved body is unchanged.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/togaf_architecture_phases.rs::a_contract_change_reopens_the_gate`

### P4 — the delivery design gate, compliance and waivers (`Plan D4`, was P2)

A delivery project's design gate resolves only against a live approved contract trace-linked to it;
absent, draft or superseded all refuse. A phase-G review records exactly one of the six levels; a
deviation is waived only with an accepting owner and a reassessment date.

- Given a delivery project with no governing contract, when its design gate is requested, then it
  is refused and no approval row is written.
  `Verify:` `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test togaf_delivery_design_gate`
- Given a superseded contract, when design is requested, then it is refused naming its status.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/togaf_delivery_design_gate.rs::a_superseded_contract_refuses_design`
- Given a review, when a second compliance level is recorded, then it is refused; a waiver without
  an owner or a review date is refused.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/architecture_compliance.rs::one_level_and_a_dated_waiver`

### P5 — phase H produces a change or a kata, never both (`Plan D5`, was P3)

Every phase-H review records exactly one typed outcome — a change request with impact under the
change gate, or a kata candidate routed to the kata lane; a review with no verdict cannot close.

- Given a scope change, when the verdict is recorded, then a `project_register_item(kind='change')`
  with impact exists and is routed to the change gate.
  `Verify:` `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test togaf_h_change`
- Given a systemic finding, when it is recorded, then the verdict is a kata candidate and no change
  register row is written.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/togaf_h_change.rs::a_systemic_finding_produces_a_kata_candidate`
- Given a review with no verdict, when the phase-H gate is requested, then it is refused.
  `Verify:` `crates/api/tests/togaf_h_change.rs::an_unrecorded_review_refuses_the_gate`

### P6 — the console surface and the seed (`Plan D6`)

The Architecture destination renders the four tabs against the live rows (the design study previews
it in #216); the seed's T9 gate is the §12 row's; the T9/P0 output categories land with #221.

- Given the console, when the Architecture destination opens, then the four tabs render against the
  live reads and each action changes its row.
  `Verify:` `node docs/design/scripts/check-v2.cjs` (design study) and the deployment-gated console smoke.
- Given the seed, when it is regenerated, then T9's gate text is the §12 row's.
  `Verify:` `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py --check`

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |

## Parts and acceptance criteria
### P1 — A real feature lands: lane → PR → CI → review → merge → deploy → live verify
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.4 · §9.1 (1–9) · §12 T6 — Requirement: a development project records one repo and one lane in its charter, then each step as evidence — branch, PR, the CI run's verdict, an independent reviewer who is not the implementer, the merge, the deploy and the live check — and no step may be skipped.

- **P1.1** Given a development project chartered against one repo and one lane, when it reaches closure, then the closure record links the lane, the PR, the CI run, the reviewer's decision (a different principal from the implementer), the merge SHA, the deployed digest and the live check.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::a_development_project_records_every_step_from_lane_to_live_verify` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given a CI run whose verdict is red, when the project asks for the merge gate, then the merge is refused and the refusal is recorded — never retried until green.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::a_red_ci_run_refuses_the_merge_gate` (to create)
- **P1.3** (live, deployment-gated) Given the merged change deployed, when the live check runs, then the serving digest is the merged commit's build and the project's acceptance check passes.
  Verify: `curl -fsS "$CONVEYOR_BASE_URL/health"` plus the project's own acceptance command, both recorded in the closure record

### P2 — The project cannot change its own gates
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §9.3 · §6.4 (Never, earned autonomy) · §5.4 — Requirement: the gate set, approval policy, eval instrument and benchmark suite that judge a development project are changed only by a separate governance project with a different approver set; the project's own attempt is refused and recorded, the implementer never decides its own merge gate, and auto-merge is a tenant policy row that defaults off.

- **P2.1** Given a development project in flight, when it attempts to change the gate set, approval policy or the instrument that measures it, then the change is refused, the refusal names the surface and the approver set it needs, and the gate set is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::a_development_project_cannot_change_the_gates_that_judge_it` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a merge gate on the project's own work, when the implementing job's principal decides it, then the decision is refused and the gate stays pending for a human.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::the_implementer_cannot_decide_its_own_merge_gate` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a tenant with no auto-merge row, when the merge gate is evaluated, then a human must approve; given a row, then its approver kind, conditions and expiry are read from the row rather than from code.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::auto_merge_defaults_off_and_reads_the_tenant_policy_row` (to create)

### P3 — Rollback tested
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §9.1 (8) · §9.3 — Requirement: every deployable development change carries a rollback plan recorded before the deploy, a deploy whose rollback was never exercised is refused, and the exercised rollback is proven against the live service.

- **P3.1** Given a deployable change with no recorded rollback plan, when the deploy gate is asked to decide, then it refuses with a reason naming the missing rollback evidence.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs::a_deploy_without_a_tested_rollback_is_refused` (to create)
- **P3.2** (live, deployment-gated) Given a deployed change with a recorded plan, when the rollback is exercised, then the prior digest serves again, `/health` is 200 and the closure record carries both digests and the rollback's evidence.
  Verify: `curl -fsS "$CONVEYOR_BASE_URL/health"` at the restored digest, with both digests in the closure record

refs and their independent count, and fewer than two independent refs is a typed refusal, never a stored lesson.

- **P1.1** Given a lesson proposal with one evidence ref, when `lessons.propose` is called, then it is refused `422 lesson_evidence_insufficient` naming the count, and no lesson reaches `reviewed`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::one_evidence_ref_is_refused` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs`)
- **P1.2** Given two refs that resolve to the same card or the same run, when the proposal is counted, then they are one independent ref and the proposal is refused.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::two_refs_from_one_run_are_one_independent_ref` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given the same input reaching the database without the action, when the insert runs, then a CHECK refuses the row and no lesson with a single independent ref is stored.
  Verify: `crates/store/tests/lesson.rs::the_database_refuses_a_lesson_with_one_independent_ref` (to create at `crates/store/tests/lesson.rs`)

### P2 — Two independent refs + review promotes a source draft
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.6 · §10.3 · §10.4 · D36 — Requirement: with two independent refs a person's review is the only
act that promotes the lesson to a knowledge source draft, through the existing source/pack release path; the proposer
cannot review, nothing live is published, and no model or embedding runs.

- **P2.1** Given a lesson with two independent refs, when a person holding the review scope approves it, then the lesson is `promoted`, a source draft exists in draft state, and no `capability_knowledge` pin changed.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::two_independent_refs_and_a_human_review_promote_a_source_draft` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given a lesson proposed by a job's executor principal, when that same principal calls `lessons.review`, then the review is refused for want of the review scope and the lesson stays `proposed`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::the_proposing_job_cannot_review_its_own_lesson` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a promotion that succeeds, when the action returns, then it recorded no `inference_call` and stored no embedding — the conveyor hosts neither (§7.6, last rule).
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::promotion_calls_no_model` (to create)

### P3 — A bad run never becomes doctrine
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.6 · §9.4 — Requirement: a lesson recorded from execution is born `proposed` and no execution path
auto-promotes it; a rejection is durable and only a new independent ref reopens it.

- **P3.1** Given a failed run, when the improvement loop records its lesson, then the lesson is `proposed` and every `capability_knowledge` pin a live job resolves is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::a_failed_run_records_a_lesson_that_is_not_doctrine` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a lesson rejected at review, when the identical proposal returns with no new independent ref, then promotion is refused and the rejection stands.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/lessons.rs::a_rejected_lesson_needs_new_independent_evidence` (to create)

issues.body:
## Goal
An operations job family detects a pod failure, triages it, mitigates it through an approved gated write, resolves it and records a postmortem; a destructive ops action without the tenant's configured approvals is refused before it reaches the cluster; and restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip are all callable write verbs.

## Plan / audit source
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.5 · §9.2 · §12 T7 row · `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.md` row `actions:operations` (= `new`) · `seed/programme.json` T7 `meta.gate`. No V2 slice plan exists at the baseline; the spec row is the plan.

| Adopted-from | — |

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.5 (charter, inputs, outputs, read tools, gated write tools, autonomy, Never) | main@6c46d92e |
| Spec | `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §9.2 (incident card fields, runbook, read-first, least privilege, postmortem) | main@6c46d92e |

| Code | `crates/actions/src/spec.rs:Effect`, `:Confirm`, `:Scope` — the `ops:write` scope exists (`crates/actions-derive/src/lib.rs:227`) | main@6c46d92e |
| Code | `crates/api/src/copilot/proposal.rs:required` (destructive ⇒ proposal, copilot channel only) | main@6c46d92e |

| Test | `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs`; `crates/api/tests/ops_incident.rs` | to create |
| Issue | #73 · #75 · #76 | closed (2026-11-19) |

## Baseline
- Code: `main@6c46d92e` · measured 2026-11-19 (re-baseline; supersedes `5cf3d75` (2026-11-13))

| Part | State | Evidence |

| P1 triage → approved mitigation → resolve → postmortem | ABSENT | measured 2026-11-19: `git grep -n -i 'runbook\|postmortem\|ops_incident' -- crates migrations seed` → no table, no action; `governed_asset` admits `requirement\|principle\|adr` only (`migrations/0002_domain.sql:256`); the `incident` card type exists (`seed/catalogue.json`, 76 types) and `metrics.reconcile` opens one (`crates/actions/src/metrics/mod.rs:932`) but nothing records severity, runbook, mitigation or postmortem |

P2.2's quorum is `approval.required_decisions`, not a second policy field |
| P3 restart, scale, rollback, flag-flip callable | **PARTIAL** (re-baselined) | `ops.restart`/`ops.scale`/`ops.rollback` exist with `ops:write`, `effect: destructive` and a read-back (`crates/actions/src/ops/writes.rs:147,223,320`), RBAC in gitops `ops-write-rbac.yaml` (namespaced, `resourceNames: ["conveyor"]`); `ops.flag_flip` is absent (`git grep -n 'flag_flip' -- crates` → no hits); `ops_write.rs::the_write_reads_back` proves the read-back |

Reused, not rebuilt: `approval` / `approval_decision` already carry `required_decisions` with one decision per approver, the andon cord is live (`andon_state` + `ANDON_ALLOWED_KINDS`), and `crates/actions/src/process/step.rs` gates runs on it.

### Re-baseline 2026-11-19 (`main@6c46d92e`)

The 2026-11-13 rows are superseded by the measured 2026-11-19 rows. The remainder of this unit is
**P1 (incident lifecycle, runbook, postmortem, kata link), `ops.flag_flip`, P2.2's quorum test and the
named tests** — not the whole family the original table listed as ABSENT.

P1.4 is the one part that cannot be proved here: the ops write credential is
`resourceNames: ["conveyor"]` (`clusters/strato/services/conveyor/ops-write-rbac.yaml`), so a tenant
ops namespace and its namespace-scoped service account are **#8 (S14)**'s deliverable. This unit
merges P1.1–P1.3, P2 and P3. The repo's PR guard requires `Closes #78`, so the merge closes this
issue once; it is **reopened immediately** with P1.4 as the only remaining acceptance, carried by #8.

## Parts and acceptance criteria
### P1 — one injected pod failure: triaged, mitigated by an approved write, resolved, postmortemed
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.5 Charter/Inputs/Outputs and Laya decides · §9.2 Incident/Runbook/Postmortem · §12 T7 gate conjunct 1
Requirement: an alert or CI failure opens an incident card that carries severity and a runbook selection before any write, is mitigated only by an approved gated write with a read-back, then resolved with one linked postmortem that feeds a kata candidate when systemic.

- **P1.1** Given an alert opens an incident card for a failing pod, when the ops job triages it, then the card carries a severity from the configured set and a runbook selection, and no cluster write has executed.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::an_incident_is_triaged_with_no_write` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given a triaged incident, when the mitigation write executes under the tenant's approvals, then `mitigated_at` is set and the record names the approver, the tool version and the read-back proving the pod recovered.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::an_approved_mitigation_sets_mitigated_at_with_a_read_back` (to create)
- **P1.3** Given a mitigated incident, when the ops job resolves it, then `resolved_at` is set and one postmortem governed asset links the run, the evidence and — for a systemic finding — a kata candidate.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/ops_incident.rs::an_incident_resolves_with_a_linked_postmortem` (to create)
- **P1.4** (live, deployment-gated by #8 (S14, independent deployment)) Given a pod failure injected in the tenant's ops namespace, when the crash-loop runbook runs end to end, then the incident reaches mitigated and resolved and its postmortem exists.
  Verify: `crates/api/tests/ops_live.rs::an_injected_pod_failure_is_mitigated_end_to_end` (to create; needs the deployed ops connector)

### P2 — a destructive action without the tenant's configured approvals is refused
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.5 Write tools ("`ops:write`, a dry-run, the tenant's configured approvals") and Never · §9.2 Read-first · §12 T7 gate conjunct 2
Requirement: each destructive ops write is declared `destructive`, dry-run first, and refused before any cluster request unless the tenant's configured approval policy for that op class is satisfied — default human dual control.

- **P2.1** Given a tenant policy of human dual control for the op class, when a destructive action is called with no approval, then it is refused before any cluster request is made and the refusal is an audit event.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::a_destructive_action_without_approval_never_reaches_the_cluster` (to create)
- **P2.2** Given one of two required decisions, when the second is still missing, then the action stays refused; and given a tenant policy of one approval, the same call proceeds on one decision.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::the_tenant_policy_sets_the_quorum` (to create)
- **P2.3** Given a destructive action, when the caller asks for a dry-run, then a plan and its predicted read-back are returned and nothing is mutated.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::a_dry_run_returns_a_plan_and_mutates_nothing` (to create)

### P3 — restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip are callable
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.5 Write tools ("the full write set ships in v1") and their read-backs · §9.2 Read-first/Least privilege · §12 T7 gate conjunct 3
Requirement: all four write verbs exist as declared tools that the ops job can call through the broker, each returning a read-back and an audit event, and no verb exists outside the action registry's declaration.

- **P3.1** Given the ops write verbs published, when the ops job calls restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip under approval, then each executes, returns a read-back and records a `tool_call` and an audit event.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::the_four_write_verbs_are_callable_and_read_back` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a cluster verb the action registry does not declare, when a job requests it, then the call is refused and no request is made.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/ops.rs::an_undeclared_verb_is_refused` (to create)

| P2 regression reverted | PARTIAL | `git grep -n '"revert"' -- crates/domain/src/eval/climb.rs apps/server/src/benchmark_improvement.rs` → `Decision::Revert` and the `keep\|revert\|inconclusive` verdict are recorded; `git grep -ni 'revert' -- crates/store/src/procedure.rs crates/actions/src/procedure` → no hits: nothing reverts a procedure version |
| P3 self-approval refused | PARTIAL | `git grep -n 'evals:approve' -- crates/actions/src/eval/mod.rs apps/server/src/eval_runner.rs` → a sign-off is human-only and `KataExecutor` deliberately lacks `evals:approve`; `git grep -n 'job_catalogue' -- migrations crates` → no hits: no V2 adoption gate |
| P4 unmeasurable kata not opened | PARTIAL | `git grep -n 'kata.open.sop' -- seed/processes/named.yaml` → the V1 process opens on `definition_of_ready: {checks: [blocked_card_present]}` plus a replayable-flow DoD; neither names an instrument or a threshold |

The V2 job spine (`job_catalogue` / `job_release` / `job_binding`) is absent: `git grep -n 'job_catalogue' -- migrations crates` → no hits.

## Parts and acceptance criteria
### P1 — A procedure change is measured on a held-out instrument
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.3 · §9.4 — Requirement: observation, problem statement and hypothesis (with a pre-registered
prediction and instrument version) are recorded before the candidate exists, and the change is measured on the held-out split.

- **P1.1** Given a kata whose target surface is a procedure, when the hypothesis Get completes, then the prediction and instrument version are recorded before any measurement run exists.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_gets.rs::the_prediction_is_recorded_before_the_measurement` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/kata_gets.rs`)
- **P1.2** Given a measured candidate, when the measurement reads the instrument, then only the held-out split is read and the result names the split and instrument version.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_measure.rs::a_procedure_change_is_measured_on_the_held_out_split` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/kata_measure.rs`)

### P2 — A regression is reverted
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.3 · §9.3 — Requirement: a measurement that regresses past the recorded threshold reverts the
candidate to its pre-kata version with the reason recorded; a flat or incomparable result adopts nothing.

- **P2.1** Given a candidate whose held-out measurement regresses past the recorded threshold, when the measurement completes, then the target surface is back at its pre-kata version and the revert records its reason.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_revert.rs::a_measured_regression_reverts_the_candidate` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/kata_revert.rs`)
- **P2.2** Given a candidate that measures flat or is not comparable, when the measurement completes, then nothing is adopted and the target surface is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_revert.rs::a_flat_or_incomparable_result_adopts_nothing` (to create)

### P3 — Self-approval refused
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.3 · §9.3 · §15.1 D31/D45 — Requirement: adoption is a person's gate; the kata runs as its own
tenant, so it inherits none of the target tenant's autonomy and cannot approve its own adoption.

- **P3.1** Given a kata's proposed adoption, when the kata's own executor principal decides it, then the decision is refused for want of approval authority and the kata stays unadopted.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_adopt.rs::the_kata_cannot_approve_its_own_adoption` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/kata_adopt.rs`)

### P4 — An unmeasurable kata is not opened
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.3 — Requirement: opening requires a named instrument and a success threshold; without both no
kata opens (the card stays put, with a comment saying why) and a second kata for the same signature is refused.

- **P4.1** Given a candidate with no named instrument or no success threshold, when the kata is opened, then no kata exists and the refusal names what is missing.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_open.rs::a_kata_without_an_instrument_is_not_opened` (to create at `crates/actions/tests/kata_open.rs`)
- **P4.2** Given a signature that already has an open kata, when the same signature escalates again, then the second open is refused and the existing kata is named.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/kata_open.rs::a_second_kata_for_an_open_signature_is_refused` (to create)

## Goal

A development job reaches coding only through the conveyor broker, every call lands as one `tool_call` row, a destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals and a schema-invalid input are both refused before the backend is touched, and a job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed MinIO object while the prompt never carries an S3 key.

## Plan / audit source

- `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.1, §11.3, §11.4, §11.8, §11.10 · §12 row **T13 — Tool platform** (`5cf3d75:cc4a6a6`) · `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.md` rows `actions:tools`, `destination:Tools`, both `new` (`5cf3d75:72596d0`)

| Brief | T13 `project-brief` (published; the 47-brief set) |

| Benefits | enabling — no direct benefit: T14–T17 and the development/operations jobs (T6/T7) run only on this spine; it is the condition on B1–B6 |

## Claim

| Field | Value |

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |

| Decision | `docs/decisions/0005-absorption-sequence-and-repo-scope.md` §Decision 1–2 · `docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md` §"Repo scope is not tool-estate membership" | main@5cf3d75 |

| Code | `crates/actions/src/spec.rs:51` `Effect`, `:1203` `validate_input` (call site `invoke.rs:804`) · `integrations/objects.rs:161` `key_for`, `:78` `Objects::from_env` · `migrations/0002_domain.sql:231` `approval_decision`, `:253` `governed_asset` · `migrations/0013_documents.sql:27` `secret` | main@18e06aca |

| Issue | #46 | closed |

## Baseline

- Code `main@18e06aca`, measured 2026-11-18 · `seed/programme.json` T13 `meta.depends_on: ["T2","P0"]`, both closed · Docs SPEC_V2 `a8d2b66ac5b0`, ADR 0005 `88698870f1a8`, ADR 0004 `ac9a7e3843b0` · Code `external.rs 637cd723bc46`, `invoke.rs 054381df082c`, `spec.rs 364dd1573484`, `objects.rs e0dda9bbfee2`

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 coding reached only through the broker | PARTIAL | `git grep -n -e toolkit -e tool_binding -- crates/actions/src crates/api/src crates/store/src migrations` → 0 files; coding is reached today by V1 external actions (`external.rs:150`) through `invoke_external` (`invoke.rs:1030`) — no binding, no pinned version, no effect ceiling |
| P2 a `tool_call` is recorded | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'CREATE TABLE.*tool' -- migrations` → 0; every `tool_calls` hit is a model-provider payload in the eval/inference records, not a call ledger |
| P3 destructive without approvals refused | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'Effect::Destructive' -- crates` → 2 hits, both reads (`spec.rs:864` assert, `api/src/copilot/proposal.rs:58`); no action declares it. `git grep -n -e 'ops:write' -e OpsWrite -- crates` → 0; no tool gate configuration exists |
| P4 schema-invalid input refused pre-call | PARTIAL | `validate_input` runs before dispatch (`invoke.rs:804`) and enforces `$ref`/`$defs`, `allOf`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`, `type`, `enum`, `required`, `properties`, `additionalProperties:false` and `items` (`spec.rs:1203`); it does not enforce `pattern`, numeric or length bounds, and there is no `422 tool_input_invalid` |
| P5 tenant-prefixed MinIO, no S3 key in prompt | PARTIAL | `objects.rs:161` returns `t/<tenant>/<document>/<hash>` — tenant-prefixed and content-addressed, but the documents adapter only: credentials from `CONVEYOR_S3_*` env (`objects.rs:78`), `git grep -ni encrypt -- crates/actions/src/integrations/objects.rs` → 0, no project/run prefix, no job-facing storage tool |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — A development job calls coding through the broker, not `nonagenticai_mcp_server`
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.3 steps 1–2 and 5 · §11.7 · §11.8 · T13 row — Requirement: `tools.call` is the only path from a conveyor job to a job backend; it resolves the binding and pinned toolkit version first and calls the registered destination alias, and V1's job-backend external actions move onto toolkit operations instead of running beside it.
- **P1.1** Given a run whose binding pins the coding toolkit, when the step calls a coding operation, then the call goes to the registered coding destination alias at the pinned version.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given the tree, when it is swept for a second control plane, then nothing calls `nonagenticai_mcp_server` and no handler calls a service directly.
  Verify: `git grep -n nonagenticai_mcp_server -- crates apps` → 0 hits + `crates/api/tests/externals_declared.rs::no_handler_calls_a_service_directly` (exists)

### P2 — A `tool_call` is recorded
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.3 step 7 · §11.8 · T13 row — Requirement: each broker call writes exactly one `tool_call` row (run/step, tool version, input hash, status, latency, bytes, cost) and one `tool.called` event, with no credential in the row and no card transition.
- **P2.1** Given a bound job, when a call succeeds, then exactly one `tool_call` row exists for that step and pinned version, carrying the input hash and sizes and no credential — and the run's card history is unchanged.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::one_call_is_one_ledger_row` (to create)

### P3 — A destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals is refused
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.4 (destructive = approval + dry-run + dual control) · §11.3 step 2 · T13 row — Requirement: the effect class is data on the tool version, a binding ceiling narrows but never raises it, and a `destructive` call with no approval configured for that tenant is refused before the destination is called.
- **P3.1** Given a tenant with no approval configured for a destructive tool, when a job calls it, then the call is refused and the destination received no request.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a binding whose ceiling is `read`, when the step selects a `write` or `destructive` operation, then it is refused `403 tool_effect_forbidden`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_binding_ceiling_cannot_be_raised_at_run_time` (to create)
- **P3.2** Given a binding whose ceiling is `read`, when the step selects a `write` or `destructive` operation, then it is refused `403 tool_effect_forbidden`.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_binding_ceiling_cannot_be_raised_at_run_time` (to create)

### P4 — Schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.3 step 3 (`422 tool_input_invalid`, `additionalProperties: false`, enums, patterns, bounds) · T13 row — Requirement: input is validated against the tool version's closed schema, including `pattern` and numeric bounds, and a failure is a `422` with zero network calls.
- **P4.1** Given a bound tool, when the input carries an undeclared property or violates a `pattern` or a numeric bound, then it is refused `422 tool_input_invalid` and the destination's request count is zero.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call` (to create)

### P5 — A job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed MinIO object with no S3 key in the prompt
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §11.10 (D57) · §15.2 #17 · T13 row — Requirement: one storage adapter over the shared MinIO instance enforces a mandatory `tenant/<tenant_id>/` prefix with project/run prefixes beneath it, server-side encryption, a content hash and a size cap, exposes no bucket administration, and takes its credentials from a sealed broker profile so a job never sees an S3 key.
- **P5.1** Given a job in one tenant, when it writes then reads an object, then the key starts `tenant/<tenant_id>/` and the read-back hash and size match.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object` (to create)
- **P5.2** Given the same job, when its prompt is compiled, then the prompt contains no access key, secret or S3 URL.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs::the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key` (to create)

## Dependencies

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card`
- **P2.2** Given an escalated signature, when the same card blocks again inside the window, then the coach records no further remedy and the card stays blocked.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::an_escalated_signature_is_not_retried`
### P3 — no coach card about a coach card
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.2 Never ("open a coach card about a coach card") · gate conjunct 3
Requirement: a coach card, and every run it starts, is terminal for the interruption path — its own failure can never open another coach card.

- **P3.1** Given a coach card, when the coach's own run fails, then no second coach card is created and the failure is recorded on the same coach card.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::a_failed_coach_run_never_opens_a_coach_card`
- **P3.2** Given a fault that also fails the coach roll, when the handler chain settles, then the board holds one coach card and no further `err.card` job exists.
  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::the_coach_chain_settles_at_one_card`
### P4 — a systemic class opens a kata
`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §6.2 Charter/Outputs ("open a kata when the evidence says systemic") · §6.3 Inputs ("coach escalations") · gate conjunct 4
Requirement: a triage the tenant's policy classes systemic opens exactly one kata and records the kata candidate on the coach card; every other class opens none.

  Verify: `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::a_systemic_class_opens_one_kata`

| Issue | #243 | merged; released this unit |

## Baseline
- Code `main@87639c0`, measured 2026-11-17 · T1 merged (`e3d7c4e`) · the five decision tables exist from T0; the ladder behaviour does not.

## Current state (measured)
| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Schema (T0) | DONE | `migrations/0040_organisation.sql:216-360` — all five tables, FORCE RLS, the decision FKs |
| P1 — one audit shape for rule / laya / human | ABSENT | the tables exist but no `crates/store` module inserts a `decision`; the three shapes are still separate (`audit_event`, `run_step.judge`, `approval_decision`); V1's `decisions.*` actions (`crates/actions/src/governance/assets.rs:1110`) are ADR assets, not the ladder |
| P2 — tenant refinement, no code change | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'refinement' -- crates migrations` → 0 files |
| P3 — pinned refinement and laya config versions | ABSENT | `git grep -nE 'policy_version\|config_version\|refinement_version' -- crates migrations` → 0 files |
| P4 — a generated draft cannot transition a card | ABSENT | `git grep -nE 'struct (Generation\|GeneratedDraft\|DraftArtefact)' -- crates` → 0 rows; `crates/actions/src/inference/mod.rs` is a ledger read surface only |

## Parts and acceptance criteria
### P1 — one audit shape for a rule, a laya decision and a human decision
Requirement (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.1 four rungs · §7.2 "Every decision is recorded"): each of the three rungs writes an equivalent decision record, so the three are comparable without a join and only the values differ.

- **P1.1** Given one tenant with an L0 rule outcome, an L1 laya choice and an L3 human approval, when all three are recorded, then each projects the same columns (rung, policy, option-set version, answer, confidence, actor, latency) with only values differing. Verify: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs::a_rule_a_laya_and_a_human_decision_share_one_audit_shape` (to create)

### P2 — a tenant refinement changes a threshold without a code change
Requirement (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.2 per-tenant, per-case configuration; refinements are versioned and gated): a tenant's `decision_policy_refinement` overrides the threshold value, the fail action or the laya config, and takes effect through a gated policy action with no build or deploy.

- **P2.1** Given a platform policy at `min_confidence` 0.8 that refuses an 0.7 answer, when the tenant publishes a refinement at 0.5, then the identical input is accepted and no code changed. Verify: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs::a_refinement_changes_a_threshold_without_a_code_change` (to create)

### P3 — every decision pins the refinement and laya config versions
Requirement (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.2 laya inference is tenant-scoped): a decision row names the exact policy, refinement and laya config versions it used, so it reproduces after any of them is superseded.

- **P3.1** Given a decision taken under refinement v1 and laya config v1, when v2 of each is published afterwards, then the stored row still names v1/v1 and a write with any pin missing is refused. (The wire replay under the pins is the laya client's slice: slice 1 evaluates an injected confidence, so there is no upstream call to replay yet.) Verify: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs::every_decision_pins_the_refinement_and_laya_config_versions` (to create)

### P4 — a generated draft cannot transition a card
Requirement (`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §7.1 the hard rule · §7.4 a result becomes applicable only through an action with a gate): the generation result type is never accepted by a transition function, and applying a draft artefact is an action whose gate is L1/L3.

- **P4.1** Given the card transition entry point, when a generated draft type is offered where a transition input is expected, then it does not compile. Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-domain --doc` runs a `compile_fail` doctest on that entry point (to create)
- **P4.2** Given a stored draft artefact, when an action tries to apply it to a card, then the attempt is refused and the only accepted path is the gated action that leaves a decision record. Verify: `crates/actions/tests/decision_ladder.rs::a_generated_draft_cannot_transition_a_card` (to create)

## Dependencies

| blocks | #78 | §12 "T7 after T2/T4 and T13" | open |
| blocks | #76 | §12 "T13 after T2" | open |
| blocks | #85 | §12 "T16 after T2 and T13" | open |
| blocks | #88 | §12 "T12 after all" | open |

## Definition of ready
- [ ] Baseline named and doc blob shas recorded; every spec/code/test reference resolves at its ref and every `#N` resolves.
- [ ] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:` command or test target.
- [ ] Dependencies complete, typed and cited; `Blocker:` present iff `status:blocked`.
- [ ] One-PR scope, file-disjoint from other ready issues or explicitly sequenced.
- [ ] Scope corrections applied (no old-system shutdown/parity, no 348-flow retirement, no old-ledger import, no 218-item parity).

## Definition of done
- [ ] Every scenario passes at the PR head; `Evidence at completion` has one row per scenario.
- [ ] Repo gate green at the exact head (`rbuild --gate`); tests added/updated per part, none skipped.
- [ ] Docs updated; migrations numbered and `--check-lock` handled when the served spec moves.
- [ ] Every CARRIED-BY-#9 part re-checked on merged main.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #N` MERGED; issue closed; branch deleted.

## Out of scope
- The consumers author their own questions and option sets: PM routing (T3), coach remedies (T4), kata candidates (T5). Only seeded cases a test or §7.3 needs are added here.
- No prompt compiler (§7.7), budget or ledger change (§7.5) — `inference_call` is consumed as it stands; no broker, tool binding or metering roll-up (T13, T11).
- Old-system freeze/dump/shutdown, 348-flow retirement, old-ledger import, 218-item parity and old-service rollback are not part of this issue.

## Deployment prerequisite
No — schema plus library, proved locally against real Postgres.

## Open questions

| 1 | Does `decision` subsume `approval_decision`, or reference it? §7.1 keeps L3 as `approval` + `approval_decision`. | architect | keep both; `decision` carries the rung and points at the approval via `approval_id` |
| 2 | **Name collision:** the ADR family already owns `decisions.*` (`decisions.create|get|list|transition|update`, `crates/actions/src/governance/assets.rs:1110`), while §10.4 names the ladder `decisions.open|evaluate|decide|escalate`. | architect | the ladder uses **`ladder.*`** (`ladder.record|evaluate|decide|escalate`), policies use `decision_policies.*`/`refinements.*`, configs `laya_configs.*`; the T2 PR amends §10.4 and records the split |

## Goal

One project carries a baseline, a change request and a refused self-approval; WSJF recomputes from its inputs; the portfolio view lists the in-flight set; a dependency cycle is refused; and the MSP programme-definition rows exist — a benefit profile refuses an incomplete measurement record, a benefits-map edge names its five levels, and a tranche review with no evidence is refused.

## Plan / audit source

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |

| P1 baseline, change request, refused self-approval | ABSENT | `git grep -n 'project_baseline\|project_register_item' -- crates apps migrations tests` → no hits. `requested_by` is written (`crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs:342`) and never compared to `approver_id`. |
