## Goal

`https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design/` serves the SPEC_V2 studio design pack from the conveyor
app image, with `/design` redirecting there and the SPA plus every API route unchanged.

## Plan / audit source

Owner request (2026-11-12), plan
`~/.claude/plans/docs-design-studio-html-docs-design-stu-iterative-rabbit.md`. No `S##` plan
deliverable: this is the publication of the design pack itself.

## References

| Kind | Reference | Resolves at |
|---|---|---|
| Design spec | `docs/design/STUDIO-SPEC.md` | to create (this unit) |
| Design entry | `docs/design/studio.html` | to create (this unit) |
| Code | `crates/api/src/web.rs:serve` | origin/main |
| Code | `Dockerfile` (web stage) | origin/main |
| Code | `.dockerignore` | origin/main |
| Test | `crates/api/src/web.rs::tests` | origin/main (extend) |
| Issue | v1 PR #36 (archived) (SPEC V2) | open, related only |
| Issue | #6 (S12 app UI) | open, related only |

## Baseline

- Code: `origin/main` · measured 2026-11-12
- Live: `https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/` byte-identical to `origin/main:apps/web/index.html`;
  `/style.css` 200 `text/css`; `/does-not-exist.css` 404 `application/problem+json`.

## Current state (measured)

| Part | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1 land the design pack | ABSENT | `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main docs/design` → README.md, UI-SPEC.md, web-ui.html only; `studio.html` and `v2.*` are untracked in the shared checkout |
| P2 serve `/design` | ABSENT | `curl -s https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design` → 200 SPA `index.html` (549 bytes); `web.rs:serve` maps every extensionless path to the root index |
| P3 publish the pack in the image | ABSENT | `.dockerignore` excludes `docs/`; the Dockerfile web stage copies only `target/site`, `index.html`, `style.css` |
| P4 verify live | ABSENT | deployment-gated by the normal main pipeline |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — land the design pack in the repo

Requirement: the current 35-file `docs/design` pack is committed so the image build can copy it.

- **P1.1** Given the pack exists only as untracked files, when the branch is committed, then
  `docs/design/studio.html`, `v2.js`, `v2.css`, `STUDIO-SPEC.md` and the assets are tracked.
  Verify: `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD docs/design | wc -l` → 80 (the 35-file pack plus the
  System architecture page and its committed diagrams) and
  `node docs/design/scripts/check-studio.cjs` (234), `check-learning.cjs` (139),
  `check-v2.cjs` (158), `check-workbench.cjs` (119), `check-architecture.cjs` (141).

### P2 — serve `/design` from the static handler

Requirement: an extensionless path that resolves to a directory with its own `index.html` is a
static sub-site; the slashless form redirects, the slash form serves the index, everything else
keeps the SPA fallback.

- **P2.1** Given a site root containing `design/index.html`, when `GET /design`, then 308 with
  `Location: /design/` (query preserved).
  Verify: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-api --lib web::tests` (to create).
- **P2.2** Given the same root, when `GET /design/`, then 200 `text/html` with the studio body;
  `GET /design/assets/x.css` → 200 `text/css`; `GET /design/missing.css` → 404 (never SPA).
  Verify: same test target.
- **P2.3** Given the same root, when `GET /boards`, then 200 with the root `index.html`.
  Verify: same test target (no SPA regression).

### P3 — publish the pack in the image

Requirement: the web stage copies the runtime pack to `/out/site/design`, with `studio.html`
also present as `design/index.html`; scripts and Markdown are not published.

- **P3.1** Given an image built from this tree, when the container starts, then
  `/srv/site/design/index.html` and every referenced CSS/JS/font/svg exist.
  Verify: `kubectl -n conveyor exec deploy/conveyor -- ls /srv/site/design` (deployment-gated).

### P4 — live publication

Requirement: the deployed host serves the pack; the SPA and API are unchanged.

- **P4.1** Given the merged image is rolled out, when `GET https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design`,
  then 308 → `/design/`; `/design/` is 200 with `<title>Portfolio · Conveyor</title>`; every
  referenced asset is 200 with the right content type; `/design/missing.css` is 404
  `application/problem+json`.
  Verify: `curl -sI https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai/design` and the per-asset loop (deployment-gated).
- **P4.2** Given the same rollout, when loading `/design/` at 1440 and 390, then one h1, no
  console errors, no failed asset requests, no horizontal overflow.
  Verify: browser pass recorded in `Evidence at completion` (deployment-gated).

### P5 — the System architecture page

Requirement: a new `architecture` destination renders the SPEC_V2 high-level design as ArchiMate
3.2 views, the low-level design as pre-rendered Mermaid diagrams, and a UI map for every sidebar
destination. It is a design study: no backend, no write path, no runtime Mermaid.

- **P5.1** Given `#architecture`, when the page opens, then the h1/breadcrumb/sidebar are correct,
  the five tabs render, three ArchiMate views and thirteen Mermaid figures are present, and every
  sidebar destination appears in the UI map.
  Verify: `node docs/design/scripts/check-architecture.cjs` (141).
- **P5.2** Given the Dockerfile web stage, when the image is built, then
  `/srv/site/design/architecture/diagrams/*.svg` exists alongside the pack and is served with
  `image/svg+xml`.
  Verify: the extended `web::tests::a_directory_with_an_index_is_served_under_its_trailing_slash`
  plus the P3.1 `kubectl exec` listing (deployment-gated).

## Dependencies

| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |

| related | v1 PR #36 (archived) | SPEC_V2 is the content the pack depicts; no ordering | open |
| related | #6 | S12 app UI rebuild; file-disjoint from `docs/design` + the static handler | open |

## Definition of ready

- [x] Baseline named (`origin/main`, measured 2026-11-12).
- [x] Every reference resolves at its ref, or is marked to create.
- [x] Every part has ≥1 scenario with a `Verify:`.
- [x] Dependencies typed and cited; no blocker.
- [x] One-PR scope; file-disjoint from the other open units.

- [x] Docs updated (`docs/design/README.md`, `STUDIO-SPEC.md` name the published URL and the architecture page).

## Goal
Make the written delivery protocol self-consistent and self-enforcing: the three repo-local skills say what `03-DELIVERY.md` says, a report-only sweep routine exists that classifies the whole queue, and two repo-level guards refuse the two failures measured on 2026-11-11 — a commit in the shared root checkout, and a PR with no issue or `Closes` line.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — the protocol and the three skills agree
Link: `03-DELIVERY.md` § "Labels and states", § "CI budget and WIP cap", § "Issue creation"; the three skills.
- **P1.1** Given a full PR cap, when `issue-pickup` runs, then it allows the claim (branches are unlimited) and `issue-deliver` alone refuses the PR.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'unlimited' .claude/skills/issue-pickup/SKILL.md` → ≥1 line; `git grep -n 'refuse' .claude/skills/issue-deliver/SKILL.md` → the PR-cap refusal.

  Verify: `git grep -n 'Blocker: #' .claude/skills/issue-deliver/SKILL.md` → ≥1.
- **P1.3** Given a plan that spans two slices, when `issue-create` writes labels, then it applies both slice labels; it also states the docs-only classification and points at the split set (the #6/#18/#22/#23 siblings).
  Verify: `git grep -n 'two slice\|both slice' .claude/skills/issue-create/SKILL.md`; `git grep -n 'docs-only' .claude/skills/issue-create/SKILL.md`.
- **P1.4** Given v1 PR #9 (archived) is merged, when `03-DELIVERY.md` is read, then the train block is historical, the in-flight-adoption procedure is stated, and the two guards are named.

### P2 — the report-only sweep routine
- **P2.1** Given the live repo, when the sweep runs, then it prints a table classifying every open `unit` issue (ready / claimed / in review / blocked), flags ready-with-branch, claimed-without-branch, PR-without-`Closes`, open-issue-with-merged-PR, and maps every non-main head to an issue — changing nothing.
  Verify: run the commands in `.claude/skills/issue-sweep/SKILL.md`; output pasted in the PR; `gh issue list --json number,labels` identical before/after.
- **P2.2** Given a drift row, when read, then the skill names the owning session's action and forbids the sweep from flipping labels.
  Verify: `git grep -n 'report-only' .claude/skills/issue-sweep/SKILL.md`; `git grep -n 'never.*label\|does not.*label' .claude/skills/issue-sweep/SKILL.md`.

### P3 — the two guards
- **P3.1** Given the shared root checkout, when `git commit` runs there, then it is denied with the exact worktree command; in `.worktrees/issue-<n>` it is allowed.
  Verify: `python3 .claude/hooks/tests/test-guards.py` → exit 0, cases `root-commit-deny`, `worktree-commit-allow`.
- **P3.2** Given `gh pr create`, when the head is not `issue/<n>-*` or the body has no `Closes #<n>` (`Fixes`/`Resolves` accepted), then denied; the positive case is allowed.
  Verify: same test file, cases `pr-nonissue-deny`, `pr-no-closes-deny`, `pr-ok-allow`.
- **P3.3** Given an unparseable command, when a guard sees it, then it allows (fails open), so a parse gap can never block every session.
  Verify: same test file, case `unparseable-allow`.
- **P3.4** Given the two scripts, when the settings file is read, then each is registered as a `PreToolUse` Bash hook and the file is valid JSON.
  Verify: `python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('.claude/settings.json'));print(len(d['hooks']['PreToolUse'][0]['hooks']))"` → 2.

If a live deny is ever observed not to fire, the protocol text remains authoritative and the fix is the registration, not the rule. |

| P2 decision | **READY — design chosen** | the post-merge run is still ≥20 min (25.5–28.2 min); skip checks on a tree-equality hit but never on a push to main; fail open |
| P3 implementation | **ABSENT until this unit** | #17's public-mirror truth landed; the change is in `ci-public.yml` |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — measure the remaining duplication
Given #19 and #20 are merged, when three changes land (docs-only, small code, dependency-touching), then each PR run's and merge run's wall clock and test-step duration are recorded.
Verify: `gh run view <id> --json jobs` for six runs, tabulated here. **DONE 2026-11-23** (25.5–28.2 min post-merge).

### P2 — decide from the numbers
Given the P1 table, when the merge run is still ≥ 20 minutes, then this issue moves to `status:ready` with the chosen design; otherwise it closes as "no longer worth the risk" with the table as the evidence.
Verify: this issue's state and the table. **P2 says go.**

### P3 — implementation
Given a merged tree identical to an already-tested PR head, when the **merge-group** run runs, then the code gates may be skipped while the required `checks` context reports success — and a **push to main** still runs the full suite and builds/publishes the image (the deploy is never suppressed).
The tree-equality check fails open: any doubt about the PR head's tree or its check results runs the full suite.

- **P3.1** Given a queue entry whose tree equals the PR head's and whose five required checks are green, when `classify` runs, then `checks_skip=true`; `checks-shard` is `skipped`; `checks` is `success`; the queue merges.
  Verify: the #22 PR's own merge-group run — `gh run view <id> --json jobs,event` shows `checks-shard` skipped and `checks` success.
- **P3.2** Given the same merge, when the push-to-main run runs, then the image is built and published from the merged tree (the skip never reaches a push).
  Verify: the push run's `image` job conclusion `success` and the published `sha-<merge>` tag.
- **P3.3** Given any doubt (no PR number, an unreadable PR head, a tree difference, a required check not green), when `classify` runs, then `checks_skip=false` and the full suite runs.
  Verify: the step's fail-open branches; the first queue entry after a main advance runs the shards.

## Dependencies
| Relation | Issue | Why (source) | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| blocked-by | #17 | the CI/ARC rebuild must settle the caller and pool shape before a workflow change lands | **closed** (PR #676) |
| acceptance-blocked-by | #19, #20 | the measurement is only meaningful after the cost levers land | closed |

Blocker: none — #17 is closed; the amendment records that the public repo's `ci-public.yml` is the canonical workflow, and this change lands there.

## Definition of ready
- [x] P1 table complete (nine runs across three changes) — measured 2026-11-23; P2's threshold is met.
- [x] Design chosen and written here (the classify `checks_skip` output, fail open, push never skips).
- [x] `deploy` preservation stated as a scenario with a verify (P3.2).

## Definition of done
- [ ] The decision is recorded (implemented) with the measurement.
- [ ] No change lands that can skip the deploy: a push to main always runs the suite and never skips the image.
- [ ] One PR `Closes #22` merged; the queue entry and the push run are the evidence.

## Out of scope
- Changing the deploy, dispatch-truth or deploy-gate jobs.
- Any private-archetype change (the public repo cannot consume it; #17 records the constraint).

## Deployment prerequisite
No — the skip is confined to the `merge_group` event; a push to main is untouched.

## Open questions
| # | Question | Owner | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Does a squash-merge tree always equal the PR head tree? | this issue | compute it, never assume — if GitHub's merge produces a different tree, equality fails and the full suite runs (fail open) |

## Evidence at completion
| Scenario | Command / run | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | `gh run view <id> --json jobs` for the nine runs | 25.5–28.2 min post-merge; the queue adds a third full run | 2026-11-23 |

The skip path is exercised by the next quiet queue entry and is tracked on the #565 PR. | 3eda60b2 |
| P3.2 | the push run at the merge tree | `ci` runs on push; the tree step is `merge_group`-only, so no skip exists there. | 3eda60b2 |
| P3.3 | `classify` log of run 45472634253 | `trees differ (f0b8611a… vs abf315e3…); running the full suite` → shards success, `checks` success. | 3eda60b2 |

## Goal
Land the durable CI configuration this **public** repository can actually run: `ci-public.yml` as the canonical public mirror of the private archetype's gates, a full run that produces a verdict inside its declared timeout, and the run time and queue wait recorded on every run rather than inferred.

## Plan / audit source
The 2026-11-11 CI time audit (the lever table cited here); `docs/plans/03-DELIVERY.md` § "CI budget and WIP cap"; the public-repo constraint recorded at the top of `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml`.

## Amendment — 2026-11-24 (adoption)

The claim was abandoned (last comment 2026-11-15T10:06:55Z, no branch, no PR; the 2026-11-15 slice merged as #134). This session adopted it under the 48 h rule and measured the premise:

- This repository is **public**; `gitops-production` (the archetype) is **private**. A public repository may only call public reusable workflows (GitHub's own rule), so `uses: [private-repo]/.github/workflows/rust-service.yml@main` cannot resolve. The `ci.yml` caller that P1/P2 described does not exist at `origin/main` and cannot exist while the repo is public.
- `ci-public.yml` is therefore the canonical public mirror: its header (lines 1–20) records the constraint, and its check job is copied step-for-step from the archetype's `rust-library` gates.
- P1/P2 are amended to verify the mirror rather than a caller that cannot exist. P3/P4 are unchanged and delivered in this repo.

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — tenant recipe authoring
Requirement: a tenant admin can create, version, activate and retire a recipe through `prompt_recipes.create|list|get|activate|retire` with `prompts:read|write`; every mutation is audited by the existing `action_invocation` row; one active version per `(tenant, key)` holds; a new run may not pin a non-active version.

- **P1.1** Given a tenant admin, when they create and activate a recipe version, then the action exists with its scope, the audit row is written, and exactly one version is active.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test prompt_recipes` (to create)
- **P1.2** Given a non-active (draft or retired) version, when a new run tries to pin it, then it refuses with the existing typed error.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test prompt_catalogue` (exists; extend) + `crates/actions/src/prompt/mod.rs::resolve`
- **P1.3** Given two activations racing, when both commit, then one wins and the other refuses (the unique active index).
  Verify: `prompt_recipes` (race case)

### P2 — memory selection into the compiled prompt
Requirement: the compiler selects the card's memory from the recipe's `selector`, renders `prompt.memory` (hot rows first, one digest only if room remains), and the same recipe + facts hash identically.

- **P2.1** Given a card with memory records, when the prompt compiles, then `prompt.memory` carries the selected records and `PromptFacts` records the selection identity.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-domain --test prompt_memory` (created) + `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test memory the_prompt_selection` (created)
- **P2.2** Given no selectable memory, when it compiles, then the section is absent and compilation still succeeds (unless the recipe marks it required).
  Verify: same target
- **P2.3** Given two runs with the same recipe and the same selected facts, when they compile, then the bytes and the hash are identical.
  Verify: same target (byte/hash case)

## Goal
Prove the job lease is safe for long agent work under two workers — a handler that outlives `JOB_LEASE_SECS` runs exactly once, a killed worker's work is reclaimed, and a stale token writes nothing — and change the policy only if the proof fails.

## Plan / audit source

| P2 two-worker long-handler proof | **ABSENT** | no test runs two live workers against a handler that exceeds the lease without a kill |
| P3 kill/restart proof | **DONE** | `apps/server/tests/jobs_kill.rs`: SIGKILL mid-handler, reclaim on lease expiry, stale token writes nothing |
| P4 policy change | **CONTINGENT** | required only if P2 fails |

## Parts and acceptance criteria

### P1 — renewal and fencing (carried by the merged train)
Requirement: a worker that still owns the job keeps extending its lease; a worker that lost it cannot, and its finish writes nothing.
- **P1.1** Given a handler outliving `JOB_LEASE_SECS`, when the renewal loop runs, then `store::jobs::renew` extends only with the same `lease_token`.
  Verify: `apps/server/src/worker.rs::spawn_renewal` + `crates/store/src/jobs.rs::renew` (code present on main; covered by P2.1).

### P2 — the two-worker proof (the remaining work)
Requirement: a legitimate handler beyond the lease completes exactly once while a second worker polls the same tenant.
- **P2.1** Given `JOB_LEASE_SECS=2` and a handler that runs longer than the lease, when two worker processes poll the same tenant, then the handler runs once — its call counter is 1 and the second worker never claims the row.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_lease_two_workers` (to create at `apps/server/tests/jobs_lease_two_workers.rs`)
- **P2.2** Given the same run, when the first worker finishes, then the row is `succeeded` with `attempts = 1` and no further renewals occur.
  Verify: same test, asserted after the handler returns.
- **P2.3** Given the second worker polls while the lease is alive, when it claims, then it gets nothing (the `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claim returns no row).
  Verify: same test, asserting the second worker's claim count is 0.

### P3 — kill/restart (already proved; keep green)
- **P3.1** Given SIGKILL mid-handler, when the lease expires, then the restarted worker reclaims (`attempts = 2`) and the stale token changes 0 rows.
  Verify: `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_kill`

Closes #865

## What

The live unit-ledger findings run. The collector stops overstating the delivery ("54 in flight" was 23 open plus 31 closed; "56 failures" triple-counted orphan PRs and applied a unit-only DoR rule to eight non-unit issues), classifies every defect the kernel certifies, and the issue checker now enforces the same per-part `Verify:` rule the model certifies. The evidence run and its certificates are committed under `docs/evidence/units/2026-11-27-findings/`.

## Why

#865: use the prover functionality to find the issues and unfinished work that should be improved. The 11:00 evaluation (`docs/evidence/units/2026-11-27/`) named 56 failures; reading its facts showed four instrument defects and a much sharper finding set.

### The instrument's own defects (fixed here)

Closes #837

## What

A delivery unit's certificate is now derived by the engine from its own rows, and the unit's
Definition of done refuses to close without one when the charter requires it.

- `UnitRecordFacts` + `checkRecord` beside #836's GitHub-observed `checkUnit`; every field is an
  `Option` that fails closed.
- `proofs.attest` derives the facts from `development_project`, `development_step`, the three gate
  decisions and the `proof_policy`, renders the source, and writes nothing.
- `proofs.record` for `subject_type: unit` re-derives the facts and refuses a caller's substitute
  (`422 proof_facts_not_derived`), including a consistently forged report rendered by the engine's
  own renderer and checked by the prover.
- `development_projects.close` resolves the certificate through the factored `lean_proof` arm:
  advisory reports the outcome in the closure and proceeds; required refuses with
  `422 gate_evidence_missing`.
- Migration 0081 adds the `unit` proof subject and `proof_policy`. The specification pin is frozen
  at charter; the implementer may tighten `required` but never loosen it, and the pin is never
  rewritten.

| P1.1 / P1.2 / P1.3 — derive without writing, deterministic, unchartered and no-issue-ref refusals | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test proofs_attest` | 9 passed |
| P2 — record re-derives; caller facts and recomputed tamper refused | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test proofs_record` | 18 passed |

The live primary is at migration **79** and has no `proof_policy` (measured 2026-11-27T16:28Z);

Closes #842

## What this delivers

Any signed-in tenant member can report a bug or request a feature from `/feedback` in the app; the
tenant sees its own submissions with the operator's status; the platform operator reads every
tenant's feedback with `conveyor admin feedback list` and triages it.

- **P1** `6276f033` — migration 0079 (`feedback`, FORCE RLS, the kind/status/shape CHECKs), the
  store (`insert/get/list/triage` + the all-tenant read), and the store tests.
- **P2** `bab4d6ee` — `feedback.create`/`.list`, the `feedback:read|write` scopes (read open to
  every role, write member+), the registry pin (600 actions), `actions.json` and the served-spec
  lock (631 operations), and the action tests.
- **P4** `0bf92919` — `conveyor admin feedback list|triage` over the platform pool, one scoped
  transaction per tenant (the `seed_programme(pool, None)` shape), with the author email resolved.
- **P3** `a7a0bc39` — the `/feedback` route and screen, linked from the Operations rail; the form
  captures the route; the tenant's list; the signed-out gate.

## Why not a platform action or a GitHub bridge (measured)

`Tenancy::Platform` is parsed (`resolve.rs:199`) but no action declares it, and the agent surface
refuses it for a tenant-bound caller (`agent_surface.rs:82`); `principal.rs` has no platform role —
the global `platform_admin` grant gates the CLI and the super-admin routes. The GitHub token is a
per-tenant sealed secret opened only inside a tenant's publish job (`publish.rs:8`). So the
operator's cross-tenant read is the admin CLI over the platform pool, which keeps RLS on and
crosses no tenant boundary in a query.

## Evidence at this head (`a7a0bc39e`)

The seven role playbooks that still performed their live act through `scripts/programme-record.py` now act through the conveyor's own action route with the session bearer:

- **pmo-lead** — `changes.request`, `cards.get/list`, `tranches.*`, `approvals.list`; live act `changes.request` → `approvals.list` + `tranches.review_list`.

- **solution-architect** — `architecture.artifacts_*`, `contracts_request/get`, `phases_advance`; live act `contracts_request` → `contracts_get`. The approval actions stay a distinct approver's and are never listed.
- **standards-author** — `documents.compose/publish/get`; live act `documents.compose` → `documents.get`.

Every playbook declares `allowed-actions` in its frontmatter. `crates/actions/tests/skill_allowlists.rs` grows `ROLE_PLAYBOOKS` 8 → 15 and adds `no_role_playbook_names_the_python_record_tool`, so the Python act cannot return by prose.

| Gate | Command | Result |

Closes #836

## What

Two halves, one unit:

- **The model and the renderer (A1).** `UnitObs` gains the two body-observable facts (the linked
  PR's `Closes #N`, the issue's `Verify:` per part); `checkUnit` and `ruleResults` make each rule's
  outcome kernel-provable, not just the aggregate. `render.rs` gains the `unit_ledger` arm: sorted
  by key, duplicate keys and more than 200 units refused, and a failing ledger deliberately renders
  so the kernel can refuse it. Migration 0079 adds the `unit_ledger` subject; the separate controls
  file holds eleven negatives.
- **The collector and the evaluation (A2).** `proofs.render` is the renderer's public face, so a
  non-Rust collector obtains the exact source `proofs.record` requires instead of re-implementing
  the renderer. `scripts/proof/collect_units.py` (self-test in the `checks` job) fetches a hashed
  snapshot, pairs the window's deliveries, writes facts with per-unit provenance, and certifies
  chunks of 200 through `proofs.render` → `lean4.check` → `proofs.record`, then a programme bundle.

## Evidence

- Kernel, in the prover pod: the model exits 0; the corpus at 40/80/200 units exits 0 at
  14 554 / 22 094 / 44 714 bytes (wall 4.7 / 4.7 / 5.9 s including exec); 11/11 controls are
  kernel-refused; `String.startsWith` is not `decide`-reducible, so prefix facts are derived,
  never Lean computation.
- Rust: `proof_render` 17/17 (golden literal, determinism, duplicate key, >200, failing ledger);
  `proofs_record` 15/15 including `unit_subject_kind` and
  `proofs_render_is_the_source_record_requires`; `registry` 15/15; the parity action sweep 1/1;
  `mcp_meta` 1/1; `--print-openapi --check-lock` OK; `build-coverage.py --check` current;
  `actions.json` 599.
- Offline evaluation (snapshot committed): **320 completed units, 54 in flight, 12 orphan merged
  PRs, 128 automation excluded**. **56 of 320 fail the model**: `verifyParts` 50, `mergeComplete`
  15, `closesKeyword` 12 (the orphans), `onePull` 5, `oneBranch` 4, `ciBudget` 0. Two renders of
  the snapshot produce the same corpus hash and byte-identical facts. Cross-check against
  `scripts/ci/board.py`: 9 units pass the checker and fail the model (the checker accepts one
  `Verify:` in the exact section; the model requires one per part), 6 the reverse, 293 agree —
  both answers recorded.
- The evidence section, the run directory and the report are in
  `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` § A2 and `docs/evidence/units/2026-11-27/`.

### Evidence at completion

| Scenario | Artefact | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `scripts/lean/check-model.sh corpus --sizes 40,80,200` | 40/80/200 exit 0 at 14 554 / 22 094 / 44 714 B |
| P1.2 | the recorded table + chunk count | 320 units → 2 chunks (200 + 120); 200-unit source measured |
| P2.1 | positive corpus + `positive_control` | `checkUnit goodUnit = true` elaborates |
| P2.2 | `UnitModel.controls.lean` | 11/11 refused (two branches, two PRs, draft, three CI, issue pending, branch live, unknown branches, no `Closes`, missing `Verify:`, empty ledger, falsified `ruleResults`) |
| P2.3 | model source + universal theorems | no Mathlib / `native_decide`; the model exits 0 |
| P2.4 | `proofs_record::unit_subject_kind` | 201, subject `unit_ledger`, on a fresh PostgreSQL 18 (migration 0079 applied) |
| P3.1 | collector self-test + two renders | same corpus hash and byte-identical facts; per-unit provenance |
| P3.2 | `proofs_record::proofs_render_is_the_source_record_requires` + `unit_subject_kind` | the engine path is proven against the stub; **live 201 + reverify deployment-gated** |
| P3.3 | `units.json` + `report.md` | 56/320 fail; per-rule totals; corpus hash; **kernel verdict over the real chunks deployment-gated** |
| P3.4 | the `Verify:` cross-check | 9 checker-pass/model-fail, 6 reverse, 293 agree — both answers recorded |

## Deployment gate

One scenario is post-rollout: the live certificates. `proofs.render` does not exist until this PR
deploys. After the rollout: grant the tenant's `mcp` channel exactly `lean4.check`,
`proofs.render`, `proofs.record`, `proofs.reverify`, `proofs.get` and `proofs.list` (merging the
live `channels.policy_get` overrides, never stomping them), run `collect-units.sh certify`, and
record the response bodies — the chunk certificates with their verdicts, a `proofs.reverify`, and
the programme bundle — in the evidence doc and on #836. Until then the evaluation above is the
collector's facts and local mirror, not a kernel verdict over the real chunks.

## Resume

`scripts/proof/collect-units.sh --self-test`, then `fetch`, `render`, `certify`, `report`. The
snapshot is committed, so `render` is offline and deterministic; `certify` reads
`~/.conveyor/nonagentic.token` and the deployed engine.

## Risks

- The evaluation will embarrass: the findings are real, named by unit and rule, and attributed to
  no person.
- `verifyParts` is stricter than the CI checker by design; the disagreements are recorded with
  both answers rather than reconciled silently.
- The grant widens the tenant's machine channel by six actions; it is the A0 `403` fix, merged
  with the live overrides and reversible with `channels.policy_reset`.
- Facts are a snapshot; the kernel certifies facts ⇒ verdict, never GitHub reality.

Closes #847

## What

C0 — G0 conformance. Two things the delivered baseline got wrong, fixed:

1. **The record now tells the live truth.** The four inception records are reconciled to G0's live
   close-out by read-back, not by re-dating: the register's ten typed rows are `approved` with their
   live ids (seven v2 rows, three current v3 rows, three superseded originals recorded as history),
   and the contract table names the live Phase-A SoAW v2 and the live Phase-F delivery contract with
   their distinct approver and gates. The governance record closes W2a/W2b/W2c, I-WALK-1/2/3 and
   D-WALK-1/6, records the G0 evidence rows (live host matrix, deployed sign-in, the deployed digest and the
   engine defect fixed in the merged follow-up), and ties the benefit to the live B8 profile. The SoAW records its live contract; the epic
   records PI-4 delivered and the real issue numbers.
2. **The instrument can see the action sheet, and CI proves the specs ran.**
   `modules_present()` tested guessed file paths (`src/api/manifest.js`, …) while the delivered
   client provides the same capabilities in `client.js`, `shell.js`, `schema.js` — so the instrument
   reported all 598 actions `absent`. It now detects the capability in the ship-able seam sources
   only (not a destination caller, not a `*.test.js`; a rename is no longer a false negative),
   pinned by self-test fixtures. The walk job now feeds its Playwright JSON report to
   `build-walk-coverage.py --check --require-verified --report`, so a registered route whose spec
   did not run and pass fails the job; the coverage record is regenerated by the instrument.

No `apps/walk` code, no Rust, no seed, no runtime change. No image deploy is needed.

## Why

The four build wings (#814–#817) start from this baseline. A record that still said the delivery
contract was "to create in G0", and an instrument that could not see the delivered action sheet,
would have made every later parity claim contestable — and the P6 gate unpassable. The plan's
Decision 1 (conformance first), Decision 2 (correct the instrument, not the product) and Decision 3
(read-back, never re-date) are recorded on #847.

## Evidence (at head `7312c13571dae9c77d062016acb8010968a2124f`)

Live read-backs through the deployed engine (`conveyor admin action invoke`, tenant `nonagentic`):

|---|---|

| `registers.list` | CR-WALK-001 `01a21bf7-d0a1…` approved; `01a21bf8-ca68…` (the PM change-gate gap) open |
| `documents.list` | six published documents, all `active`, with versions and ids |
| `benefits.get` | B8 `01a21af9-cfcd-73ab-8eff-39cab33f7525`, baseline `value: null` — unmeasured, never zero |

Local gates at the exact head (all exit 0): `build-docs --check`, `check-docs` (12/12),
`check-outputs` (+self-test), `check-data`, `check-delivery`, `check-standards` (+self-test),
`check-coverage --self-test`, `check-output-standard` (+self-test), `generate-standards --check`,
`publish-standards --check`, `build_docs_preserve`, `walk_coverage.sh`, `no-private-refs` (5367
files), `audit-programme-conformance`, and the walk's own `node --test` and `tsc --noEmit`.

Instrument summary after the change: `routes 52 (absent 49, registered 3); actions 598 (absent 0,
schema-rendered 598); gaps 0`. The report contract proven locally in both shapes and in CI:
with the report the check exits 0 (`verified 3`); without it, exit 1 naming each registered route
"not verified by this run's report".

Walk workflow: run [46007743517](https://github.com/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs/46007743517)
at this head — census green, walk green, instrument step
`routes 52 (absent 49, registered 0, verified 3); actions 598 (schema-rendered 598); gaps 0`.
Earlier dispatches were superseded by branch pushes and cancelled by the workflow's own concurrency
group; run 46006399854 failed *inside the new step* because Playwright 1.65.0 writes report paths
relative to `testDir` (`shell/entrance.spec.ts`), which the first normaliser did not map — the
failure is the step doing its job, and `7312c1357` fixes it with a measured, self-test-pinned

## Resume

`6db14bd70` record, `70ef25418` instrument + report step, `b68c10c0b`/`65144b9cc` register list and

Closes #832

## What

The broker now enforces the run's declared spend budget **before** dispatch, and the tool ledger
carries the cost it actually incurred:

- a `spend`-class call with no declared budget, or with the budget exhausted, is refused
  `429 tool_budget_exceeded` with zero upstream calls (`v1-w4a-1`);
- every dispatched call's cost is derived from the handler's `inference_call` rows at the same
  read-time formula every report uses, and written to `tool_call.cost`;
- a `captures_usage` action reached directly (workflow node, process step, agent loop) is gated at
  the invoke boundary, so a run cannot bypass the ceiling by not going through `tools.call`;
- an `internal_agent` binding with no declared ceiling refuses run start `422 budget_missing`
  (`v1-p75-1`).

The ceiling resolves from the job release's `anatomy.limits.cost_budget_usd`, the binding's
`meta.limits` override, and a lower `run.inputs.limits`.

## Why

`v1-w4a-1:T13` is the last open P0 on a tranche-3 member, and `v1-p75-1:T11` is the same mechanism.
The owner's 2026-11-27 directive is that no tranche is reviewed until it is fully complete.

## Source

Ported from the #526 lane (`8f1e57706`, the P0 wave) — the lane's 44-file commit is not
cherry-pickable, so this takes the spend-budget pieces only: `run_budget_tx`,
`binding_budget_tx`, `cost_of_invocation_tx`, the broker's check and cost write, the invoke
boundary gate, the run-start gate, and the lane's 14-test `tool_budget.rs`. Main already carried
the schema (`tool_call.cost`, `commercial_price.unit`, `inference_call.usage_unit`,
`run.job_binding_id`) and `Effect::Spend`/`InvokeOutcome::invocation_id`, so there is no migration.
The lane's `credential_alias` fixture field is removed: it belongs to `v1-w4a-4`, out of scope.

## Evidence

- `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test tool_budget` → **14 passed, 0 failed** at the
  final head (`3511c056d`). The suite proves: refusal before the stub backend's counter moves; a
  priced call's derived cost in `tool_call.cost`; the three budget sources and their precedence;
  an internal-agent run start refused without a ceiling; reads and unbudgeted legacy runs not
  gated by the spend rule.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked`, `git diff --check` clean.

The other T13 P1s (`v1-w4a-3/4/5/6`, `v1-p111-*`), the tranche-3 review, and any pricing-seed
change.

Closes #831

## What

The six tranche-4 code findings are fixed, each with a test and a `resolved_by` receipt in the v1
ledger; the two live review items are handled by the book (P6 published; P5's re-review runs after
this fix deploys — no waiver).

| Finding | Fix | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| `v1-w2b-2:T10` | `project_tranche_state_tx` distinguishes a standalone project from a programme-bound project with no tranche row; the start gate refuses the latter (409 `tranche_not_authorised`) | `tranche_review::a_programme_project_with_no_tranche_row_cannot_start` |
| `v1-p82-1:T10` | `materialise_pi_tx` requires an approved approval on the cadence's target (`cadence/<id>/materialise`); the unattended tick creates nothing and leaves the cadence `planned` | `programme_cadence::an_unapproved_pi_plan_does_not_materialise` |
| `v1-p6-1:T4` | `coach.remedy` applies the bounded effect in its own transaction (block/move/retry/repull; ask is the gate); `process_runs.start` enforces a block or a pending ask (409 `coach_blocked` / `coach_ask_pending`). The systemic kata starts before the block, since it is the coach's escalation, not the card's dispatch | `coach::{a_block_remedy_stops_the_next_dispatch, a_retry_remedy_lets_the_next_dispatch_run, a_move_remedy_places_the_card}` |
| `v1-p81-1:T9` | the phase gate reads an **adopted** profile only; a phase the profile does not name falls back to the standard's mandatory `artifact_type` rows, never an empty satisfied set | `architecture_gates::a_phase_closes_on_the_adopted_profile_or_the_standard` |
| `v1-p81-2:T9` | closing Phase G requires a live delivery contract, its compliance review, and an active waiver when the review is non-conformant or irrelevant — for every track, at the design gate | `architecture_gates::phase_g_needs_the_contract_the_review_and_a_waiver` |
| `v1-p81-3:T9` | an adopted profile is immutable; adoption cites an approved architecture-board decision whose subject is that profile | `architecture_gates::an_adopted_profile_is_immutable_and_adoption_needs_its_decision` |

Blast-radius fixes ride the same branch, each found by the suite and verified locally:
`projects.create` starts the root run in its own transaction, so the P1 gate firing there leaves a
valid project, board and start card without a run (the same non-fatal state as an unready
capability, never a failed create); the parity and api ADM tests adopt their tailored profile on a
real board decision and state explicitly empty tailored sets where the profile carries no
artefacts (an absent key falls back to the standard — the finding's point); and the H test closes
G through the universal Phase-G gate with a live delivery contract and its compliant review.

The ledger commit repairs the 41 citations this unit's source edits moved and re-cites the six
changed-code quotes to the current guard lines; `verify-findings` reports no failure in these six
findings. Main's 35 pre-existing citation drifts (16 SPEC_V2, 12 coverage.json, 2 ingest.rs, 2 app.rs,
3 receipt commits lost to an earlier squash merge) are untouched.

## Live halves

- **P6 — published.** `documents.compose` published the T14 closure review live:
  `01a21ca3-bfd4-739f-828d-4972d2b801ea`, category `closure-review`, unit T14, project T14,
  `published_at 2026-11-27T10:53:43Z`; read back via `documents.get`. It is written from the live
  record and records the `scientific_processor` clause as **open item 1 with an owner**, not a waiver.
  The audit's `closed_without_closure_review:T14` clearance waits on #526's live snapshot refresh.
- **P5 — no waiver (owner ruling 2026-11-27).** The live T4 review is immutable (one review per
  contract), so the fix is the work itself (P3/P4) plus, after this merge deploys: a new delivery-
  contract version for T4, its board approval, a **conformant** review against it citing this unit's
  tests and the deployed behaviour, and the old contract superseded. Recorded on #831; it cannot run
  before the fix is serving.

## Evidence

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test tranche_review --test programme_cadence --test architecture_gates` | 10 + 4 + 3 passed |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test coach` | 17 passed |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test cadence_jobs` | 1 passed (its fixture now approves the PI plan, as the P2 gate requires) |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test programme_close` | 16 passed (create leaves the card without a run until the tranche is authorised) |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test parity_http_mcp` | 9 passed (the phases_advance sample adopts its profile) |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test write_path --test process_start` | 14 + 22 passed |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test organisation_loop` | 17 passed (its ADM path already adopts) |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test togaf_architecture_phases --test togaf_h_change` | 7 + 8 passed (adopted profiles; G closed through the Phase-G gate) |
| `cargo test -p conveyor-api --test architecture_compliance --test architecture_capability --test architecture_artifacts --test togaf_delivery_design_gate` | 8 + 11 + 6 + 8 passed |
| `python3 scripts/verify-findings.py docs/evidence/v1-conformance-findings.json` | the six findings verify; main's 35 pre-existing drifts remain (unchanged) |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked`, `git diff --check` | clean |
| `build-coverage --check`, `build-programme-seed --check`, `check-programme-definition`, `check-data.cjs` | green |
| `preflight` | green (clippy `--all-targets -D warnings`) |

The full nextest suite, the design-pack job and the image are the PR's CI verdict.

## Risks

- P5's live re-review is post-deploy by construction; the issue's live-audit row stays open until

## What

The walk's canvas now mounts the wasm ECS engine (`data-engine="ecs"`) instead of silently rendering the labelled fallback everywhere.

`WorldConfig` (`crates/walk-world/src/resource.rs`) deserializes with a **required** `seed`; `new_json` parses the config before overwriting `config.seed` from the constructor argument. The app's `World.config()` omitted the field, so `new WasmWalkWorld(...)` threw `missing field 'seed'`; `startEngine` caught it and fell back. No local or CI spec noticed because `world.spec.ts` accepted `/ecs|fallback/`. The strict deployed spec (`e2e/deployed/game.spec.ts`) found it on the live host during #835's acceptance.

Fix: one module `SEED`, carried in the config (the constructor argument stays authoritative — `BigInt(SEED)`), a unit test pinning the payload, and the browser spec now demands `ecs`.

## Evidence at the head (`e51be550c`)

| Part | Scenario | Command / test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | the engine config carries the seed and the census rows | `apps/walk/src/world/index.test.js::the engine config carries the seed and the census rows` | pass (24/24 unit tests) |
| P2.1 | the suite demands the engine | `npx playwright test e2e/world` against the real server | **2/2 pass**, `data-engine="ecs"` strictly |
| P2.1 | no regression elsewhere | full local suite, `PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=chromium DEV_AUTH_TOKEN=dev:alice` | **12/12 pass** |
| — | types | `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` | pass |
| P3.1 | live | deployed OIDC spec after this PR's image deploys | **post-merge**, deployment-gated |

The isolation is measured, not assumed: the old app on the live host with a fresh session reached `fallback` (deployed run 2026-11-27); the new app with a fresh local seed reaches `ecs` locally.

## Notes

- The fallback stays for environments where wasm is genuinely blocked; the catch is unchanged.
- A local trap met during validation: the dev seed's licence `last_confirmed` is 60-minute TTL, so a server left running >60 min answers `403 licence_required` and the world never mounts. CI seeds fresh per run; this PR does not change that.

Closes #839

## What

G0 delivers the Gemba Walk as a working client at **`https://game.nonagentic.ai/`** — its own host, its own public Keycloak client `conveyor-game`, and the same image and service as the operator app. CR-WALK-001 / ADR 0024 record the change; the live governance chain is below.

**Serving and identity (W2a)**

- `crates/auth`: `CONVEYOR_GAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` is an explicit optional second first-party client; the verifier's `azp` check is a membership test over exactly `{conveyor-web, conveyor-game}`. The configured audience stays `conveyor`; the game id is never defaulted from it.
- `crates/api/config`: `CONVEYOR_GAME_HOSTS` (normalised, port-stripped) and `CONVEYOR_GAME_PUBLIC_URL`; `validate_auth` fails closed unless the host and client id are set as a pair.
- `crates/api/lib`: a router-level `game_host_gate` **outside** the routes — axum routes pre-empt the fallback, so this is the only place that can refuse `/mcp` (a real route) and the live design window on the game host.
- `crates/api/web`: per-host `/config.json` (the game client id on the game host), the walk tree at the game host's root, the operator origin's `/walk/*` 308 to configuration (never the request `Host`), and the legacy game-host `/walk` redirect. The no-host dev/CI sub-site remains.
- `crates/api/tests/web_hosts.rs`: the contract through `app()` against a real server — `/mcp` 404 on the game host, per-host client ids, the operator `/mcp` untouched, the 308 with its query, and a hostile `Host` that cannot move the redirect.

**The client (W2b)** — a plain-ESM SPA: config → PKCE S256 (token in memory, dev cookie) → manifest → router/shell → world. The shell owns the HUD, room map, palette, DOM sheets and toasts; the canvas is decorative and every capability has a DOM path. Portfolio is the G0 exemplar: `programmes.list` through the action contract, a create sheet with `Idempotency-Key`, an update sheet with `If-Match`, a refetch after every write, and the server's refusal verbatim. The world loads `crates/walk-world`'s wasm (FrameView, picking, keyboard movement, camera toggle) and falls back to labelled room panels without it.

**Build and CI (W2c)** — `dev-server.mjs` serves the tree at the root on 8932 and proxies the API with `Host: game.nonagentic.ai`; the Dockerfile builds the pinned wasm and copies the tree to `/srv/site/walk`; `walk.yml` runs the instrument, `node --test`, `tsc`, the walk-world tests, the wasm build and the Playwright suite against the real server.

## Independent merge gate and its fixes

`aa-pr-auditor` returned **NO** at `4ae03bafc`: the azp allowlist, the `validate_auth` host/client pair and the canvas pointer→sheet dispatch were implemented but untested (deleting the game client's membership would 401 the live host with every test green). Fixed on the branch:

- `56306155f` — tests at each seam: the allowlist through `Verifier::with_client_ids` and the production `from_config` path (game accepted, third client and missing `azp` refused, unset game client does not widen); `validate_auth` refuses host-only and client-only, accepts and normalises the pair; the canvas dispatch opens the wall/room sheet and the fallback panels stay clickable (4 node tests).
- `27aca7357` — the a11y keyboard spec was red on CI run 45968809957 (focus raced the shell's map re-render); it now waits for the canvas `data-engine` settle point and uses the live locator's `press`. Verified locally against the real server: 1/1.

## Evidence at the head (`27aca7357`)

| Part | Scenario | Command / test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| W0 | census + instrument, host-rooted | `build-walk-coverage.py --check` / `--self-test` / `walk_coverage.sh` | 52 routes / 598 actions; 0 failing |
| W1 | spike + ADR 0023 | run 45953201576; `docs/evidence/walk-spike.md` | green |
| W1a–d | ECS, command, replay, FrameView | `cargo test -p walk-world` (CI) + the browser golden | 11 native tests; wasm hash = `e454532d51893682` |
| W2a | host matrix | `crates/api/src/web.rs` tests + `crates/api/tests/web_hosts.rs` | pass (the live server probe also: game `/config.json` = `conveyor-game`, game `/mcp` 404, operator `/mcp` 401, `/walk/portfolio` 308) |
| W2b | shell, Portfolio read/create/update/refusal, a11y | `apps/walk` Playwright suite (local Chromium) | **12/12 pass**, including the wasm golden |
| W2b | unit + types | `node --test src` (19) and `tsc -p . --noEmit` | pass |
| W2c | workflow validity | `actionlint .github/workflows/walk.yml` | pass |

Repository gates: docs 298/0 + 12/12, `no-private-refs`, `check-outputs` 255, programme seed/definition/state, `generate-standards --check`, V2 coverage, `cargo fmt --check`. **All required checks are green at `27aca7357`** — preflight (run 45970126028), walk (45970136480), ci/checks/checks-shard (45970136497), design-pack, image, service-image, CodeQL. `4ae03bafc` re-pins `programme::SPEC_V2_SHA256` for D68, per the model-drift procedure (`docs/spec/lean/README.md` § Model drift) — the Lean model is unchanged, stored certificates keep the digest they were proven on, and the two proof suites pass locally at the new pin (`proof_programme` 5/5, `proof_package` 4/4).

## Change control (live, read back)

| Act | Row |
|---|---|
| Scope baseline (14 WBS items) | `01a21bf7-b7b2-7480-99ea-438e630f4a9c` |
| Change CR-WALK-001 | `01a21bf7-d0a1-7a30-a17b-bd0e4809b9df` approved |
| Board decision | `01a21bf8-0bd5-779e-9a2d-9824bb1e2b41` |
| SoAW v2 (v1 superseded) | `01a21bf7-f6f5-7a41-a88e-12389b89b42d` live, distinct approver |
| Delivery contract | `01a21bfb-1241-7db1-9874-eacca12914b4` live |
| Artefacts v2 | Requirements `01a21bfa-9804…`, Solution `01a21bfa-9e5a…`, Technology `01a21bfa-a48d…` approved |
| Documents | ADR 0024 `01a21bf9-e2d7…`; CR `01a21bf9-ea76…`; brief/analysis/architecture design v2 |

**Measured gap, not hidden:** `changes.request` is unavailable — the only PM job binding is retired and the PM release's `proc-pm` is not a published process. The change is a baseline-backed register row decided by the Board, and the gap is a project issue row `01a21bf8-ca68-776a-85f3-a78494434210`.

## Deploy state (measured, in order)

1. **Merged and read back:** [[private-repo]#5459](https://github.com/[private-repo]/pull/5459) (the tunnel ingress, the VirtualService host and the `CONVEYOR_GAME_*` env). Live read-back: the deployment carries `CONVEYOR_GAME_HOSTS=game.nonagentic.ai`, `CONVEYOR_GAME_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=conveyor-game`, `CONVEYOR_GAME_PUBLIC_URL=https://game.nonagentic.ai`; `conveyor-public-vs` (`istio-system`) hosts both names; `game.nonagentic.ai` resolves through Cloudflare.
2. **Realm Job run and read back:** public client `conveyor-game` exists in realm `conveyor` with redirect `https://game.nonagentic.ai/*`, web origin `https://game.nonagentic.ai`, PKCE S256, and the `conveyor` audience mapper; the authorize probe with that client id, redirect and a PKCE S256 challenge returns the login form (200).
3. **Measured deviation until this PR's image deploys:** the host is routed and currently answers the *old* image, so `https://game.nonagentic.ai/config.json` says `client_id: conveyor-web`. No data exposure (the operator app's sign-in redirect is not registered for this origin, so sign-in cannot complete there), but it is the wrong surface. This PR is the fix: on the new image the game host answers the walk tree and `conveyor-game`.
4. **Post-merge:** image deploy → Flux read-back of the deployed sha → the live host matrix (`/config.json` = `conveyor-game`, `/portfolio` 200, missing asset 404, `/mcp` and `/design/*` 404, operator unchanged, `/walk/*` 308) → a real `conveyor-e2e` sign-in on the game host under the deployed OIDC project.

## Residual, explicit

- The live production sign-in and host are post-merge evidence, not claimed here. The dev-cookie path is what this PR proves end to end.
- The PM `changes.request` gate remains unavailable until `proc-pm` or a PM binding exists (issue row above).
- No primacy claim: `apps/web` remains normative until the measured P6 gate.
- The mock stays untracked; no fixture or snapshot is fetched (a spec asserts it).

Closes #813

## What

- **System architecture** — `/architecture` renders the tenant's models, their generated views and

- **Knowledge & memory** — `/knowledge` shows a released position's effective configuration and

## T13 — a missing operation opens a tool request; publish rebinds the step

`v1-p116-1` (P1, SPEC_V2 §11.6 item 3) — tranche 3's last exit criterion. Rebased on

## What changed

- **The record.** `store::authoring::tool_request_open_tx` writes an
  `authoring_asset(kind='tool_request')` with `intake_id NULL` — the engine raises the request, not
  a caller drafting from an intake — and returns the open row instead of drafting a second one.
- **The trigger.** `procedures.ingest_sop` classifies every step action: declared engine action →
  approved imported action (#3) → published tool → **missing**. One request per missing operation,
  naming the operation, the step position and the procedure. A `requested_tools` entry that no step
  names carries `step_position: null`.
- **No blanket refusal.** `procedures.validate` no longer returns 422 `sop.cannot_grant_tool`. It
  reports the gap in `checks`, sets `valid=false`, and leaves the draft retryable.
- **The rebind.** Migration `0077` adds `tool_id` / `tool_version` to `process_step`;
  `tool_authoring.publish` binds every unpinned step for the published action at the published
  version, and leaves an existing pin alone (binding is forward-only, never a silent upgrade).

## What

Docs-only unit that decides and designs the Gemba Walk's world layer, then makes every document say the same thing.

- `docs/decisions/0022-bevy-ecs-world-layer.md` — **Accepted** as a delegated rule decision (not a human signature). `bevy_ecs 0.20.1` exact-pinned as the simulation behind `WorldView`; `bevy_ecs` + `bevy_app` + `bevy_time` only, with `bevy_app`'s `web` feature under `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")` because `bevy_time` reads the clock through `bevy_platform`; **no** `bevy_render`, `bevy_winit`, `bevy_asset` or umbrella crate. The renderer stays undecided (ADR 0023, canvas-2D against WebGL2).
- `docs/design/GEMBA-WALK-ECS.md` — the architecture description: the three state classes (server truth mirrored and never authored, session, derived); the crate and its API; entities keyed by `RecordKey {kind, id}`; components and resources; the `FixedUpdate`/`Update` schedules and their ordered sets; the **Message-vs-observer rule** written against the 0.20 API; the command state machine with intent-only writes; idempotent projection and the two-generation despawn guard; determinism as a schedule property; the wasm surface; budgets; the `FrameView` adapter contract; the headless test matrix; security; extension rules.

## Why the API details are normative

Bevy 0.20 is not the API most sessions remember: since 0.17 the buffered stream is `Message` (`MessageReader`/`MessageWriter`), `Event` is the observer API, and 0.20 renamed the observer parameter to `On<E>`. A `MessageReader` ordered before its writer sees the message **next frame**, so every same-frame dependency is an explicit `.chain()` with a test for it. Systems run in parallel by default, so determinism is enforced with ordered sets plus `ScheduleBuildSettings { ambiguity_detection: LogLevel::Error }` in tests.

## Amendments (the engine is no longer an open question)

ADR 0021 decision 5 · `GEMBA-WALK-SPEC.md` §6.2/§6.3/§12 · `GEMBA-WALK.md` decision 7 and the P0 stage · `01-inception-analysis.md` (constraints, risks, open questions) · `02-architecture-design.md` (P9, D1, AD7) · `03-artifact-register.md` (four v2 rows + the ECS document row) · `05-safe-epic.md` (enablers E8–E11) · `07-governance-and-evidence.md` (W1 re-scoped, W1a–W1d) · the design and plans indexes.

No `/walk` code, no crate, no `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` change: the crate is G0's W1a.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| B2.1 Message/observer rule | `grep -c 'MessageReader\|MessageWriter'` / `grep -c 'EventReader\|EventWriter'` on the ECS doc | >0 / 0 |
| B2.2 determinism is a schedule property | `grep -n ambiguity_detection` | present |
| B3.1 no stale engine text | `grep -rn 'Bevy 0.18' docs/` · `grep -rn 'engine is not assumed' docs/` | 0 · 0 |
| B3.2 register v2 | `grep -c 'GEMBA-WALK-ECS' 03-artifact-register.md` | 2 |
| B4.1 docs gates | `build-docs.py --check` · `check-docs.cjs` · `check-outputs.cjs` · `no-private-refs.sh` | 294 documents · 12/12 · 255 pages · OK 5,254 files |
| B4.1 programme gates | `build-programme-seed.py --check` · `check-programme-definition.py` · `programme_state.py --check` · `check-coverage.cjs` | all exit 0 |
| B5 live publication | `documents.compose` → `publish` → `get` | pending merge + deploy, recorded on #806 |

Two traps worth recording: `build-docs.py` indexes only `git ls-files`, so a new document must be `git add`ed before the build or it silently vanishes from the pack (measured here: 292 → 294 documents after the add); and `crates/actions/src/proof/programme.rs` pins `sha256(docs/SPEC_V2.md)`, which this unit does not touch — the v1 unit had to re-pin it.

Closes #756

## What

**P2 — the declared-vs-evidenced register.** A delivery project's standard class now has a public
result instead of a CI-only verdict: `crates/pack/src/register.rs` resolves each project's class
from the embedded standard (`key`/`track`/`status`/`measured_status`), and publishes, per project,
the kinds the class declares, the kinds the published rows evidence, the kinds still missing, and
the documents behind them. It also publishes the invariant the retired checker carried: a seed
`expected_outputs`/`closure_outputs` set that disagrees with its class is a visible `drift` row,
never a silent pass. The conformance gap register's posture rides beside it.

- `conveyor snapshot` writes `data/register.json` + `data/register.js`, lists both in the manifest
  and embeds the same object as `snapshot.js.register`; the live `/design` view builds it from the
  rows it already reads, so the two projections cannot describe different published sets.
- `docs/design/delivery.js` renders `registerRail` in the programme view: totals, class chips, one
  chip per project with a gap that drills to the project page and the unit's GitHub issue, and the
  conformance posture. `check-data.cjs` refuses a register that is published but not manifest
  listed, or whose `.json`, `.js` and `snapshot.js.register` disagree.
- `publish.rs` names both files as generated, so a later pack without them deletes them.

**P3 — the dead checker half.** `scripts/check-output-standard.py` drops the four comparisons the
register now owns (category membership, seed-vs-class, orphan coverage, console-copy equality) and
keeps the template/heading/source lint; `--check-copy` and its two self-test cases go with them.

**P1 (already on the branch).** Every output page states its provenance (`data-provenance-*`), with
`unrecorded` where the row holds nothing.

Closes #787

A failing `lean4.check` answered `diagnostics: []` next to a non-empty `stdout`. Lean writes
its compile errors to **stdout** in this deployment, and `runner.rs` parsed stderr only, so the
one thing an operator needs — why the proof failed — was discarded. `valid` comes from the exit
code, so certificates were never wrong; every refusal was just undebuggable.

## Change

One helper, `diagnostics_for(&RunOutcome)`: parse `stdout` first (where the errors are), then
`stderr`, and drop an exact duplicate so a line echoed on both streams is reported once. The
three call sites — `check`, `elaborate`, `prove` — all use it; `parse_diagnostics` stays as the
line parser it always was. `git grep 'parse_diagnostics(&run.stderr)'` is empty outside the
helper itself.

## Proof (red → green)

New stub-`lake` tests reproduce the deployed shape exactly — the error line on stdout, stderr
empty — and drive all three paths end to end through `run_lean`:

```
$ cargo-guard test -p conveyor-lean4-prover --lib runner::      # before the call-site change
runner::tests::a_failing_check_returns_the_error_it_printed ... FAILED
runner::tests::a_failing_elaboration_returns_the_error_it_printed ... FAILED
runner::tests::a_failing_proof_returns_the_error_it_printed ... FAILED
test result: FAILED. 9 passed; 3 failed
  panicked: diagnostics must carry Lean's own error (stdout here): stdout="...:3:2: error: unknown identifier 'foo'" stderr=""
```

After: 12 passed, 0 failed — including `a_clean_run_reports_no_diagnostics` (P1.2: success is
not turned into noise) and the two helpers' unit tests (both streams combined; a duplicate
reported once). `cargo fmt --check` clean; `clippy -p conveyor-lean4-prover --all-targets --
-D warnings` clean via cargo-guard (interactive, m4); `cargo metadata --locked` clean.

## Definition of done

- [x] P1.1 — a failing check returns the error it printed (test named for it)
- [x] P1.2 — a compiling source still reports no diagnostics
- [x] P2.1 — one parser, every call site (check, elaborate, prove)
- [ ] live re-check on the deployed prover after the image lands (recorded in the issue)

Closes #779

## What

A delivery unit is now a `development_projects` row a session can find and resume:

- **Idempotent charter.** `development_projects.charter` replays by project key: the same repo,
  lane, implementer and issue returns the same row; a different one is refused
  `409 charter_mismatch`; a key that names an unchartered project is refused
  `409 project_exists_without_charter`.
- **`issue_ref`.** `owner/name#N` is a charter field, shape-checked in the action and by a DB
  CHECK, with one unit per issue via a partial unique index. A second unit for the same issue is
  refused `409 issue_already_chartered`.
- **`development_projects.list`.** Filters by repo, status and issue; returns the project key and
  the latest recorded step, so a resumed session needs no stored id.

## Why / source

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §9.1/§9.3/§10.1: the development project is the unit of a delivery, the conveyor
owns the progress rows, and a unit must not be reconstructed from files. Issue #779; the measured
state and BDD scenarios are on the issue.

## Acceptance evidence (at `df2e2811ad340a637cfc732fe689875f6aec35bd`)

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1–P1.2 | `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test development_project` | **15 passed**; `charter_is_idempotent_by_key`, `charter_refuses_a_mismatched_replay` |
| P2.1–P2.2 | same run | `charter_records_the_issue_ref`: valid ref read back; malformed `779` is 422 with field code `issue_ref_invalid`; a second unit for the same issue is 409 `issue_already_chartered` |
| P3.1–P3.2 | same run | `list_filters_by_repo_status_and_issue`: repo, status and issue filters; `latest_step` is `null`, then `branch` after the step is recorded |
| P4.1–P4.2 | — | **Not run: acceptance-blocked-by #760.** The session bearer does not exist at this head; the code side is ready — `development_projects.*` is not machine-forbidden — and the grant is one `channels.policy_set` after #760 lands. |
| Registry | `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-actions --test registry` | **13 passed**, including `committed_action_dump_matches_the_registry` |
| Clippy | `~/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py clippy -p conveyor-actions -p conveyor-store --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Format / metadata | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` | clean |
| Design / parity | `build-coverage.py --check`, `build-v2-coverage.py --check`, `check-parity.py --require-native`, `check-programme-definition.py`, `build-programme-seed.py --check`, `programme_state.py --self-test/--check`, `audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` | all exit 0 |
| Served spec | `conveyor --print-openapi --write-lock`, then `--check-lock` | exit 0; three hashes moved (`GET /api/actions`, `charter`, `get`) and the `list` operation added |

The migration applied on every fresh test database the file creates (the harness migrates each
one); no step was skipped.

## Risks

- A replay with **no** explicit `key` derives a new key and is refused by the issue index rather
  than replaying. The delivery skill must pass the stable key; that is the idempotent path.
- The charter answer is the charter view (no steps/gates/closure), on both create and replay; the
  full record is `development_projects.get`. Existing behaviour, unchanged.
- The migration is expand-only (nullable column, CHECK, partial unique index); a prior release
  reads the table unchanged.

Branch `issue/779-unit-record` at `df2e2811a`. After #760 merges, the P4 grant probe is the
remaining live half and is recorded on #760.

## What

Sessions act on the conveyor as a **machine principal**: an opaque licence bearer minted on the tenant's active `conveyor` licence, introspected by `crates/auth`, resolved to an `app_user` row of kind `service` with the MCP channel authority. This replaces the per-action `kubectl exec` transport with one mint per day and plain HTTPS afterwards.

- `crates/auth`: `LicenceSyncClient::active_license_id` (with `X-Tenant-Id`, needed because the read set excludes `license-manager`) and `create_license_token` (POST `/licenses/{id}/tokens`), plus stub tests.
- `apps/server`: `conveyor auth token` (mint, owner-only cache, one-hour reuse window) and `conveyor admin machine-principal ensure` (subject from introspection, idempotent, refuses a human row; sets `app.current_tenant` for the FORCE-RLS `membership` insert).
- The licences `api_client` row maps the dedicated secure-apps client `conveyor-channel` to owner `agent` — agent issues only {agent, conveyor}, so the mint is scoped to those apps and the granted tenant. It is **ops data, not a migration**: a migration would violate the `tenant_owner` FK on a fresh database, where owners are seeded by fleet provisioning. The row (and the `tenant_app_grant` for `agent`) are written once by the operator and are live on the estate.
- The companion infrastructure change (secure-apps client `conveyor-channel` with `license-manager` + `license-reader`, and the conveyor deployment's `CONVEYOR_SESSION_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`) is a separate PR in the infrastructure repository; it and its realm job are **applied live** and green.

## Acceptance (run 2026-11-26 against the live estate)

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Mint with the dedicated client | `conveyor auth token --tenant nonagentic` | token file `0600`, expiry `2026-11-27T16:08Z`, `reused:false` |
| Cache reuse | second run inside the window | `reused:true`, same expiry |
| Principal, idempotent | `conveyor admin machine-principal ensure …` ×2 | `created:false`, role `kata_executor`, subject `licence:…` both times |
| Granted action over HTTPS | `POST /api/actions/programmes.list/invocations` | `200`, one programme row |
| More granted reads | `approvals.list`, `meetings.list` | `200` |
| Grant is load-bearing | `tranches.list` before / after the grant | `403` → `422` (schema), i.e. authorised |
| Ungranted act | an act outside the 60-grant set | `403` `action-forbidden` |
| MCP | `initialize` + `tools/list` on one pod | `200`, **49 tools incl. `programmes_list`** |
| Ledger attribution | `action_invocation` + `app_user` | `programmes.list | ok | service | licence:…` |
| Revocation | revoke, then call immediately / after 65 s | `200` (60 s cache) then `401 invalid token` |

Known observation, not this change: `tools/list` over the public host round-robins to the other replica and answers `404 no route for POST /mcp`; against one pod it is `200`/49 tools. The session-affinity DestinationRule is live but does not pin through the ingress path.

## Gate

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean at `04bce8da8`.
- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` → ok.
- `preflight.yml` on `issue/760-session-channel` → **green** (fmt + `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`).
- Unit tests: `conveyor-auth --test licence` **10 passed**; `conveyor-server --lib session::` **4 passed**.

## Note

The channel grant set stored for the tenant is a curated 60 actions across `programmes.*`, `tranches.*`, `registers.*`, `benefits.*`, `documents.*`, `changes.*`, `approvals.*`, `meetings.*`, excluding `.delete`/`.retire`/`.revoke`/`.reset`. The final allowlist per role is #753's; any action it names that is missing is one `channels.policy_set` call.

Closes #760

pulls.body:
Closes #776

The mint now authenticates as its own platform-owned client, `conveyor-bundle-minter`, and a
deployment that forgot the credential is told which variable is missing — instead of sealing a
token the licences service refuses at the next introspection.

## Why the backend's credential cannot be reused

The licences mint route is owner-scoped. `conveyor-backend`'s `api_client` row belongs to `fr`
while the tenant's licences belong to `platform`, so a role grant alone would still be refused
`403`, and the role grant would widen a credential that every other conveyor call uses. One
service, one credential, one blast radius.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/api/src/config.rs` | `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_ID` / `BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `bundle_minter_credentials()`, whose error names the missing setting |
| `apps/server/src/admin/upstream_tokens.rs` | `fill` takes the minter client; `MINTER_NOT_CONFIGURED` is the refusal, returned before any HTTP call and before any row is written |
| `apps/server/src/main.rs` | the minter client is built only for `--mint`; a BYO fill no longer builds a licences client at all |

## Parts

| Part | Scenario | Where |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | the mint names the minter client in the token form body | `crates/auth/tests/licence.rs::the_mint_uses_the_minter_client`, `config.rs::the_minter_uses_its_own_credential_and_refuses_without_one` |
| P1.2 | no existing caller changes behaviour | the backend credential is untouched and still used by provisioning, billing and `licence.sync`; the BYO path never had a licences client to lose |
| P2.1 | a mint with no minter credential exits non-zero, names the variable, writes no row | `apps/server/tests/upstream_tokens.rs::a_mint_without_the_minter_credential_is_refused` |

**A conflict in the issue, and how it was resolved.** P1.2 reads "given only `SERVICE_CLIENT_*`,
when the mint runs, then it is authorized as before", while P2.1 requires the mint to refuse with
only `SERVICE_CLIENT_*` present. They cannot both hold. P2.1 wins: it is the issue's title, it is
the "no silent fallback" part, and a fallback to the backend credential is the exact bug the issue
was opened for. P1.2 holds for every caller that is not the mint.

## P3 — live acceptance, still blocked on infrastructure

P3.1 needs three things that live outside this repository, and the issue records them as
`acceptance-blocked-by: owner`:

1. a `conveyor-bundle-minter` client in realm `secure-apps` holding `bundle-token-minter` and
   nothing else (the `realm-patch-job-bundle-minters.yaml` pattern; there is no conveyor entry yet);
2. a matching `api_client` row with `owner_key=platform` — the table is
   `public.api_client (realm, client_id, owner_key, cross_owner)` and `conveyor-backend`'s row is
   `owner_key=fr`, which is why the role grant alone was refused;
3. the `lean4-prover` catalogue app with a plan and a licence for `01a1cf6d-…` (owner decision
   2026-11-26: a new app, not the tenant's `conveyor` licence).

Until then the deployed pod has no `BUNDLE_MINTER_*`, so `--mint` answers
`bundle minter credential not configured: BUNDLE_MINTER_CLIENT_SECRET` — the intended refusal, not
a silent success.

Closes #762

The drills #746 left unproven are now measured against the deployed engine — the image carrying
`0076`, #746 and `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_LEAN4_URL`.

## What the deployed engine did

| Scenario | Answer |
|---|---|
| `lean4.check` with the renderer's own slice certificate | `valid: true`, 1 509.88 ms |
| `lean4.check` with `theorem nope : 1 = 2 := by decide` | `valid: false` (the corpus is not vacuous) |
| `proofs.record` naming that invocation | `201`, `verdict: proven`, `certificate_sha256 31feb1ba…4648` |
| `approvals.request`, `required_kinds: ["lean_proof"]`, no evidence | `422 gate_evidence_missing` — *this gate requires a "lean_proof" evidence item to open; the request names none* |
| the same gate with the certificate | `200`; `evidence[0]` cites the certificate digest and the pinned spec |
| a consistently rewritten certificate (facts, `facts_sha256` **and** `certificate_sha256`), fresh check green, then `proofs.reverify` | `422 proof_source_not_rendered` — *the stored source is not this rendering of the stored facts* |
| recorded refusals | `action_invocation: proofs.reverify → refused`, `audit_event {"outcome":"refused"}` |

The credential is a licence token minted on the tenant's **own `conveyor` licence**, sealed with
`conveyor admin upstream-token --service lean4 --token-stdin`; the prover introspects it and takes
the tenant from the licence.

## What this does not prove

- That the facts in a certificate describe what happened in the database — the refinement
  assumption every certificate names.

Closes #763

## What

`compliance()` now selects only live **delivery** contracts for the Phase-G `compliance_review_missing`
rule: `kind == 'delivery_contract'` or `phase_code == 'f'` (case-insensitive). A live Statement of
Architecture Work is not a compliance subject, so a v2 project whose SoAW has no review is no longer
flagged. The self-test gains the three contract cases: SoAW + reviewed delivery contract → no gap;
SoAW + unreviewed delivery contract → gap; SoAW only → no gap.

This extracts the one-file fix already on `issue/526-u5a` at `7796da7f0` (the #526 evidence blobs
stay on that lane). It is 41 insertions and 1 deletion in `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py`.

## Why

The unfiltered rule red T1, T2, T9, T10 and T11 on `compliance_review_missing` even where the live
delivery contract had a compliant review, because the rule also demanded a review of each project's
live SoAW. The role skill added in #753 names the correct subject; this is the code half. The
snapshot comparison on the same data: **7 → 1** `compliance_review_missing` entries, and only that
rule changes (203 → 197 gaps); the remaining T4 entry is a real delivery contract with no review.

Closes #746

A delivered slice, a delivered work product and the programme release each carry a Lean certificate a third party can re-check. The engine now **owns the source it certifies**: `proofs.record` and `proofs.reverify` refuse a source that is not `render(facts, theorem)`. Without that binding "re-render and compare" is advisory, and a caller can certify a theorem their facts do not state.

This is the second half of the #744 split, which #746's own body records as a written split under the 03-DELIVERY exception: #744 delivered the store, the `proofs.*` actions and the `lean_proof` arm; this unit delivers the corpus, the renderer, the programme and package certificates, and the required-evidence mechanism.

## What landed

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| P1 | Measurement against the real prover, recorded in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` |
| P2 | `docs/spec/lean/DeliveryModel.lean` — core Lean only, embedded verbatim into every certificate, plus `README.md` stating what is proven and what is assumed |
| P3 | `crates/actions/src/proof/render.rs` — a pure renderer plus the `proof_source_not_rendered` binding |
| P4 | `proof/programme.rs` — the release bundle: the §12 slice set, one leaf per built slice, each with a distinct certificate digest |
| P5 | `proof/manifest.rs` — a package's own manifest: migrations vs ledger, routes vs served document, every named check passed |
| P6 | `required_kinds` on gate evidence — `require_evidence` alone only refuses an *empty* list, so a caller that omitted the proof was accepted; the programme release gate now names `lean_proof` and its absence is `422 gate_evidence_missing` |

The model carries `(slice, certificate digest)` pairs, so one certificate cannot stand in for two slices; `checkProgramme` refuses a shared digest. The renderer emits only `by decide` and refuses facts whose text names a native reduction, so a `trust: kernel` certificate can never rest on the compiler.

## Local gate at `351f1be8` (after merging `origin/main`)

```
registry              13/13    parity_http_mcp   7/7
proof_render          10/10    proof_programme   5/5   proof_package  4/4
proofs_record         11/11    proofs_reverify   8/8   pm_gate_proof  7/7
lean_corpus            6/6    conveyor-api lib 29/29   store s07_schema 3/3
cargo fmt --all -- --check        clean
--print-openapi --check-lock      clean
build-docs                       279 documents, 0 failures
node check-docs.cjs               12 checks passed
scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh     OK, 5201 files
scripts/build-coverage.py --check current
```

Kernel checks on the exact artefacts, run inside the prover's own pod with `lake env lean` (`leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2`): model 0, slice 0, slice-missing-evidence 1, escaping model 1, 20-leaf bundle 0 (3.1 s), dropped leaf 1, shared digest 1. The renderer's emission format was checked the same way once per kind.

## Deployment — the live scenarios follow this merge, not precede it

The deployed engine runs `main`, so P6.1/P6.2 (the live gate refusal and the tamper drill) can only exercise this code once it is merged and rolled out. Three prerequisites, all outside this repo:

1. `gitops-production#5450` adds `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_LEAN4_URL` to both containers (open).
2. The tenant's `lean4.token` is sealed — there is **no `lean4-prover` licence app** in the licences catalogue (measured: `no_active_license` for the tenant; `conveyor`, `inference-router` and `coding` are active), so the token is minted on the tenant's own `conveyor` licence. A dedicated app is a licensing decision, not a code one.
3. Migration `0076` reaches the deployed engine through the normal image rollout.

The two live drills will be recorded in `docs/evidence/proof-of-delivery.md` on the deployed commit and reported on the issue. Everything else in the issue's acceptance is green at the head above.

## Also

`03-DELIVERY.md` and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/unit.md` gain the correction #744's two PR reds earned: a unit that adds/removes an action **or changes an input schema** must name and run the registry, parity, `--check-lock`, `build-coverage` and the design-pack index locally before the PR.
