pulls.body:
Closes #744

## What

The delivery-proof capability: a Lean prover verdict becomes a durable, re-checkable
certificate, and a gate can require one.

- **`crates/actions/src/proof/mod.rs`** — `proofs.record|reverify|get|list`. A certificate is
  built from what the engine already persisted for a `lean4.check|prove` invocation: the Lean
  source is read from the stored request body (the engine's own request hash must match, so a
  caller cannot substitute it), the verdict and computation time from the stored response, and
  the facts digest is computed here rather than accepted. A caller cannot supply a verdict —
  there is no field for one. `proofs.reverify` is the comparison half of a fresh check (the
  caller runs `lean4.check` again under a new key): it refuses a source, verdict or recomputed
  digest that differs, and writes nothing, because the table is append-only.
- **`resolve_evidence`** (`crates/actions/src/pm/mod.rs`) gains a fourth arm, `lean_proof`, and
  one parameter, the gate's spec pin. It refuses unless the certificate is `proven`, on the
  pinned `spec_sha256`, with `certificate_sha256` and `facts_sha256` that still describe their
  columns — each failure with its own `422` code. `approvals.request` and `pm.route_gate` accept
  `pinned_spec_sha256` and write it into `meta` beside the resolved evidence.
- **`UpstreamService::Lean4`** (`apps/server/src/admin/upstream_tokens.rs`) — `lean4.token`,
  minted against the `lean4-prover` licences app: one service, one secret.
- **`migrations/0076_lean_proof.sql`** — the `proof` table (RLS enabled + forced, append-only
  grants) plus the `action_invocation` idempotency index the invocation lookup needs.

## Why

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.3/§5.4 make evidence a closed set a gate resolves, but nothing said what
"the evidence is sufficient" means in a form a third party can re-check without trusting the
conveyor. The prover is already a workspace crate with declared actions (`crates/actions/src/
integrations/lean4.rs`, #561) and the ingress from the `conveyor` namespace is merged
(`gitops-production#5449`), so the marginal cost here is the store sound one, not the prover.

What Lean proves, and what it does not, is stated in `docs/plans/proof-of-delivery.md`: the model
and the record, not that the Rust implementation refines the model. Every certificate names the
assumption, the spec hash and a prover identity the conveyor asserts from configuration.

The corpus, the programme certificates and the live gate are #746, which needs this merged.

- [x] No credential, private hostname or private address in the diff.

## What lands

SPEC V2 §10.4 declares six `analyse.*` evidence producers; only `analyse.site` and `analyse.video`
were registered. This PR adds the other four as read-only `ActionSpec`s over new pure functions in
`conveyor-analysis`:

| Action | Pure analyser | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| `analyse.app` | `app::coverage(routes, pages)` | `app-destination-missing`, `app-destination-unserved`, `app-destination-unreachable`, `app-route-unmapped` over the 11 §10.5 destinations |
| `analyse.brand` | `brand::analyse(document, facts)` | palette, typography and voice consistency against caller-supplied brand facts |
| `analyse.content` | `content::analyse_quality(document)` | the existing CRO/marketing scan plus `content-heading-*`, `content-no-sources`, `content-filler` |
| `analyse.report` | `report::analyse(document, claims)` | one `report-claim-unverified` / `report-claim-empty` per failed claim |

All four are `kind=internal`, `effect=read`, `idempotent=true`, `scopes=["documents:read"]`,
`tenancy=tenant`; they write no row, emit no event, read no clock, and decode stored bytes lossily.

Closes #738

## What

`console.js` sets `state.token` before it awaits `loadManifest()`. A render that lands in that window has `consoleOn()` true and `C.can()` false for every action. `consoleLoadProcedures` read that as permission denied, resolved `{items: []}` and set `loaded = true` for the life of the page — the Procedures destination never fetched.

- `docs/design/v2.js`: the loader now refuses to load until `C.manifest()` exists. Boot's completion emits an `onChange`, which re-renders and retries; a lost session clears the token, so the existing `consoleOn()` guard covers that path.
- `docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs`: new case 2c-race — `/api/actions` is held until boot has asked for it, the route is changed while `can()` is still false, the manifest is released, and the seeded SOP row must render.
- `docs/design/data/coverage.{json,js}`: regenerated; the actions' recorded line numbers moved with the insertion.

## Why

`main` went red at `c005f69f` in run 45617747425 (design-pack): `check-console` waited 30 s for `text=Synthetic receiving SOP` at `check-console.cjs:4747`. The tree is identical to PR #737's head `176b186e`, whose design-pack passed (run 45613914509) — a startup race, not a data regression.

## Evidence at `e39264b6`

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 — the race is caught | `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` with the loader guard reverted | **FAILS** — `waiting for locator('text=Synthetic receiving SOP')`, the same shape as the main run |
| P1.1/P1.2/P1.3 | `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` with the guard | PASS |
| the other surfaces | `check-v2`, `check-studio`, `check-learning`, `check-workbench`, `check-architecture` | PASS (architecture: 148 checks) |
| the pack's data and claims | the full design-pack step (`build-coverage --check` … `build-docs.py --check`) | ALL OK |
| coverage data | `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` after regeneration | current |
| diff hygiene | `git diff --check` | exit 0 |

## Risks

- The guard delays one render, never data: if the manifest never arrives the session error path clears the token and the snapshot surface renders.
- No server, schema or workflow change; the pack's other `can()` sites gate controls, not data loading.

Closes #630

## What

- The run now **pins its executor kind** at creation (`0074_run_executor_kind.sql`, nullable + backfill from `job_binding`), alongside the `job_binding_id` and `release_hash` the row already carried.
- `runs.list` / `runs.get` expose all three; the Execution room renders the pin in the run history and the run detail instead of naming it as a gap.
- `tool_calls.list` now joins `tool_binding.credential_alias` and `run_step.output` (via the ledger's `binding_id` and `run_step_id`), so the run detail's **tools panel** names the tool version, the credential alias and the returned evidence — or the failure when the call failed.
- The old "Not in this read" panel is gone; the screen renders the ledger.

## Why

The run inspector named the executor/pin and the T13 ledger as gaps. The data existed in two places the projection did not read: the binding (kind, alias) and the run step (evidence). `executor_kind` was not pinned on the run at all — the T0 audit's "a pinned release does not pin the executor configuration" — so 0074 copies it at creation.

## Evidence at `6e9fca6d`

- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test runs` — PASS (`the_run_carries_its_executor_and_binding_pin`).
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test tool_ledger` — PASS (`the_ledger_names_the_version_alias_and_evidence`).
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --lib embedded_migrations_are_exactly_the_s0_set` — PASS.

- preflight run `45581821371` — success.
- The two browser scenarios in `apps/web/e2e/execution.spec.ts` run in the `web` workflow on this PR; this box has no Node tooling, so they are not claimed as locally run.

## Risks

- 0074 is expand/contract: a nullable column plus a backfill; an application-only rollback remains sound.
- The kind is copied at creation, not joined at read time, so a later binding edit cannot rewrite a run's history.
- `tool_calls.list` gains two left joins on primary keys; a call with no grant or no step keeps `NULL` and renders "—"/the error, never a fabricated value.

Branch `issue/630-t18-run-inspector`; worktree `.worktrees/issue-630`.

## What

S21 step 11 closes the work-package execution level. Four defects the level still carried, plus the live proof:

- **P1 — an accepted gate applies its draft.** `decision_policy.meta.on_accept ∈ {park, apply}` (absent = park) is validated at authoring (`422 invalid_policy_meta`); the executor's accepted arm applies the draft through the one `apply_draft_tx` gate that `ladder.apply_draft` and `run.resume` also call, in the finish transaction, with the recorded L1 decision. A declared apply that cannot apply fails the run `draft_apply_invalid`. A cardless `internal_agent` run is already refused `capability_not_ready` by the dispatcher (`executor/mod.rs:458`); the executor's `apply_skipped: no_card` branch is defence in depth.
- **P2 — no model call without compiled text (`v1-p77-1`).** An active `internal_agent` must name a resolvable prompt: domain `validate_agent_config`, `capability_agents.create|update` (`422 prompt_ref_required`), readiness (`prompt_not_configured`) and `agent.run` (`409 capability_not_ready` before any inference). Every recorded call carries a 64-hex `prompt_sha256`.
- **P3 — the recipe ceiling is authorable (`v1-p77-2`).** `prompt_recipes.create` writes `budget_chars` (0 refused); the compile's measured refusal is reachable from an authored recipe and makes no call. Section budgets were already writable — the register's wording is corrected in the receipt.
- **P4 — the release compiles its knowledge layers (`v1-w1a-2`, P0).** Migration `0072` adds `organisation_layer` (base, industry, department archetype, each department in declared order, job). This closes that gate honestly and refreshes the record.

The earlier service-decided gate stays in the record as history.
- `authoring.review` accepted the human gate and `authoring.publish` wrote meeting_type v2 `01a211da-c391-7867-86dd-d22f9cfed5d5`; the meeting pinned at v1 still resolves v1 (`docs/evidence/t19f/gate/06-authoring-review.md`, `07-authoring-publish.md`).

- The first resumed `--apply` re-ran the sitting's contract request before that guard existed and created a duplicate draft delivery contract; it was superseded (`10b-supersede-duplicate-contract.md`), and the two live governance contracts are untouched.

## The record

- `docs/plans/T19F/evidence.md` (v3): the blocked invariant now passes; the human seat is named as FR Test, never the owner's account; the publication section states the strict publish is the follow-on conformance unit.
- `docs/plans/T19F/closure-review.md` (v2, published): the policy-v2 row passes; the PR row names #711/`9ace4e81`; the strict row stays `open (disclosed)`; project closure remains deferred to the tranche-6 review (T19F stays `active`).

At `bb921073` on `origin/main` `7d5ef094`: `git diff --check`; `build-coverage.py --check`, `build-v2-coverage.py --check`, `build-programme-seed.py --check`, `check-programme-definition.py`, `programme_state.py --check`, `audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` and `--check-standard`, `check-output-standard.py --self-test`/plain, `generate-standards.py --self-test`, `generate-standards.py --check --snapshot docs/design/data`, `publish-standards.sh --check`, `scripts/ci/tests/standards_pack.sh`, `publish_audit.sh`, `board.py --self-test`, the seven `check-*.cjs`, `build-docs.py --check` — all pass. ## What

The media extractor falls back to `Authorization: Bearer <licence>` when no `X-Tenant-Id` is present, so the conveyor's external action engine (`HandlerRef::External`, which can send only `Authorization`) can call the media read surface. The `X-Tenant-Id` licence keeps the router's first precedence; a disagreeing `Authorization` licence is logged, not refused. The #226 bare-header vouch path is unchanged.

## Why

#561 measured the five `media.*` provenance rows as `DROP` because the media routes authenticated on `X-Tenant-Id`, which the external handler cannot send. This is the enabling fix; the media toolkit declaration follows.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — PASS.

## What

The gate refuses it verbatim and the run records it as blocked rather than forging a decision. This is a genuine open action for a person, not a waived check.
- **Programme-wide conformance debt makes the strict publish red independently of T19F**: T5/T6/T8/T15/T17 closed since the accepted baseline (new/worsened P0s) and the S18/S21/SPEC-V2 ledger rows. The plan's own fallback applies: report-only publish with the exact findings committed in `conformance.json` and the log. T19F's own finding is `project_in_unauthorised_tranche` P1 — the declared state until the tranche-6 review; closing T19F would manufacture a P0, which the plan forbids.
- **The publish transport**: the box cannot compile, so `publish-data.sh` ran with `CONVEYOR_BIN` shimming `snapshot` to the deployed binary on strato against the primary with the pod's 0600 env file; `~/Movies/nonagentic_homepage` has no `design/` tree today, so the mirror step wrote to a scratch target. Both are recorded in the logs.

## What

Implements the two T19 follow-ups: the versioned forum-policy authoring route through T17, the T9 board-sitting binding and the T10 cadence materialisation, with their UI surfaces and generated programme data.

Closes #680

## What

`scripts/materialise-rework.py` now parses the **first JSON object** in the CLI's stdout instead of
requiring the whole stream to be JSON. `response_document()` scans for a `{`, decodes with
`json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode`, and ignores (logs at debug level) any text before or after the
document. `invoke()` keeps its refusal path unchanged: a non-zero exit still raises `ActionError`
carrying stderr.

## Why

Measured live on #545 (2026-11-24): `conveyor admin action invoke` wrote a WARN line to stdout;
`json.loads(completed.stdout)` raised `Extra data: line 2 column 1`, the tool recorded a package as
failed **after the card had committed**, and the retry duplicated cards (six retired through
approval-gated `cards.archive`, two restored). The `RUST_LOG=error` workaround stays on #545; this
fix removes the tool's dependence on a clean stdout.

## Track

- [x] **Unit work** — the `Closes` line above names the unit issue.

## Checks

      design-pack list (`scripts/ci/tests/standards_pack.sh` included) are green at the PR head.

```
stdout = '{"output": {"id": "card-1"}}\nWARN conveyor: a log line on stdout\n'
```

## What
The research and Lean wave of the tool estate: the webscraper's two POST operations (`webscraper.scrape_url`, `webscraper.scrape_bulk`) and the Lean prover's three (`lean4.check|elaborate|prove`) are declared as External actions, and `seed/toolkits/webscraper.json` and `seed/toolkits/lean4.json` publish them as draft toolkits with health paths. Closes #656

## What this delivers

The work-package level's L1 gate is now honest end to end. The ladder builds the laya case from
the effective policy and an **authored, versioned option set**; the engine performs the request as
the external action `ladder.precheck` (outside any transaction); and `ladder.evaluate` records a
decision **only** from the engine's recorded exchange — the claim's request hash must match, the
status must be 2xx, and the measured `duration_ms` becomes the decision's latency.

- `decision_option_sets.set|get` author and read the menu; the one row's version increments and its
  children are replaced in the same transaction (`0068`'s partial unique indexes).
- A policy declares `meta.question_type = "choice"`; the case's criteria are the authored keys and
  its instructions list `key — label`. An answer outside the set is `422
  laya_answer_not_in_options`; a declared choice with no set is `409 option_set_missing`; inline
  options are refused.
- `fire_when` is parsed and validated in `crates/domain`, written through the policy actions
  (an explicit `null` clears it), and evaluated before any call. A non-firing case is never asked,
  records no decision, and the step proceeds.
- The executor uses the **same** case builder (it previously constructed its own copy), so the
  authored menu and `fire_when` reach in-process gates; it makes exactly one laya request per gate.
- `decision.input_hash` / `meta.case_sha256` are the case's sha256; the engine's FNV claim hash
  stays the idempotency witness (the P1b cut had conflated them).

2. Build a constant, schema-valid case body → `a_call_for_another_case_is_refused` red (201).

Closes #410

## What

`produce.speech` and `media.transcribe` now present the calling tenant's sealed `licence.token` to
the mini2 model hosts, and a licence refusal becomes a typed `403 action-licence-refused` naming
the secret and the tenant instead of a passthrough 502/422.

## Why

Both hosts run an armed licence gate that resolves the tenant from a licence token
(`POST /license/introspect`). The actions declared `auth: None`, so every call was refused: speech
`503 license_unavailable`, transcription `401 token_not_found` (measured 2026-11-19, #410). The
transcription gate prefers `X-Tenant-Id` over `Authorization`, and it accepts a bare value there as
a token — so the bare tenant id the engine already sends is exactly what it introspected as
`token_not_found`. A licence-auth call now sends `X-Tenant-Id: Bearer <sealed token>` as well;
either header resolves the same tenant from the token.

## What

The merge-group run may skip the code gates when — and only when — its tree is exactly the tested PR
head's tree and that head's required checks are green. The required `checks` context still reports
success; a push to main never takes the skip, so the image that deploys is always built. Every doubt
fails open to the full suite.

## Design

- `classify` gains a `checks_skip` output. On `merge_group` only, it parses the PR number from
  `github.event.merge_group.head_ref`, reads the PR head through the API, fetches `pull/<n>/head`,
  compares that tree with the merge-group head's tree, and re-reads the five required check-runs
  live (`filter=latest`). Any failure to read, fetch or compare leaves `checks_skip=false`.
- `checks-shard` gains `&& needs.classify.outputs.checks_skip != 'true'`; the aggregate `checks`
  accepts the skip exactly as it accepts the existing docs-only and generated-only skips.
- The `image` job and `publish-service-images` are untouched; the classifier's event gate means a
  push to main never sets the skip.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Evidence |
|---|---|
| P3.1 a tree-equal queue entry skips `checks-shard` and keeps `checks` green | this PR's own merge-group run: `classify` `checks_skip=true`, `checks-shard` `skipped`, `checks` `success`, queue merged |
| P3.2 the deploy is never suppressed | the push-to-main run at the merge SHA: `image` success (skipped checks never reach a push) |
| P3.3 fail open | the step's early exits; a queue entry after a main advance logs `trees differ` and runs the shards |

Closes #22

## What

#17 P4: the `checks` job (the required context) now records the run's **queue wait**
(`run_started_at - created_at`) and **wall time** to the job summary on every run, read from the
Actions API rather than inferred from `gh run list`'s rounded fields. An unreadable answer is
written as such, never as a number. The step runs on failure too (`always()`), so every completed
run carries the measurement.

## Amendment, measured at `origin/main@a8c22f8e`

P1/P2 as written describe a `ci.yml` caller of `gitops-production/.github/workflows/rust-service.yml@main`.
That caller cannot exist: this repository is **public** and `gitops-production` is **private**, and a
public repository may only call public reusable workflows. `ci-public.yml` is the canonical public
mirror — its own header (lines 1–20) records the constraint and attributes the gates to the
archetype's `rust-library`. The issue body is amended to that truth; P3 is evidenced from the job
timeline below.

## Summary

Delivers the platform fix for #669: a rollback across a migration boundary could not serve the prior digest because the older binary's sqlx migrator failed on an applied version it does not embed (`VersionMissing(70)`). Three parts, no new migration:

1. **The runtime migrator tolerates newer applied versions.** `crates/store/src/migrate.rs` keeps the fail-closed embedded `MIGRATOR` and adds `runtime_migrator()`, which runs the same embedded set with sqlx 0.9's `set_ignore_missing(true)`. `migrate()` uses it; the runtime-role assertion and the runtime-grants re-application are unchanged. Checksum validation for known migrations is **not** weakened — sqlx still returns `VersionMismatch` for an edited embedded migration.
2. **The schema generation is recorded in T6's deploy/rollback/closure evidence.** `Step::Deploy` and `Step::RollbackExercise` name `migration_generation` (the max applied migration version at deploy time); the rollback names both digests and the generation; the closure document carries the deploy generation and the full rollback evidence.
3. **The obligation is documented and enforced.** `migrations/README.md` and the store/deploy-gate comments state that every migration must be expand/contract (backward-compatible with the immediately prior release) and that a non-additive migration requires a restore-based rollback through the gated ops path. The deploy gate refuses a non-additive plan with no `restore_path`; `development_projects.rollback` refuses an application rollback (`schema_restore_required`) and names the plan's restore path.

## Evidence

Local gate (worktree `.worktrees/issue-669` off `origin/main@f4c2947e`):

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — pass
- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` — pass
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — pass (exit 0)
- `cargo test -p conveyor-domain --lib development` — 4 passed
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --lib migrate` — 3 passed
- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test migrate_tolerance` — 2 passed (tolerance + control `VersionMissing` + checksum `VersionMismatch`)
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test development_project` — 8 T6 scenarios passed (including the two new P3.2 offline scenarios)
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test parity_http_mcp` — 7 passed
- The 31-command design-pack list from `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` — 31/31 pass
- `served-spec.lock.json` regenerated with `--print-openapi --write-lock`; the only changed operation is `development_projects.rollback` (new required input field)

Preflight: run `45447267256` on `1e9106ce` (the push-triggered run — the ONE preflight for this head).

## Live re-proof (not run in this PR)

After this merges and the deployed image carries the fix (`CONVEYOR_GIT_SHA` check), the rollback exercise is re-run with the owner's go-ahead, and both digests plus the migration generation are recorded on #669 and #80 (P3.2). No live rollback was attempted before the deployed image carried the fix.

Proof boundary (measured on the live deployment, read-only): the `migrate` init container runs the **same digest** as the app. A fixed release can therefore only be rolled back to a **post-fix** predecessor and tolerate a newer schema; the historical revision 332 (`sha256:2bce9455…`, embeds 0069) predates this fix and its own migrator still fails closed, so that particular rollback remains unproducible. The post-merge `rollout undo` from the fixed revision targets the immediately prior revision (currently `sha256:d2d15fe1…`, embeds 0070) and proves P3.2's digest evidence; the tolerance itself is exercised live when a later schema-advancing deploy is rolled back to this fixed release.

Closes #669

## What this changes

Completes the ownership decision recorded by #668 on the CI side: the artefact record and the rework register belong to the live publish (`docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh`). A refresh and a test both stop deriving them.

### P1 — the refresh leaves the record half alone

`.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` no longer runs `docs/design/scripts/publish-standards.sh`. A refresh regenerates `docs/design/data/issues.json`, the programme seed (`seed/programme.json`, `docs/design/data/output-standard.js`), the measured coverage (`coverage.json`/`coverage.js`, `docs/evidence/v2-coverage.*`) and nothing else. The record, the register, the standards pages and the evidence ledgers are never written by a refresh. `build-docs.py --check` stays (read-only and cheap). The no-change check names the generated paths, so a refresh whose only change is issues/seed/coverage opens its PR.

```diff
-          # The standards pack is derived data too: ...
-          docs/design/scripts/publish-standards.sh
+          # ⛔ The standards record half is NOT regenerated here. The register is the live
+          # publish's object and the record is derived from it; a refresh that republished them
+          # from the issue-driven seed would make the pack disagree with the published register
+          # the moment a unit closes (measured on the automated refresh #665, 2026-11-24).
+          # `design-pack` checks the committed pack, and `docs/design/scripts/publish-data.sh`
+          # (the live, read-only publish) owns the record, the register and the pages.
           python3 docs/design/scripts/build-docs.py --check
-          if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- docs/design/data seed/programme.json docs/design/docs docs/evidence/rework-register.json docs/evidence/standards-findings.json)" ]; then
+          if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- docs/design/data seed/programme.json)" ]; then
```

### P2 — the pack test validates the published pack

`scripts/ci/tests/standards_pack.sh` now validates the committed `docs/design/data/standards.json`, `docs/design/data/rework.json`, `docs/evidence/rework-register.json` and `docs/evidence/standards-findings.json`:

- schema (`design-standards/v1`, `conveyor-rework/v1`, `conveyor-v1-findings/v1`), summary arithmetic, unique package keys, required fields (`dod`, `evidence`), every `acceptance_command` naming its package key, every unresolved mandatory artefact naming a package the register carries;
- `docs/design/data/rework.json` equals `docs/evidence/rework-register.json` as JSON (the carriers differ only in key order/escaping — `check-data.cjs` compares them the same way);
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-standards.cjs --data docs/design/data --documents docs/design`;
- the `materialise-rework.py` dry-run plans against the committed register;
- the generators' two-run determinism is kept as a self-test (run1 vs run2), never compared to the committed pack.

The byte-comparisons of a snapshot-derived register or record against the committed pack are gone, so a branch whose issue-driven seed moves cannot redden `design-pack` by construction.

`docs/design/README.md` records the ownership boundary, and `publish-standards.sh` refuses a write when the snapshot derives a register different from the published one (the seed has moved past the last live publish).

## Evidence

### (a) `standards_pack.sh` green at this head

`bash scripts/ci/tests/standards_pack.sh` → exit 0:

```
standards_pack: 592 artefacts (230 evidenced, 173 partial, 189 absent), 216 findings, 432 packages (430 open); the committed record, register and findings agree
standards_pack: OK — the committed pack is a valid published record and register
```

### (b) the moved-seed case that is red on main

On this tree, the issue registry moved one unit — `#2` (S02, whose measured coverage is already `built`) — to `CLOSED` and `scripts/build-programme-seed.py`, `scripts/build-coverage.py` and `scripts/build-v2-coverage.py` ran. S02's seed status moved `active` → `closed` (live snapshot stays `active`).

- **HEAD's test on that moved tree: exit 1** — `run1/data/rework.js docs/design/data/rework.js differ: char 301111, line 8594` → `standards_pack: docs/design/data/rework.js is stale or missing` (the #665/#670 class);
- **this PR's test on the same tree: exit 0** — it validates the committed published pack;
- **the whole 31-command `design-pack` list on that moved tree: 31/31 green** (`check-console` retried once under machine-wide browser contention; it passed).

The scratch move was reverted before committing (`git restore`; the tree is clean at 95f65181).

### (c) workflow lint

Closes #86

## What

T15 — tool authoring and BYO tools on the tool platform (SPEC_V2 §11.3–§11.6, §11.8; D42, D43, D50; issue #86). One migration, one authoring/BYO module pair, two acceptance suites.

- **P1 spec → published tool.** `toolkits.import_openapi` and `tool_authoring.draft` write a `governed_asset(kind='tool_draft')`; `tool_authoring.validate` / `.test` / `.review` gate it; `tool_authoring.publish` writes one immutable toolkit version whose tools dispatch through the broker's registered-destination arm. Publication refuses wildcard egress, a free-form input schema and a write with no idempotency declaration; a missing effect class publishes as `read`.
- **P2 publication approval.** The publication gate reads the tenant's `approval_policy` row for `tool_authoring.publish`: approver kind, quorum (`required_decisions`) and expiry, defaulting to one human decision. A destructive tool needs a named approver at review and a policy that names a human — a waiver or an auto policy is refused. The published version is recorded on the approval (`meta.published`).
- **P3 BYO MCP.** `toolkits.register_mcp` registers a streamable-HTTP endpoint with its egress allowlist and credential alias; `toolkits.discover_mcp` discovers its tools into a draft (RMCP's client transport on the existing 3.9.0 pin — no second stack); `tool_binding.tool_keys` exposes only the bound subset; the broker uses the binding's credential alias, records one `tool_call` row naming the binding and one `tool.called` event. A call-time `url` is refused by the now-closed `tools.call` schema.
- **P4 effect ceiling.** `tool_authoring.publish` with the authoring job's own `binding_id` refuses a draft above that binding's ceiling; `tool_authoring.promote` refuses a tenant admin and requires a development project whose review gate is approved.
- **Infrastructure.** Migration `0070` (0069 belongs to T8); `tool_source`, `tool_promotion`, `tool.source_id`/`destination`, `tool_binding.tool_keys`, `tool_call.binding_id`, `approval_policy.required_decisions`, and the `tool_draft` kind. Issue #86 is `acceptance-blocked-by` #557, not construction-blocked. Catalogue reads and the binding-creation actions are #557's surface, so this PR does not build a second one: the acceptance tests seed the `tool_binding` row they need (the same fixture shape T13's `tool_platform.rs` uses) and read catalogue rows through `conveyor-store`. Closes #80

## What

T6 delivers the development project: the self-development path on conveyor itself. A development
project is an ordinary `project` row with a charter that records **one repo, one lane, the
implementing principal, the gate set and the measuring instrument before any branch**. Every
delivery step is then one immutable evidence row in §9.1's order — branch → PR → CI verdict →
independent review → merge → rollback plan → deploy → live check — and closure links them all.

- **P1 delivery path** — `development_projects.charter|record_step|review_gate|merge_gate|
  deploy_gate|close|get`. `record_step` refuses a skipped predecessor; `close` requires every
  required step plus the three approved gates and writes the closure record (lane, PR, CI run,
  reviewer, merge SHA, deployed digest, live check). A red CI verdict refuses the merge gate, is
  recorded by the invoke layer and never opens a gate.
- **P2 cannot change its own gates** — `development_projects.change_judging_surface` refuses the
  project's own attempt to change its gate set, approval policy or instrument, naming the surface
  and the governance approver set, and leaves the charter unchanged. The one decision writer
  refuses the implementing principal on a development gate; the gate stays pending for another
  person. Auto-merge **extends the existing `approval_policy` surface** (migration adds
  `approver_kind`, typed `conditions`, `expires_at`) rather than forking a second one: it defaults
  to `human`, requires typed terms and a future expiry, and the merge gate reads kind/conditions/
  expiry from the row. An eligible policy records a `decided_by_kind = 'rule'` decision.
- **P3 rollback** — the deploy gate refuses a deploy with no recorded rollback plan, or with an
  untested one, naming the missing evidence. `development_projects.rollback` records an exercised
  rollback with both digests and the 200 at the restored revision; closure carries it.

Migration `0068_development_project.sql` adds `development_project`, `development_step`,
`development_closure`, one pending-gate index and the policy columns. The six offline scenarios
live in `crates/actions/tests/development_project.rs`; domain unit tests cover the step order,
evidence shapes and auto-merge condition arithmetic. P1.3/P3.2 are live and are recorded on the
issue after the deploy, per the issue's deployment-prerequisite section.

## Why

`docs/SPEC_V2.md` §5.2 (project types), §5.4 (gates/dual control), §6.4 (development project),
§9.1 (the nine steps), §9.3 (the system cannot grade its own homework), §12 T6, D34. Issue #80.
The measured gaps this closes: no `development` project path, no PR/CI/merge/deploy evidence rows,
no `approval_policy` reader for an earned auto-merge, and no deploy refusal for a missing rollback.

**Decisions recorded from the issue's open questions (Defaults applied):**

pulls.body:
Closes #661

## Why

A streaming `POST /api/chat/completions` sent **no response bytes** until the upstream's first
chunk: `stream_completion` awaited `router().stream()` (whose `open_stream` awaits
`chunks.next()`) before building the SSE response. On the local 27B backend that is the whole
prefill (~63 s), so the site chat's first-byte budget expired before its spinner had anything to
render. The incident fix raised the caller's budget; this is the router-side fix the follow-up
promised.

## What

- The open future is now owned (`Arc<RouterService>`, cloned request/hops/`x-provider`) and raced
  against `INFERENCE_ROUTER_STREAM_HEADERS_GRACE_MS` (default **35 000**; `0` disables).
- **Inside the grace**, behaviour is byte-identical to `main`: a shed/refusal keeps its HTTP
  status (502/503/404), so retrying callers still see a retryable code. The config loader rejects a
  non-zero grace below `provider_slot_wait_seconds`, so a 30 s shed can never silently become a
  mid-stream error.
- **After the grace**, the SSE head goes out immediately and `GracefulStream` yields
  `: keepalive\n\n` at once and every `INFERENCE_ROUTER_STREAM_KEEPALIVE_MS` (default **10 000**,
  under every caller's 30 s idle watchdog) while the open is pending. When the upstream opens it
  hands off to the existing `RelayStream` — same frames, same one-row booking, same `[DONE]`.
- An open that fails after the head becomes `data: {"error": …}` + `data: [DONE]` and the same
  never-opened ledger row (`stream_status` null, the refusal's code as `status`).
- A client that leaves while the open is pending books one `client_disconnect` row.

## Tests

- `a_slow_open_flushes_headers_and_keepalives` — the head returns before a 400 ms first chunk,
  body starts with the comment, then the unchanged five data frames + `[DONE]`.
- `keepalives_are_emitted_while_the_open_is_pending` — ≥2 comment frames before the first delta.
- `a_refusal_after_the_grace_ends_with_an_error_frame` — 200 + error frame + `[DONE]`.
- `a_refusal_inside_the_grace_keeps_its_status` — identical status to the `grace=0` baseline.
- `an_open_that_fails_after_the_head_is_flushed_is_still_one_row` (DB) — the row keeps `502`,
  `stream_status` null.
- `a_disconnect_while_the_open_is_pending_is_booked` (DB) — `client_disconnect`, no hash.
- `a_stream_is_relayed_chunk_for_chunk_and_terminated` (existing) still passes unchanged; the
  config loader's four new validation tests pass.

## Verification

- `preflight.yml` at this head; `cargo test -p conveyor-inference-router --lib` and
  `--test write_path` locally.
- Deployment is a gitops digest bump of `clusters/strato/services/inference-router/rust-deployment.yaml`
  after merge; the live time-to-headers check is recorded on the issue once Flux rolls.

## Rollback

Set `INFERENCE_ROUTER_STREAM_HEADERS_GRACE_MS=0` (no rebuild), or revert this PR.

## What this unit does

S21 step 9 — the work package's handoff. One explicit action, `cards.assign`, in one transaction: it
sets the card's active, tenant-scoped job binding, records what the receiver must know as one hot
`work_package_memory` row, and starts the card's bound run through the same path `runs.create` uses
(andon, binding pin, attempt, `run.execute` enqueue, `run.created`). One live root run per card
(SPEC_V2 §6.6.5): a card with a live run refuses `409 card_has_live_run` naming it, before any
write, with `uq_run_live` the race backstop. The handoff presents the card's version
(If-Match/`_version`) like `cards.update`/`cards.move`: a stale card is `412`. Scopes
`cards:write` + `runs:write`; agent-reachable. No migration, no new scope, no new event kind.

`memory.remember`'s body is extracted as `remember_tx` and `runs.create`'s run-creation body as
`create_bound_run_tx`, so both entry points share one writer and one path; their existing suites are
unchanged. The handoff note is an ordinary hot row the next run's compiled prompt selects, with the
row id inside `prompt_sha256`.

## Evidence at the head (`01c224d2`)

- `card_handoff` **11 passed** (14 with the support module); `prompt_catalogue` **7 passed** (the
  handoff row is selected by the facts read); `registry` **12 passed** (531 actions, internal 513,
  external 18); `parity_http_mcp` **7 passed** (the handoff sample answers 201 over both transports).
- `clippy -p conveyor-actions -p conveyor-store -p conveyor-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  exit 0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` exit 0.
- `served-spec.lock.json` **562 operations**, `cards.assign` present, `--check-lock` exit 0.
- `build-coverage --check`, `build-v2-coverage --check`, `build-programme-seed --check`,
  `check-docs.cjs`, `build-docs --check` (142 sources) and `board.py --dry-run` all green.
- Five reversal proofs fired and restored: the memory insert, the live-run pre-check, the binding
  check, the andon check and the note's source (`docs/evidence/S21-HANDOFF.md`).
- Found in flight: the first cut passed the freshly read version to the UPDATE instead of the
  precondition's version; `a_stale_card_is_refused` caught a silently accepted stale If-Match, and
  the handler now passes the parsed version.

Design: S21 §21, ADR 0017, CONTRACT §27, DATA-ARCH §2.29. Receipt: `docs/evidence/S21-HANDOFF.md`.

Closes #649

## Summary

T18-3b makes the Authoring destination **operate** the T17 family instead of only reading it. The
screen now carries the mock's four tabs — **Intake queue · Draft catalogue · Review & publish ·
Dependency status** — and every step is a governed action:

- **Intake queue** records a brief and its document references (`authoring.intake`) and lists the
  intakes the catalogue can name, each with its draft count and state.
- **Draft catalogue** writes one asset from an intake (`authoring.draft`); §5.7's dependency
  refusal is shown verbatim and no row is created.
- **Review & publish** requests the `authoring.review` gate (`approvals.request`), records the
  review an approved gate carries (`authoring.review`) and releases the asset
  (`authoring.publish`).
- **Dependency status** resolves every draft's `depends_on` against the published catalogue and
  renders the §5.7 order rail.

No fixture row is rendered; every empty state names the action that would create the row, and
every refusal is shown with the server's code and field.

## Two measured corrections to the issue (carried, not dropped)

1. **There is no intake read.** The family registers `authoring.intake|draft|review|publish|assets`
   and no intake list (`crates/actions/src/authoring/mod.rs:228-371`; the store has
   `intake_create_tx` only, `crates/store/src/authoring.rs:238`). The queue is therefore the draft
   catalogue grouped by `AssetOut.intake_id`, plus the intake this screen has just recorded from
   its own action's response. The brief/sources read is carried by **#655** (T17b).
2. **The dependency refusal is at the draft, not at publish.** `asset_draft_tx` calls
   `ensure_dependencies_published` (`crates/store/src/authoring.rs:310`; the doc comment at
   `:267-268` says "enforced at the draft, not at publish"). `asset_publish_tx` re-checks at
   `:450`, but no API path can unpublish a dependency, so the refusal is only reachable when the
   draft is attempted. P2 was renamed *dependency-ordered drafting*; its scenario and `Verify:`
   name are unchanged.

Review still needs what it always needed: an approved `authoring.review` gate whose
`meta->>'target'` is the asset id (`crates/store/src/authoring.rs:55,365-396`), decided by a human
other than the requester — the spec decides it as the seed's second admin, `dev:reviewer`
(`apps/web/e2e/helpers.ts:98`), because `approval_policies.set` refuses a non-destructive action
(`crates/actions/src/control/policies.rs:122`).

## Evidence

| `the authoring destination shows the live catalogue` | `npx playwright test e2e/authoring.spec.ts` | PASS | `9bba6f65` |
| `the intake queue reads the tenant's rows` | same | PASS | `9bba6f65` |
| `an unpublished dependency refuses the draft` | same | PASS | `9bba6f65` |
| `a reviewed draft publishes behind its gate` | same (gate decided as `dev:reviewer`) | PASS | `9bba6f65` |
| `the authoring screen has no horizontal page scroll at 1280 and 390` | same | PASS | `9bba6f65` |
| the whole browser suite, as `web.yml` runs it | `npx playwright test` — fresh Postgres 18, dev seed, process catalogue, model stub, serve + worker | **120 passed** | `9bba6f65` |

## Checks

- The web crate's compile check for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (rustup 1.100.0, the toolchain the pin
  names) — passes.
- Clippy over the web crate with `-D warnings` — no finding in `screens/authoring.rs`; the crate's
  pre-existing findings in `architecture.rs`, `cockpit.rs`, `approvals.rs`, `boards.rs` and

Closes #77

## What

T5 Kata, P1–P4, as one unit on `issue/77-t5-kata` (P1 commit `29197235`; P2–P4 commit `2a525681`; the CI-found corrections and the merged-main integration follow on the same branch, head `e21cb448`).

- **P1**: the kata is an ordinary job on the V2 spine. The kata migration adds `kata`, `kata_get`, `kata_measurement`; `kata.open|get|observe|analyse|hypothesise|propose|measure` run the Gets in order; the hypothesis is an atomic pre-registration and `kata.measure` reads only the locked held-out (`test`) split.
- **P2**: `kata.measure` direction-corrects the delta with the metric's `better` and compares it with the threshold recorded at open. A regression past the threshold restores the procedure key to the pre-kata version pinned at open, retires the candidate and appends an append-only `kata_revert` with its reason and evidence. Flat or incomparable results adopt nothing.
- **P3**: `kata.adopt` is a person's gate. It declares `evals:approve` — `Admin` literally, never the machine role `kata_executor` — and refuses any non-`user` principal. Only a measured improvement is adoptable; the decision is an append-only `kata_adoption` row.
- **P4**: `kata.open` refuses without a named instrument and a success threshold, naming every missing piece (422 `kata_not_measurable`); the instrument's split must already be locked; a second open for a live signature is 409 `kata_signature_open` naming the existing kata. The owner lookup runs after `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`, so the duplicate refusal is a 409 rather than a 500.

The final tree merges `origin/main` at `a8f67c3e` (authoring and meetings). The kata migrations are **`0066_kata.sql`** and **`0067_kata_gate.sql`** (main owns 0064 authoring and 0065 meetings); the instrument may precede the prediction, `baseline_version_id` is pinned, and `kata_revert`/`kata_adoption` are append-only.

## Acceptance evidence

| Scenario | Test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_gets.rs::the_prediction_is_recorded_before_the_measurement` | pass locally (`kata_gets` 4/4); queue run is the final gate | e21cb448 |
| P1.2 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_measure.rs::a_procedure_change_is_measured_on_the_held_out_split` | pass locally (`kata_measure` 4/4); queue run | e21cb448 |
| P2.1 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_revert.rs::a_measured_regression_reverts_the_candidate` | pass locally (`kata_revert` 5/5); queue run | e21cb448 |
| P2.2 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_revert.rs::a_flat_or_incomparable_result_adopts_nothing` | pass locally (`kata_revert` 5/5); queue run | e21cb448 |
| P3.1 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_adopt.rs::the_kata_cannot_approve_its_own_adoption` | pass locally (`kata_adopt` 4/4); queue run | e21cb448 |
| P4.1 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_open.rs::a_kata_without_an_instrument_is_not_opened` | pass locally (`kata_open` 5/5); queue run | e21cb448 |
| P4.2 | `crates/actions/tests/kata_open.rs::a_second_kata_for_an_open_signature_is_refused` | pass locally (`kata_open` 5/5); queue run | e21cb448 |

The five kata binaries were run green on the kata tree (real Docker Postgres 18); the merged-main commit only renumbers the migrations and merges main's lists, and the queue's run exercises them again.

Merged-tree proofs at `e21cb448`:

- `registry.rs`/`api/lib.rs`: both sides' actions kept — **538 actions, internal 520, external 18**; `docs/design/data/actions.json` regenerated to 538.

## What

T19 — the decision forum — is implemented end to end. A meeting is a card plus a typed record:
`meeting_type` policy (version-pinned), the meeting instance, agenda items that resolve existing
approvals/register items/assets/cadence slots, attendance for humans and job bindings, one live
typed position per participant per item, and `close_item`'s outcome arithmetic over those positions
and the linked approval's stricter policy. Commitments and actions become cards; minutes are a
chaired `governed_asset(kind='minutes')`; the human seat is available in the web room, over
Telegram and over MCP; participant-hours enter the D52 roll-up; a closed forum with no decision is
a retirement candidate; and the `/meetings` destination ships both in the real app and the design
pack.

- `migrations/0065_meetings.sql` (T17 owns 0064): the five tables, their RLS, the `approval_decision` participant
  extension, and the `minutes` governed-asset kind.

## Why

The meeting is where programme management, architecture, analysis and project management actually
decide, and until now only the resulting `approval` row survived. §6.8/D66 make the meeting a
first-class card whose record is rows — the deliberation, dissent, conditions and commitments —
without creating a second decision store.

Closes #626

## What changed

**The router no longer substitutes a model.** The chain path answers `404 unknown_model` for a name
no provider declares. A model id exactly one enabled provider serves auto-pins to it (the metrics
fixture's `metric-model` is the canonical case); the router-pick sentinels (`""`, `default`,
`gemma`) still ride the chain, and a `shared_aliases` entry rides it by design (that path used to
503 `steering_alias_unavailable` before reaching the chain — fixed). `X-Provider` pinned dispatch is
unchanged. Live measurement before the change: 86 `claude-sonnet-5-5` calls were answered by
pgx-local over 30 days.

**The documented OpenAI knobs are forwarded**: `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, `stop` (string or
array), `parallel_tool_calls`, `chat_template_kwargs`. A provider whose catalog entry forces a
reasoning dialect overrides only that key (`enable_thinking` / `reasoning_effort`); the caller's
other keys survive. `ChatMessage.content` is now optional (absent = null) and every null is sent
upstream as `""` — the router half of #620.

**Pacing.** A queue shed is a 503 with `Retry-After: 5`; an upstream 429/503 is a 503 carrying the
upstream's own `Retry-After` (delay-seconds or HTTP-date); every other upstream failure stays 502.
Chain exhaustion carries the hint only when the failure names one.

**Conveyor's clients.** The copilot retries a router 502 three times (250/500 ms) under the same
`(turn, round)` idempotency key — the engine releases the claim on failure, so the replay
re-executes; `parse_answer` stays outside the loop, so a paid-for malformed answer is never
re-bought. The engine now distinguishes `action-upstream-unreachable` (never answered — never
replayed) from `action-upstream-failed` (answered 5xx — safe to replay). The scientific client
retries 429/5xx with the same rules and never a read timeout.

**Test harness.** The copilot stub now runs on its own OS thread and runtime (#476's prescribed
fix), which also removed the round-cap test's transport flake (3/3 green after the change; it
failed 1/4 before).

## Evidence

- `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-inference-router` — all binaries green (150 lib tests + 11
  integration binaries), including the new 404/sentinel/shared-alias/Retry-After/payload tests.
- `conveyor-inference-router --check-lock` — `lock OK: 27 operations` after the regenerated
  `contract/openapi.lock.json` (36 schemas: the capture's 35 + `AnyObject`).
- `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-scientific --lib clients::inference` — 4/4, including the
  retry-then-succeed and the 400-sends-once cases.
- `cargo-guard.py test -p conveyor-api --test copilot_retry` — 5/5 consecutive runs; the
  round-cap, turn and truncated binaries green 3/3 (rounds) and 1/1.
- `clippy -p conveyor-inference-router -p conveyor-actions -p conveyor-api -p conveyor-scientific
  --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.
- Preflight: run 45261477058 success on this head.

## The live row this depends on (done before merge)

`capability_agent` carried one foreign `model_ref` (`cap.kanban_coach.handle_error.v2`,
tenant `nonagentic`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`). Migrated through the product action
(`capability_agents.update --if-match 1` via the worker CLI); it now reads `local-llm`, version 2,
status active. The other 123 agents already read `local-llm`; the `eval` table is empty.

After Flux rolls: `model:"claude-sonnet-5-5"` must 404, `model:"default"`/omitted must still answer
`pgx-local`, and a `stop`-bounded request must actually cut — recorded in the issue.

## What this lands

S21 step 8 — the **Request** source, the fourth source of SPEC_V2 §4.5. The current step's declared action, PDDL action text, **resolved input**, **declared outputs**, `on_result` and gate become one request document:

```json
{"step":{"position":2,"attempt":1},"action":"agent.run","action_text":"…","input":{…},"outputs":["output"],"on_result":"fail","gate":"gate.precheck"}
```

- It renders in the process (Request) section as `request (data; never instruction): <json>`, whole, inside the section budget (over budget refuses with the measurement — no truncation).
- The same document is the `laya.judge` case input on the process path, so L1 and L2 cannot disagree about what was asked.
- The store reads `run_step.input` (persisted at claim) and the frozen `process_step.outputs`/`action_text`/`gate_kind` in one primary-key read. The compiler reads; it never re-resolves the template and never writes.
- A synthetic run-level `internal_agent` `agent.run` step contributes **none** of its executor envelope; its Request stays the release definition, and the run-level judge now receives that release request from the same `release_request` builder.
- The request is inside the compiled text, so it is inside `prompt_sha256`.
- **No migration**, no new action, scope, route or served-spec operation.

Closes #637

## What changed

`crates/store/tests/schedule.rs::defaults_are_seeded_once_per_tenant_and_are_idempotent` asserted that a `materialise` call with a fresh `Utc::now()` creates nothing right after `seed_defaults`. `seed_defaults` stamps `next_run_at` from its **own** `Utc::now()` (`crates/store/src/schedule.rs:seed_defaults`), and `Cron::next_after` truncates to the next whole minute. When seeding lands in the last moments of a minute, the test's later instant has already crossed the seeded `* * * * *` boundary, so those rows are legitimately due — the test failed once on the #604 merge (#625) with `future schedules create no job` at `crates/store/tests/schedule.rs:91`.

The test now derives the boundary from the seeded rows instead of the wall clock:

- `earliest = min(next_run_at)` for the tenant.
- At `earliest - 1 s`, `materialise` creates no job (the original property, now deterministic).
- At exactly `earliest`, exactly the enabled schedules with `next_run_at <= earliest` materialise (the other half of the boundary, extended coverage).
- No sleep, no skipped assertion.

## Production change

**None.** This is a test-clock defect, not a production race: a schedule seeded just before its boundary is supposed to fire on the first tick at or after that boundary. `seed_defaults`, `Cron::next_after` and `materialise` are unchanged.

Closes #604.

## Why

`one_approval_is_multicast_then_the_losers_are_closed` failed three times in CI shards and once in
the merge queue (`FAIL [12.452s]`, run 45172597794) with `timed out waiting for the webhook's two
sends`. The 10 s poll budget was the visible symptom; the defect underneath is an ordering race:

- `offer_interaction` enqueues `delivery.send` for the webhook offer.
- The test recorded the decision and ticked `interaction.close` without waiting for that request
  POST.
- `interaction_close` expires every live delivery of the offer. When the close sweep won, the
  request delivery was expired before it was sent, so the stub could never see two hits and the
  final wait was unsatisfiable — a longer deadline alone would hang and still fail.

## Change (test-only)

`apps/server/tests/interaction_dispatch.rs`:

1. Wait on the webhook stub's **first** hit before the human answer is recorded — the request is
   delivered before the answer can race the close sweep. The final wait still requires both the
   request and the closure notice, unchanged.
2. Replace `wait_for`'s fixed 100 × 100 ms = 10 s budget with a 30 s `Instant` deadline polled
   every 100 ms. No sleep-based skip, no weakened assertion.
3. Refresh the second-wave comment, whose premise (the first wave racing its own send) no longer
   holds.

No production code changed: the webhook `SEND_TIMEOUT` is per-POST and was not the failure; the
worker queue delay was.

## Verification

- Local gate: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1`,
  `git diff --check` — all green at `d1f4fcd`.
- Compile/clippy: preflight run 45253555977 (this branch).
- Test verdict: the PR's `checks-shard (1)` runs
  `conveyor-server::interaction_dispatch::one_approval_is_multicast_then_the_losers_are_closed`
  alongside the full suite, which is the load that produced the flake.
- Acceptance command: `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test interaction_dispatch --locked -- --exact one_approval_is_multicast_then_the_losers_are_closed`.

## Risk

Test-only, one file. The multicast/one-winner semantics and every assertion are unchanged; the
only new observable is that the test now waits for the offer it is about to close.

## What

pgx vLLM behind the inference router reasons on every call, and reasoning tokens count against `max_tokens`; a `finish_reason:"length"` reply can still look complete, and a tool call's `function.arguments` string can be cut mid-JSON. `model_reply` read neither, so a partial tool call could execute with fabricated `{}` arguments.

- `length` → non-retryable 422 `inference-truncated` (a 5xx would make the workflow tick retry the same capped call).
- empty/whitespace arguments → `{}`; a non-empty unparseable arguments string → non-retryable 422 `inference-bad-tool-arguments`.
- seed model refs `router/medium|high|small` → router tiers `tier-medium|tier-high|tier-flash`. Under an active policy the router matches the string against `hop.model` and would refuse `router/*` with 400 `outside_policy`.

## Evidence

- preflight (compile + tests) green: https://github.com/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs/45135930305
- live through the deployed API (`completions.create`, sealed `inference.token`, `model:"tier-medium"`): `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, `get_weather({"city":"Amsterdam"})`, `served_provider:"pgx-local"`, `served_model:"local-llm"`; replaying the assistant tool call with `content:""` + `role:"tool"` returned `finish_reason:"stop"` with the answer.
- `router/medium` also resolves today (no active tenant policy), so the seed change is forward-looking rather than a live break.

Closes #12

## What

P1–P5 of S18's executor-backed producers. The conveyor producer drives the real `agent.run` loop against the configuration pinned at start; the baseline arm is a bounded one-shot source/edit producer; the process arm hosts each case as a `benchmark` card and runs the published `swebench-fix` process; `eval_runs.start` accepts an `agent_run` subject through the executor; and the improvement job observes, compares and starts runs through the public actions.

This PR carries P3d's collection: a terminal process run's typed `RunOut.output.patch` becomes the case patch, hashed and recorded `ok`, so the existing grading path proceeds. A failed/cancelled run, a null/absent patch, an empty answer, `NONE`, or an over-cap patch is `no_attempt` — never an invented patch. Collection spends no attempt and starts no second run: the attempt was spent by the start tick, and `record_produced_tx` only writes a still-pending case.

## Why

Issue #12; plan `docs/plans/slices/S18-kata-improvement.md` §5 §6 §7; audit `docs/evidence/2026-11-10-plan-audit.md` §W11 §W14. Owner chose the typed contract 2026-11-23 (issue comment 7095061697): `benchmark` card → `swebench-fix` process → `RunOut.output.patch`. The plan's stale `benchmark_arm` target is corrected to `conveyor-api` (this issue's DoD), with the design-pack index regenerated.

Closes #612

## What this adds

S21 step 7 — the run's episodic memory. The prompt's Memory source gains its third class (the run's own prior steps), `memory.recall` stops serving the derived digest as a hot row, and a process run's terminal attempt is proved to reach the next run's prompt.

- **P1 — the run's prior steps reach the prompt.** `PromptFacts.prior_steps` renders ahead of the card's rows in the one `## Memory` section: `- [step/<status>#<position>.<attempt>] <action> <status>: <body>`. Selection is the run's own `run_step` rows — `succeeded`/`failed` only, `(position, attempt)` lexicographically before the current step (so a retry sees its earlier failed attempt), ordered, bounded by the selector's `step_limit` (default 8, max 32) with `include_steps` (default true). A child reads only its own rows. Bodies render whole; an over-budget section refuses `SectionOverBudget` with the measured size — there is no truncation path. The semantic `position.attempt` identity is in the text, so the selection is in the prompt hash.
- **P2 — `memory.recall` keeps the digest out of hot.** `hot_for_card_tx` filters `kind <> 'digest'`; the digest remains reachable through the prompt selector's `include_digest` and the cold/strata read.
- **P3 — the process attempt is proved.** The terminal attempt writer is #599's (every path); this unit proves a process root run's attempt is read by the next run on the card. No second writer.

No migration: `run_step` and `work_package_memory` exist and the selection uses `run_step_run_idx`; the selector's new members live in the existing `prompt_section.selector` jsonb. No served schema moved (`--check-lock` exit 0).

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `process_agent_resolved::a_second_step_reads_the_first_steps_output` — step 2's system message carries `[step/succeeded#1.1]` and step 1's output | pass |
| P1.2 | `prompt_catalogue::the_runs_prior_steps_are_selected_and_isolated` — the current position's earlier failed attempt is selected with its error | pass |
| P1.3 | the same test — a child run's prompt contains none of the parent's steps | pass |
| P1.4 | `prompt_memory::prior_steps_are_deterministic_and_hashed` — same facts, same bytes; a changed body or a changed `position.attempt` changes the hash | pass |
| P1.5 | `prompt_memory::a_prior_step_over_budget_refuses_with_the_measurement` — `SectionOverBudget { kind: Memory, measured, limit }`, never a clip | pass |
| P2.1 | `memory::a_digest_covers_the_unconsolidated_rows_once` — flipped from "three hot rows, digest first" to "two hot rows, no digest" | pass |
| P2.2 | the same test — `select_for_prompt_tx` still appends exactly one digest | pass |
| P3.1 | `process_agent_resolved::a_second_step_reads_the_first_steps_output` — the next run on the card compiles `[attempt/system#…] … run <id> attempt 1 succeeded` | pass |
| P3.2 | `run_memory::only_root_card_runs_record_memory` — a child writes none | pass |

Two issue scenarios are asserted inside a shared-fixture test rather than two files: P1.2/P1.3 in `the_runs_prior_steps_are_selected_and_isolated`, and P3.1 at the end of `a_second_step_reads_the_first_steps_output`. No scenario is skipped.

## Measured at f65ec3a5 (later heads add only generated/doc syncs: `cf5a643a` the republished register, `c55fea68` the architecture page's embedded diagram source)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `crates/domain/tests/prompt_memory.rs` | 8 passed |
| `crates/store/tests/prompt_catalogue.rs` | 5 passed |

## Reversal proofs

Each guard was disabled, its tests turned red, then restored and re-run green.

| Guard removed | Test that turned red |
|---|---|
| the prior-step render arm | `prompt_memory::the_runs_prior_steps_render_before_the_card_rows`, `prior_steps_are_deterministic_and_hashed` |
| the prior-step selection in `facts_for_run_tx` | `prompt_catalogue::the_runs_prior_steps_are_selected_and_isolated`; `process_agent_resolved::a_second_step_reads_the_first_steps_output` |
| the `kind <> 'digest'` filter in `hot_for_card_tx` | `memory::a_digest_covers_the_unconsolidated_rows_once` |

## Generated / docs

- ADR 0015; CONTRACT §25; DATA-ARCH §2.27 and §3.2; S21 §18 and its header/§17 next-lane; the S21 index row; the run-sequence diagram (three Memory classes) and its two SVGs; `docs/evidence/S21-MEMORY.md` with the measured table and reversal proofs.

- `c55fea68` syncs `docs/design/architecture.js`'s embedded `run-sequence` source to the `.mmd`; the design-pack failure was `check-architecture.cjs:137` (source drift), not the console flake that appears at another locator.

- The first preflight caught a missing `prior_steps` field in the domain lib-test initializer (the integration suite builds its facts with `..PromptFacts::default()` and hid it from a targeted run). Fixed at `f65ec3a5`; the domain lib suite passes 302/302 and the preflight is green.

- Prompt hashes move for process runs with prior steps; that is the contract change, and the tests that pin a compiled process prompt were updated explicitly, not relaxed.
- A routinely large step output can make the Memory section refuse; the remedy is a larger `budget_chars` or a shorter step output. The ADR records the decision.
- Out of scope (issue #612): card-driven run creation, `memory.remember` write-back, automatic apply of an L1-accepted draft, the step's `input_template`/`outputs` as Request, any budget mechanism (#526's), parent-run memory in a child, UI, PDDL storage, a second compiler.

Closes #611

## Why

The post-#11 gold probe is 0/3: matplotlib's `[pdf]`/`[eps]` comparisons die with
`Error: /invalidfileaccess in --run--` on `/testbed/result_images/...`.

Read-only probes in `swe-bench` on the three failing images (`matplotlib-23412`, `-23476`,
`-24627`) disprove the PATH-shadow theory and measure the real cause:

- The `/bench-bin/gs` shim **is** what the eval resolves (`command -v gs` → `/bench-bin/gs`);
  there is no `gs` in `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/bin` or `/opt/miniconda3/bin`.
- The image's GPL Ghostscript 9.55 refuses **every** read and write under `/testbed`
  (`invalidfileaccess`, `Last OS error: Permission denied`) with no permit, with
  `--permit-file-read=/testbed/`, `--permit-file-write=/testbed/`,
  `--permit-file-control=/testbed/`, exact-file permits and globs, and with `-dNOSAFER`
  (this build ignores it). The same binary reads and writes `/tmp` normally, and the pod is
  root writing `/testbed` from Python.

## What

`/bench-bin/gs` now runs a Python relay (`gs_relay.py`, shipped in the same wrapper
ConfigMap). It mirrors every `/testbed` literal in matplotlib's interactive PostScript
stream (`<< /OutputFile (DEST) >> setpagedevice (SRC) run flush`) under a private `/tmp`
root, runs the real Ghostscript there, and copies the outputs back **before** forwarding
Ghostscript's prompt — matplotlib checks the destination exists as soon as it reads the
prompt. Non-interactive calls (`--version`, file operands, `-c`) are exec'd unchanged.

No change to test selection, tolerances, gold semantics, the P1 security context, the
image digests, or the runner script's PATH ordering.

## Evidence

- Local gate: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked`, `py_compile`, and a
  protocol stub test (banner → one `setpagedevice` request → output copied back before the
  forwarded prompt; stale destination replaced; source mirrored).
- The manifest test (`benchmark_jobs`) asserts the ConfigMap ships both files verbatim, the
  shim execs the relay, the relay names `/usr/bin/gs`, `/testbed`, `tempfile.mkdtemp` and
  `setpagedevice`, and the mount/PATH-order assertions are unchanged.
- The live acceptance is deployment-gated: P2 (3/3 resolved) and P3 (full gold + empty
  controls) run on the digest built from the merge.

## What

The registry refresh fell one derived artefact short. After `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` it regenerated the programme seed, the measured coverage (to a fixpoint), the v2 coverage and checked the docs — and stopped. `docs/design/data/rework.js`, the standards record, the artefact pages and the two ledgers are derived from the same seed (and the checked-in v1 ledger), and `design-pack` compares them byte-for-byte. A refresh that changed the seed therefore left `rework.js` stale: PR #598's `design-pack` job went red at `publish-standards: docs/design/data/rework.js is stale or missing` (run 45089929073). #248 taught this block the coverage fixpoint; #547 added a second derived artefact and the workflow was never taught it.

The generator reads the committed snapshot: no database, no pandoc, no wall clock, and two runs are byte-identical.

## Verification

- Reproduced from the open generated PR's registry (`automation/issue-registry-20261122T223756Z`): after `build-programme-seed.py` + `build-coverage.py` + `build-v2-coverage.py`, `publish-standards.sh --check` fails on `docs/design/data/rework.js` — the exact #598 failure.

- `actionlint` on the changed workflow: clean.

Closes #599

## What this adds

S21 step 6 — the work package's run. The card now names its job binding, the run inherits it, and every terminal root run of a card records one work-package memory row that the next run's compiled prompt reads.

- **P1 — the card names its binding.** `cards.create` / `cards.update` accept `job_binding_id` (tenant-scoped, must be `active`; `422 job_binding_unusable` otherwise); `CardOut` exposes it; `cards.duplicate` leaves it unset. `runs.create` inherits the card's binding when the request omits one; an explicit conflicting binding is `422 card_binding_mismatch` before the INSERT; a card with no binding keeps the plain-run path. Pin/stale checks stay in `insert_run_tx`.
- **P2 — the terminal run writes its memory.** `store::run`'s hook (`enqueue_memory_consolidation` → `record_run_memory`) inserts one `work_package_memory` row (`kind=attempt`, `source=system`, `run_id` set, status + error class in `meta`) through the existing store writer, in the same transaction as the terminal status, then enqueues the existing per-card `memory.consolidate` job. A child run and a card-less run write none. **Every terminal path writes it**: `transition_run_tx`/`fail_run_tx`, `cancel_run_tx`, and both reap sweeps (`run.execute` and `process.step`) through `record_run_memory_for_id_tx`. A rolled-back finish leaves neither the status nor the row.
- **P3 — the live proof.** Two `#[ignore]`, env-gated tests: the model leg and the full router+laya leg. Both seal `inference.token` from `CONVEYOR_LIVE_INFERENCE_TOKEN` — the name the inference client resolves (`crates/actions/src/integrations/inference.rs:37`); the first cut sealed only `laya.token` and would still have answered 401.

**Found and fixed in flight (9f1d4558, 61ef8a8c).** The first implementation wrote the row only in `transition_run_tx`/`fail_run_tx`; `cancel_run_tx` and both reap sweeps moved runs to a terminal state without it. All three now record the attempt in the caller's transaction, with store and server proofs and three reversal proofs. The red `checks-shard (1)` was the same change surfacing in `process_agent_resolved`: its post-run recompile now legitimately includes the run's own attempt row; the test asserts the row, reconstructs the compile-time facts and compares the hash the model actually saw. An independent audit then found: `run_failure` mapped a transient database refusal in the terminal memory insert to a *permanent* job failure (a blip could strand a reaped run live behind `uq_run_live`), now retryable; and the P2.1 rolled-back clause had no test, now `run_memory::a_rolled_back_finish_leaves_neither`.

**Not this step:** the budget. `v1-p75-1`/`v1-w4a-1` are resolved on `origin/issue/526-u5a` (commit `8f1e5770`, `tool_budget.rs` 14 passed). The token ceiling (`max_tokens`, recorded-only) is that gate's residual. ADR 0014 records both decisions and why.

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `card_binding::a_cards_binding_reaches_its_run` | pass |
| P1.2 | `card_binding::a_conflicting_binding_is_refused` | pass |
| P1.3 | `card_binding::an_unusable_binding_is_refused_on_a_card` (draft + another tenant) | pass |
| P1.4 | `card_binding::card_out_carries_the_binding` | pass |
| P2.1 | `run_memory::a_succeeded_root_run_records_one_attempt` | pass |
| P2.1b | `run_memory::a_rolled_back_finish_leaves_neither` (the rolled-back clause) | pass |
| P2.2 | `run_memory::a_failed_run_records_its_class` | pass |
| P2.3 | `run_memory::only_root_card_runs_record_memory` (child + card-less) | pass |
| P2.4 | `internal_agent_runtime::the_next_run_prompt_reads_the_prior_attempt` | pass |
| P2.5 | `run_memory::a_cancelled_run_records_one_attempt` | pass |
| P2.6 | `run_memory::a_cancel_path_records_one_attempt` (`cancel_run_tx`) | pass |
| P2.7 | `run_memory::a_reaped_run_records_one_attempt` (`reap_dead_runs_tx`) | pass |
| P2.8 | `process_reap::a_dead_step_job_is_reaped_as_crashed_and_frees_the_card` (the process reap attempt) | pass |
| P3.1a | `internal_agent_runtime::the_live_model_executes_the_compiled_prompt` (`--ignored`) | **blocked: caller licence** |
| P3.1b | `internal_agent_runtime::the_live_run_executes_against_the_real_router_and_laya` (`--ignored`) | **blocked: caller licence** |

**Live proof: blocked on a credential, not on reachability.** Issue #599's P3.1 is scoped "(live; blocked only if the estate endpoints or credentials are unreachable)" and its DoD asks that the live verification be *recorded*. A tunnel to the estate's `inference-router` answers `/health` 200; a chat call answers `401 {"detail":"Caller licence could not be introspected; caller is not authorised"}` (`x-ir-error-classification: unlicensed`), which the executor records as `action-upstream-failed: inference answered 502`. The conveyor's bearer is the tenant's sealed `inference.token`; a throwaway test tenant has none, and minting a licence for one is a production licensing act with no cause. Details and the unblock path are in `docs/evidence/S21-RUN.md`. The tests are committed, refuse when their endpoints or tokens are unset, and now seal the correct `inference.token`; a stub is not reported as the proof.

| `crates/actions/tests/card_binding.rs` (new) | 7 passed |

## What

Implements S19's P1–P5 on one ledger-derived accounting model:

- **P1** — `eval.report` prices only the run's `inference_call` rows; unpriced usage is explicit. The report and the climb read the same model and agree to the cent.
- **P2** — a climb's spend includes subject, judge and failed calls; a regrade charges the subject once, never twice.
- **P3** — cache read/write tokens price at their class rates, or the row is explicitly unpriced (never full-rate input, never free).
- **P4** — the hard execution ceiling is enforced at the shared run boundary (`409 cost_ceiling_reached`); an unpriceable ceiling is refused (`422 ceiling_unpriceable`); the round-admission threshold is distinct (`409 round_admission_ceiling`).
- **P5** — `narrative_md` reads per-round cost and quality from the same model; the `train | test | Δ test` columns are gone.

The shared model is `crates/actions/src/eval/cost.rs` (`price_usage`, `price_call`, `spend_slot`, `ledger_spend_tx`); `report.rs`, `climbs.rs` and the climb actions call it rather than summing their own rows.

pulls.body:
## Why

Measured on the live router after Inkling-2-Mini went live: a streamed call relays
~57 ms-spaced chunks, but every reasoning token arrives as `content: null`. The
reasoning channel is parsed into `ChunkDelta`, which has **no field for it**, so it
is dropped at deserialisation:

```
{"role":"assistant","content":""}          ← upstream deltas were {"reasoning":"The user asks"}
{... "delta":{"content":"","role":"assistant","tool_calls":null} ...}
```

Consequences for a streaming consumer: silence while the model thinks, a client-side
TTFT that includes that silence, and no way to show or measure the trace. The
non-streamed path already normalises both upstream spellings
(`parse_openai_response`); the streamed path did not.

## What

- `ChunkDelta` gains `reasoning_content`, and `parse_openai_chunk` maps both upstream
  spellings onto it — vLLM's `reasoning` (what this build streams) and the
  OpenAI-compatible `reasoning_content`.
- **Presence is asymmetric on purpose.** Every other delta field is emitted even when
  null, because the pydantic reference was. `reasoning_content` is omitted when absent:
  the parity oracle's captured stream (`contract/golden/completion_stream.body`)
  predates the channel, so an inert chunk must serialise exactly as it always has.
  A reasoning-bearing chunk gains the field — strictly additive. The alternative
  (always emit `"reasoning_content":null`) would diff every frame of every stream
  against a fixture that can never contain it.
- The ledger capture keeps folding the answer only; the row records what the caller
  was answered, and folding the trace would change hashes for a comparison the oracle
  never made.

## Tests

Four new: an inert delta omits the key (and keeps the null convention on `tool_calls`);
the upstream `reasoning` spelling lands on `reasoning_content` and does not leak back
out; a parsed upstream reasoning chunk surfaces through `to_sse`; and a content-only
frame carries no reasoning key — the parity guard.

## Rollout

Image pin in the gitops counterpart (branch `lane/ir-stream-reasoning-pin`), same
order-safe pattern as #591: the old image ignores nothing (this is a wire addition),
and the new image is inert for models that do not reason.

Closes #590

## What

The applying gate for S21 step 5. A `handover` now parks the `internal_agent` run in `waiting_approval` with its step `succeeded` and the draft unattached; the `executor` approval's `meta` names the draft. A person's approval records the bound L3 `gate.draft_apply` decision in the approval's transaction, settles the run `running` and enqueues `run.resume`; the worker applies the draft through the one hardened `apply_draft_tx` and finishes the run `succeeded` without a second model call. A rejection or expiry cancels the run and leaves the draft unattached. `ladder.record` refuses a forged human rung or a pending approval, and `ladder.apply_draft` accepts only a decision bound to the exact draft (rework `v1-w1c-2:T2`). No migration.

S21 §15 names this lane: the step-4 runtime generated the draft but failed the run on a handover, so the pending approval could never apply it, and `ladder.apply_draft` admitted any accepted card decision. SPEC_V2 §5.1/§7.1/§7.4 and rework `v1-w1c-2:T2` (P0) are the source. Closes #590.

## The defect (measured, not assumed)

Inkling-2-Mini went live on pgx on 2026-11-22. Its `chat_template.jinja` keys thinking on
`reasoning_effort` (`none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`, **default 0.9**) and has **no
`enable_thinking` variable at all**. This router forwarded
`chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking = request.enable_reasoning`, which the template drops as an
undefined variable — so every caller that asked for **no** reasoning (the default: `false`) got
effort **0.9**. The polarity was inverted, silently.

The same template spends ~130 reasoning tokens even at `reasoning_effort: "none"`, so a 64-token
budget returned an empty `content` — which `parse_openai_response` promotes into the answer, i.e.
the thinking trace was served as the response.

## What changed

- `reasoning_dialect`, per provider: `enable_thinking` (the default — byte-identical to today for
  every catalog entry that omits it) or `reasoning_effort` (`false -> "none"`, `true -> "high"`,
  where `high` = 0.9 = the model's own default, so the opt-in path is unchanged).
- `min_completion_tokens`, per provider: raises — never lowers — a caller's `max_tokens` cap. A cap
  cannot force generation (the model still stops at EOS); it only stops a budget that cannot
  produce content from being honoured into a broken answer.
- Both live on `RenderOptions`, so `chat_payload` keeps four parameters and the streaming and
  non-streaming paths cannot drift.

No contract change: `enable_reasoning` stays a bool; the ledger serialisation and the OpenAPI
surface are untouched. A level-bearing `reasoning_effort` on the caller side is a separate lane.

## Tests

Ten unit tests: the default dialect sends the historical kwarg; `false -> none`; `true -> high`; no
kwargs when the flag is false; the floor raises 64, leaves 1024 alone, leaves `None` alone; an
absent dialect defaults to `enable_thinking`; both fields load; an unknown dialect fails the
catalog load.

## Rollout

Configured by the gitops counterpart (branch `lane/ir-pgx-reasoning-dialect` in
`[private-repo]`): `pgx-local` gets `reasoning_dialect: reasoning_effort` +
`min_completion_tokens: 256`, with the image pinned to this build. An old image ignores the keys
and a new image without them keeps today's behaviour, so the two land safely in either order.
