#448 — the Procedures destination operates the T16 intake and its gates

## What changed

- **P1 — the views carry the derivation facts.** `ProcessOut` gains `source_asset_id`, `knowledge_pack_ref`, `converter_version` and `approval_id`; `StepOut` gains `action_text`, `pddl_preconditions` and `pddl_effects`. The store row already held them; the read view now returns them, and `sop_ingestion` asserts each on the action's own response body.
- **P2 — the page operates the intake and the gates.** `v2.js` `procedures()` is live signed in: `procedures.ingest_sop|ingest_process|ingest_rdf` (local file, pasted text or URL), `procedures.validate`, `procedures.review_source`, and both publication gates. Every listed gate carries its own decision control (the requester cannot decide their own gate), a reload control picks up the second person's decision, and `processes.publish`/`procedures.publish` select the approved gate by its **own gate name and target** and send its id as the top-level call property. `console.js` `action()` gained the `approvalId` option.
- **P3 — no PKO store.** The PKO editor tab and every served PKO claim are removed (owner decision 2026-11-19); the knowledge-pack pairing replaces them, and `check-console` asserts the rendered page matches no `/pko/i`.
- **P4 — signed out and design mode.** The page is public and renders the published `config.procedures/processes/process_steps` read-only with zero `/api`; `?design=1` keeps the study; the coverage class is `live` and the v2-coverage destination verdict is `exists`.
- **Owner-approved widening:** SPEC_V2 §5.6/§7/§10/§12/D53/D55, the architecture ER/pipeline diagrams and the remaining design copy (STUDIO-SPEC, README, learning) are corrected to the implemented model — an ontology is a strata knowledge-pack import, and procedural knowledge is the procedure itself.

## Evidence

- P1: `sop_ingestion` 13/13, including the new `processes.get` assertions (draft and published paths).
- P2: `check-console` case 2c — both gates requested before either is decided; each decided through its own listed control; each publish carrying its own gate id (`gate-1` for the process, `gate-2` for the judge); a mutant reverting to the last-request slot fails the stub's assertion.
- P3: `check-console` renders the signed-in and snapshot pages and asserts no `/pko/i`; `git grep -i pko docs/design` leaves one non-rendered code comment.
- P4: `check-v2` 266 checks / 0 errors; `check-console`, `check-studio`, `check-learning`, `check-workbench`, `check-architecture` pass; `build-coverage.py --check`, `build-v2-coverage.py --check`, `build-docs.py --check`, `check-data`, `check-docs` current.
- Rust: full suite **3426/3426** (the docker/Redis-only `bus_delivery` test excluded on m1 — CI's containerised job covers it), doctests, fmt, clippy, audit (6 allowed warnings).
- Two independent deep audits refused the first heads; every finding is closed on this head.

Closes #448

## What this lands

U1 of the retrospective MSP/TOGAF programme: the instrument that measures whether the programme
actually operated its own gates, and the first measurement of it.

- **Snapshot exposure.** `msp.json` tranches now carry `authorised_at` and
  `authorisation_review_id`; `architecture.json` carries `compliance_reviews` and `waivers`; each
  published output carries `published_at`. The programme boundary still filters all of them;
  review findings/evidence and waiver narrative stay out of the public payload.
- **The standard.** `governance/conformance.json` is a rule matrix by class/track/ADM
  phase/plateau, not a fourth per-project list. It references `seed/output-standard.json`, the
  programme seed and the adopted profile (pinned by canonical hash).
- **The auditor.** `scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py`, stdlib only, deterministic, with a
  self-test that mutates a conformant base once per rule. It checks MSP, TOGAF, temporal and
  cross-source conformance, emits stable gap ids and writes a JSON register plus a short MD scan
  sheet. Checks whose evidence the snapshot cannot carry are marked `P2 unprovable`, never `P0`.
- **The publish gate.** `publish-data.sh` snapshots to a temp dir and audits before it replaces
  the pack. Report-only by default while the baseline is accepted; `CONFORMANCE_STRICT=1` turns a
  new/worsened P0/P1 into a hard stop. `scripts/ci/tests/publish_audit.sh` proves both paths.
- **CI and stale-file handling.** The design-pack job runs the self-test, the standard check and
  a report of the checked-in snapshot. `GENERATED_DATA` now includes `architecture.json`,
  `conformance.json` and `conformance.md`.

## The measured gap register (2026-11-20 snapshot, `a33e6562`)

| Severity | Count |
|---|---:|
| P0 | 22 |
| P1 | 54 |
| P2 | 60 |

Headline P0s: **19 closed projects in tranches 1–8 whose tranche is still `planned`**, plus
`tranche 0 review: continue did not authorise tranche 1`, plus DESIGN-PUBLISH and T14 closed
without their class-required closure review. The register also finds 16 delivery projects with no
live contract, six placeholder benefit baselines, three missing programme baselines and the live
meta's missing ADM phase. Full rows: `docs/evidence/conformance-gap-register.json`;
baseline: `docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` (76 P0/P1 entries, owner + expiry, proposed —
acceptance belongs to the authority-repair unit).

## Evidence

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Auditor self-test | `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --self-test` | OK (17 rule cases + determinism) |
| Standard | `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --check-standard` | OK |
| Real snapshot report | `python3 scripts/audit-programme-conformance.py --snapshot docs/design/data --report` | 22 P0 / 54 P1 / 60 P2 |
| Baseline ratchet | `... --strict --baseline docs/evidence/conformance-baseline.json` | OK |
| Publish gate | `bash scripts/ci/tests/publish_audit.sh` | OK (strict refuses, report publishes) |
| Programme definition | `python3 scripts/check-programme-definition.py` | OK |
| Coverage | `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` | OK |
| Output standard | `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py --self-test` and `python3 scripts/check-output-standard.py` | OK (9/9 refusals) |
| Design pack | `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs`, `check-docs.cjs`, `build-docs.py --check` | OK |
| Rust compile/lint | [preflight 44783189373](https://github.com/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/runs/44783189373) | success (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`) |

The new `snapshot_conformance` store test runs in this PR's CI (preflight does not execute
tests). It asserts the tranche link, the review/waiver projection and the programme boundary.

## Scope

U1 only. Enforcement of the bypasses, the authority repair/re-baseline, per-project retrospective
records, benefit measurement and T12's viability gate are follow-on issues. This unit changes no
governance state and fabricates nothing.

Closes #501

Closes #502
Closes #503

## What

One branch carries both conformance fixes, because they are two halves of the same rule: a claim
the programme cannot prove must be refused at the write.

1. **Benefits integrity (#502)** — `benefits.update` and `benefits.create` now enforce the
   realization rule in the store. An update that sets `status = "realized"` loads the benefit's
   `benefit_transition` and refuses with `422 benefit_baseline_missing` unless both
   `baseline_measured_at` and `post_measured_at` are recorded; a create that asks for `"realized"`
   is refused outright, because a transition cannot reference a row that does not exist yet.
2. **Tranche authorisation record (#503)** — the seed and its validator now record tranche 1 as
   `authorised` (the tranche-0 `continue` outcome) instead of `planned`, and a new store test
   proves a seeded tranche-1 project passes the start gate while a `planned` tranche is refused.

No schema, migration or action signature changes.

## Why

SPEC_V2 §8.3: "A benefit whose baseline was never measured cannot claim an improvement," and a
project "does not start before the first tranche is authorised". Both mechanisms already existed —
`upsert_transition_tx` and `review_tranche_tx` — but neither write path that mattered consulted
them: the benefit status write ignored `benefit_transition`, and the seed encoded tranche 1 as
`planned` after the recorded `continue` review. The T10 acceptance named the first gap (#82); the
assessment named the second.

## Track

- [x] **Unit work** — the `Closes` lines above name the two unit issues.

## Checks

- [x] Local gate: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → 0 · `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1`
      → 0 · `python3 scripts/check-programme-definition.py` → 0; the compile/test verdict is the
      PR's CI.
- [x] Every commit is signed off with `git commit -s`.
- [x] No credential, private hostname, private address or private infrastructure detail.

## Credit

no credit

## Acceptance evidence

```

0
$ cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1
0
$ python3 scripts/check-programme-definition.py
check-programme-definition: 6 benefits, 6 links, 14 tranches, 48 projects — OK

test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
sha=940c23fdb84f71cc392b924b6fce9b9365e346b2
```

- with the `spine.rs` guard reverted, `a_realized_status_needs_a_complete_transition` and
  `a_created_benefit_cannot_start_realized` fail (`0 passed; 2 failed`);
- with the seed line reverted to `planned`,
  `a_seeded_tranche_one_project_starts_after_the_continue_review` fails.

### Scenario evidence — one row per BDD scenario in the two issues

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |

| #502 P1.1 no transition + realized → 422, version unchanged | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test benefit_lifecycle a_realized_status_needs_a_complete_transition` | pass (fails without the guard) | `940c23f` |
| #502 P1.2 complete transition + realized → 200 realized | same test, allow arm | pass | `940c23f` |
| #502 P2.1 create realized → 422, no row | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test benefit_lifecycle a_created_benefit_cannot_start_realized` | pass (fails without the guard) | `940c23f` |
| #503 P1.1 seeded tranche 1 reads `authorised` | `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test seed_programme_definition a_fresh_tenant_seeds_its_msp_definition` | pass (fails with the pre-change seed) | `940c23f` |
| #503 P1.2 a seeded tranche-1 project starts; a planned tranche is refused | `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test seed_programme_definition a_seeded_tranche_one_project_starts_after_the_continue_review` | pass (fails with the pre-change seed) | `940c23f` |

## Resume

- Branch: `issue/502-benefit-realized-transition`
- HEAD: `940c23fdb84f71cc392b924b6fce9b9365e346b2`
- Next step: merge through the queue; then record the snapshot row (P2.2) on #503.

## Risks / follow-ups

- `benefits.create` still accepts every other status; only `realized` is refused.
- The six programme benefits remain `draft` with unmeasured baselines — the BCM's measurement
  work, not this PR's.
- The seed encodes the tranche review's *outcome*, not a review row: a review row needs a
  `reviewed_by` app_user that a bare seed tenant does not have, and fabricating the sponsor's
  evidence would be worse than the gap.

- `docs/design/v2.js`: a live snapshot now renders the platform's own `measure.inference` on the Metering screen — calls, tokens and cache hits as totals, by caller and by model, plus the snapshot's `note` that fixes the cost rule. Closes #496

## What

`classify` now computes `generated_only` for pull requests, pushes to main and merge-queue
entries, from the generated set the registry automation writes (`seed/programme.json`,
`docs/design/data/**`, `docs/design/docs/**`).

- On a **PR** and on the **merge queue**, a generated-only change skips `checks-shard`, the
  `image`/`service-image` build+smoke steps (both jobs still conclude success, so the required
  contexts keep reporting) — and validates every changed JSON in `classify` so a malformed seed
  can never ride the fast path.
- On a **push to main** the suite and the server `image` still run: the Dockerfile bakes
  `docs/design/**` into the image (`Dockerfile:88-93`) and `seed/programme.json` is compiled in
  (`crates/store/src/seed_programme.rs:36`). Only `publish-service-images` skips, because the 8
  service images copy one binary and carry no generated file.
- `dco` runs on `merge_group` too, feeding `merge_group.base_sha`/`head_sha`, so it can become a
  required context without stalling every queue entry (P3.2 is a separate post-merge step).

## Why

The registry automation is 27% of merges, and each one paid the full 11-job PR fan-out
(`checks-shard` 16m37s, `image` 15m15s) plus 8 service-image rebuilds on main. The merge queue
already re-validates a tree; it does not release one.

## Track

- [x] **Unit work** — the `Closes` line above names the unit issue.

## Checks

- [x] Local gate: `actionlint .github/workflows/ci-public.yml` → exit 0; `cargo fmt --all -- --
      check` → exit 0; `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` → exit 0.
- [x] Every commit is signed off with `git commit -s`.
- [x] No credential, private hostname, private address or private infrastructure detail.

## Credit

no credit

## Acceptance evidence

```
$ actionlint .github/workflows/ci-public.yml
(no output — exit 0)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check          # exit 0
$ cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 >/dev/null   # exit 0
sha=0b73b3b3
```

The classify script was executed as written, against real ranges:

```
$ # a61defc8 — the registry automation's own merge (seed/programme.json + docs/design/data/*)
EVENT_NAME=pull_request PR_BASE=a61defc8~1 PR_HEAD=a61defc8 → generated_only=true, docs_only=false
$ # this branch's code change
EVENT_NAME=pull_request PR_BASE=origin/main PR_HEAD=HEAD → generated_only=false
$ # malformed generated JSON fixture
seed/programme.json = "{bad" → ::error::… not valid JSON; exit 1 (nothing skipped)
```

### Scenario evidence — one row per BDD scenario in the issue

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | the next automation PR after this merges — `gh api .../runs/<id>/jobs` | post-merge run (named in the issue) | — |
| P1.2 | that PR's merge_group run — shards skipped, `checks` success | post-merge run | — |
| P1.3 | malformed generated JSON fixture, classify executed locally | **pass** (exit 1) | 0b73b3b3 |
| P2.1 | main run after the next automation merge — `image` builds, `publish-service-images` runs (seed changed) | post-merge run | — |
| P2.2 | a data-only push — `image`/`service-image` build steps and `publish-service-images` skipped | post-merge run | — |
| P3.1 | this unit's own queue run — `dco completed/success`, not skipped | post-merge run | — |
| P3.2 | ruleset GET contains `dco` after P3.1; next queue run green | post-merge config step | — |

- [x] Every locally provable scenario has a row at this SHA; the run-dependent rows name the
      exact post-merge run that closes them
- [x] The issue's acceptance gate is green at this SHA
- [ ] Tests named per part exist and ran — P1–P3 are proved by the deployed runs above; P1.3 ran
- [ ] The issue's Definition-of-done checklist is satisfied (post-merge runs)
- [x] No second PR exists for this issue

## Resume

- Branch: `issue/496-ci-cost`
- HEAD: `0b73b3b3`
- Next step: after merge, verify P3.1 on the queue run, then add `dco` to the ruleset (P3.2)

## Risks / follow-ups

- `publish-service-images` now depends on `classify`; if `classify` ever fails on main, the 8

Closes #394

## What

- **`seed/programme-definition.json`** — the buildout’s own MSP definition: the six benefit profiles (B1–B6) with the six field groups’ values, the six benefits-map edges, the fourteen tranches (0 closed, 1–13 planned) and every project’s ADM phase/plateau.
- **`scripts/check-programme-definition.py`** — refuses a missing baseline/target/method/owner, a link naming no benefit, non-contiguous tranches, and a project with no ADM placement. It is wired into the design-pack CI, so a bad definition cannot be seeded.
- **The loader** (`crates/store/src/seed_programme.rs`) inserts the benefits, links and tranches inside the existing tenant-scoped seed transaction. Each insert is guarded by its natural key: a second run inserts nothing, and an approved/edited row is never overwritten. The counts are separate from the project counts, so the existing programme seed contract is unchanged.
- **The generator** merges each project’s ADM phase/plateau into `seed/programme.json` meta (the seed owns those keys); T11 now reads `G` / `capability`, P0 `Preliminary` / `definition`.
- **Tests** — `crates/store/tests/seed_programme_definition.rs`: a fresh tenant gets 6 benefits, 6 links and 14 tranches; a repeated seed inserts nothing and leaves a published (approved) profile untouched.

## Why / source

The live programme has these rows, but they were created by hand; a fresh tenant had no way to carry them. Issue #394; SPEC_V2 §8.1/§8.3; P0 §6–§7. The source values are the measured live rows (B1–B6, the map, tranches 0–13) and the project set in `seed/programme.json`.

## Acceptance evidence

| Scenario | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `python3 scripts/check-programme-definition.py` → 6 benefits, 6 links, 14 tranches, 48 projects | PASS |
| P1.2 | the same checker on a copy with B1’s baseline removed → exits 1 (`benefits[0].baseline is required`) | PASS |
| P2.1 | `crates/store/tests/seed_programme_definition.rs::a_fresh_tenant_seeds_its_msp_definition` | runs in CI (the compile gate) |
| P2.2 | `::a_repeated_seed_is_a_no_op_and_never_overwrites_a_published_row` | runs in CI |
| P3.1 | `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py --check` → current; T11/P0 meta carry the ADM placement | PASS |
| P4.1 | `build-coverage --check`, `build-v2-coverage --check`, `build-docs --check`, `check-data.cjs` | PASS |

## Gate

This repository has **no `preflight.yml`**; under the 2026-11-20 build route (no local Rust compilation), the PR’s own CI is the compile/test gate. Local non-compiling gates are green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, the definition checker, the seed/coverage/v2/docs/data checks, `no-private-refs`, the commit hook’s workflow lint.

## Resume

Branch `issue/394-msp-seed`: claim `6fc788c0`, unit `bf0edd2e`.

## Risks

- The loader inserts only absent rows; it never updates an existing benefit, link or tranche, so a live tenant with the hand-made rows is untouched.
- The checker treats the owner as a **role** (`BCM`) in the definition; the profile rows leave the job FKs null (as the live rows do) until the BCM is staffed — the issue’s open-question default.

The construction half of S14's deployment gate. References #8 — the release receipt (P6) and the live post-roll proofs land in a second PR that closes the issue (owner decision, 2026-11-20: a receipt cannot name its own commit).

## What this delivers

### P5 — the repeatable installer
`conveyor admin install --tenant <slug> --name … --admin-email … --admin-name …` creates or converges a fresh tenant in one command:

- `store::platform::create` (the wizard's production path), with the first admin converged by **verified email** first (`platform::ensure_human`, extracted from `create` and shared) so the audit row names a real person, never a synthetic id;
- the catalogue and the **default process catalogue** (`seed_catalogue` + `process_seed::apply_all`) — idempotent on a second run;
- the tenant-scoped content named by `seed/tenant-install.json` through the **real action engine** (`capabilities.bind_knowledge`, `schedules.upsert`), never raw SQL. The manifest ships the three engine housekeeping schedules; `knowledge` is empty because no knowledge pack exists at this baseline (a tenant's packs are imported from its own documents) — stated, not faked.

Idempotency: the tenant id resolves by slug, `platform::create` converges on the id, the seed creates nothing on a second run, and each schedule upserts by kind. `apps/server/tests/install.rs` proves the first run and the converge.

### P3.1 — the native acceptance harness
`acceptance/native.toml` + `scripts/acceptance.py` + `.github/workflows/acceptance.yml`:

- every required CI context on the commit under test must conclude `success`, and the repository's own required-check authority (the `main` ruleset, measured: 6 contexts) must not name one the manifest omits;
- every deployed surface answers its declared status; 404/422/5xx are never "reachable", and 401 counts only where declared (`/mcp`, `/api/me`);
- every command runs with per-runner zero-selected detection (nextest `--no-tests=fail`, libtest `running N tests`, Playwright `stats`) and a declared `min_tests` floor.
- `--self-test` proves 8/8 refusals. Live run on main `81c2c2c5`: **all six contexts + six probes pass**.

### P3.2 — the deployed suite's auth actually works
`apps/web/playwright.config.ts` had the OIDC **setup** project inheriting `use.storageState` for a file it creates: on a clean checkout the deployed run died with ENOENT before signing in. Fixed; the setup project now starts with an empty state. Proven against `https://conveyor.nonagentic.ai` with the realm's `conveyor-e2e` principal (read-only subset — results in the receipt PR).

### P7 — the tenant ops namespace (owner-added)
Companion gitops PR `[private-repo]#5383`, merged `21b5f5e6`: namespace `nonagentic-ops`, Role `conveyor-ops-write` (patch deployments, get/list replicasets) bound to the `conveyor-worker` SA. It is already proven: **#78's P1.4 ran end to end through it** (incident mitigated 08:06:14Z, resolved 08:06:24Z, postmortem linked) — evidence on conveyor#78.

## Measured defects found and recorded

1. **The `incident` card type was absent from the live tenant** — `ops.incident` refused with a 422 whose generic message hides the field error (`card_type_code`). Fixed with the per-tenant catalogue import (`migrate --seed --tenant nonagentic`, created 1 / skipped 133). Recorded on #78.
2. The admin CLI unwraps a top-level `input` member; `ops.mitigate`'s own input has one. The mitigation document must be nested once more (in `scripts/ops-live-proof.sh`).
3. The ops writes answer `503 service ops unconfigured` on the serve pod by design; the gated write runs only from the worker pod.

Closes #484

## What
1. `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml`, job `image`: steps `build` and `smoke` carry `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'merge_group' }}`. The job's own `if` and the main-only `push to ghcr.io` step are untouched. A job whose steps are all skipped concludes success, so the required `image` context still reports on the queue ref.
2. New `.github/workflows/preflight.yml`: `workflow_dispatch` + `push` on `issue/**`, `lane/**`, `slice/**`; `concurrency: preflight-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; one job using the public archetype `nonagenticai/ci-workflows/.github/workflows/rust-preflight.yml@d2ae87a417b00013838ba18841cdd1642b83fb89` with `cache_shared_key: checks` and no postgres input (conveyor has no `sqlx::query!` macros). Replaces rbuild, retired 2026-11-20; writes no required status.

## Why
Ruleset 27178695 uses a merge queue, so every merge re-runs the whole pipeline and the Docker image build is the PR critical path: 924 s on #473's PR run. The queue re-validates a tree; it does not release one.

## Evidence at HEAD
| gate | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| actionlint 1.7.12 | `actionlint .github/workflows/ci-public.yml .github/workflows/preflight.yml` | exit 0 |

`collect_pack` walked the **deployed image's entire pack** and overlaid the temp snapshot on it, so every publish PR also committed the image's hand-authored files. When the image lagged main, the publish silently reverted main.

The proof run (#475) is the measurement: its publish branch carried a `docs/design/v2.js` **9 lines behind main**, and the `design-pack` data step failed on exactly that drift — every `actions_invoked[*].line` in the committed `coverage.json` was 9 higher than a fresh build, while every project status matched. The surface checks never ran.

The publisher's file set is now the temp's generated data and docs only. The target branch owns every hand-authored file, and the existing `GENERATED_DATA` / deletion rule already keeps hand-authored paths out of deletions. The image is still the generation input (its issue registry), never commit content.

## Acceptance evidence (at `6a66b2b1`)

| Part | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --lib publish` (m4, cargo-guard) | **4/4**, including `a_publish_commits_only_the_generated_files` (a temp `data/`+`docs/` dir is returned verbatim) |
| Gate | `cargo clippy -p conveyor-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (m4) | exit **0** |
| Gate | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit **0** |
| Regression | the existing publish tests (`pack_files_land_under_docs_design`, `stale_generated_pages_are_deleted_and_hand_authored_files_are_not`, the DCO trailer) | pass |

## Post-merge proof

The worker image rolls out from the merge run. The next publish's diff must list only generated files (`docs/design/data/*` snapshot files and `docs/design/docs/*` output pages/index), and its `design-pack` data step must be green. That, with the already-proven `dco`, completes #400's DoD.

## Risks

- A pack file that exists only in the deployed image (and not on the target branch) is no longer published. That is the intent: the branch is the source of truth; the image is only the generation input.
- The generated docs index (`docs/documents.js`) is produced by the pack build inside the image and is not in the temp; it is not committed by a publish (unchanged from before). If it must be regenerated with the outputs, that is a separate unit.

pulls.body:
Closes #472

## Problem

Measured on `main@7ff187ff`, run `44671755483`:

| job | seconds | required? |
|---|---|---|
| `gate / gate` | 1122 | **no** |
| `image` | 1121 | yes |
| `checks` | 917 (clippy 154, suite 729) | yes |
| `service-image` | 121 | yes |

`cargo clippy` runs twice per PR, and no job reuses a compile between runs: `actions/cache` covered the registry only, and the Dockerfile's `--mount=type=cache` lives on the builder, which a GitHub-hosted runner replaces every run.

## Change

**The `gate` job is deleted.** It is a CI mirror of the pre-commit gate, it is in none of ruleset 27178695's six required contexts, and it recompiles a workspace that `checks` just compiled. (The push-side half of the same problem is #426, and the hook default changed in gitops-production PR #5379.)

**`checks` → `checks-shard` (2-way matrix) + a `checks` aggregator.** The aggregator is not ceremony: GitHub names a matrix job's checks `checks (1)` / `checks (2)` while the ruleset requires the literal `checks`, so a bare matrix would leave every PR waiting on a context that can never report. The aggregator carries the stable name, so the shard count can change without touching the ruleset. `fmt`, clippy, doctests, `cargo audit` and the contract fixtures stay on shard 1 because nextest cannot partition doctests; `--no-tests=fail` keeps an empty shard visible as a red.

**Registry-only `actions/cache` → `Swatinem/rust-cache`**, pinned by commit. It caches dependencies rather than the workspace's own crates and prunes to its own budget, which is what the old "target/ would thrash the 10 GB budget" comment was really guarding against. Saved on `main` only — a PR's merge ref cannot share an entry with main, so saving one there only evicts main's.

**`image` gets buildx + `type=gha` layer cache.** What survives between runs is everything before the first `COPY . .`: apt and the pinned rustup toolchain, which were being paid once per stage. Exported on `main` only, for the same branch-scope reason.

## What this does not fix

**The image build's compile stays cold.** `cache-to: type=gha` exports layers, not cache-mount contents, and `COPY . .` invalidates the build layer on every source change. Getting that compile cached needs a dependency layer in the Dockerfile (cargo-chef or an equivalent manifest-only stage), which is a separate change with its own deploy risk and is not in this PR. Until then the expected `image` time is ~900 s, not the ~450 s the plan targeted — I will record the measured number on #472 rather than claim it.

## Verification

```
actionlint                      # clean
uvx zizmor==1.32.0 --persona=auditor --min-severity=medium --format=plain .   # no findings
bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh   # OK
cargo fmt --all -- --check      # OK
```

No Rust source is touched, so the suite itself is unaffected; this PR's own run is the lane's single pre-merge CI run.

Post-run checks recorded on #472: all six required contexts still report, `gate` is absent, `checks-shard` shard durations are within 1.4×, and `gh api repos/nonagenticai/conveyor/actions/caches` stays under 10 GB.

Closes #450

## What changed

The registry still declared five V1 External actions whose destinations were two live Python
services and one service that does not exist. SPEC_V2 §11.2 (§11.3 "they do not run beside it as
a second path"), §11.10 (D57) and #46 already ruled what each must become; this PR executes it.

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts.list` | External → `artifact_service` (Python) | internal read of the `document` catalogue (`crates/actions/src/documents/artifacts.rs`), same name and filters, returns the shared `DocumentOut` page |
| `billing.summary` | External → `billing-service` (Python) | internal read of the ledger (`crates/actions/src/metrics/mod.rs`), `total_usd` via the existing `conveyor_cost_tx` derivation plus call counts (#46) |
| `workers.list` | External → `worker_management` (no workload exists) | internal: the durable queue's `(kind, status)` counts plus the host registry (`crates/actions/src/workers.rs`, `crates/store/src/host.rs`) |
| `providers.list` | External → `worker_management` | internal: the tenant's registered inference destination (`tenant_inference_endpoint`) |
| `graphs.list` | External → `worker_management` | **deleted** — nothing in the conveyor models a worker graph, and §11.2 rules the service legacy |

Ground that went with them: the three `seed/toolkits/{artifacts,billing,worker_management}.json`
manifests are removed (a toolkit binds External handlers only), the registry's exact-count
assertion moves to `(471 internal, 13 external)`, the parity samples and
`docs/design/data/actions.json` drop `graphs.list`, `served-spec.lock.json` is regenerated, and
the S09 plan/SPEC text record the retirement.

Every remaining External destination is a Rust service — coding, the mac-mini model servers
(speech, transcription, images, inference), strata-rag — or the third-party laya engine (#76) and
the in-process fixtures transport. `crates/actions/tests/external_inventory.rs` is the durable
guard: a new External naming an unclassified runtime fails CI.

## Verification

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| the four actions answer from seeded conveyor state, with no external URL set | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test tool_destinations` | 4 passed |
| every External destination is classified and none is Python | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test external_inventory` | 3 passed |
| the registry is exactly the declared set, and the committed dump matches | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry` | 12 passed |
| the toolkit import wave still publishes, probes and reports | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test estate_toolkits` | 9 passed |
| the repository's local gate at this head (`a4af7bb9`) | `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` | `gate: OK` — fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, audit, nextest **3437 passed / 7 skipped**, doc tests, private-refs, betterleaks |
| the served spec and its lock agree | `conveyor --print-openapi --check-lock` | exit 0, 515 operations |
| design pack, coverage and derived data are current | `check-*.cjs`, `build-coverage.py --check`, `build-v2-coverage.py --check` | green |

Live proof on the deployed image is recorded on the issue after the merge.

## Out of scope, stated plainly

- The Python `artifact_service`, `billing-service` and `provisioning` deployments keep serving
  other consumers (agent-api, onboarding); removing them is a separate owner-approved cluster
  change. `provisioning` is control-plane per D57, and `billing-service` remains the platform's
  charging system (D52) — the conveyor's Platform screen still proxies to it through a BFF route,
  which is not a tool path.
- `storage-api`/`secrets` are not conveyor dependencies (D57).
- The mac-mini stack (verified running Rust binaries) and `laya` are out of scope by owner ruling.
- Publishing the `retrieval` toolkit needs a Deployment URL for the live Rust strata-rag — a
  gitops lane, not a rewrite.

T7 — Operations: the incident lifecycle and the fourth gated write (#78)

Closes #78

## What this delivers

SPEC_V2 §6.5 · §9.2 · §10.4 · §12 T7, on the parts still missing at `main@6c46d92e` — the six
reads, restart/scale/rollback, the `ops:write` scope and the tenant `approval_policy` gate were
already merged (#170, #171, #282).

- **The incident is a card** (§9.2): `ops.incident` opens a card of the catalogue type `incident`
  carrying `service`, `severity`, `detected_at` and the run/evidence links in `card.meta`. No
  second table (§10.3 "reused, not created"), therefore **no migration**.
- `ops.triage` records the severity and a **published** runbook procedure; no cluster write can
  precede it.
- `ops.mitigate` is itself `effect: destructive`, so the engine's one gate runs before the handler
  with the composed target `incident/<id>/<verb target>` — the decision names the incident *and*
  the exact object. It dispatches to one of the four write verbs inside the same transaction and
  records `mitigated_at`, the approver(s) from the immutable decision rows, the verb version and
  the read-back.
- `ops.postmortem` writes the one `governed_asset` of kind `postmortem` (0044 already widened the
  CHECK) and opens exactly one kata candidate when the finding is systemic; `ops.resolve` sets
  `resolved_at` only once that postmortem is linked.
- `ops.flag_flip` — the fourth §6.5 write: one environment variable on one container, with the dry
  run, the approval target `namespace/deployment/<d>/flag_flip/<FLAG>=<value>` and a read-back
  naming the observed value. The patch carries the **whole** containers list: a JSON merge-patch
  replaces arrays, and a one-element list would silently drop every other container.

## Scenarios

| Part | Scenario | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | triaged with no write | `ops.rs::an_incident_is_triaged_with_no_write` |
| P1.2 | approved mitigation, approver + version + read-back | `ops.rs::an_approved_mitigation_sets_mitigated_at_with_a_read_back` |
| P1.3 | one linked postmortem; a kata only when systemic | `ops.rs::an_incident_resolves_with_a_linked_postmortem`, `ops.rs::a_systemic_finding_opens_exactly_one_kata`, `crates/api/tests/ops_incident.rs` |

Closes #389

## What

The New-project form hardcoded `project_type = "delivery"` as a free-text default and let the operator type any string. On the deployed tenant there is no `delivery` catalogue row, so accepting the default was a `422 invalid_value` on `project_type_code`. The control is now a `<select>` fed by `catalogues.list` (`kind: "project_type"`, `include_inactive: false`):

- the options are exactly the tenant's active codes (value) with their labels;
- the default is the first active code, set when the read lands;
- **Create** is disabled until a real code is selected;
- a loading, failed or empty catalogue renders a disabled control that says so instead of inventing a type, and the submit path refuses an empty code with a message.

No action, model or migration change: `catalogues.list` already answers the vocabulary.

## Acceptance evidence (at `80f3d5a5`)

Method: the repo's native stack on m4 (throwaway Postgres 18, `conveyor serve` :8932, `conveyor worker`, model stub :8941, `dev-server.mjs` :8933), the branch's wasm built with `cargo leptos build --frontend-only --cargo-locked`.

| Part | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | `cd apps/web && DEV_AUTH_TOKEN=dev:alice BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8933 npx playwright test e2e/board.spec.ts -g "project type"` | **1 passed** — the select's values equal the codes `catalogues.list` returns, the selected value is one of them, and a project created with it appears in the index |
| Regression | `npx playwright test e2e/board.spec.ts` | **5/5 passed** (keyboard, drag, the project/card/edit/archive round-trip, paging) |
| Compile | `cargo leptos build --frontend-only --cargo-locked` (wasm32) | green |
| Gate | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit 0 |
| Gate | `cargo clippy -p conveyor-web --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` | exit **0** |

- The form needs `catalogues:read`; a caller without it sees the unavailable control and cannot create a project. That is the action's own scope, not a new gate.

Closes #386

## What

The programme queue's badge counted due-now outputs only, so a closed project whose declared at-closure category had no published document still read green. `programmeQueue` now derives `closureMissing` for projects whose `status === "closed"`, names the missing categories in the project's row, and appends `<n> closure output(s) owed` to the queue badge. An active project's at-closure set is not owed yet: its missing categories are neither counted nor named. The due-now count (`rows.filter(row => row.next.length > 0).length`) and the next-output selection are unchanged.

The rule mirrors the action-side gate `crates/actions/src/programme.rs::assert_closure_outputs_published`, which refuses a close with missing at-closure outputs; this display is the honest reading of a closed project that got there before the gate.

pulls.body:
Closes #85

## What changed

T16 — SOP / process-document ingestion, the human publication gate, PDDL execution and the
source gate — **re-scoped by the owner's decision of 2026-11-19 to follow the strata decision**
recorded in #413 / PR #419: no PKO tables, no `pko.*` actions; an OWL/Turtle document becomes a
`strata_ingest` knowledge pack the derived procedure names. Issue #85's body carries the re-scope
and the 12 acceptance scenarios.

**Intake (P1).** `procedures.ingest_sop` stores a PDF/text/URL source as a
`governed_asset(kind='sop_source')` with provenance (media type, sha, converter), converts it
through the model seam into a **draft** SOP judge and a **draft** executable process whose steps
carry PDDL action text plus ground-literal preconditions and effects, and creates capability,
agent and job drafts (the agent's `allowed_actions` stays empty). `procedures.ingest_process`
reads BPMN 2.0 XML with a `quick-xml` pull parser — activities are steps, gateways are gates.
`procedures.ingest_rdf` stores the document, hands it to `strata_ingest` through the existing
`documents.ingest` transport and records the job id as `knowledge_pack_ref`; nothing local parses
or reasons. `procedures.validate` refuses a tool request by name (`sop.cannot_grant_tool`) and
malformed PDDL.

**The publication gate (P2).** `processes.publish` on a derived process requires an approved
approval for `processes.publish` naming that exact version and carrying **at least one human
decision** (a tenant policy row may waive the gate). The approval id is recorded on the released
version in the same transaction, and exactly one `process.published` event is emitted. The
requester-cannot-decide rule is the store's one writer (`record_decision_tx`), unchanged.

**The source gate (P5).** `procedures.review_source` is a person's act (non-user actors and the
supplier are refused) and walks the legal `draft → in_review → approved` path. An unreviewed
source refuses a publish (`422 source.unapproved`) and a binding; a binding also refuses a draft
process (`409 process.not_published`).

**Versioning (P3).** A re-ingest forks the next version; the published row keeps its original
source asset, converter and knowledge-pack references, and the new draft names the new ones.

**PDDL execution (P4).** The step executor evaluates a step's ground-literal preconditions
against the run's own fact state (the previous position's recorded `pddl_state_after`, else the
process's `pddl_init`) before the claim; a false precondition fails deterministically at that
position with `pddl_precondition_false` and applies the step's `on_result` policy. A succeeded
step's effects apply and `pddl_state_before/after` are recorded on its `run_step`.

**Schema.** `migrations/0060_procedure_ingestion.sql` (columns only; 0058 already added
`action_text`): the source/pack/converter/domain/init/approval columns on `process`, the source
and pack on `procedure`, the precondition/effect literals on `process_step`, and the fact state
on `run_step`. Both migration ledgers record 60.

pulls.body:
Closes #421

## What changed — `apps/server/src/worker.rs`

- **The tick spawns each claimed job instead of awaiting it inline.** The poll loop used to run `run_job(&job).await`; one handler that never returned stopped every other job. Measured twice on 2026-11-19: a failed run's coach run held the only worker for as long as its model call blocked, and every queued step starved until a manual `kubectl rollout restart`.
- **Bounded concurrency**: `MAX_IN_FLIGHT_JOBS = 8`. The semaphore is acquired **before** the claim, so the worker never claims a job it has no permit to run; a hung handler costs one permit, not the queue.
- **The lease renewal is bounded** by `MAX_JOB_RUNTIME = 30 min`. Renewal exists so a legitimately long step is not reclaimed mid-flight and run twice (audit V1), but a hung handler used to renew forever — hiding its own expiry from every other worker. Past the bound the renewal stops and warns; the lease expires and the queue reclaims the row on a later attempt (the attempts cap dead-letters it). A blocked poll cannot be preempted, so this bounds the damage, not the task.
- The worker log now names the concurrency: `worker polling ... concurrency=8`.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| a hung handler must not stop the next job | `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-server --test worker_concurrency --locked` | **PASS (3.04 s)** with the fix; **FAIL after 20.68 s** with `worker.rs` reverted to `origin/main` — the second job never ran. The regression test uses a real `conveyor worker` child and a stub whose first `/licenses/active` request hangs for 60 s; two jobs are queued and exactly one must complete while the other is in flight. |
| the kill/reclaim contract still holds | `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-server --test jobs_kill --locked` | covered by the repo gate |
| the repo gate | `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` at `b9f5843c` on m1 | `gate: OK`, exit 0; `WORKTREE_TARGET=ABSENT` |
| live | worker logs after deploy | PENDING |

## Scope

The blocked poll itself is not interruptible (tokio cannot preempt it); this change makes a hang survivable and visible rather than fatal to the queue.

pulls.body:
Closes #409

Corrects `scripts/prove-estate.sh`, the script #396 shipped. Four defects, each measured by running
the script against the deployed estate (`nonagentic`):

1. **Binary path.** `CONVEYOR_BINARY` defaulted to `/usr/local/bin/service`; the image carries
   `/usr/local/bin/conveyor` (`kubectl exec … --version` → `no such file or directory`).
2. **The seed printed the wrong thing and read the run id too late.** The `set_config(...)` GUC
   answer was stdout, and the final `SELECT` ran **after** `COMMIT` — where `set_config(…, true)`
   is already gone, so RLS hid the row and the id came back empty. A first run only looked right
   because the value it captured was the tenant id. The query is silenced with `\o` and the id is
   read inside the transaction; the comment warns that this heredoc is unquoted, so no backtick
   may appear in it.
3. **The seed was not idempotent.** A project may carry one live run (`uq_run_project_live`), so a
   second seed died on the unique index. It now reuses the live run and inserts only the bindings
   that are missing.
4. **`call-all` used an invented job id.** The coding service refuses `probe-job` (`400 invalid job
   id`), so the read-class call P1.2 wants could never succeed. The proof now creates one lint job
   through `coding.jobs_create` (JSON built with `python3`, not shell quoting) and reads that job
   back. A refused destination is counted and reported per toolkit with exit 1, instead of
   `set -e` hiding every call after it.

## Acceptance, run on the deployed estate (tenant `nonagentic`, run `01a1f354-…`)

| Part | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `scripts/prove-estate.sh publish` | unchanged (already published by #83) |
| P2.1 | `… seed` twice | `seeded run 01a1f354-2a2d-75a9-b730-92910baf9663` both times — one line, the run id |
| P3.1 | `… call-all` | `created coding job 44698c8a-…` → `coding.jobs_get` returns it; `image_gen.generate` ok; `REFUSED: transcription.transcribe` (asr 401) and `REFUSED: speech.synthesize` (tts 503) reported, not swallowed; exit 1 with the count |

pulls.body:
## Problem

A metered external call cut off by the action timeout or by a cancelled run loses the tokens the provider already served. `invoke_external` wrapped `builder.send()` in `tokio::time::timeout`, and the whole action is wrapped again; dropping either future closes the connection mid-generation, and the inference-router books a zero cost event for an attempt whose client leaves.

Measured 2026-11-19, tenant `nonagentic-conveyor`:

- `inference_router_tokens_total{kind="prompt"}` 191,979 vs `vllm:prompt_tokens_total` 254,984; `vllm:request_prompt_tokens_sum` (completed requests only) 193,152 → ~61.8k prompt tokens from requests that never completed.
- Two `run` rows were `cancelled` in the window, `inference_router_provider_attempt_seconds_total` stepped +89.4 s at the cancel, and no `action_invocation` row exists for those attempts (every recorded `inference.chat` row is `ok`).
- `LocalLlmMeteringCoverageLow` read 0.75.

## Fix

For a metered action (`spec.captures_usage`: inference, imagegen, audio), `send_metered` runs the send **and the body read** in a task of its own; the caller awaits a oneshot under `spec.timeout_ms`. A timeout or a dropped caller future (a cancelled run) leaves the task draining to the terminal chunk, so the router completes and books the usage; the action still reports its timeout. Unmetered external actions keep the old abandon-on-timeout behaviour (`send_once`) — no background spend where none was already paid for.

## Tests

- `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs::tests::a_metered_call_drains_its_body_after_the_action_timeout` — the caller times out and the body still reaches its last chunk.
- `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs::tests::an_unmetered_call_is_abandoned_when_its_caller_leaves` — the unmetered path still drops the body.
- `crates/actions/tests/inference_call_drain.rs::a_cancelled_metered_call_is_read_to_completion` — the real `invoke` future is aborted after the upstream sees the request; the response is read to its last chunk.

## Validation (local, before CI)

- `cargo fmt -p conveyor-actions -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p conveyor-actions --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --locked` — **746 passed, 0 failed** across 92 test binaries. `a_flushall_replays_from_postgres_without_a_double_outcome` is excluded locally: it requires a **second private** Redis (`TEST_REDIS_PRIVATE_URL`) and starts a container otherwise; this host cannot run that container, and CI (with Docker) runs it.

## Live verification (after the image rolls)

A cancelled run's `inference.chat` attempt lands in `billing_cost_events`; `local_llm:metering_coverage_ratio:1h` stays ≥ 0.99 across a burst containing a cancellation; `LocalLlmMeteringCoverageLow` stays quiet.

Closes #412

## What

Adds `.github/workflows/web.yml`, path-filtered to `apps/web/**` and the workflow file itself.
A non-UI PR starts no browser job at all (the filter is evaluated before any runner starts).

The job, on a GitHub-hosted public runner:

1. boots Postgres 18 (`--shm-size=1g`, `max_connections=300`) and Redis;
2. applies `scripts/db-roles.sql` to a fresh `conveyor_e2e`;

Closes #408

## Why

`issue-registry` runs on **every push to `main`** and reuses the open generated PR's branch. A branch whose PR is in the merge queue cannot be updated — GitHub answers `GH006 … A pull request for this branch has been added to a merge queue` — and the script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so the run went red. Measured 2026-11-19 on the same code: `3c1944a8` (09:18Z) and `bf24293c` (09:26Z) failed, `afdb6044` (09:27Z) and `ba70b428` (09:35Z) were green. It is a race with the queue, not a broken generator.

## What changed (`.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` only)

- **Before** the regeneration: read the open generated PR's `mergeQueueEntry` through GraphQL and, when it is queued, write the reason to the step summary and `exit 0` — a queued generated PR is already the deliverable, and the next push after the queue lands refreshes it. A no-op run now costs seconds instead of minutes of generation.
- **At the push**: the queue can land between the check and the push, so that one refusal (`GH006` + `merge queue`) is also a no-op; every other push failure still prints the error and exits 1.

## Verification

- `bash -n` on the workflow's script: OK.
- The GraphQL query dry-run against the repository: the open generated PR (#405) answers `mergeQueueEntry: null`, merged PRs answer null — the shape is right.
- Live evidence (DoD): the next push to `main` after the merge produces a green `issue-registry` run — a refresh or a recorded no-op, never a `GH006` failure.

Closes #400

## What

Two defects made every generated publish PR red (PR #384, closed before this branch):

**P2 — the commit had no DCO sign-off.** `GitHub::create_commit` sends only `message`, `tree` and `parents`; the GitHub API attributes the commit to the sealed token's user and adds no `Signed-off-by`. The repo's `dco` job greps every non-merge commit for `^Signed-off-by: .+ <[^<>@ ]+@[^<> ]+>$` and failed on `b5d8a142`. The publisher now reads the token's own user (`GET /user`) and appends the trailer naming that same account — `<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` is the address GitHub exposes without a public email. One extra API call per publish.

**P1 — the no-snapshot fixture was loading a generated snapshot.** The generated pack overwrites `docs/design/data/snapshot.js` with a live payload that carries `msp`. `check-console.cjs`'s case 1 is defined as the homepage/file:// shape with **no snapshot loaded** (it asserts "No published snapshot is loaded" and "the WBS study tab is not public"). On a publish branch its server fell through to the static pack, so the fixture loaded the generated payload, `live.msp` made the public plan ribbon add the WBS tab, and the case failed at `check-console.cjs:1824` (`1 !== 0`). That server now answers 404 for `/data/snapshot.js` in case 1 only. The with-snapshot shape is unchanged and still covered by case 1c, which explicitly renders the WBS tab read-only from the published snapshot.

The generated data itself is untouched; no hand edits to the pack.

## Acceptance evidence (at `3df5f9e2`)

| Part | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P2 | `cargo test -p conveyor-server --lib publish` (m4, cargo-guard) | **3/3**, incl. `a_publish_commit_is_signed_off_for_the_token_user` |
| P2 | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --lib integrations::github` (m4) | **3/3** |
| P1 | `node docs/design/scripts/check-console.cjs` with `docs/design/data/snapshot.js` replaced by a snapshot carrying `msp`, old script (origin/main) | **FAILS** at `check-console.cjs:1824`, "the WBS study tab is not public" |
| P1 | the same data, this branch's script | **PASSES** — 4 servers, 0 unhandled page errors |
| Gate | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit **0** |
| Gate | `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (m4, cargo-guard) | exit **0** |

The generated pack from #384 was not available for the P1 evidence: the PR was closed and its branch deleted at 09:00Z. A snapshot carrying the same triggering field (`msp`) reproduces the exact assertion.

## Post-merge proof (named, not skipped)

The issue's final DoD clause — a fresh console publish produces a green PR — needs the deployed worker. After the image roll, run `publish.start` for tenant `nonagentic`; the new PR must have both `dco` and `design-pack` green. The issue stays open until that is recorded.

## Risks

- `user_identity()` adds one `GET /user` per publish. The sealed token is a classic PAT (user read is implicit); a future fine-grained token must allow it.
- The public with-snapshot shape still renders the WBS tab read-only (case 1c); that is intended and unchanged.

The cockpit rendered `CockpitBody` inside `match data.get()`; every SSE-triggered refetch produced a new `CockpitData` and re-created the subtree, so an edit in progress lost its Save control (`element was detached from the DOM`, `cockpit.spec.ts:38`). pulls.body:
Closes #83

T14 makes the estate's Rust tools **tools of the conveyor**. T13 (#76) shipped the tables, the
broker and `tools.call`, but nothing wrote a toolkit, so no run could resolve one; there was no
probe, no zero-use report and no outage unbind. This is that half.

## What landed

**`toolkits.publish` — the import wave.** `seed/toolkits/*.json`, one manifest per estate service,
each declaring its destination service, status (`published` or `draft`) and the actions it exposes.
Publishing is content-addressed: the manifest's hash is stored on the version it produced, so a
second publish is `unchanged`, a changed manifest inserts the next `toolkit_version`, and a
published row is never updated except for its status transition. **Each tool's `input_schema` is
copied from the live `ActionSpec` at publish time** — a hand-written schema would drift the first
time an action changed, and the drift would surface as a `422` on a legitimate call.

| toolkit | service | tools | status today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `coding` | coding | `jobs_create`, `jobs_get` (`coding_jobs.*`) | published |
| `speech` | tts | `synthesize` (`produce.speech`) | published |
| `transcription` | asr | `transcribe` (`media.transcribe`) | published |
| `image_gen` | image_gen | `generate` (`media.generate_image`) | published |
| `retrieval` | strata_rag | `query` (`retrieval.query`) | draft — URL unset |
| `artifacts` | artifacts | `list` (`artifacts.list`) | draft — URL unset |
| `billing` | billing_service | `summary` (`billing.summary`) | draft — URL unset |
| `worker_management` | worker_management | `workers`, `providers`, `graphs` | draft — upstream retired |

**`tools.probe`** — read-only health per published toolkit. The destination is never invented: the
service alias comes from the toolkit row, the base URL from the same `CONVEYOR_EXTERNAL_<SERVICE>_URL`
the dispatcher reads, the health path from the manifest. A failure disables that toolkit's bindings
with a `probe_disabled` marker; a later green probe re-enables **only** what it unbound, so a binding
an operator switched off by hand stays off. `dry_run` reports without touching bindings.

**`tools.usage`** — every published tool version with its calls over a bounded window
(`window_days`, default 30, 1..=365) and the zero-use subset named. The count comes from the
`tool_call` ledger, never a process counter.

**The refusal names the tool.** `tools.call`'s `409 tool_not_ready` now carries
`errors[] = [{"field": "tool", …}]` — the wire form of §11.9's `blocking[]`, the same mapping
`capability::readiness` already uses. `store::tool::resolve` already filtered `b.enabled` and
`status='published'`, so the probe's unbind needs no new gate.

**Two scopes**: `tools:read` / `tools:write`, admin-only for the write side. Publishing, probing and
unbinding are platform administration; `tools.call` deliberately stays on `runs:write` because a
job's authority is its binding.

## Evidence (local, at `c1d6ea85`)

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 publish is idempotent, a change bumps the version | `estate_toolkits::a_publish_is_idempotent_and_a_change_bumps_the_version` | PASS — 8 toolkits `created`, then all `unchanged`, then `coding` v1→v2 |
| P1.3/P2.1 a draft toolkit is unbound and uncallable | `estate_toolkits::an_unconfigured_toolkit_is_draft_and_uncallable` | PASS — `409 tool_not_ready`, `errors[0].field="tool"`, **zero destination hits** |
| P4.1 a failed probe unbinds; the call is 409 | `estate_toolkits::a_failed_probe_unbinds_and_the_call_is_409` | PASS — green → live; 500 → `unreachable`, 1 binding disabled; refusal before the backend, no ledger row |
| P2.2 the refusal lifts | `estate_toolkits::a_probe_green_toolkit_is_callable` | PASS — `bindings_restored=1`, call succeeds, one `tool_call` row |
| P4.2 an in-flight run finishes | `estate_toolkits::an_in_flight_run_finishes_after_the_unbind` | PASS — unbind lands mid-dispatch, call still 200, ledger kept |
| P3.1 zero-use flags only uncalled tools | `estate_toolkits::the_zero_use_report_flags_only_uncalled_tools` | PASS — called tool count 1, uncalled flagged; `window_days: 0` → 422 |

Whole gate at the head: **3364/3364 nextest passed** (7 skipped), `clippy --all-targets -D warnings`,
`cargo fmt --check`, doctests, `--print-openapi --check-lock`, the design pack (coverage / data /
docs `--check` and the six rendered-surface checks), `no-private-refs.sh`, betterleaks — all green.

## Regenerated, and why

## What changed

`scripts/ci/gate.sh` ran `cargo` directly, so every invocation built into the **calling worktree's** own `target/` — 48 GB measured on `.worktrees/issue-366` (2026-11-18) — outside the free-disk floor and build slots `cargo-guard.py` exists to enforce.

The gate now resolves **one** build route before anything runs:

- **Guard installed** (`${CARGO_GUARD:-$HOME/.claude/scripts/cargo-guard.py}`): `--print-target` returns `<repo>/target/claude` (derived from `--git-common-dir`, so every worktree and session shares it). `clippy`, `nextest` and the doc tests run **through the guard** (30 GiB floor, two build slots, jobs=4, incremental off). A `cargo metadata` preflight applies the floor before the Postgres/Redis containers start.
- **No guard**: the same `<repo>/target/claude` is derived directly, and the route line says plainly there is no floor or slot control.
- Both branches print `==> build route: …`; `--print-route` prints it and exits without building. `cargo fmt` and `cargo audit` stay unguarded (they do not compile). No `--target-dir` anywhere.

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 no per-worktree target | `bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` in a worktree, quiet host | `gate: OK`, `GATE_RC=0`, 3353/3353 tests passed (7 skipped); `WORKTREE_TARGET=ABSENT`; the build used `…/conveyor-377/target/claude` (31 G). A first run under a concurrent suite failed only `conveyor-media`'s macOS-Chrome 300 s-ceiling test, which skips when no browser is present; the quiet run is green. |

Closes #372

## What

**Part 1 — one issue source.** `scripts/build-programme-seed.py` now reads `docs/design/data/issues.json`, the registry `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` writes immediately before it, instead of calling `gh issue list` a second time. `--issues-file` overrides the path; an explicit but missing path fails closed; a checkout with no exported registry falls back to the live list and names that route. The workflow already fetches the file first, so the shipped seed and registry are one read by construction.

**Part 2 — no reopen wedge.** `.github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` finds the one open generated PR (on the fixed head or a timestamped one) and updates it. With no open PR it pushes a fresh `automation/issue-registry-<timestamp>` branch and opens a new PR. It never reopens a closed generated PR: after a force-push, GitHub refuses that reopen permanently (measured: #355, #367).

## Why / source

The workflow is green on its last run only because no issue changed between its two live reads; the structural defect is in the source. A closed-without-merge generated PR force-pushes its branch on the next run, which makes `gh pr reopen` fail forever. Sources and the baseline are in issue #372; both defects are measured at `main@f14b7d36`.

## Acceptance evidence

| Scenario | Command / test | Result | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test seed_programme seed_programme_links_the_registered_issues` | **1 passed**, 3 filtered out | `c356e9d` |
| P1.2 | synthetic registry `--issues-file /tmp/issues-mod.json` (adds #999, label S12) → S12 issues `[6, 26, 27, 28, 370, 375, 999]`; missing explicit file → exit 1; default `--check` current | **PASS** | `c356e9d` |
| P2.1 | `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*gh pr reopen' .github/workflows/issue-registry.yml` → 0; extracted run block `bash -n` → OK | **PASS at head**; next main run confirms | `c356e9d` |
| P2.2 | jq simulation: fixed head → update #7; timestamped head → update #9; no PR → fresh `automation/issue-registry-<UTC>`; mixed list → first generated head | **PASS** | `c356e9d` |

## Gate at the exact head

- `rbuild -- fmt --all -- --check` → rc 0
- `rbuild -- clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` → rc 0
- `scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` → rc 0
- `python3 scripts/build-coverage.py --check` → rc 0
- `python3 scripts/build-programme-seed.py --check` → rc 0
- Workflow YAML parses (`ruby -ryaml`), run block `bash -n` → OK

## Resume

Branch `issue/372-issue-registry-source`: claim `3002bd04`, fix `c356e9df`. No handoff — this PR is the delivery.

## Risks

- P2's wedge path cannot be reproduced locally; its structural proof is the removal of the `gh pr reopen` command and the fresh-branch selection. The next push to `main` is the live confirmation.
- The generator now prefers the committed registry; to refresh it, run `scripts/fetch-issues.sh` first (the `gh` fallback remains for a checkout that has never exported one).

pulls.body:
Closes #75

## What this is

T4 — the kanban coach, built as SPEC_V2 §6.2 and §10.4 specify: every interruption yields
**one coach card** carrying **one closed-set triage** and **at most one remedy**; a repeat
signature escalates to a human instead of opening a second card; a coach card never produces a
coach card; a systemic class opens exactly one kata.

## The model

- The coach card is an ordinary `card` row of the new catalogue type **`coach`**, on the
  interrupted card's board, in the interrupted card's lane (issue decision Q1). No new card table.
- `coach_interruption` records the interruption: the coach card, the interrupted card and run,
  the rendered signature (`card | error class | failing process/step`, decision Q2), the closed
  triage and its confidence, the window, and the escalation/kata links. One **open** row per
  `(card, signature)` — a partial unique index, so a repeat cannot open a second card.
- `coach_remedy` is the at-most-one remedy, append-only (the runtime role holds no UPDATE/DELETE).
- The repeat window, the confidence floor and the systemic classes are read from the tenant's
  `decision_policy` row of kind `coach.window` — T2's store, never a second one (decision Q3).
  Absent row = 24 h, floor 0.7, `conveyor_defect` systemic.

## The actions (SPEC §10.4)

| Action | Effect | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `coach.interrupt` | write | closes expired windows, then either escalates the open same-signature interruption (one human approval, no second card) or creates the coach card + interruption + the coach run on it |
| `coach.triage` | write | records one class from `transient\\|conveyor_defect\\|job_defect\\|project_decision\\|external` with its confidence and narrative; out-of-set is a 422 |
| `coach.remedy` | write | writes the one remedy from `retry\\|move\\|repull\\|block\\|ask\\|note` (derived from the class, or supplied and validated); below the confidence floor only `ask`, which opens the human gate; a systemic class opens exactly one kata |
| `coach.escalate` | write | the explicit human escalation |

The remedy is never the model's: the coach agent's `allowed_actions` carries `coach.triage` and
**not** `coach.remedy`; the computed step supplies it.

## The interruption path

- `err.card` now calls `coach.interrupt` instead of starting a coach run on the interrupted card.
  Its existing at-least-once flow (move → comment → coach, per-run idempotency keys) is unchanged.
- The per-card depth cap now counts **interruptions** (a run count on the interrupted card would
  read zero forever, since the coach runs on its own card).
- Recursion guard at the **enqueue** boundary: a failed run of the `cap.kanban_coach.` family or
  of a card of type `coach` queues **no** `err.card` job at all. `err.card`'s own refusal stays as
  the defence for a job queued before this change.

## Seed content

- `seed/catalogue.json` gains the `coach` card type (75 types).
- `seed/processes/named.yaml` gains a **new** process key `cap.kanban_coach.handle_error.v2`
  (+ its agent and SOPs) — the seed loader never revisits a published key, so a v1 tenant only
  gets the new behaviour through a new key. Step 2 is now a computed `coach.remedy`; the old
  unconditional `call kata.open` is gone, which is the P4 rule.
- Live application (after deploy): `conveyor migrate --seed --tenant nonagentic` and
  `conveyor migrate --process-catalogue --tenant nonagentic`.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Test |
|---|---|
| P1.1 one card, one triage, one remedy | `crates/actions/tests/coach.rs::an_interruption_yields_one_coach_card_one_triage_and_one_remedy` |
| P1.2 closed sets refuse | `::an_out_of_set_triage_or_remedy_is_refused` (422, row unchanged) |
| P1.3 low confidence → ask + gate | `::a_low_confidence_triage_routes_to_ask` |
| P2.1 repeat escalates | `::a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card` |
| P2.2 escalated is not retried | `::an_escalated_signature_is_not_retried` |
| P3.1 no coach about a coach | `::a_failed_coach_run_never_opens_a_coach_card` |
| P3.2 no further err.card job | `::the_coach_chain_settles_at_one_card` |
| P4.1 systemic → one kata | `::a_systemic_class_opens_one_kata` |
| P4.2 transient → none | `::a_transient_class_opens_no_kata` |

Gate and contract updates in the same branch: migration `0057_coach.sql` (in the embedded set),
`scripts/grants-runtime.sql`, `docs/design/data/actions.json` (466 actions),
`served-spec.lock.json` (497 operations), the registry expectation (448 internal / 18 external),
the process-catalogue count (334), four parity samples (transport parity on the refusal path —
behaviour is the coach suite), the catalogue-install and migration-ledger counters, and
`docs/evidence/v2-coverage.*` (the `actions:coach` row is now `exists`) with its docs mirror.

Closes #366

## What

Native spreadsheet support in the conveyor: a new `crates/sheets` (workbook model, deterministic
OOXML `.xlsx` writer, `calamine`-backed reader), the stored-ZIP writer extracted into
`crates/zipstore` so the deck and the sheet emit one archive implementation, and two internal
actions — `sheets.export` (inline base64, or `as: "document"` through the documents surface) and
`sheets.import`. The served lock, the design pack's action list and the counted registry move from
460 to 462 action routes.

## Why

The tool-estate assignment (2026-11-18): every tool the conveyor consumes is Rust, and xlsx —
consuming it and, above all, producing it for matrices and data tables — was the one capability

1. **`.xls`/`.ods` import is not implemented.** The plan said `calamine` would bring it for free;
   merged ranges are only exposed by its concrete `Xlsx` reader, and merged ranges are part of the
   model. Import accepts OOXML workbooks; anything else is a typed `unreadable` refusal.

   v2,workbench}.cjs` require `playwright-core`, which this repository does not install — that gap

   cached results, dates, merged ranges, names and order round-trip exactly.

  row import-lost one row. Found by the proptest, fixed by adding the range's start offset; the
  regression is checked in at `crates/sheets/tests/roundtrip.proptest-regressions`.
- The shared-string writer looked each string up by linear scan (quadratic on a large sheet) and
  the reader allocated a rectangular grid (a single cell at row 100,000 would allocate 100k × width
  cells). Both are now a hash lookup and a sparse map.
- My own `export_over_inline_cap_is_refused` asserted on `ActionError::detail`, which is the generic
  "the input does not match the action schema"; the specific refusal is a field error. Caught by the
  first full local gate; asserted on `errors` now.

## What this delivers

T10 — SAFe gives the programme its cadence, MSP its tranche review and benefit track. All five parts of the issue are implemented with the issue's own `Verify:` targets.

- **P1 — PI planning materialises the backlog by WSJF within WIP.** `spine::materialise_pi_tx` drafts one card per `wbs_node(kind='deliverable', status='open', card_id IS NULL)` in the board named by `meta.board_id`, ordered by `(business_value + time_criticality + risk_reduction) / job_size` computed in the query (no stored score), bounded by the active lane's `wip_limit` minus its live cards. The cadence moves `planned → materialised` in the same transaction; `apps/server::cadence::tick` runs on every worker pass and is idempotent. A zero `job_size` is a typed refusal at the domain and unstorable in the table.
- **P2 — no demo, no credit.** `credit_demo_tx` records one credit per (cadence, deliverable) only when the deliverable is accepted and exhibits at least one evidence ref (`gate_evidence_missing` otherwise); the evidence is copied onto the credit; a repeat returns the same row.
- **P3 — the retro produces lessons.** One coach card per retro cadence (`open_retro_tx`, found by `meta.cadence_id`), findings recorded on it, and `close_retro_tx` refuses while any finding has no `lesson` proposal, naming the finding. `lesson` rows carry the evidence refs and the cadence; T8 later owns review/promote (the pack's single-credit rule keeps `lesson` T8's).
- **P4 — the end-of-tranche review is a programme decision.** A `continue` review authorises the next tranche in the same write (`authorised_at` + `authorisation_review_id`); pause/stop keep their states; a review without baselines, benefit status and the risk register is refused. `assert_project_can_start` now reads the tranche first and answers `409 tranche_not_authorised`. A baseline change cites an approved change request (`rebaseline_requires_change`), never the review. A dependency slip names the benefits at risk through the `benefit_link` edges over the slipped project's outputs.
- **P5 — benefits realization is a procedure after delivery.** `benefit_realization_tx` computes the delta against the measured baseline, attributed to the profile's operational area; a post-measurement without a baseline is refused `benefit_baseline_missing`; `close_programme_tx` refuses without a realization plan (`realization_plan_missing`) or its post-closure owner (`post_closure_owner_missing`).

Migration `0056_cadence_tranche.sql`: `lesson`, `programme_demo_credit`, and the tranche authorisation columns. The cadence tick also credits demo evidence and opens the retro card, so the new store functions have their callers.

## Evidence at this head

Closes #76

## What

T13 — the tool platform's spine (SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10, §12 T13). One migration
(`0053_tool_platform.sql`; renumbered from 0052 because #339 landed first) adds `toolkit`, `tool`,
`tool_binding` and the append-only `tool_call` ledger — RLS enable+force on each, and the runtime
role keeps no UPDATE/DELETE on the ledger. A new `tools.call` action, dispatched by the engine as
`HandlerRef::Broker`, resolves the run's binding and pinned tool version, enforces the binding's
effect ceiling, validates against the tool version's closed schema (the shared validator now
enforces `pattern` and numeric/length bounds), gates a destructive tool on an approved approval
naming it, then dispatches **the declared external action the tool names** — no second control
plane — and writes exactly one `tool_call` row plus one `tool.called` event after the call. A job
storage adapter (`tenant/<tenant_id>/…` keys, SHA-256 per object, 64 MiB cap, SSE-S3 on the sealed
instance) completes P5.

## Why

Issue #76's Definition of Done: a development job reaches coding only through the conveyor broker;
every call lands as one `tool_call` row; a destructive call without the tenant's approvals and a
schema-invalid input are both refused before the backend is touched; a job writes and reads a
tenant-prefixed object while the prompt never carries an S3 key. T13 is the tranche the programme
runs first (owner decision 2026-11-18) and it unblocks T6/T7/T14/T15/T16.

## Track

- [x] **Unit work** — `Closes #76`.

## Checks

- [x] The local gate at the PR head — results below.
- [x] Every commit is signed off; the sign-off is mine.
- [x] No credential, private hostname, private address or private infrastructure detail. The S3
      proof used a throwaway local server and its documented dev credentials, exactly as
      `prove-s3.sh` does.

## Credit

georgiedekker

## Acceptance evidence

| P1.1 | `tool_platform.rs::a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker` | PASS — the bound coding tool reaches the registered `/api/jobs` alias; exactly one destination call |

| P3.1 | `tool_platform.rs::a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused` | PASS — 403 `approval_required`, zero destination requests |
| P3.2 | `tool_platform.rs::a_binding_ceiling_cannot_be_raised_at_run_time` | PASS — 403 `tool_effect_forbidden`; widening the binding in SQL admits the same call |
| P4.1 | `tool_platform.rs::a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call` | PASS — 422 `tool_input_invalid` for an undeclared field, a `pattern` violation and a numeric bound; zero network calls |
| P5.1 | `tool_platform.rs::a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object`; `s3_wire.rs::the_job_storage_adapter_round_trips_under_the_tenant_prefix` | PASS — key prefix, hash and size match; the wire leg passes against a real RustFS server (`CONVEYOR_S3_SSE=none`, as `prove-s3.sh` sets) |

Closes #319

## What

The evidence-review service is absorbed into `apps/scientific` as the review family — 55 operations
over ten route modules, the actor seam, the six blinding layers, the derived flow ledger and the
sealed inclusion-set export. P1 (the capture) and P2 (the schema) were already on this branch; this
PR lands P3, P4 and P5.

- **Actor seam.** A licence token proves the tenant and is a *machine*; a human decision carries
  `X-Actor-Token`, a user JWT verified against the realm's JWKS (pinned issuer, required audience,
  `azp` allowlist, asymmetric algorithms only). A service principal is a machine even when it has a
  subject. No decision body has a reviewer field.
- **Schema access.** One transaction per request, `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant`,
  `app.actor_subject_id`, `app.actor_role` — transaction-scoped because PgBouncer pools server
  connections. The runtime role is the non-owner, `NOBYPASSRLS` role already in the Deployment, so
  `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` binds.
- **Blinding.** Structural, not declarative: own-assignment queues and cursors, a single blinded
  read, `404` never `403`, no aggregate while the caller owes a decision (L6), and governed
  unblinding that writes its audit row before the disclosure is returned.
- **Flow ledger.** Derived on every read from immutable history, with the newest-work settling rule
  (an all-or-nothing timestamp comparison), conservation checked on every derivation, and
  `projection_stale` making a cache disagreement visible.
- **Seal.** SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical manifest, with a separate canonical payload digest;
  the same inclusion set seals once (a repeat is a replay serving the recorded row), and the stored
  bytes are served after the ledger moves.
- **Contract.** `apps/scientific/contract/openapi.lock.json` grows from 18 to 73 operations from the
  P1 capture (never from this implementation), and every ported operation is registered, locked and
  named in the capture with its module and its check.

## Why

ADR 0006/0007: the tool estate completes in this workspace. Every other conveyor tool already runs a
Rust image; the evidence-review service was the last one not absorbed. Its repository is retired and
its database roles were deleted on 2026-10-30, so the port creates what it needs rather than
inheriting it.

## What this delivers

T9 — the conveyor runs a TOGAF ADM capability, not a document library.

- **The artefact standard and repository (D1).** `artifact_type` seeded by the tailored profile; `architecture_artifact` (catalog, matrix, diagram, principles catalog) with its entries and typed links; approve is immutable and a supersede writes a new version that cites its predecessor; `repository_search` follows `reuse` edges across projects, phases and plateaus.
- **The Preliminary capability (D2).** The tailored `adm_profile` (phase set, mandatory set per phase+plateau, the contract kind closing each phase); the Architecture Board as a `governance_body` row (`board_open` idempotent on its key, `board_get`, `board_decide` writing the approval); the nine-dimension maturity and seven-category skills assessments, each refused unless every dimension/category is present.
- **The architecture project, phases and contracts (D3).** `projects.create`/`pm.charter` with `project_type_code = architecture` materialise Preliminary and A–H as `wbs_node(kind='phase')` rows; a phase advances only when one plateau's mandatory set is approved and its contract is live; a superseded contract re-opens the gate and its replacement names it two-way.
- **Delivery compliance and change (D4/D5).** `pm.route_gate` with `gate = design` resolves only against a live architecture contract — absent is `409 architecture_contract_missing`, superseded is `409 architecture_contract_not_live` naming the status, and no approval row is written; one compliance level per contract; a waiver needs an accepting owner and a reassessment date; a Phase-H review records exactly one typed outcome (change register row or kata candidate), and H cannot close on an unrecorded review.
- **Console (D6).** The **Architecture** destination in `apps/web` with four tabs — Capability, ADM phases, Artefact repository, Board & compliance — including the phase-advance refusal shown verbatim and the artefact inspector over entries and links. The design study already carries the ADM destination and `check-v2.cjs` exercises it.

## Measured before building

Resuming the pushed foundation at `a93cf399`, four defects made the issue's own scenarios unprovable and are fixed here: `governance_body` had no write/read action (`board_decide` 404'd); `materialise_phases_tx` was called by nothing (a project had no phase nodes, so advance always refused); the `architecture` project type was absent from both catalogue seeds (`projects.create` refused the code); entries/links/contracts had no read actions and `profile_get` returned no `artifact_type_id`.
