Closes #62

## What

The programme's plan state is now **actual state**: GitHub issues are the work definition,
conveyor rows are the execution state, and the design site renders the join. The build-time plan
seed is gone, so nothing fabricates boards, cards or runs at image build.

- **P1** remove the plan seeder end to end: `seed_plans.rs`, `seed/plans.json`,
  `seed/plans/card-types.json`, `scripts/build-plan-seed.py`, `docs/design/data/plan-seed.js`,
  the `--seed` call, the DESIGN fallback and the check assertions. `seed_programme`,
  `seed/catalogue.json` and `seed/processes/` stay.
- **P2** `conveyor admin retire-plan-seed --tenant <slug>` archives the 63 seeded cards through
  the real `cards.archive` handler (archive lane, `card.archived` event, audit row), skips leased
  or live-run cards, is idempotent and tenant-scoped. It does not delete.
- **P3** `cards.create` accepts a bounded `meta` object (≤16 KiB, JSON object, `422` otherwise):
  the real `issue` / `unit_key` / `process_key` / `plan` link. The public snapshot still exports
  only those named keys, never the whole meta.
- **P4** the Plan **Boards** tab joins each project's `meta.issues` to the published issue
  registry and to non-archived cards/runs: issue state, real card or **not intaken**, lane, run,
  evidence. No seed fallback; DESIGN mode says the boards are live-only. Portfolio progress is the
  linked issues' closed/total plus the real card count.
- **P5** `conveyor admin action invoke` and `conveyor admin intake` call the same action engine as
  HTTP (`Authority::Internal`, `Role::KataExecutor`, the tenant's own actor) — the operator path in
  an OIDC-only deployment. `intake --project T0 --issue 34` is the first real card.

## Evidence at completion

pulls.body:
## What this changes

The absorption baseline: the workspace, build and gate machinery the three service units (#44–#46) will use.

- **Members are globs.** `Cargo.toml` lists `crates/*` and `apps/*`; a new service is a directory, not a root-manifest edit. `Cargo.lock` gains only the new package.
- **`crates/platform`** — the shared kit: `config` (`BIND_ADDR`/`DATABASE_URL`), `telemetry` (tracing), `health` (`GET /health`), `db` (pool + `sqlx::migrate!` wrapper). No domain types, no feature flags.
- **`crates/platform/src/bin/conveyor-health.rs`** — a database-free liveness server over the kit.
- **`docker/Dockerfile.service`** — a generic multi-stage template (`ARG PACKAGE`, `ARG BIN`), public digest-pinned base, explicit cache ids.
- **`scripts/ci/affected.sh`** (+ `affected.py`) — changed paths → affected packages via `cargo metadata` reverse dependencies; root/lock/toolchain/`.cargo/`/`scripts/ci/`/`crates/platform/` select everything. Fixture matrix in `scripts/ci/tests/affected.sh`.
- **`scripts/ci/gate.sh`** — the public local gate: fmt, clippy, audit, full suite, guards, with ephemeral Postgres 18 + Redis on random local ports, removed on exit.
- **`compose.yaml`** — the `strata` profile uses a digest-pinnable image; no `../strata_rag` build context.
- **`.github/workflows/ci-public.yml`** — one **new** job, `service-image`, builds `Dockerfile.service` on a hosted runner and asserts `/health`. The root `image` job never exercised the template. No other job is touched; #17 was notified (additive).

Closes #43

## Why the extra job

The template could not be proven on this machine: mini3's Docker Desktop VM is 2.35 GiB and the release build dies with `ResourceExhausted`; m1 and hp2 have no Docker; worker3 (Docker 29.8.1, 21 GiB free) is the registry + all-PV host and was not used. The CI job is the durable proof and runs on every PR. It builds the probe binary, so it needs no database and stays cheap.

## Evidence at `fe50153`

| Scenario | Command / test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 | `cargo metadata --no-deps`; `rbuild -- check -p conveyor-platform` | 12 packages; check exit 0 |
| P1.2 | `rg "^pub mod" crates/platform/src/lib.rs` | config, db, health, telemetry |
| P2.1 | `service-image` job in this PR's run | build + `/health` — see the run's `service-image` job |
| P2.2 | `rg "registry\.redacted\|ghcr\.io/nonagenticai" docker/Dockerfile.service` | none; digest-pinned public `debian:12-slim` |
| P3.1 | `bash scripts/ci/tests/affected.sh` | 11/11 |
| P3.2 | `affected.sh --base origin/main --head HEAD`; `--files ""` | 12 packages; empty prints nothing, exit 0 |
| P4.1 | `TEST_DATABASE_URL=… REDIS_URL=… rbuild --gate` | **exit 0** at `fe50153` (fmt, clippy, full suite, audit; 4 allowed unmaintained warnings). `gate.sh` itself is not run on this estate host — the estate routes builds through `rbuild`; the script mirrors the `checks` job step-for-step |
| P4.2 | `PATH=/nonexistent /bin/bash scripts/ci/gate.sh` | `missing docker: install Docker and start the daemon` |
| P5.1 | `docker compose config -q`; `rg "\.\./" compose.yaml` | clean; no `../` |
| P6.1 | `rg "^members" -A3 Cargo.toml`; metadata count | `crates/*`, `apps/*`; 12 packages |
| P7.1 | `service-image` job: build | in this run |
| P7.2 | `service-image` job: smoke -> `{"status":"ok","service":"conveyor-health"}` | in this run |

## Risks

- The `service-image` job adds ~5–8 minutes to a run, in parallel with `checks`; wall-clock is set by `checks`.
- `gate.sh` is the first script a public contributor runs with Docker; it binds random ports and removes the containers on exit, including on failure.
- No existing CI job, archetype input or ghcr push is changed.

pulls.body:
## What

The programme stops being 47 bare projects. Every plan unit is a card on its project's board, each card names a real process, and the public design site renders those rows (Plan → **Boards**, LIVE) instead of the WBS fixture. The mock rows also become the seed: the same committed document feeds the seeder and the DESIGN fallback.

- `seed/plans/card-types.json` (explicit unit→type map; **T0 pinned to `architecture_task`**) and `seed/plans.json` / `docs/design/data/plan-seed.js`, generated by `scripts/build-plan-seed.py` — 47 projects, 63 units.
- `crates/store/src/seed_plans.rs`: idempotent boards/lanes/cards; the `it` project type (the `program` matrix is empty and would make cards unmovable); closed issues land in Done on first insert; later runs only advance Intake→Done; hand-moved, leased and live-run cards are untouched; `meta.seed_name` guards renames.
- `store::board::ensure_board_from_template_tx` shared by `projects.create`, `project_requests.promote` and the seeder; the action's 409/422 contract is unchanged.
- Snapshot: cards carry only the named seed keys (`unit_key`, `issue`, `process_key`, `plan`), never the free-form `meta`; `snapshot.js` now carries the issue registry and feedback (it was built before they were inserted); `--git-sha` records the published commit.
- Design site: a live **Boards** tab on Plan & WBS (project → lanes → cards, process and issue links) with the committed plan seed as the DESIGN fallback; Portfolio project rows derive completed/total card counts from the snapshot; tabs that still render fixtures keep `V2 · PROPOSED`.
- publish seeds are image inputs (`include_str!`), so a publish refreshes only the issue registry — regenerating the seeds at publish time would disagree with the running binary the moment an issue closes.
- `scripts/build-v2-coverage.py`: SPEC §10.3–§10.5 against the code — 42 rows (10 `extend`, 32 `new`), curated verdicts carry their reason; published as JSON plus a Documents page.
- Programme seed: SPEC §12 T-slice dependencies and gates are no longer dropped; the S06a inline-comment and S21 no-frontmatter parser defects fixed.

## Verification (local, at PR head)

- `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-store --test seed_plans --test seed_programme --locked` — 7 passed.
- `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-actions --test board --test board_satellites -p conveyor-server --test snapshot_deterministic --locked` — 12 passed.
- `rbuild -- nextest run --no-tests=fail --locked` (workspace, 1228 tests) — **environmental stop:** 1050 passed, then the m1 throwaway Postgres hit `No space left on device` (host Data volume 100%). The 8 affected store tests reran green in isolation (`prompt_catalogue`, `process_seed`, `process_tree`, `prompt_audit`, exit 0). The full suite is for CI's clean runner.
- `rbuild -- clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — exit 0 (workspace).
- `rbuild -- test --doc --locked` — exit 0.
- `rbuild -- audit` — exit 0 (4 allowed warnings).
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-{v2,studio,learning,workbench,architecture}.cjs` — 169/234/139/119/142 checks passed, no runtime errors or external requests; `check-docs` 12; `check-data` green.
- `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` — 1143 files, 0 failures.
- Generators deterministic: `build-programme-seed.py --check`, `build-plan-seed.py --check`, `build-v2-coverage.py --check`.

## Not in this PR

The process-catalogue install, the live seeding, the snapshot and the homepage publish are operational steps after the merge (the design-site publication runbook). T0 (#34) is the next lane; this seed creates its card.

Closes #55

## What

The public CI secret scan runs **betterleaks 1.10.1** instead of gitleaks 8.30.1, and the allowlist + rule set are renamed to match.

## Why

The estate swapped scanners on 2026-11-13 ([private-repo]#5170). This repo does not consume the shared archetype — it deliberately runs a full-tree scan, because it is published — so it needed its own change.

## `--config` is load-bearing

betterleaks only auto-loads a target's config under `--unsafe-auto-load-config`, so a bare `betterleaks dir` scans with its **built-in** defaults. Those are not gitleaks' defaults: measured on this tree, that alone produced **605 findings** (600 `generic-credential-uri` on ordinary local dev DSNs, 5 `generic-password` on compose placeholders), none of them real — a red gate on arrival. Passing the repo's config gives **0**, and makes CI agree with the local pre-commit/pre-push hooks, which have always used that file.

Two of betterleaks' extra default rules (`generic-credential-uri`, `generic-password`) are disabled by owner decision (2026-11-13) so this swap does not change what the gate catches.

## Renames

| before | after |
|---|---|
| `.gitleaks.toml` | `.betterleaks.toml` |
| `.gitleaksignore` | `.betterleaksignore` |

betterleaks reads either name; the rename only makes the file say which tool reads it. The four allowlist fingerprints are unchanged and still suppress.

## Evidence

| Scenario | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| P1.1 the pinned asset verifies | `sha256sum -c` against the v1.10.1 `checksums.txt` | `c174b42d…` matches |
| P1.2 a planted token fails the scan | `betterleaks dir` on a scratch tree with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` | exit 1, RuleID printed |
| P1.3 the real tree is clean | `betterleaks dir --config=.betterleaks.toml --gitleaks-ignore-path .betterleaksignore .` | **no leaks found** |

3.0.0

This release contains adjustments to the syntax tree to account for ongoing Rust language development from the 3 years since syn 2.0.0 and to anticipate some in-flight Rust language RFCs.

These include: default values in fields, pinned type sugar, raw lifetimes, generator blocks and functions, unnamed enum variants, attributes in tuple types and tuple patterns, named arguments in parenthesized generic argument lists, lightweight clones, const traits, const function pointers, mutability restricted fields, supertrait auto implementation, final associated functions, trait implementability restrictions, const blocks in path arguments, item-level const blocks, return type notation, never patterns, function delegation, mutable by-reference bindings, in-place initialization, field projections, explicitly dyn-compatible traits, view types, file-level frontmatter, generic const arguments, guard patterns, lazy type aliases, explicitly safe foreign items, super let, unsafe fields, pattern types, heterogeneous try-blocks, function contracts, async function trait bounds, static closure coroutine syntax, unsafe binder types, move expressions, for-await loops, and postfix keywords.

Breaking changes

Modifiers

To reserve more room for language evolution, there are 10 new non-exhaustive structs in the syntax tree having the following commonality:

  • Name ending in Modifiers. {BlockModifiers, ClosureModifiers, ConstModifiers, FieldModifiers, FnModifiers, ImplModifiers, LocalModifiers, TraitBoundModifiers, TraitModifiers, TypeModifiers}

  • Each implements Default. The default value is guaranteed to comprise no tokens.

pulls.body:
## What

Both `build` and `web` stages now declare **explicit, disjoint cache ids**:

| stage | registry | target |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | `id=cargo-registry-build` | `id=cargo-target-build` |
| `web` | `id=cargo-registry-web` | `id=cargo-target-web` (+ `id=cargo-leptos-web`) |

## Why (measured)

PR #39's `image` job — the first build of this repo on a **cold** builder (run `43315568696`, job `131522580101`) — failed at 2.7 s into the web stage:

```
error: failed to compile `cargo-leptos v0.3.11`
  failed to download `tracing-subscriber v0.3.23`
  failed to unpack package `tracing-subscriber v0.3.23`
  failed to open `/usr/local/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-…/tracing-subscriber-0.3.23/.cargo-ok`
  File exists (os error 17)
```

BuildKit builds the two independent stages **in parallel**, and a `--mount=type=cache` with no `id=` defaults its id to the mount target — so both stages unpacked crates into the *same* directories at the same time. ARC never hit it because its builder was warm; a fresh GitHub-hosted runner reproduces it deterministically.

## Verification

- **P1.2** `grep -n 'type=cache' Dockerfile` → 5 mounts, every one with an explicit id, and the two stages' ids are disjoint.
- `docker buildx build --call=check .` → **Check complete, no warnings found.**
- **P1.1** this PR's `image` job (build + smoke on a cold builder) is the acceptance test and the reason the PR exists. Note: this PR's `checks` job will stay red until #39 (the `--shm-size` fix) merges — the two failures are independent.

Closes #40

pulls.body:
## What

`ci-pg` now starts with `--shm-size=1g` in `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml`.

## Why (measured)

The first real GitHub-hosted run (run `43313232334`, job `checks`) ended:

```
Summary [ 268.171s] 1058/1225 tests run: 1055 passed, 3 failed, 4 skipped
FAIL conveyor-store::prompt_catalogue {the_builtin_catalogue_is_idempotent_and_a_pin_is_exact,
     the_recipe_budget_round_trips_and_a_zero_budget_is_refused,
     one_active_version_per_key_is_a_database_rule}
panicked at apps/server/tests/common/mod.rs:246/254:
  PgDatabaseError { code: "53100", message: "could not resize shared memory segment
  \"/PostgreSQL.…\" to 33554432 bytes: No space left on device", file: Some("dsm_impl.c") }
```

All three are migration paths (`scripts/db-roles.sql` / embedded migrations per fresh database). Postgres parallel workers allocate dynamic shared memory in `/dev/shm`, and a plain `docker run` gets Docker's **64 MB** default — the ARC/dind runner this workflow replaced had more. Not a suite defect: the same suite is green on `main`'s ARC history and on the local gate.

## Verification

- **P1.1** container shared memory: `docker run -d --name shm-probe -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres --shm-size=1g --tmpfs /var/lib/postgresql -p 127.0.0.1:15432:5432 postgres:18 -c fsync=off` → `docker exec shm-probe df -h /dev/shm` → **`shm 1.0G 0 1.0G 0% /dev/shm`** (probe container removed).
- **P1.2** the suite: this PR's own `checks` job — that is the acceptance command, and the reason the PR exists. Expected: `Summary … 0 failed`.
- `actionlint` clean; only `.github/workflows/ci-public.yml` is touched.

Closes #38

## What this changes

The public collaboration surface for the repository:

- **`SECURITY.md`** — private vulnerability reporting is the only report path; scope, response
  expectations, a 90-day coordinated-disclosure window and a safe-harbour clause.
- **`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`** — Contributor Covenant v2.1, private contact, enforcement path.
- **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** — every path owned by the current sole collaborator.
- **`docs/decisions/0004-tool-estate.md`** — the ruling: the tool estate is in scope of this
  repository; `SPEC.md` §2 and `parity.yaml` P-0006 remain the reference record and are **not
  edited**. Includes the repo-scope vs tool-estate distinction, the shared-service deployment
  rule, and the absorption contract.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md` v2** — the public gate replaces the private `rbuild`; fork →
  `issue/<n>-<slug>` → PR; DCO sign-off; required checks + maintainer review; what never lands.
- **`README.md`** — links to the published design, the issue queue, contributing, security and the
  licence.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — cargo, github-actions and docker, weekly.

Not touched: `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/SPEC_V2.md`, `parity/**`, `docs/design/**`,
`.github/workflows/**`.

Closes #42

| Scenario | Command / test | Result |

| P1.2 | `rg -n 'main\|best effort\|no bounty\|disclosure\|public issue' SECURITY.md` | pass |

| Gate | `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`; `bash scripts/ci/no-private-refs.sh` | pass; `exit 0`, 1143 files |
| P1.1, P7.1, P7.2 | repo settings (private vulnerability reporting, branch protection, secret scanning, Dependabot) | **applied after merge** — see below |

## Post-merge settings (P1.1, P7)

Applied immediately after this merges, then read back with the issue's commands: private
vulnerability reporting, branch protection on `main` (PR + the four CI checks, admin enforcement,

security updates. Applying branch protection before this PR merges would block its own merge.
